author: jonathanpeppers
body:
## Summary

Updates `ScalarEmitter.EmitSortMethod` in the source generator to emit **platform-specific** compare-and-swap patterns for numeric types. By default, a runtime `X86Base.IsSupported` check selects branchless `Math.Min`/`Math.Max` on x86 (JIT lowers to `cmov`) or branching `if/swap` on ARM (where branch prediction outperforms `csel` data-dependency chains). The JIT dead-code-eliminates the unused path.

Adds a `Branchless` property to `SortingNetworkAttribute` for explicit control.

Fixes #32

## Changes

### `ScalarEmitter.cs`

**Default (auto-detect) — generated code:**
```csharp
if (X86Base.IsSupported)
{
    { int t0 = Math.Min(e0, e1); int t1 = Math.Max(e0, e1); e0 = t0; e1 = t1; }
}
else
{
    if (e0 > e1) { int temp = e0; e0 = e1; e1 = temp; }
}
```

**`Branchless = true` — generated code:**
```csharp
{ int t0 = Math.Min(e0, e1); int t1 = Math.Max(e0, e1); e0 = t0; e1 = t1; }
```

**`Branchless = false` — generated code:**
```csharp
if (e0 > e1) { int temp = e0; e0 = e1; e1 = temp; }
```

### `SortingNetworkAttribute.cs`

New `Branchless` property:
```csharp
[SortingNetwork(27, typeof(int))]                        // auto-detect (default)
[SortingNetwork(27, typeof(int), Branchless = true)]     // force branchless
[SortingNetwork(27, typeof(int), Branchless = false)]    // force branching
```

## Type Coverage

| Pattern | Types |
|---|---|
| **Platform-adaptive (x86: Min/Max, ARM: if/swap)** | `byte`, `sbyte`, `short`, `ushort`, `int`, `uint`, `long`, `ulong`, `float`, `double` |
| **Branching always** | `char`, `nint`/`nuint` (delegates), `string`, custom `IComparable<T>` |

## Benchmark Results

CI run: https://github.com/jonathanpeppers/SortingNetworks/actions/runs/25268017631

### int scalar sizes 23-32 — GeneratedSort Ratio vs ArraySort (Random data)

| Size | Ubuntu x64 (EPYC 7763) | Windows x64 (EPYC 9V74) | macOS ARM (M1) | ARM64 (Neoverse-N2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 23 | **0.82x** | **0.68x** | **0.75x** | 1.56x (scalar only) |
| 24 | **0.73x** | 1.02x | **0.77x** | 1.34x |
| 25 | **0.87x** | **0.85x** | **0.75x** | 1.89x |
| 26 | **0.81x** | **0.84x** | **0.76x** | 1.43x |
| 27 | **0.69x** | **0.83x** | **0.76x** | 1.37x |
| 28 | **0.73x** | **0.73x** | **0.60x** | 1.22x |
| 31 | **0.75x** | — | — | 1.68x |
| 32 | **0.78x** | — | — | 1.78x |

**x86**: 13-32% faster across all sizes — `cmov` eliminates branch misprediction on random data.

**macOS M1 (ARM)**: 23-40% faster — Apple Silicon's wide out-of-order pipeline + excellent branch predictor handles sorting network branches well with `if/swap`.

**Neoverse-N2 (ARM)**: Ratios >1x on Random/Reversed/Duplicates are expected — this is a narrower ARM server core where `Array.Sort`'s introsort is competitive at these sizes. Sorted data is 0.53-0.62x (40-50% faster) because branching `if/swap` skips swaps entirely.

### SIMD sizes 27-28 (unchanged — SIMD path is not affected)

| Platform | Size 27 Random | Size 28 Random |
|---|---|---|
| Ubuntu x64 | **0.69x** | **0.73x** |
| Windows x64 | **0.83x** | **0.73x** |
| macOS M1 | **0.76x** | **0.60x** |

## Test Results

All 470 tests pass across 4 new test methods:
- `PlatformSpecific_EmittedForNumericTypes` (10 types)
- `BranchlessTrue_EmitsOnlyMinMax` (int, float)
- `BranchlessFalse_EmitsOnlyBranching` (int, float)
- `BranchingSwap_EmittedForNonMinMaxTypes` (char)

author: seanwevans
body:
### Motivation
- `check_reusable_inputs` collected `(input_name, line, column)` tuples and called `sorted()` directly, which raises `TypeError` in Python 3 when `line`/`column` values mix `int` and `NoneType` during comparisons. 
- The change ensures sorting is deterministic and safe even when position metadata is missing. 
- This prevents runtime crashes when scanning reusable workflows that reference inputs without full position information.

### Description
- Replace direct `sorted(references)` with `sorted(..., key=...)` in `ghast/core/scanner.py` using a key that orders by input name and treats `None` line/column values deterministically by using boolean flags and `-1` fallbacks. 
- Preserve original behavior of reporting findings while preventing comparison between `None` and `int`. 
- Add a regression test in `ghast/tests/core/test_scanner.py` that monkeypatches `get_position` to return mixed `(int, int)` and `(None, None)` values and asserts that `check_reusable_inputs` returns findings instead of crashing.

### Testing
- Ran the reusable-input-focused tests with `pytest -q ghast/tests/core/test_scanner.py -k reusable_inputs` and observed all relevant tests passed with output `4 passed, 17 deselected`. 
- The newly added regression test `test_check_reusable_inputs_handles_mixed_position_types` passed under the same run. 
- No test failures were introduced by this change.

author: shawn-sandy
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `/prompt-book` command and bundled prompt catalogue to help users discover and use `acss-kit` and `acss-utilities` features without memorizing command syntax. The prompt book is a curated collection of 13 natural-language prompts mapped to every shipped slash command, organized by use case.

## Key Changes

- **New `/prompt-book` command** (`plugins/acss-kit/commands/prompt-book.md`)
  - Prints the full prompt catalogue with no arguments
  - Prints a single section by number (e.g., `/prompt-book 5`)
  - Falls back to table of contents if section number is invalid
  - Read-only; never modifies files

- **Bundled prompt book** (`plugins/acss-kit/docs/prompt-book.md`)
  - 13 sections covering: project setup, component generation, theming, utilities, and tuning
  - Each entry includes: when to use, copy-paste prompt template, and expected outcome
  - Covers all commands across both `acss-kit` and `acss-utilities` plugins
  - Includes prerequisites, composing prompts, and tips sections

- **Documentation updates**
  - Added `/prompt-book` to the acss-kit README help commands section
  - Updated CLAUDE.md command matrix to include `/prompt-book`
  - Added cross-reference in acss-utilities README pointing to the prompt book
  - Bumped acss-kit version to 0.8.0 and added changelog entry

## Implementation Details

- The prompt book is designed as a read-only reference that ships with the plugin install, ensuring all users have access to the same canonical prompts
- Prompts use bracketed placeholders `[like this]` to mark values users should customize
- The command implementation reads the markdown file verbatim without summarization, preserving exact copy-paste readability
- Supports both full catalogue browsing and targeted section lookup for quick reference

author: ccbuildalot23
body:
## Summary
- New agent `studio-operations/chris-email-triage.md` defining a Gmail-triggered triage workflow for Chris's priority senders
- Workflow: read thread → log to Airtable `Central Hub > Follow-ups` → draft reply in Chris's voice (warm, peer-level, no em dashes, 3-5 sentences) → post one-line briefing to Slack `#chris-briefing`
- Hard constraints baked in: never send, never commit on Chris's behalf, only acts on the listed sender allowlist (LaToya/Mansa, Foley Hoag, clinical contacts, personal network)

## Important: external trigger required
Claude Code agent definitions don't fire on their own when external events (like a new Gmail message) happen. To make the "Gmail webhook → run this agent" trigger work end-to-end, an external service has to invoke Claude Code with the email payload. Options:
- Zapier / Pipedream / n8n → Gmail trigger → HTTP call to a Claude Code runner
- Google Apps Script on Chris's mailbox → push to a webhook endpoint
- A small Cloud Function watching Gmail push notifications

The agent definition is the "what to do" half; this PR doesn't include the "how it gets invoked" half.

## Open questions for Chris
- Confirm the exact Airtable base name (`Central Hub`) and table name (`Follow-ups`) — agent assumes these but will fall back to fuzzy match
- Confirm Slack channel `#chris-briefing` exists (no Slack MCP is wired in this repo yet, so the Slack post step is described in the prompt but not connected to a tool)
- Confirm sender email addresses for Fredous, Ehesane, Patrice, Javier, Shannan — the agent currently matches on display name + known domains

## Test plan
- [ ] Confirm Airtable base/table names and field schema (Sender, Subject, Received, Thread Link, Summary, Urgency, Reply Needed)
- [ ] Wire up an external trigger (Zapier/Pipedream/Apps Script) to invoke the agent on new mail from listed senders
- [ ] Add Slack MCP to the agent's tools list once available, or swap step 4 for a different briefing channel
- [ ] Run end-to-end with a test email from each sender category (Mansa, legal, clinical, personal) and verify: Airtable record created, draft saved (not sent), Slack briefing one line
- [ ] Verify "no em dashes" rule holds across 10+ generated drafts
- [ ] Verify agent does nothing when an email arrives from a sender not on the allowlist

author: bemsick
body:
## Summary

The user opened the live app on iPhone and the first screen (`/dashboard`) was on the old light/corporate theme — anti-pattern KPI stack (5 separate floating cards), no bottom tab bar, no Fraunces typography, "Quick Links" button stack the design spec explicitly killed. The HOS polish from PRs #59/#61 only reskinned `/h/*` and `/intel/*` surfaces; operator-side pages were missed. This fixes that.

### Changes

**A. `/dashboard` now redirects to `/h/dashboard`**
- The HOS dashboard already has every KPI on the legacy operator dashboard, plus floor preview, reservations, and alerts.
- One-line route change in `client/src/App.tsx`.

**B. Back-office shells rewritten on top of HospitalityShell**
- `components/AppShell.tsx` — used by SettingsSuppliers, SettingsLocations, SettingsTeam, SettingsBilling, BillingPage, MenuEngineeringPage. Now wraps in HospitalityShell so all 6 inherit the dark coral surface, Fraunces typography, bottom tab bar, and safe-area insets in one stroke. The hamburger menu icon (explicit anti-pattern per design-spec.md §7 — *"Sidebar navigation (hamburger) — Hides primary destinations — Bottom tab bar on mobile, left rail on tablet/desktop, always visible"*) is gone. Primary nav lives in the bottom tab bar; cmd-K covers the long tail.
- `modules/ModuleShell.tsx` — used by 12 pages (Order Guides, Reorder Needed, Recipes, Drift, Benchmarks, Item History, Admin Flags, Admin Billing, Automation Settings, Locations, Market Post, Revenue Optimizer, UpgradeGate). Same treatment — wrapped in HospitalityShell, all 12 inherit the new shell.

**C. Direct-AppNav pages reskinned**
- `ItemsPage` (`/items`)
- `POListPage` (`/orders`)
- `SourcingListPage` (`/sourcing`)
- `InventoryCountPage` (`/inventory/count`)

Each one now wraps in `<HospitalityShell title="…">` and drops `<AppNav>`.

**D. SettingsSuppliersPage header**
Reskinned to use Fraunces + dark token colors.

### Anti-patterns removed
- Hamburger menu icon (AppShell) — gone
- "Quick Links" button stack — never reached the new shell, AppShell rewrite drops it implicitly
- Light corporate horizontal nav tabs — gone (replaced by HOS bottom tab bar + topbar)
- AppNav (legacy bottom strip) — removed from 4 direct callers
- Inline white card styles + `var(--color-border)` light borders on operator headers — replaced with dark token colors

### Tests
- `client/src/components/UpgradeGate.test.tsx` updated: renders now wrap in `<MemoryRouter>` since HospitalityShell calls `useNavigate`.

### Verification
- `pnpm test` → 132/132 green
- `pnpm build` → green
- Typecheck clean

Screenshotting was not run because the dev environment cannot authenticate the live Clerk session (the May 2 QA report confirmed this is the standing blocker for unattended QA). Code-level changes documented inline.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open the app on iPhone, navigate to `/dashboard` — should redirect to `/h/dashboard` (the polished HOS dashboard)
- [ ] Visit `/items`, `/orders`, `/sourcing`, `/inventory/count` on mobile — confirm bottom tab bar appears, dark theme applied, Fraunces in headings
- [ ] Visit `/settings/suppliers` (and other settings sub-pages) — confirm dark theme, settings sub-nav strip styled with HOS pills
- [ ] Visit `/order-guides`, `/menu-engineering`, `/inventory/reorder-needed` — confirm same shell
- [ ] Confirm hamburger icon is gone from operator pages
- [ ] Confirm cmd-K still works for navigation across all surfaces

### **User description** ## Summary Beat 4c shipped with \`ecs:ListTaskDefinitions\` ungranted → 403 in dev on first delete. This script catches that bug class at PR-time: \`\`\` $ pnpm iam:coverage IAM coverage check - handler files scanned: 5 - distinct AWS actions used: 20 - granted actions in policy: 28 ✅ IAM coverage OK \`\`\` ## How it works 1. Walks \`src/extensions/fleet/api/*.ts\` 2. Parses AWS-SDK imports for \`*Command\` constructor names 3. Maps each → IAM action via SDK package prefix (\`@aws-sdk/client-ecs\` → \`ecs:\`) 4. Asserts every action is in \`GRANTED_ACTIONS\` (hardcoded mirror of ender-stack \`task_ecs_write\`) ## Verified Stripped \`ecs:ListTaskDefinitions\` from the granted list and re-ran: \`\`\` ❌ IAM coverage gaps (1): src/extensions/fleet/api/agents-delete.ts: ListTaskDefinitionsCommand → action "ecs:ListTaskDefinitions" not in GRANTED_ACTIONS \`\`\` Catches the exact bug we hit. author: monkopedia

## Summary
- `RpcObjectFactory.create()` was allocating a new `RpcObject` on every `toStub()` / `serialized()` call for generic service subtypes
- Added a global atomic copy-on-write cache (`cachedCreate()` extension) in `RpcObjectFactory.kt` keyed by `(factory, typeArgs)`, so repeated calls with the same type arguments return the same instance
- Updated all four platform `rpcObject()` implementations (JVM, Native, JS, WASM) to use `cachedCreate()` instead of `create()`

author: roryford
body:
## Summary

Closes #982.

PR #974 (server collapse) made `BaseChatServer` (executable) depend directly on `BaseChatBackends`. The auto-generated `BaseChatKit-Package` Xcode scheme builds every executable, and both `bck-tools` and `BaseChatServer` now had unconditional `BaseChatBackends` deps — producing two `Copy llama.framework` tasks pointing at the same path:

```
Multiple commands produce '.../Build/Products/Debug/Frameworks/llama.framework'
```

This broke `xcodebuild test -scheme BaseChatKit-Package -only-testing BaseChatMLXIntegrationTests` at the build phase.

## Fix

Mirror the established `Fuzz`-trait pattern documented at `Package.swift:43–47`: gate `BaseChatBackends` and `BaseChatInference` behind the `Server` trait on the `BaseChatServer` executable target so they only join the build graph when the trait is explicitly enabled. The `#else` no-op stub in `BaseChatServerCommand.swift` (added in #946) keeps the executable linkable when `Server` is off, so this is purely a build-graph adjustment — **no runtime behavior change**.

`bck-tools` remains the sole executable in the auto-scheme with an unconditional `BaseChatBackends` dep, so there is no longer a collision.

## Validation

- [x] `swift build --disable-default-traits` — passes
- [x] `swift build --traits Server` — passes
- [x] `swift test --filter BaseChatServerTests --traits Server --skip-update` — 48 tests, 0 failures
- [x] `rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/BaseChatKit-* && xcodebuild test -scheme BaseChatKit-Package -only-testing BaseChatMLXIntegrationTests -destination 'platform=macOS'` — `** TEST SUCCEEDED **` (13 executed; 12 skipped because no fixture model matched on this checkout, 1 skipped pending #802 — none related to the build conflict)

## Behavior note

When the `Server` trait is **on**, all deps are present and the server runs as before. When **off**, the executable compiles to the no-op stub from #946 that prints `BaseChatServer was built without the 'Server' trait.` This matches the pre-#974 default-traits behavior.

author: emremy
body:
## Overview

This release introduces **unique indexes**, **stable key-based helpers**, **JS array migration utilities**, and a comprehensive **JS Array vs ColQL benchmark suite**.

The goal of v0.3.0 is to make ColQL more practical for real-world backend usage while strengthening correctness guarantees and improving performance transparency.

---

## Highlights

### 🔐 Unique Indexes (Data Integrity + Fast Lookup)

ColQL now supports **unique indexes**:

```ts
users.createUniqueIndex("id");
users.createUniqueIndex("email");
```

Guarantees:

- Duplicate inserts are rejected
- `insertMany` is all-or-nothing on duplicates
- Updates cannot violate uniqueness
- Deleted keys can be reused
- Unique indexes never return stale row positions

Supported:

- numeric columns
- dictionary columns

Not supported:

- boolean columns

---

### 🔑 By-Key Helpers

Stable-key operations are now first-class:

```ts
users.findBy("id", 123);
users.updateBy("email", "a@b.com", { active: false });
users.deleteBy("id", 123);
```

- Require a unique index
- Do not rely on unstable `rowIndex`
- Provide predictable single-row semantics

---

### 🔄 JS Array Migration Helpers

Easier transition from JS arrays:

```ts
const users = fromRows(schema, rows);

users.firstWhere({ id: 1 });
users.countWhere({ active: true });
users.exists({ country: "TR" });
```

- Thin wrappers over the query engine
- Fully typed
- Preserve lazy execution behavior

---

### 📊 JS Array vs ColQL Benchmark Suite

New benchmark comparing:

- JS object arrays
- ColQL scan
- equality index
- sorted index
- unique index

Across:

- 1k / 100k / 1M rows
- memory usage
- filtering
- projection + limit
- lookup
- range queries
- mutations

Key observations:

- ~6–7x lower memory usage vs JS arrays at 1M rows
- sub-millisecond indexed lookups
- projection + limit significantly faster
- JS arrays remain faster for simple full scans
- `filter(fn)` is a full-scan escape hatch and can be expensive

> Benchmarks are local reference results, not universal guarantees.

---

### ⚡ Performance Improvements

- Optimized structured scan hot path
- Reduced 1M-row scan latency from ~40ms → ~20ms
- Bulk compaction for `deleteMany`
- Avoid unnecessary unique index rebuilds
- Clearer benchmark measurement (setup excluded from timing)

---

### 🧪 Expanded Test Coverage

- Real-world scenario tests:
  - user directory (id/email uniqueness)
  - product catalog (SKU uniqueness + range queries)
  - session/token registry
  - feature flags
- Mixed operation sequences (insert → update → delete → rebuild → serialize)
- Edge cases for unique indexes
- Parity checks against JS array oracle

---

## Design Notes

- Equality and sorted indexes remain performance-only
- Unique indexes add data integrity guarantees
- Row indexes are not stable identifiers
- Unique indexes are not serialized and must be recreated after restore
- Broad mutations may be slower than raw JS arrays due to safety guarantees

---

## When to Use ColQL

ColQL is most useful when:

- Data is already in-process
- Memory efficiency matters
- Indexed lookups or range queries are needed
- You want structured queries without a database roundtrip

JS arrays may still be preferable for:

- Small datasets
- Simple scans
- Minimal logic

---

## Breaking Changes

None.

---

## Notes

This release focuses on correctness, clarity, and real-world usability rather than adding heavy features or external integrations.

### Motivation
- Prevent duplicate delegate bindings and redundant handler invocations caused by multiple `AddDynamic` calls. 
- Ensure controllers immediately reconcile HUD and turn ownership state for late join/reconnect/refresh paths by providing a local fallback for turn-start handling.

body:
## Summary

Add a workflow that auto-applies labels to PRs based on changed
file paths. Rules live in `.github/labeler.yml`.

## Labels mapped

- `documentation`: `docs/**`, `**/*.md`
- `github actions`: `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/actions/**`

Other labels in the repo (`bug`, `enhancement`, `refactor`, etc.)
remain manual — they describe intent that can't be inferred from
file paths.

## Why `pull_request_target`

`pull_request_target` runs in the base repo's context with write
access, so the action can label PRs from forks (which
`pull_request` can't, due to read-only tokens from forks). Safe
here because `actions/labeler@v5` does not check out PR code — it
only reads file paths from PR metadata via the API.

`sync-labels: true` prunes labels that no longer apply when a
PR's file set changes between pushes.

## Runner

`runs-on: ubuntu-latest` — GitHub-hosted, no external
dependencies, appropriate for a 1-step labeler that does no
compilation.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML lints clean via pre-commit `check-yaml`
- [x] Commit-msg hook passes on both commits
- [ ] First post-merge PR is the live test (`pull_request_target`
      reads workflows from the base branch, so it won't fire on
      this PR)

author: afreidah
body:
## Summary

Item B from #676. The six background workers and the drain manager become independent DI services. \`NewBackendManager\` no longer constructs them; production code resolves each worker through DI, and the worker fields on \`BackendManager\` are kept as DI-populated convenience handles for dashboard rendering, config-reload paths, and tests.

### Architecture

| Concern | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Worker construction | inside \`NewBackendManager\` | per-worker DI providers (\`ProvideRebalancer\`, \`ProvideReplicator\`, ...) |
| Worker.Ops dep | \`*backendCore\` (auto-satisfied via promotion) | \`*proxy.BackendManager\` |
| drain.Manager | sub-manager built by \`NewBackendManager\` | top-level DI service \`ProvideDrainManager\`, wired into BackendManager via \`WireDrain\` |
| Worker compound-store adapters (\`rebalancerStore\`, \`replicatorStore\`, \`overReplicationStore\`) | inline in \`internal/proxy/stores.go\` | inline in DI providers |
| Lifecycle service factories | \`NewXService(manager, locker)\` reading worker off manager | \`NewXService(manager, worker, locker)\` taking the worker explicitly |
| \`SetIntegrityConfig\` side-effect | forwards to embedded \`m.Scrubber\` | stores config only; \`serve.applyWorkerConfigs\` pushes to scrubber via DI |
| \`ui.New(manager, ...)\` wrapper | wrapped \`fromManager()\` and \`NewWithDeps()\` | single \`ui.New(*Deps)\` constructor |

### Construction order

\`provideConcreteStore → BackendManager → MultipartManager / ObjectManager / dashboard.Aggregator → workers (each independent) → drain.Manager (needs CleanupWorker + MultipartManager) → lifecycle.Manager\`. drain.Manager calls \`mgr.WireDrain(dm)\` which sets both the public \`mgr.DrainManager\` field and the unexported \`backendCore.drainMgr\` (so eligibility filters see drain state).

### Tests

\`proxytest\` gains an \`AttachWorkers(mgr, mock)\` helper that mirrors the per-worker DI providers inline, so cross-package tests holding a \`*BackendManager\` populate worker fields without standing up an injector. The proxy package's own tests use a private \`wireWorkersForTest\` (same idea, can't import the proxytest subpackage from within proxy without a cycle). Service-factory tests in \`internal/di\` use a new \`servicesFixture\` struct that bundles the manager + each worker.

body:
Replaces the mock-data `ProductListVM` implementation with real DB-backed product listing/detail pages, adds SEO-friendly slug URLs for products/categories/suppliers, and wires up search + pagination (pageSize=12) + sidebar filtering.

## Domain & Data Layer

- Added `Slug NVARCHAR(300)` to `Product`, `Category`, `Supplier` models and all INSERT/UPDATE SQL
- Created `ICategoryRepository` / `ISupplierRepository` extending `IGenericRepository<T>` with `GetBySlugAsync` / `SlugExistsAsync`; `IProductRepository` gets the same methods
- New `SlugHelper` in `BusinessLayers`:
  - `GenerateSlug(name)` — full Vietnamese diacritic → ASCII normalization
  - `MakeUniqueAsync(baseSlug, existsAsync)` — appends `-1`, `-2`, … until unique

## Business Layer

New methods exposed on `CatalogDataService` and `PartnerDataService`:

```csharp
CatalogDataService.GetProductBySlugAsync(slug)
CatalogDataService.GetCategoryBySlugAsync(slug)
CatalogDataService.ListAllCategoriesAsync()          // no-pagination, for sidebar
CatalogDataService.GetUniqueProductSlugAsync(name, excludeId)

PartnerDataService.GetSupplierBySlugAsync(slug)
PartnerDataService.ListAllSuppliersAsync()
PartnerDataService.GetUniqueSupplierSlugAsync(name, excludeId)
```

## Website Routes

Registered before the default route to prevent `/loai-hang` / `/hang` literals being swallowed by the `{slug}` catch-all:

| URL pattern | Action |
|---|---|
| `/san-pham` | `Product/Index` |
| `/san-pham/loai-hang/{categorySlug}` | `Product/Index` (category filter) |
| `/san-pham/hang/{supplierSlug}` | `Product/Index` (supplier filter) |
| `/san-pham/{slug}` | `Product/Detail` |

Query strings `?q=` (search) and `?page=` compose with all route patterns.

## Views

- `Product/Index.cshtml` — model is now `PagedResult<Product>` (no `ProductListVM`); sidebar renders real DB categories + suppliers with active-state highlights; fully functional `GetDisplayPages()` pagination
- `Product/Detail.cshtml` (new) — thumbnail gallery switcher, attributes table, breadcrumb, category/supplier badge links

## Admin

- `Product/Category/Supplier` `SaveData` actions auto-generate slug from name when the field is blank (preserves existing slug on update)
- Edit forms expose an optional Slug input with hint text

## SQL

- `SGENERGY_DB.sql` — `Slug` column + unique filtered index (`WHERE Slug IS NOT NULL`) on all three tables; seed data includes slugs
- `sql/Migration_AddSlug.sql` (new) — idempotent `ALTER TABLE` migration for existing databases

## Summary

Stopped the infinite auto-merge review/reroute loop by preserving merge-conflict retry state across approvals, blocking SSH-agent fetch failures during auto-merge, and preventing review_poll from rerouting tasks that already exhausted max attempts.

### What was done

- Preserved `merge_conflict_retries` in transient counter resets so the merge-conflict circuit breaker now survives repeated `Approve` cycles.
- Updated auto-merge conflict recovery to detect SSH-agent `git fetch` failures (`sign_and_send_pubkey`, `agent refused operation`, `communication with agent failed`) and block the task with a PR comment instead of silently leaving it in review.
- Added a review-poll guard that blocks approved conflict tasks when rerouting would exceed `workflow.max_attempts`, avoiding pointless `Routed` transitions that `task_init` will reject.
- Expanded store and review-poll tests to cover the preserved merge-conflict counter semantics and the new max-attempts block behavior.
- Ran `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo nextest run` successfully.
- Committed the changes as `813f2009 fix(auto-merge): stop infinite review reroute loop`.

author: lnds
body:
## Summary

The "Pipe across lines" example in `docs/kaikai-minimal.md` claimed
this shape compiles:

```kai
xs
  |> filter(. > 0)
  |> map(. * 2)
  |> sum
```

It did not. `parse_pipe_rest` (`stage2/compiler.kai`) called
`p_skip_newlines` only AFTER consuming `|>` / `|`, never before, so
the trailing newline after `xs` terminated the expression and the
leading `|>` started a fresh, failing statement. This PR closes the
doc-vs-impl discrepancy.

The fix is a single peek-and-skip at the head of `parse_pipe_rest`:
peek past leading newlines, only commit to the new parser state if
the next token is `TkPipeApply` or `TkPipe`. If neither matches,
return the **original** parser so the enclosing statement boundary
still sees those newlines (so `xs |> f \n let y = ...` still
terminates the pipe at `let`).

The relaxation is scoped to pipe tokens. The `|` separator in
`type T = A | B` is consumed by `parse_sum_body` outside the
expression grammar. Match arms in current kaikai are
newline-separated and do not use `|`. Both remain unaffected — the
sum-type variant-per-line shape (`examples/minimal/interp.kai`) and
the multi-arm match shape (every existing fixture) stay green.

## Acceptance criteria from #130

- [x] `parse_pipe_rest` skips leading newlines before checking for
  `TkPipeApply` / `TkPipe`. (`stage2/compiler.kai:1849`)
- [x] Regression fixtures wired into `make test`:
  - `examples/pipes/leading_pipe_apply.kai` — `|>` chain, each pipe leading.
  - `examples/pipes/leading_pipe_map.kai` — `|` chain, each pipe leading.
  - `examples/pipes/leading_pipe_mixed.kai` — alternating `|>` and `|`.
  - `examples/pipes/trailing_pipe_still_works.kai` — pre-existing trailing form.
  Wired through new `test-pipes` target → `test` and `test-fast`.
- [x] Negative regression — `match` arms across lines: `make test-match`
  and `make test-protocols` continue to pass; existing match-based
  demos (`examples/minimal/interp.kai`, every match arm in
  `stage2/compiler.kai` itself) compile unchanged.
- [x] Negative regression — `type T = A | B | C` per-line: same
  `examples/minimal/interp.kai` exercises this shape, `make tier0`
  green.
- [x] `docs/kaikai-minimal.md` "Pipe across lines" example continues
  to compile — covered by the three new fixtures (which mirror that
  example's shape).
- [x] Selfhost on both backends green — `make tier0` reports
  `selfhost byte-identical`. The relaxation is purely additive: every
  input that parsed before still parses to the same AST.
- [x] CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased] / Fixed` (doc-vs-impl
  discrepancy fix, not a feature).

## Lane discipline

- VERSION untouched.
- `[Unreleased]` header preserved (no promotion).
- `tier0` / `tier1`-equivalent suites pass locally:
  - `make tier0` — selfhost byte-identical, demos baseline holds.
  - `make test-pipes` `test-sugars` `test-match` `test-stdlib` `test-modules` `test-loop` `test-protocols` `test-demos-core` `test-aspirational` — all green.
  - `examples/effects/issue_107_signal_trap.kai` (the SIGINT
    fixture) is the one local failure; it's a sandbox /
    process-signaling artifact unrelated to parser changes — it
    works when invoked directly with absolute paths and CI is the
    source of truth for it.
- Tier 1-ASAN not required for this lane (parser only — no runtime
  / emit changes).

## Lane parallelism

The `multi-arg-match-sugar` lane (#129, PR #133) merged before this
one. Rebased against `origin/main`; the multi-arg match arms still
parse and `make test-match` is green. The `|` between match arms in
that sugar is parsed by `parse_match_arms`, never reaching
`parse_pipe_rest` — leading-pipe relaxation does not touch it.

## Test plan

- [x] `make tier0` (selfhost byte-identical, demos baseline 26/26)
- [x] `make test-pipes` (4/4 fixtures pass, including the new
      trailing-pipe regression check)
- [x] `make test-sugars` (existing pipe coverage unchanged)
- [x] `make test-match` (multi-arg match sugar still green after
      the relaxation)
- [ ] CI tier1 (final source of truth — gate set to auto-merge)

Closes #130.

author: rasbandit
body:
## Summary

Hotfix to clear flaky test that failed on PR #66's main-deploy CI even though it passed on the PR run. Same code, different luck.

`list_vaults/1` orders by `created_at ASC`. Postgres timestamps round to second precision, so two vaults created in the same second tie and Postgres returns no guaranteed order. The test `\"returns vaults ordered by inserted_at ascending\"` inserts two vaults back-to-back and asserts insert order — flaky whenever both inserts land in the same second.

Fix: add `id ASC` as tiebreaker. ID is a monotonically increasing serial PK so insertion order is deterministically preserved.

## Why this needs a separate PR

PR #66 (Phase B.1) merged but its main CI hit this flake. `deploy-fastraid` was skipped because unit-tests failed. Phase B.1 is sitting on main but NOT in production. This PR's deploy run will carry both PR #66 + this fix to FastRaid.

Bumps backend 0.5.23 → 0.5.24.

## Summary

Closes the loop on the metrics chain shipped across PRs #262, #298, #299, #300, #301, #302, #304, #305: an HTTP endpoint that actually exposes the recorded counters/gauges/histograms in Prometheus exposition format.

- \`engine/api/routes/metrics.py\` — \`GET /metrics\` returns the active \`MetricsBackend\`'s exposition text. Recording-style backends render via \`render_prometheus()\`; \`NullBackend\` returns a 200 placeholder so scrapes never report failed even when no exporter is wired.
- \`engine/api/router.py\` — include the new router with the \`observability\` tag (no path prefix; \`/metrics\` is conventional).
- \`engine/app.py\` — switch the process metrics singleton to \`PrometheusBackend\` at lifespan startup so production scrapes return real counters/gauges/histograms by default. Operators who want a different backend (OTel, StatsD) call \`set_metrics()\` after \`create_app()\` returns.

The endpoint is intentionally unauthenticated; operators restrict access via reverse-proxy / network ACLs (the standard Prometheus pattern). Content-Type is \`text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8\`.

Refs #34. Multi-process collector, bucketed histogram exporter, and metric-catalog HELP descriptions still deferred.

author: alexcheema
body:
## Why

Workers currently reconstruct active image inputs by reacting to `InputChunkReceived` events directly. That breaks the event-sourcing boundary once we add snapshot restore, because a snapshot gives a component state, not the historical events used to build transient buffers.

This PR makes active request input chunks part of durable `State`, so workers can derive their local image views from state instead of treating events as the source of truth.

## How

- Add `State.input_chunks`, keyed by command id and chunk index.
- Reduce `InputChunkReceived` into state in `apply()`.
- Drop input chunks when the corresponding generation task is deleted.
- Rebuild worker input buffers and image hash cache from `State.input_chunks`.
- Stop API-wide image-hash deduplication so each request sends the chunks its state entry needs.

## Tests

author: gambtho
body:
## Summary

PR3 of the UI redesign — brings the legacy pages onto the design system. After this PR every page in the app uses the same primitives (Card, DataTable, Pill, PageHeader, Topbar, Button, Modal, Input/Select).

## New primitives

- **`DataTable`** — shared table chrome (head, head-cell with align, alert/muted rows, message rows for loading/error/empty). Replaces ad-hoc `<table>` markup that grew up across Jobs, JobDetail, and every legacy page.
- **`Modal`** — overlay primitive with Escape + backdrop-click dismissal, initial focus, `role=\"dialog\"` / `aria-modal`. Used by all confirmation and form modals.
- **`Input` + `Select`** — bordered control + accessible `<label>` wrapper. Generates a stable id so screen readers announce the field even when callers don't supply one.

## Reskinned modals (used across pages)

- **`ConfirmDialog`** — built on `Modal`, accepts optional title and custom confirm-button label (Disconnect / Remove / Delete).
- **`SecretModal`** — built on `Modal` + `Input`, autoFocus moves to the appropriate field per mode, backdrop-click is disabled so a half-typed secret can't be lost by misclick.
- **`ScheduleOverrideForm`** — \"Reset to YAML\" pushed to the left so the primary save action sits in the rightmost slot users expect.

## Reskinned pages

| Route | What's new |
|-------|------------|
| `/runs` | Status filter chips (All/Failed/Running/Succeeded), free-text filter on job/repo/error, error/loading/empty states. **Now reads `?schedule_id=…` from the URL** and feeds it to `runs.list`, so the deep link from JobDetail's \"All runs →\" finally works. |
| `/settings/repos` | Connected repos table with sync status, repo opens in github.com, disconnect via ConfirmDialog. Failing-sync rows pinned with red bar. |
| `/settings/secrets` | List/create/rotate/delete with the new SecretModal + ConfirmDialog. |
| `/settings/providers` | GitHub Copilot Enterprise OAuth device flow — same logic, new chrome. Code displayed in a high-contrast block, YAML output as a syntax-coloured `<pre>`. |
| `/settings/users` | Invite form (Input + Select + Button) on top, user table below. Self-protections preserved; errors surfaced in a banner so role changes no longer silently revert. |
| `/settings/audit` | Chronological audit log with action-prefix group filter (secret/repo/schedule/user) and free-text filter. |
| `/login` | Pre-auth landing reskinned. Brand mark with the green-glow dot, GitHub mark + sign-in, version stamp. |

## JobDetail change

\"All runs →\" now passes `?schedule_id=…` (closes the misleading-link TODO from PR2's review). The Runs page consumes it and shows a clear \"clear filter ✕\" affordance.

## Test plan
- [x] \`npm test\` — 12 files, **86 tests** pass (was 77)
- [x] \`npm run build\` — clean typecheck + production build

## Summary

Follow-up to [#39](https://github.com/goldenwo/universal-memory/pull/39) (which closed [#22](https://github.com/goldenwo/universal-memory/issues/22) by adding T17 stale-symlink coverage and the bridge exec-bit fix at `a9877d0`).

PR #39 fixed `plugins/claude-code/universal-memory/bin/um-bridge-claude-mem` from git mode 100644 → 100755 because T15 in `installer/install-plugin-cc.test.sh` asserts `[ -x ]` on the installed bridge. That same root cause — git-tracked mode 644 on files that need exec on Linux/macOS — applies to the parallel CLIs in the same `bin/` dir. This PR fixes the rest.

## What changed

12 files flipped from `100644` → `100755` via `git update-index --chmod=+x`. **Mode-only change** — every blob hash is identical before/after (verified via `git ls-files --stage` snapshots). Commit shows `12 files changed, 0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.

| File | Why it needs exec bit |
|------|----------------------|
| `bin/um` | Top-level dispatcher; users add it to PATH and invoke directly |
| `bin/um-capture` | fs-direct CLI; also wrapped by `um-capture.sh` which gates on `[ -x ]` ([um-capture.sh:12](plugins/claude-code/universal-memory/bin/um-capture.sh:12)) |
| `bin/um-capture.sh` | `um capture` subcommand `exec`'d by dispatcher ([um:115](plugins/claude-code/universal-memory/bin/um:115)) |
| `bin/um-forget` | `um forget` subcommand `exec`'d by dispatcher ([um:124](plugins/claude-code/universal-memory/bin/um:124)) |
| `bin/um-list.sh` | `um list` subcommand `exec`'d by dispatcher |
| `bin/um-preview` | Top-level CLI |
| `bin/um-recent.sh` | `um recent` subcommand `exec`'d by dispatcher |
| `bin/um-search.sh` | `um search` subcommand `exec`'d by dispatcher |
| `bin/um-state.sh` | `um state` subcommand `exec`'d by dispatcher |
| `bin/um-supersede` | `um supersede` subcommand `exec`'d by dispatcher |
| `bin/um-tail.sh` | `um tail` subcommand `exec`'d by dispatcher |
| `bin/um-tunnel` | Top-level CLI |

## Why it was silent

Two things masked this on existing setups:

1. **Windows checkouts** ignore Unix exec bits — every file appears executable regardless of git's stored mode. The repo's primary dev environment is Windows + git-bash.
2. **`installer/install-cli.sh`** (the standalone CLI installer that produces `~/.local/bin/um`) does its own `chmod +x` on every script it copies ([install-cli.sh:109](installer/install-cli.sh:109), [install-cli.sh:136](installer/install-cli.sh:136)). That self-correcting install path hid the underlying git-mode bug for users.

The path that was actually broken: `installer/install-plugin-cc.sh` does `cp -r "$src" "$target"` which preserves source mode bits. So fresh `~/.claude/plugins/universal-memory/bin/*` on Linux/macOS would be mode 644, breaking direct invocation and breaking the umbrella dispatcher's `[ -x "$SUBCMD_SH" ]` gates.

## Out of scope (intentionally untouched)

| Path | Why stays 100644 |
|------|-----------------|
| `bin/translate.mjs` | ESM module, no shebang, imported (not exec'd) by `um-bridge-claude-mem` |
| `bin/lib/*` | Sourced by other scripts |
| `bin/*.test.sh`, `bin/*.test.mjs` | Run via `bash <path>` / `node <path>` in test runners |
| `hooks/*.sh` | Invoked via `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/*.sh"` per [hooks.json](plugins/claude-code/universal-memory/hooks/hooks.json) |
| `hooks/lib/*` | Sourced |

Codex plugin (`plugins/codex/universal-memory/`) currently has no `bin/` or `hooks/` dirs — only `NOTES.md`, `README.md`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, and `.mcp.json`. Nothing parallel to fix there.

Per the discovery context, this PR also intentionally does **not** add a CI gate or shellcheck rule for exec bits — that's a separate concern.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash plugins/claude-code/universal-memory/bin/um.test.sh` — 16/16 pass locally (Windows). Test self-chmods its temp copies, so it doesn't gate on source mode, but confirms no regressions.
- [x] Verified blob hashes unchanged: `git diff --cached --raw` shows `:100644 100755 <hash> <hash> M <path>` for every file (same hash both sides).
- [x] Verified commit is mode-only: `12 files changed, 0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.
- [ ] CI on this PR will execute `installer/install-plugin-cc.test.sh` (wired into `smoke.yml` in #39) on Linux + macOS — the test asserts `[ -x ]` on the installed bridge. Subcommand CLIs aren't directly asserted by T15, but a fresh-clone install on Linux/macOS would now produce a working `~/.claude/plugins/universal-memory/bin/um <subcmd>` chain end-to-end.

## Discovery context

Surfaced when wiring `install-plugin-cc.test.sh` into `smoke.yml` exposed the latent T15 `[ -x um-bridge-claude-mem ]` failure. The bridge fix in #39 closed the immediate CI gate; this PR closes the parallel coverage gap on the rest of the bin/ CLIs that have the same root cause.

author: seanwevans
body:
### Motivation
- Findings produced by `check_tokens` were being attributed to nested scalar YAML nodes instead of their parent step, causing line numbers to drift away from the intended step line.
- Tests like `test_check_tokens` assert that a finding's `line_number` matches the parent step, so the walker must propagate parent positions to string leaves.

### Description
- Updated the recursive `walk` in `WorkflowScanner.check_tokens` to propagate the current parent `line`/`column` down to leaf strings instead of always calling `get_position` on every node. 
- Only call `get_position` for container nodes (`dict`/`list`) and use `next_line`/`next_column` for subsequent recursion so scalars inherit their parent location. 
- Applied the same position-propagation pattern to the similar walker used in `check_reusable_inputs` to keep input reference locations aligned with their parent job/step. 

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q ghast/tests/core/test_scanner.py::test_check_tokens` which passed.

author: pbertsch
body:
## Summary

Adds a ⚙ toolbar button that opens a form for the four probe.yaml fields users actually touch. Saves write back to \`probe.yaml\` in the active workspace, preserving all other keys.

**v0.7.1 PR 2 of 3.**

## Fields exposed

| Form label | YAML path | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| Agent port | \`agent.port\` | Default 48686; users only change for parallel runs or port conflicts |
| Default step timeout | \`defaults.timeout\` | Slow CI environments / heavy animations need longer than 30s |
| Preferred iOS UDID | \`device.ios_device_id\` | Avoid \`--device\` on every run when you have multiple sims |
| Preferred Android serial | \`device.android_device_id\` | Same as above for emulators |

Deliberately tight — extending the field set is cheap once the plumbing exists, but landing a small form first beats arguing about which 20 fields to expose.

## Implementation notes

- **Preserve unknown keys on save.** \`SaveWorkspaceSettings\` reads the existing file as a raw \`map[string]any\` rather than as a \`Config\` struct, mutates only the four managed keys, and writes back. So a power user with \`recipes_folder\`, \`cloud\`, \`plugins\`, etc. keeps everything they had.
- **Empty fields are dropped, not zero-written.** Clearing a field in the UI removes the key from \`probe.yaml\` (and removes the parent map if it goes empty), maintaining the convention that \`probe.yaml\` only lists fields the user explicitly set.
- **Validation runs before disk touch.** \`agent.port\` is range-checked (0–65535); \`defaults.timeout\` is parsed as a Go duration. Invalid input → clear error, no half-written file.
- **No-workspace state.** If the user opens settings before picking a workspace, the form is hidden and a hint shows to use 📂 first.

## Test plan

- [x] \`go build ./...\` clean
- [x] \`go test ./...\` — full suite green
- [x] \`cd studio && go vet ./...\` clean
- [x] \`tsc --noEmit\` clean
- [ ] **Manual: empty workspace** — settings on a workspace with no \`probe.yaml\`, save → file created with only the fields filled in.
- [ ] **Manual: existing workspace** — settings on a workspace with rich \`probe.yaml\` (e.g. \`tests/recipes\`, custom \`reports_folder\`, etc.), save → those keys still present, only the four managed fields updated.
- [ ] **Manual: invalid input** — port \`70000\` or timeout \`5 weeks\` → save fails with toast, no file write.

author: sinity
body:
## Summary

Make Sinex xtask/devshell cache and history behavior portable and legible without embedding workstation-specific `/cache` policy in Sinex itself.

## Problem

During workstation pressure analysis, Sinex was hard to reason about at runtime:

- cache/target discovery mixed repo-local defaults with host-local `/cache` probing;
- bare/system-installed `xtask` could resolve state in surprising locations;
- preflight cache state was partly tied to source-layout assumptions instead of configured state;
- reset flows made it too easy to treat the xtask history ledger as disposable;
- target reset missed historical `.sinex/target` data after the target directory moved.

This is a slice of #910. It does not close the broader global observability work.

## Solution

- Remove Sinex's internal `/cache` detection. The portable default is `.sinex/cache`; host policy such as `/cache/sinex/<checkout>` is injected by Sinnix via `SINEX_DEV_CACHE_ROOT` / `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- Make `SINEX_CACHE_DIR` default to the cache root, and make `workspace_target_dir_for()` derive `target` from the configured cache root unless `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is explicit.
- Put preflight cache/hash/lock state under the configured `SINEX_STATE_DIR/preflight`.
- Preserve xtask history on bare `xtask reset --yes`; only `--history` resets it, and reset still preserves the old DB/sidecars as timestamped backups.
- Make target reset remove both the configured target directory and the historical `.sinex/target` directory when they differ.
- Export the target-dir resolver through the xtask library so integration helpers do not reach into a private module.

## Verification

- `nix fmt -- --check flake.nix`
- `direnv exec . rustfmt --check --config skip_children=true xtask/src/history/db.rs xtask/src/lib.rs xtask/src/config.rs xtask/src/preflight.rs xtask/src/commands/reset.rs xtask/tests/support.rs xtask/tests/scenarios.rs xtask/tests/pty_snapshot_tests.rs`
- Focused xtask tests passed under the configured `/cache/sinex/566e9bf8d5e8/target` dev target:
  - invocation `12246`
  - `9 tests run: 9 passed, 1279 skipped`
  - command covered cache-dir/env behavior, target reset behavior, and configured preflight state path.
- `direnv exec . env` confirms Sinnix injects `/cache` policy without Sinex hard-coding it:
  - `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/cache/sinex/566e9bf8d5e8/target`
  - `SINEX_DEV_CACHE_ROOT=/cache/sinex/566e9bf8d5e8`
  - `SINEX_CACHE_DIR=/cache/sinex/566e9bf8d5e8`
  - `SINEX_STATE_DIR=/realm/project/sinex/.sinex/state`

Refs #910.

author: dallanwagz
body:
## Summary
Closes #63 by attacking the failure from three angles, then bonus-fixes the install ergonomics by also shipping a merged sketch+FS image.

## Root cause
`server.serveStatic("/spa", SPIFFS, "/spa/")` is correctly registered (`marquee.ino:398`). When a request comes in for `/spa` or `/spa/`, the lib's `AsyncStaticWebHandler::canHandle()` calls `_getFile()`, which appends `index.html` and checks LittleFS. If the file (or its `.gz` sibling) doesn't exist on disk, `canHandle()` returns false, the request falls through to `server.onNotFound(redirectHome)`, and the user sees the home page.

The only way to get the SPA bundle onto LittleFS is a serial flash (`make uploadfs` / `pio run --target uploadfs`) or `esptool.py write_flash 0x300000 littlefs.bin`. **OTA — both `/update` and `/updateFromUrl` — only updates the firmware sketch.** README's "Pre-built Binaries" section pointed users at the OTA path and didn't mention LittleFS at all, and the release only attached `firmware.bin` as a top-level asset (`littlefs.bin` was inside the artifacts zip with no documentation).

So a user following the documented install path:
1. Downloaded `marquee-scroller-v3.09.2-wagfam.bin`
2. OTA-flashed via `/update`
3. Got a firmware that registers `/spa` but a LittleFS that has no SPA files
4. Visited `/spa`, hit `serveStatic` → `canHandle=false` → `onNotFound` → 302 to `/`

Same shape as issue #60 (silent redirect masking the real failure), different trigger.

## Fix

**1. firmware: `handleNotFound()` dispatcher** (`marquee.ino`)

Replaces `server.onNotFound(redirectHome)` with a small dispatcher that branches on URL prefix. `/spa*` requests get a 404 HTML page that explains the failure mode (OTA doesn't touch LittleFS) and names all three fix paths (`make uploadfs`, `esptool.py write_flash 0x300000 littlefs.bin`, or `esptool.py write_flash 0x0 merged.bin`). Everything else falls through to `redirectHome` — no behavior change for legacy routes.

**2. README "Pre-built Binaries" section**

Rewritten as a 3-row matrix mapping install scenario → which artifact to use:

| File | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| `<repo>-<v>-merged.bin` | First-time install (one esptool command) |
| `<repo>-<v>.bin` | OTA firmware update |
| `<repo>-<v>-littlefs.bin` | SPA refresh on already-current firmware |

OTA section now warns explicitly that OTA does not touch LittleFS.

**3. CI release workflow**

- New "Build merged image" step: `pip install esptool && esptool.py merge_bin` joins `firmware.bin` (at `0x0`) + `littlefs.bin` (at `0x300000`) into a single 4MB image.
- "Package release artifacts" step copies both `littlefs.bin` and `merged.bin` to top-level assets alongside `firmware.bin`.
- "Upload release artifacts bin" step uploads all three. Each is gated on file existence so the workflow stays no-op-safe if a build doesn't produce the SPA.

**4. `make merged` target**

Produces `artifacts/merged.bin` locally via the same `esptool merge_bin` command, run inside `python:3-alpine` so no host-pip-pollution. Tested locally: 4.17 MB output, ready to flash at offset 0x0.

**5. `CLAUDE.md` note**

Documents the OTA-doesn't-touch-LittleFS gotcha so future LLM agents add the runtime fallback when introducing other LittleFS-dependent features.

**6. `tests/scripts/test_spa_not_found_fallback.py`**

Three pinning tests:
- `server.onNotFound` calls `handleNotFound`, not `redirectHome` directly
- `handleNotFound` checks `/spa` and returns 404 (not 302), still calls `redirectHome` for the default branch
- The 404 body mentions both `uploadfs` and LittleFS (so the user knows the fix, not just the failure)

## Why three artifacts instead of one

OTA can't take a combined image — `Update.h` writes to a specific OTA partition based on `U_FLASH` (sketch) or `U_FS` (filesystem) markers, not absolute flash offsets, and our `/update` endpoint only handles `U_FLASH`. Even if we wanted to ship a single artifact that worked for both fresh install AND OTA, the firmware would need a substantially expanded OTA path (multipart upload + offset-aware write + boot-confirmation across two partitions). That's a much bigger change for a marginal UX win.

The compromise: serial-flash users get a one-command experience via `merged.bin`; OTA users keep the simple `/update`-with-`firmware.bin` flow they already had.

## Verification
- `pio run -e default` builds clean
- `make merged` locally produces a 4.17 MB image without errors
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_spa_not_found_fallback.py` — 3/3 pass
- Static read of `WebHandlers.cpp:83-128` confirms serveStatic returns false (not a redirect) on missing files, so the dispatcher's 404 path is the one that actually runs

## Test plan
- [ ] Hardware: OTA-flash this firmware on a device with no SPA bundle, visit `/spa` → expect the 404 explanation page (not a redirect to `/`)
- [ ] Hardware: `make uploadfs`, then visit `/spa` → expect the SPA to render
- [ ] Cut a release tag and verify `firmware.bin`, `littlefs.bin`, AND `merged.bin` all appear as top-level release assets
- [ ] Hardware: flash `merged.bin` to a wiped device and verify both firmware boots and SPA renders without any second flash

## Summary
Closes the last open finding in GHSA-62cr-vcj8-663h.

The `receive_donation` entry point queries the on-chain ledger balance and then re-reads `s.balances[idx]` to compute `expected_min`. Without the per-canister `PoolGuard` around that await, a concurrent `swap` or `add_liquidity` can mutate `s.balances[idx]` between the two reads, corrupting internal accounting relative to the ledger.

This applies the same `PoolGuard` already used by every other mutating async path in the canister (Wave 14a's B-01). One-line addition before the `icrc1_balance_of` call.

body:
### Motivation
- The async `HttpClient` accepted caller-provided URLs and passed them directly to libcurl, exposing non-HTTP schemes (e.g. `file://`) and enabling local-file disclosure / SSRF. 
- The intent is to make the tiny HTTP client safe-by-default for typical HTTP usage while preserving the existing async/curl behavior for valid requests.

### Description
- Validate the request URL scheme in `HttpClient::getAsync()` using `parse_url()` and throw `InvalidArgumentException` for any scheme that is not `http` or `https` (file changed: `src/Rxn/Framework/Concurrency/HttpClient.php`).
- Add curl-level hardening by setting `CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS` and `CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS` to `CURLPROTO_HTTP | CURLPROTO_HTTPS` so non-HTTP schemes are blocked even if input validation is bypassed (file changed: `src/Rxn/Framework/Concurrency/HttpClient.php`).
- Add a regression test `testHttpClientRejectsNonHttpSchemes` to `SchedulerTest` that asserts `file://` URLs are rejected (file changed: `src/Rxn/Framework/Tests/Concurrency/SchedulerTest.php`).

### Testing
- Ran syntax checks `php -l src/Rxn/Framework/Concurrency/HttpClient.php` and `php -l src/Rxn/Framework/Tests/Concurrency/SchedulerTest.php`, both of which succeeded. 
- Attempted to run the unit tests with `vendor/bin/phpunit src/Rxn/Framework/Tests/Concurrency/SchedulerTest.php` but the `phpunit` binary is not available in this environment, so the full test suite could not be executed here.

author: yurekami
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2081. Any kernel signature that includes a scalar value parameter, e.g.

```python
@tilelang.autotune(configs=[{"threads": 128}, {"threads": 256}], ...)
@tilelang.jit
def test_fun(N=4096, BLOCK_N=512, threads=128):
    @T.prim_func
    def kernel(A: T.Tensor((N,), T.float32), s: T.float32):  # <- scalar value param
        ...
    return kernel

test_fun()(A, 0.1)  # crashes during autotune
```

cannot currently be autotuned.

## Root cause

The autotuner asks the profiler to generate inputs for every parameter via `Profiler._get_inputs`, which calls `get_tensor_supply(...)(param)` for each one. For the scalar `s`, that path landed in `tilelang/utils/tensor.py:get_tensor`, which unconditionally raised on empty-shape `KernelParam`s:

```python
if hasattr(param, "shape") and not param.shape:
    raise ValueError(
        f"TensorType must have a shape, but got {type(param)}, "
        "likely you are trying to generate a random tensor with a dynamic symbolic shape."
    )
```

The error message was also misleading — the actual cause is a scalar value parameter, not a dynamic shape (which is detected separately by the `tir.Var` check below).

## Fix

Teach `get_tensor` to recognize scalar params and return a Python scalar of the matching dtype family (`False` for bool, `0.0` for floats, `0` for ints) so the autotuner can invoke the kernel during benchmarking. Users that need a specific scalar value can still override per-kernel via `supply_prog`.

The scalar fast path runs *before* `get_current_device()`, so this also makes input generation work on CPU-only hosts when the kernel only takes scalar params.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `testing/python/utils/test_tensor_supply_scalar.py` — CUDA-free unit test parameterised over every `TensorSupplyType` and the common dtype families (`float32/16/64`, `bfloat16`, `int8/32/64`, `uint8`, `bool`). Locks in that scalar params yield Python scalars of the right type for every supply variant.
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on both files.
- [ ] Maintainer to confirm autotune now succeeds on the repro from #2081 (I do not have a CUDA box to run `do_bench` end-to-end).

## Tradeoffs / notes

- The default scalar value is `0` / `0.0` / `False`. This is a deliberate, deterministic choice — randomized scalars would surprise users whose kernels branch on the value. Anyone needing specific scalars should use `supply_prog`, which already takes precedence over `_get_inputs`.
- The previous error path is removed because it was unreachable for legitimate uses (scalar params now succeed) and its message was actively misleading. The dynamic-shape error path remains untouched.

Closes: #2081

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Scalar (zero-dimensional) parameters are now properly handled, returning appropriate Python scalar values instead of errors. This enables the autotuner to work with scalar arguments.

* **Tests**
  * Added regression tests validating scalar parameter support across multiple data types and tensor supply modes.

author: ahmedallam222
body:
## Summary

Closes the perceived-latency gap on PDF-tier summaries (Gemini reads the full PDF, which legitimately takes 25–30s). The previous UX was a toast that vanished after 5s plus a one-shot typing indicator that also expired after 5s — leaving 20+ seconds of silence where the bot looked frozen.

### Three small UX changes, edit-in-place pattern

1. **Persistent placeholder message** — sent immediately after the user taps the button:
   ```
   ⏳ *جاري تجهيز الملخص...*
   📚 *<book name>*

   _البوت يقرأ الكتاب ويجهّز لك ملخصًا مفصّلًا. قد يستغرق حتّى دقيقة._
   ```
2. **Refreshed typing indicator** every 4 seconds while `getBookSummary` runs (a single `sendChatAction("typing")` call expires after ~5s and looks broken on long jobs).
3. **Edit-in-place delivery** — when the summary is ready, we `editMessageText` on the placeholder instead of sending a second message. Keeps the chat clean and reads as one continuous "loading → done" interaction.

Cache hits skip the placeholder entirely (the `deliverSummary` helper is called without a `placeholderMsgId`, falling through to the plain `sendMessage` path — instant). Failures and Markdown-parse errors fall back gracefully to plain text plus a fresh send.

### Before / After

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| User taps button → toast for 5s → typing for 5s → 20s of silence → summary appears as a fresh message | User taps button → toast for 5s + persistent placeholder message in chat → typing refreshed every 4s → placeholder edits in place to become the final summary |

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

🟢 low-risk: pure UX changes in the summary callback handler. No engine changes, no API changes, no env vars.

- [ ] After deploy, request any book → tap `📘  ملخص الكتاب` → confirm the placeholder message appears immediately and you can see "جاري تجهيز الملخص..." for the duration of the call (~25s for novel PDFs, ~3-5s for cached/text-tier).
- [ ] Confirm typing indicator stays animated for the full duration (it should refresh every 4s).
- [ ] Confirm the placeholder gets *replaced in place* by the final summary — there should be exactly one message in the chat for the summary, not two.
- [ ] Tap the button twice quickly — the second tap should answer with "⏳ الملخص جاري تجهيزه..." toast and NOT spawn a second placeholder (in-flight Redis lock).

### Notes

- No tests added. The existing `_test_pr19.ts` engine harness calls `getBookSummary` directly without touching the handler, so it doesn't cover this. The placeholder/edit logic is shallow enough that visual verification on Telegram after deploy is the right test.
- This is the third small fix on top of #19. Recommended deploy order: any time after #19 + #20 are live; this one is independent.

author: osakaloop
body:
⚡ Bolt: Skip expensive SVG path generation when aggregating total distance

**What**: 
Added an optional `skipVisuals` parameter to `getRouteVisualData` which bypasses the expensive PCA, Bounding Box, and SVG string generation logic. Updated `calculateLatestStats` to utilize this flag when aggregating the `grandTotalDist` across all segments.

**Why**: 
When aggregating stats across *all* user trips (e.g. `calculateLatestStats` in `tripCalculator.js`), the application was generating full SVG projection paths for every single coordinate just to throw it away, since only the `totalDist` integer was used. This causes a linear slowdown and immense garbage collection pressure on large datasets or during folder updates.

**Impact**: 
Massively reduces memory allocation and CPU overhead during synchronous data loading and aggregation, particularly noticeable for users with many trips, eliminating O(N) path generation latency.

**Measurement**:
Verify that the overall total distance in the Stats page continues to display accurately, while evaluating lower CPU profiling times during `calculateLatestStats` initialization or when switching between multiple folders.

author: credence-the-bot[bot]
body: ## Summary Enables web-origin turns to route `host_bash` execution to a connected macOS client by client ID. Before this change, `host_bash` was only available on the interface that originated the turn — a web conversation could not invoke it even with a desktop client connected. ### Changes - **Machine name labels** — macOS clients send `X-Vellum-Machine-Name` on SSE subscription; surfaced in `assistant clients list` as a `LABEL` column for human-readable targeting - **Type scaffolding** — `targetClientId?: string` added to `HostBashRequest` and `PendingInteraction` - **Event hub targeted delivery** — `publish()` accepts `targetClientId` to bypass conversation-scoped filtering and route directly to a specific client; `broadcastMessage()` threads the value into pending interaction registration - **HostBashProxy target routing** — validates explicit target client, auto-resolves when exactly one capable client is connected, falls through to untargeted broadcast for zero/multiple-client cases - **Tool schema** — `target_client_id` added as optional field to `host_bash`; multi-client ambiguity and no-client errors surface at the tool executor layer for non-host-proxy interfaces - **Tool projection** — `host_bash` is now included for `web`/non-host-proxy interfaces when at least one capable client is connected (host_file, host_cu, host_browser remain Phase 2) - **Result route binding** — `POST /v1/host-bash-result` validates `x-vellum-client-id` header against the pending interaction's `targetClientId`; mismatches return 403 and keep the request pending - **macOS client** — decodes `targetClientId` from `HostBashRequest`; accepts host bash requests for non-local conversations when the request is explicitly targeted at this client ### Security - Existing guardian auth is unchanged - Per-request client binding check added on result submission (new) - `web` is NOT declared a host-proxy interface — this is routed delegation, not local capability - Explicit approvals unchanged ### Backwards Compatibility Desktop-origin `host_bash` behavior is fully preserved. Clients not sending `X-Vellum-Client-Id` on result posts will get 400 only for requests that have a `targetClientId` set (i.e. cross-client requests). Existing macOS-origin flows always have `targetClientId == nil` so they are unaffected. ### Test Plan - Unit: event hub targeted delivery bypasses conversation filter - Unit: proxy auto-resolve single client, error on invalid explicit target - Unit: host-bash-result rejects wrong client (403), missing header (400), accepts match - Unit: tool projection allows host_bash for web when capable client connected - Unit: macOS acceptance guard — targeted non-local accepted, non-targeted non-local ignored 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

author: capt-marbles
body:
## Summary

`agents@0.11.x` leaves `mcpConnections[id].connectionState` at `AUTHENTICATING` after a 401 even when no `authProvider` is installed. Result: `getMcpServers()` and `waitForSettled` reported `"authenticating"` forever, with the SDK's internal `"OAuth configuration incomplete: missing authUrl"` string bubbling up unfiltered. Stuck-server UX dead end.

This PR detects the bad-credentials signature (`state === "authenticating"` OR `state === "failed"` with a `/OAuth configuration incomplete/i` error) via a new `isCredentialsRejection` helper, then `mcp.removeServer(id)` to clear the zombie before any later state read. Surfaces a clean, actionable "credentials rejected" error instead. Applied at both the connect path and the hibernation-restore path.

While here, also necessary for the MCP surface to actually work end-to-end:

- Stable server IDs (`mcp_<slug>` with collision suffix) so restore-from-storage can re-attach
- URL-based dedupe in connect / disconnect / forget
- Restore-on-`onStart` so post-hibernation turns find their MCP tools
- Defensive reconnect+retry on the call path + hard-rebuild fallback
- Stable `tool_<server>_<tool>` wrappers (SDK's raw keys change on reconnect)
- Cheap `debug` opt-in on `list_mcp_servers` for next-time diagnostics
- Refactor: extract background-task helpers + new `restoreHeaderAuthServer` to stay under the 700-line file cap

**Stacked on #1** — until #1 merges, the diff here includes its 17 lines of build-fix as a prerequisite.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run types:check` passes
- [x] `pnpm run lint` passes

  - Happy path: `state: ready`, 41 tools discovered, `get_me` returns user data
  - Bad-token path: `state: failed` with credentials-rejected message + HTTP 401 probe (was: `state: authenticating`, OAuth-incomplete error)

author: acehack
body:
## Summary

Aaron 2026-05-03 framing correction across 4 messages: edge-defining work is NOT speculation. If "speculation" is broad enough to cover calibration + hypothesis-formation + frontier-recognition, it covers EVERYTHING the project does (vibe-coded experiment + alignment-frontier + intellectual-backup-of-earth = all hypothesis-and-test) — making the term meaningless.

## The narrow definition

Reserve "speculation" for the literal idle-fallback case. Action hierarchy:

| Tier | What it is |
|---|---|
| Evidence | Action backed by direct observation |
| Speculative-action-for-evidence | Action that GENERATES evidence (calibration / hypothesis / edge-defining) — **the JOB, not idle-fallback** |
| Speculation (narrow) | Idle-fallback when literally nothing else |
| Inaction | Waiting / deferring |

## Why this matters

**Framing affects confidence affects substrate quality.** Calling edge-defining work "speculative" demotes it from first-class to fallback. Otto commits less rigorously to substrate it has labeled fallback.

Per Karpathy edge-runner framing: edge-running IS the job. Calibration data, hypothesis-formation, and frontier-recognition substrate ARE the edge-defining work.

## Future-Otto rule

When the never-be-idle ladder surfaces "speculative work," check if it's edge-defining. If yes, frame as edge-defining-work in chat + commits + tick shards. Replace "shifting to speculative work" → "continuing edge-defining work" or "next calibration data point."

body:
Implements [docs/GDD.md §13.8](docs/GDD.md) + [.github/wiki-ci-spec.md](.github/wiki-ci-spec.md). The wait is over.

## What landed

### Workflows (`.github/workflows/`)
| File | Purpose | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `pr-validate.yml` | lint, typecheck, unit (+ coverage), e2e (chromium PR / full matrix on push), build, optional electron build | PR to `development`/`alpha`/`stable`; push to `development` |
| `security-scan.yml` | npm audit (high blocking, moderate informational), CodeQL JS/TS, Dependency Review, CSP-presence (warn until 2026-05-16 then hard-fail — Sol F-13), gitleaks | PR + weekly Mon 08:00 UTC + push to dev |
| `a11y-scan.yml` | existing accessibility spec + axe scan (auto-skips with sticky comment if `@axe-core/playwright` not installed) | PR touching renderer/e2e/index.html |
| `nightly-soak.yml` | determinism (uses `tests/fixtures/determinism-baseline.json`), perf-bench, full Playwright matrix | daily 06:00 UTC |
| `release.yml` | validate-tag (must be on `alpha`/`stable`), build-web, build-electron matrix (win/mac/linux), build-android (signed if secrets present, unsigned + warning otherwise), release-notes (extracts from `docs/about/CHANGELOG.md`), gh-release | tag `v*.*.*` |
| `wiki-ci.yml` | implements [.github/wiki-ci-spec.md](.github/wiki-ci-spec.md) — broken `[[link]]` count (fail), missing GDD status block (fail), orphans (warn), sticky PR comment | PR touching `docs/wiki/**` |

### Existing workflows — decisions
- `ci.yml` — **deleted**, superseded by `pr-validate.yml`
- `dependency-review.yml` — **deleted**, folded into `security-scan.yml`
- `android-apk-prerelease.yml` — **retained** (Android pre-release pipeline complements `release.yml`)

### Supporting files
- `.nvmrc` → `20` (closes Sol's missing-nvmrc gap, GDD §13.8.2)
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` → single-maintainer baseline
- `.github/dependabot.yml` → weekly npm + GitHub-Actions, grouped to reduce PR noise. Targets `development`. Consistent with PR #116.
- `.github/a11y-allowlist.json` → placeholder schema
- `tests/fixtures/determinism-baseline.json` → placeholder; nightly-soak populates on first successful soak

### `package.json`
- Added `"build": "npm run build:web"` alias (workflow expectation)
- Added `"engines": { "node": ">=20.0.0 <21" }`
- `@playwright/test` already present (Sol F-07 was a false alarm — it's at `^1.59.1`)

### Documentation
- `.github/wiki-ci-spec.md` status header updated from "spec only" to "Implemented in `wiki-ci.yml`"
- GDD §13.8 left untouched (spec already matches; minor `experimental` → `development` drift from Path A reorg is a separate cleanup)

## Constraints honored
- All marketplace actions pinned to `@v4` / `@v3` / `@v2` major versions
- `npm ci` everywhere, never `npm install`
- npm cache + Playwright browsers cached
- All `secrets.*` references use `${{ secrets.X || '' }}` fallbacks; none are required
- No workflows run locally; first execution is on GitHub once merged

## Phase 4 backlog items addressed
- ✅ `.nvmrc` gap (GDD §13.8.2)
- ✅ Sol F-07 (`@playwright/test` already in devDeps — verified, no change needed)
- ⚠️ Sol F-13 (CSP-presence) — workflow asserts presence; warn-only until 2026-05-16, then hard-fail
- ⚠️ Sol F-11 (determinism job) — `nightly-soak.yml / determinism` exists but stubbed pending `npm run test:soak` script
- ⏳ Sol F-03 (IPC fuzz tests) — not addressed here; separate test work

## Pending user action
1. **Branch protection updates** — see "Branch protection click-paths" below. I did not run `gh api` against your repo; you should apply these via the GitHub UI or with your own token after the workflows run once and produce status check contexts.
2. **Code-signing secrets** (optional, for `release.yml`):
   - `CSC_LINK`, `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD` (Electron Win/macOS)
   - `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID` (notarisation)
   - `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PROPERTIES` (Android signing)
   Without these, releases produce unsigned binaries with a warning — they do not fail.
3. **`@axe-core/playwright`** — not yet a dep. Install when ready; `a11y-scan.yml` auto-detects.
4. **Run `npm install`** locally to pick up the `package.json` changes.
5. **File the "Nightly Soak Results" tracking issue** — `nightly-soak.yml` has a stub step ready (`if: false`) that posts to it once the issue exists.

- `npm run test:soak` and `npm run bench` — workflows use `--if-present` style detection; pass-noop with summary message until the scripts exist (Sol Phase-4 follow-up; M6 milestone)
- Coverage 80% line gate on `src/engine/**` and `src/systems/**` — currently soft (warning); promotes to hard gate in M6
- Tag-protection automation in `release.yml` — assumes you apply the GitHub-side tag protection rule manually (see click-paths)

Apply via **Settings → Branches → Add rule**. Status check contexts will be selectable after each workflow runs once.

**`development`** — required checks:
- `lint`, `typecheck`, `unit`, `e2e`, `build` (all from `pr-validate`)

**`alpha`** — all of `development`'s plus:
- `a11y` (from `a11y-scan`)

`priority:p1-high`, `area:ci`

- **Global** — whole-vault overview
- **Local** — N-hop neighborhood around a focal note (depth 1–3)

Click a node to open the live `<Editor>` in a resizable split next to the graph (full edit/save/inspector functionality). Right-click to pivot local mode to that note.

- Toolbar: Global/Local toggle, depth slider, node search filter, Archived/Orphans toggles, zoom controls

- **`upstream_status` dropped**: stale/current flag removed from schema and API responses. Computed staleness deferred to #100.
- **`ScriptView.create_version` dropped** (Q1 → option a): callers now call `ScriptPiece.create_version` directly with `scene_id`. ScriptView retains only pin-management actions for the V/VV rebuild in #94.

author: iskandr
body:
## Summary

Sample resolver was silently misclassifying ~165K rows because (1) curator-written mouse alleles like \`H-2Kb\` never matched IEDB's canonical \`H2-K*b\`, and (2) when multiple ms_samples in a PMID shared an allele bag, the join arbitrarily picked the first sample for every row.

Two fixes:

- **mhcgnomes normalize YAML allele tokens** before building the lookup. Mhcgnomes already canonicalizes both forms to \`H2-K*b\` — the resolver just wasn't calling it on the YAML side.
- **Per-obs-row tie-break** scoring each candidate's \`sample_label\` + \`perturbation\` tokens against the obs row's \`cell_name\` / \`source_tissue\` / \`antigen_processing_comments\` / \`assay_comments\`. Token-prefix overlap with rarity weighting (tokens unique to one candidate weight more than tokens shared by all) plus word-boundary substring containment. Per-(pmid, class) variance check drops constant study-level fields so they don't dominate the rarity score.

## Concrete impact

Newly-resolved sample-level peptides for MHC-I-relevant APM perturbations:

| intervention | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| IFN-gamma | 44 | **81,504** |
| ERAP1 | 15,087 | 61,170 |
| ERAP2 | 16,127 | 32,137 |
| Mouse TAP1 | 0 | **16,665** |
| Tasmanian devil DFT1+IFN-γ | 0 | **13,731** |
| TNF-alpha | 0 | **4,676** |

Specific PMIDs that now split correctly:
- 34428180 (Son 2021 mouse transplant): hepatocyte vs splenocyte vs skin-graft samples no longer collapse onto first pick
- 33460454 (Tasmanian devil DFT1/DFT2/fibroblasts): three samples sharing 'Saha class I' sentinel now split via cell_name
- 33968037 (Goncalves MDA-MB-231 ± IFN-γ): IFN-γ-treated rows pick the +IFN sample via assay_comments
- 30833945 (Javitt A549 + TNFα + IFN-γ): now resolves
- 31844290 (Sarkizova MEL/GBM): per-allele samples already resolved; ambiguous overlapping-allele cases now also resolve

## Test plan
- [x] 7 new unit tests in \`test_export.py\` covering: rarity weighting (DFT1 vs DFT2), word-boundary substring (the \"treated\"-in-\"untreated\" trap), empty-obs fallback, single-candidate fallback, mouse allele normalization, hepatocyte/spleen split
- [x] \`./format.sh\` clean
- [x] \`./lint.sh\` clean
- [x] \`./test.sh\` — 610 passed, 2 skipped

author: jinzhen-lin
body: ### **The DeepSeek V4 Support have been moved to https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23754** This PR add humming kernels to SGLang. This PR is based on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23754 , adding and improving support for DeepSeek V4 on top of it. Humming Kenrels: https://github.com/inclusionAI/humming vLLM supports: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34556 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41083 Humming is a universal, high-performance quantization kernel (similar to the Marlin kernel), but offers several advantages over Marlin: - Extensive Quantization Support: Supports all combinations of W{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8}A{16,8,4} for quantization inference. - Superior Performance: Humming outperforms Marlin, especially in large batch scenarios and on Hopper GPUs. - Enhanced JIT Support: Compared to the current Marlin JIT implementation in SGLang, Humming offers faster compilation. - For DeepSeek V4, Humming supports high-performance W4A8 implementation on Hopper. - Support DeepEP ## Benchmark Service start command ``` # marlin w4a16 sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /home/admin/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 12321 # humming w4a16 sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /home/admin/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend humming \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 12321 # humming w4a8 SGLANG_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype": "float8e4m3"}' sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /home/admin/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend humming \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 12321 ``` Benchmark command ``` # for prefill python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --tokenizer /home/admin/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/ \ --port 12321 \ --dataset-name random-ids \ --random-input-len 65536 \ --random-output-len 1 \ --num-prompts 128 \ --max-concurrency 32 \ --random-range-ratio 1 # for decoding python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --tokenizer /home/admin/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/ \ --port 12321 \ --dataset-name random-ids \ --random-input-len 1 \ --random-output-len 4096 \ --num-prompts 256 \ --max-concurrency 64 \ --random-range-ratio 1 ``` Benchamrk result (TPS) | | Prefill | Decoding | | - | - | - | | Marlin W4A16 | 7272.49 | 2286.72 | | Humming W4A16 | 9060.34 | 2278.49 | | Humming W4A8 | 9917.43 | 2335.14 | In SGLang, `splitkv_mla` and `paged_mqa` are used for the prefill part of DeepSeek V4, and the attention part takes longer than expected. If fixed, Humming is expected to achieve a greater e2e improvement.
