## Summary

Closes the "es L3 ablation 未CI追加" intent in **issue #47 part 1** by adding Spanish to the existing **L1 fast layer-ablation + μ-benchmark** CI track (`evaluate (layer ablation + μ-benchmark)`). The es pipeline now has end-to-end CI coverage symmetric with en / ja / zh, completing the es integration.

> Note on naming: issue #47 originally framed this under `eval_l3`, but the actually-CI-resident ablation harness is `eval_l1_fast` (text-fixture ablation against `MockAsr`). Per discussion, the right move is to extend `eval_l1_fast` rather than wire up a new `eval_l3` job. `eval_l3` (natural-speech ablation) stays out-of-scope for this PR.

## Changes

- **`tests/evaluation/fixtures/es.jsonl`** (new, 27 entries) — mirrors `en.jsonl` shape:
  - 8 `pure_filler` (`e` / `eh` / `ehm` / `ah` / `mm` at sentence start and mid-utterance)
  - 2 `contextual_filler` (`o sea` multi-word)
  - 7 `self_correction` (uses every cue in `SelfCorrectionDetector::detect_spanish`: `perdón`, `digo`, `quiero decir`, `mejor dicho`, `o sea`)
  - 10 `clean`
  - Software-deployment dialogue theme matches `en.jsonl` for tonal consistency
- **`examples/eval_l1_fast.rs`**:
  - default `--langs` now `en,ja,zh,es`
  - `evaluate_language` configs match arm extended to `"es"`
  - `build_pipeline` filter dispatches `"es"` → `SpanishFillerFilter::new()`
  - `bench_layer_latency` adds an `"es"` arm running the same `bench_filter` measurement
  - `print_language_result` + per-utterance metric: `en` | `es` → WER, others → CER
  - module doc comment updated to reflect new fixture set
- **`docs/benchmarks/ci_baseline_layers.json`**: es entry inserted alphabetically between en and ja, populated from 3 stable consecutive local runs:
    | metric | value |
    |---|---|
    | ablation/full | WER=0.4930 |
    | ablation/without_filler | WER=0.5306 |
    | ablation/without_punctuation | WER=0.0790 |
    | ablation/without_self_correction | WER=0.6498 |
    | latency/filler | p50=1.1μs / p95=1.7μs |

`without_punctuation = 0.079` vs `full = 0.493` shows `BasicPunctuationRestorer` accounts for the bulk of the surface-form delta against the lowercase / no-period reference (same dynamic as en where `full = 0.4198`, `without_punctuation = 0.0401`). `without_self_correction > full` confirms `SelfCorrectionDetector::detect_spanish` is correctly removing reparanda in the 7 self_correction fixtures. `without_filler > full` shows `SpanishFillerFilter` measurably contributes to the win on the 10 filler fixtures.

Implements the full Expenses Management module for TravelGenie (IT24101021), featuring real-time financial tracking and market intelligence.

Backend

Expense Tracking Engine: Robust schema for multi-category spend tracking (Food, Transport, Activity, etc.) linked to trips and users.
Platform Intelligence: PriceRecord model and service to maintain a global benchmark database for market prices.
Financial Analytics API: Real-time budget-vs-actual health checks and automated trip-health reporting.
Multi-Currency Support: Native backend support for LKR, USD, and EUR financial transparency.
Automated Oversight: System-triggered budget alerts and platform-wide market trend monitoring via /api/v1/expenses/admin.
Mobile

Financial Intelligence Dashboard: Visual spending health indicators and interactive budget-vs-actual analytics.
Market Price Trends: Dedicated explorer for travelers to view real-time cost benchmarks for Accommodation, Transport, and Activities.

author: paperprooflabs
body:
This PR adds support for the **did:proof** method to the Universal Resolver by introducing a new local driver. The did:proof method is designed as part of the PaperProof ecosystem and resolves DIDs by retrieving DID Documents with embedded proof metadata.

**Driver Details:**

- **DID Method:** did:proof
- **Driver Repository:** [PaperProofLabs/uni-resolver-driver-did-proof](https://github.com/PaperProofLabs/uni-resolver-driver-did-proof)
- **Specification Repository:** [PaperProofLabs/proof](https://github.com/PaperProofLabs/proof)

**Key Features:**

- **Local Driver Class Instantiation:** This PR introduces support for registering drivers via local Java class instantiation (not just HTTP endpoints), enabling more efficient driver loading.
- **DID Pattern Validation:** The driver validates did:proof identifiers using the pattern `^(did:proof:z[A-Za-z0-9]{20,})$`
- **Query Parameter Parsing:** Supports optional query parameters for customizing resolution behavior
- **Full Driver Interface Implementation:** Implements all required Driver interface methods including `resolve()`, `dereference()`, `properties()`, `testIdentifiers()`, and `traits()`

**Resolution Flow:**

1. The Universal Resolver routes did:proof identifiers to this driver
2. The driver validates the DID format and extracts the method-specific ID
3. The driver constructs a DID Document with proof-related metadata
4. The DID Document is returned in compliance with DID Core resolution format

**Framework Changes:**

- Extended `LocalUniResolverConfigurator` to support `driverClass` field for local instantiation
- Updated Spring Boot configuration in `WebAppConfig` to handle local drivers
- Added `driverClass` property binding in `DriverConfigs`
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing HTTP-based drivers

author: kofman88
body:
## Summary

User asked for a full pixel-precision audit ("переправь всю генерацию на соответствие с эталоном").  Auditing all 9 generator outputs against their reference JPGs surfaced two systemic BingX issues:

1. **Strip-copy wipe leaked neighbouring text.** "Strip from above" pasted the header bottom into the meta zone, the meta into the PnL zone, etc. The diff visualisation showed every text element appearing as a faint *duplicate* — that was actually the previous row's text re-pasted, not a font-rendering halo.
2. **Single global bg colour didn't blend.** Even with flat-fill, BingX bg varies subtly per variant (whale ≈ 10, dot ≈ 11, football ≈ 2-7) and per y-band — a global sample at (30, 250) left visible darker rectangles around the wipe destinations.

## Fix

- Replace strip-copy with flat-fill — BingX templates have no chart grid, so flat-fill is the correct strategy and removes the cross-row leak entirely.
- Per-zone bg sampling: read 5 pixels along x=10..42 at the zone's mid-y, take the median. Local-bg accurate, robust to stray bright pixels.
- Wipe rects widened to cover worst-case baked text:
  - Header: x=98..830 (was ..720) — covers "Нереализованная П/У" to x=798
  - Meta:   y=600..690 — covers Russian "р" descender
- All zone bounds nudged a few px so letter halos are wiped too.

## Test plan

- [x] All 6 BingX share variants render with single-copy, ghost-free text
- [x] Background blends seamlessly around every wipe zone (verified zoomed side-by-side for whale_plus and dot_minus)
- [x] All 3 Bybit share variants unchanged

author: pablodans
body:
The 5 mesyl-phosphonate backbone fragments (XV1, VX1, XV2, ZV1, ZV2)
shipped with a -N=N=N tail attached to the sulfonyl S, which was a
historical error -- the intended group is a methyl (S-CH3). This commit
replaces the azide tail with a methyl on all five fragments and adds
VX2, the (R)-stereoisomer of VX1, which was listed in the catalog but
had no mol2 in dat/lib_backbone/.

Pipeline used:
  1. RDKit/openbabel cirurgical edit on the upstream mol2 to delete the
     three azide N atoms and insert a tetrahedral CH3 in their place,
     anchored at S at 1.78 A (S-C bond) with C-H at 1.09 A.
  2. Gaussian 16 HF/6-31G(d) opt + Merz-Kollman ESP at the modXNA
     reference route line (Love et al., JCTC 2024):
       # opt scf=tight hf/6-31g(d) pop=mk density=current geom=connectivity
       iop(6/33=2,6/42=6)
  3. antechamber RESP fit with -at amber to recover OL15-compatible
     atom types and charges (-nc 0 enforces neutral total).
  4. Atom names re-derived to canonical OL15 by graph isomorphism with
     the previous (azide) version of each fragment, then the
     modXNA-fragment annotation re-injected with the original
     HEAD/HEAD01STRIP/TAIL/TAIL01STRIP masks unchanged.

VX2 was generated from VX1 by mirror reflection (x -> -x), producing
the enantiomeric geometry; topology is identical to VX1, so the same
modXNA mask line applies (with the residue id swapped).

Total RESP charge sum on each fragment: -2e-6 (within the resolver's
floating-point tolerance).

body:
🛡️ **Sentinel Security Fix: [CRITICAL] Leaked API Keys**

### 💡 Vulnerability
Actual Cloudflare and Groq API keys were committed to the repository in a `.ENV` file, exposing them to anyone with access to the source code. Additionally, the Cloudflare account ID was hardcoded in a placeholder format in the API URL.

### 🎯 Impact
Exploitation of these leaked keys could lead to unauthorized API usage, potential service disruption, and financial costs associated with API quota consumption.

### 🔧 Fix
1.  **Secured Secrets:** Removed `.ENV` from Git tracking and added it to a new root-level `.gitignore`.
2.  **Provided Template:** Created `.ENV.example` with redacted placeholders for safe local development.
3.  **Refactored Logic:** Updated `warp-source/app/src/server/server_api.rs` to use consistent environment variable names (`CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY_1`) and introduced a `VESPER_CF_ID` variable to replace the hardcoded account ID in the Cloudflare API endpoint.

### ✅ Verification
- Confirmed `.ENV` is no longer tracked by Git: `git ls-files .ENV` (returns empty).
- Verified `.gitignore` contains `.ENV`.
- Verified `.ENV.example` contains the correct placeholders.
- Frontend build passes with `pnpm build`.

author: pyramation
body:
## Summary

Adds blueprint type system support for the compound conditions and DataImageEmbedding features introduced in [constructive-db PR #969](https://github.com/constructive-io/constructive-db/pull/969).

**Changes:**

1. **`DataJobTrigger` — added `conditions` parameter** to `parameter_schema` in `data-job-trigger.ts`. The generated type supports:
   - Leaf conditions: `{field, op, value?, row?, ref?}` with typed operators (`=`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `LIKE`, `NOT LIKE`, `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL`, `IS DISTINCT FROM`)
   - Array shorthand (implicit AND): `conditions: [cond1, cond2]`
   - Nested combinators: `{AND: [...], OR: [...], NOT: {...}}`
   - Column-to-column comparison via `ref`: `{field: 'score', op: '>', ref: {field: 'min_score', row: 'NEW'}}`
   - Mutual exclusion with `condition_field` and `watch_fields` (documented in description)

2. **`DataImageEmbedding` — new node type** in `data-image-embedding.ts`. Composition wrapper that delegates to SearchVector + DataJobTrigger with image-specific defaults:
   - Vector field: `embedding` (512 dims, HNSW, cosine)
   - Job trigger: fires on UPDATE when `status` transitions from `pending` to `ready` and `mime_type` matches `image/%`
   - Configurable: field_name, dimensions, index_method, metric, task_identifier, status_field/values, mime_patterns, payload_custom

3. **Regenerated `blueprint-types.generated.ts`** — 56 node types (was 55). `DataImageEmbeddingParams` interface + `DataImageEmbedding` in `BlueprintNodeShorthand`/`BlueprintNodeObject` unions.

**Companion PRs:**
- [constructive-db PR #969](https://github.com/constructive-io/constructive-db/pull/969) — SQL generators (`build_condition_ast`, `data_image_embedding`, updated `data_job_trigger`)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Verify `DataJobTriggerParams.conditions` type matches the SQL generator's accepted JSON shape in constructive-db
- [ ] Verify `DataImageEmbeddingParams` defaults match the SQL generator defaults in `data_image_embedding.sql`
- [ ] Test that blueprint autocomplete works correctly for both `conditions` and `DataImageEmbedding` in an IDE

### Notes

The `conditions` type uses `oneOf` in the JSON Schema to support both the object form (single leaf or combinator) and array form (implicit AND). The `value` field is typed as `any` in the generated TS because the actual type is resolved at runtime from the PostgreSQL column type via `information_schema.columns` — this is intentional.

author: conka8
body:
## Summary

Implements task 4 from `docs/DEVELOPER_NEXT_STEPS.md`: a single new document, `docs/PUBLIC_DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md`, that spells out the prerequisites for ever exposing the API or dashboard
beyond `127.0.0.1`.

This PR is documentation only. No code changed.

## What is in the checklist

Eleven sections covering everything the developer brief and existing safety notes already implied:

1. **Authentication** - API key vs OAuth vs cookie, uniform across endpoints, key rotation, gating `/docs` and `/health`.
2. **Rate limiting** - per-IP and per-identity ceilings, harder limits on the engine endpoints than on `/generate_probes`,
   proxy-level body-size cap as defense in depth on top of the Pydantic field-length limits.
3. **HTTPS** - TLS termination at the reverse proxy, TLS 1.2+ only, HSTS, http→https redirect, verified auto-renewal.
4. **CORS** - explicit origin allow-list (no wildcards), narrow methods/headers, `allow_credentials` gated on the auth model.
5. **Logging** - never log `claim` / `argument` / `context` /  `probe_answers.answer`; log report id + polarity + scores;
   structured JSON; disable Swagger UI in production.
6. **Data retention** - `InMemoryStore` is ephemeral and fine; `FileStore` needs a retention sweep, encryption at rest in
   regulated environments, and a deletion path.
7. **Network exposure** - keep `--host 127.0.0.1` behind the proxy; run as non-root, sandboxed, with resource limits; the
   `FileStore` root is the only writeable path.
8. **Dependency hygiene** - pinned versions, Dependabot or `pip-audit`, 7-day patch SLO.
9. **Engine integrity** - carry-over from `DEVELOPER_NEXT_STEPS.md`: deterministic engine stays authoritative, every input is
   untrusted, the dashboard's strict CSP must not be weakened.
10. **Pre-launch verification** - eight security headers on every endpoint, `/docs` gated, dry-run 401/403/429 probes,
    backup-restore tested, runbook documented.
11. **Reasonable scope today** - explicit envelope so the checklist does not block local-demo workflows: `127.0.0.1`
    plus optional SSH port forwarding is safe; the moment any other condition is true, the checklist applies in full.

Each item is a checkbox so the doc reads as a literal pre-flight list, not prose.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest projects/effective_boolean_filter/tests/` - 145 passed (no code change)
- [x] GitHub Actions `Python tests` workflow green on this PR
- [x] `MANIFEST.json` lists the new doc
- [x] `DEVELOPER_NEXT_STEPS.md` links to it
- [x] No public network exposure introduced

author: b2jk-industry
body:
## Summary

Three Codex findings on the verify-ens CCIP-Read implementation that shipped in #446. All three are **EIP-3668 conformance issues** — the original implementation worked against our own gateway but diverged from the spec on three points.

| # | Sev | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **P1** | OffchainLookup follow doesn't check `sender == resolver` | Added sender-mismatch guard in `call_text_via_ensip10` |
| 2 | **P1** | Always GET, even when URL template lacks `{data}` | Added `http_post_json` to transport; dispatch on `{data}` presence |
| 3 | **P2** | Retry policy inverted: retried on 4xx, stopped on 5xx | Flipped: 4xx terminal, 5xx + transport try next URL |

### P1 — Sender check (EIP-3668 §"Client Lookup Protocol")

A resolver could bubble an `OffchainLookup` from a *nested* call to an attacker-controlled contract; without the sender check, the client would issue gateway requests + a callback `eth_call` against that untrusted address. `call_text_via_ensip10` now compares `lookup.sender` against the resolver address (lowercase, prefix-stripped) and refuses to follow on mismatch.

### P1 — POST fallback when `{data}` is absent

EIP-3668: `{data}` in URL template → GET (data in URL); `{data}` absent → POST with JSON body `{"sender":"0x..","data":"0x.."}`. The previous always-GET path wouldn't resolve against POST-only gateway templates (common for short URLs). Added `JsonRpcTransport::http_post_json` (default impl errors; `ReqwestTransport` implements it). Our own gateway template still uses GET — no change to live behaviour.

### P2 — Retry-class inversion

Previous policy: retry on 4xx, stop on 5xx. Spec policy: 4xx is *terminal* for that lookup (gateway has authoritative data + is rejecting; trying another gateway won't help); 5xx + transport errors trigger trying the next URL. Without this fix, transient 502s short-circuited and "404 not found" burned through every gateway's quota in turn.

## Tests

6 new unit tests (215 → 221 total, all green):
- `is_http_4xx_recognises_404_but_not_5xx_or_transport` — boundary check on the new helper
- `follow_uses_get_when_url_has_data_placeholder` / `follow_uses_post_when_url_lacks_data_placeholder` — dispatch
- `follow_does_not_retry_after_4xx` / `follow_retries_next_url_after_5xx` — retry policy
- `resolve_raw_text_rejects_offchain_lookup_with_mismatched_sender` — sender check

## Live verification

\`\`\`
$ SBO3L_SEPOLIA_RPC_URL=https://eth-sepolia.g.alchemy.com/v2/... \\
  cargo test -p sbo3l-identity --test ccip_read_sepolia_live -- --include-ignored
running 2 tests
test research_agent_subname_resolves_via_ccip_read ... ok
test research_agent_endpoint_record_resolves_via_ccip_read ... ok
test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
\`\`\`

The legitimate single-resolver path still works because our `OffchainResolver.resolve(name, data)` correctly sets `sender = address(this)` in the OffchainLookup revert.

- [x] cargo fmt --all -- --check (clean)

### Motivation

- Prevent spoofing where `Authorization: Bearer <victim_id>:anything` was accepted and used as the authenticated user for dashboard CRUD operations.

First of three staged PRs working through #133's deferred ACs (per the staging proposed in [this comment](https://github.com/IamMrCupp/claude-project-kit/issues/133#issuecomment-4365529750)). Closes the **template + bootstrap + session-start + docs** parts; leaves the multi-initiative exemplar (PR B) and the ADR (PR C) for follow-ups.

## Summary

Multiple long-running workspaces are about to spin up across personal + work projects, all hosting many initiatives over months. This PR ships the workspace-scope phase-tracking template that the existing `workspace-CONTEXT.md` (Current Initiative pointer) and `workspace-plan.md` (initiative roster) were designed to anchor against.

- **`templates/workspace/workspace-phase-N-checklist.md`** — new template. Mirrors per-repo `phase-N-checklist.md` at workspace scope: Section/Item structure, Acceptance testing block, Phase exit checklist. Crucial differences vs. per-repo: each item records branches + PRs across **multiple repos**, items reference a tracker key shared across the per-repo PRs, acceptance tests typically span repos, and the Phase exit checklist includes the "if this completes the active initiative, archive this checklist" step.
- **`bootstrap.sh`** — copies the new template alongside `workspace-CONTEXT.md` + `workspace-plan.md` whenever `--workspace <path>` creates a workspace. Dry-run preview echo line updated to match.
- **`templates/.claude/commands/session-start.md`** + dogfood-synced `.claude/commands/session-start.md` — adds `workspace-phase-N-checklist.md` to the workspace-mode load list so the slash command surfaces the active initiative's current phase up front.
- **`SETUP.md` "Long-running workspace layout"** — new sub-section under "Single-initiative vs. long-running workspaces". Documents the three workspace-scope files (CONTEXT / plan / phase-N-checklist), the per-repo + workspace layering, and the archival ritual when an initiative wraps.
- **`PROMPTS.md` Prompt 11** — paired prompt for users who want the same multi-initiative session-start flow without the slash command. References the slash command as the packaged form.
- **`tests/bootstrap_workspace.bats`** — one new test asserting the file is created with correct headers (Workspace Phase, Active initiative, Acceptance testing, Phase exit).

## What ticket-driven, multi-repo work looks like in this template

The template's Section A example shows a single item that spans two repos:

```
### A.1 {{Task title}}

- **Tracker:** {{KEY-NNN if applicable}}
- **Repos:**
  - **{{repo-a}}** — branch `{{type/KEY-NNN-slug}}` → PR #{{N}}
  - **{{repo-b}}** — branch `{{type/KEY-NNN-slug}}` → PR #{{N}}
- **Status:** [ ] merged
```

This matches the existing JIRA-driven workspace convention from #61 (same ticket key reused across multiple repo PRs, single shared tracker entry).

author: davedev42
body:
## Summary

Two more silently-degradable code paths pinned, both no-hardware:

### `tests/runner.rs` — event-worker pins

- **`runner_event_worker_forwards_event_tick_to_poll`** — pins the `RunnerConfig::event_tick` → `EventPoll::next_timeout(d)` plumbing at `src/runner.rs:402, 407`. Existing `runner_config_default_pins_field_values` only checked the field's default *value*, not that the runner actually forwarded it. Test installs a `RecordingEventPoll` whose `next_timeout` writes its `Duration` argument to a shared `Arc<Mutex<Option<Duration>>>`, spawns a runner with `event_tick = 173ms`, polls until the worker has called `next_timeout` at least once, and asserts the recorded duration matches. A regression that hard-coded `Duration::from_millis(50)`, swapped to `poll_interval`, or passed `Duration::ZERO` would silently change the event cadence.

- **`runner_event_worker_exits_when_events_receiver_dropped`** — pins `src/runner.rs:408-410` (`if ev_tx.send(event).is_err() { break }`). Test takes + drops the events receiver, pushes 8 events into the recording poll's queue (forcing `ev_tx.send` against the closed channel), then runs `runner.stop()` on a side thread with a 3-second deadline. If the event worker leaked (regression: `let _ = ev_tx.send(event)`), the main worker's join of the event handle would hang forever. Bounded-time observable contract that doesn't peek at internal thread state.

### `nokhwa-core/src/types_tests.rs` — fulfill empty-list framerate pins

Existing `fulfill_empty_format_list` only covered `AbsoluteHighestResolution`. The framerate variants have identical `?`-on-empty short-circuits in separate match arms but no test:

- **`fulfill_absolute_highest_framerate_returns_none_for_empty_format_list`**
- **`fulfill_highest_framerate_returns_none_for_empty_format_list`**

A regression adding a fallback to one arm without the others (e.g. "return `CameraFormat::default()` if empty") would slip through. Two two-liner tests close the symmetry; pure logic, microsecond runtime.

ADR 0008 step 4 — first real cron use case stacked on top of #72's
timer scaffolding (now merged at 8c4e8e5). Re-opened from #73 after
its base branch was deleted on #72 squash-merge.

The Coder VM nightly fires a fresh ephemeral workspace that plans
the exe stack and ships the artifact to GCS.

## What lands

### IaC (`tofu/exe/coder.tf`)

- `google_secret_manager_secret.exe_tofu_encryption_passphrase` —
  shell only; operator uploads the value once after first apply.
- `secretmanager.secretAccessor` IAM grant: workspace SA → that
  secret.
- `google_storage_bucket_iam_member`: workspace SA →
  `roles/storage.objectAdmin` on `local.state_bucket`.

### VM startup_script

- `/usr/local/bin/coder-cron-spawn-job` — VM-side analog of
  `cdr-job`: generates a unique workspace name, calls
  `coder-cron-run create` with the `exe-dotfiles-job` template,
  polls `lifecycle_state` until `ready`, deletes via trap.
- `coder-cron-tofu-plan.service` — `bash -c` wraps the multi-step
  command (systemd ExecStart treats `&&` as a literal arg).
- `coder-cron-tofu-plan.timer` — daily 04:23 UTC, `Persistent=true`,
  `RandomizedDelaySec=600`, enabled at boot.

### Workspace-side script (`exe/scripts/cron-tofu-plan.sh`)

1. Clone dotfiles to `/root/cron-tofu-plan`
2. Fetch `TF_ENCRYPTION` passphrase from Secret Manager
3. `tofu init && tofu plan -refresh=false -out=plan.bin`
   (`-refresh=false` because workspace SA lacks CF/TS API tokens)
4. Ship `plan.bin` + `plan.txt` + `run.log` to
   `gs://gen-ai-hironow-tofu-state/jobs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/tofu-plan-<HHMMSSZ>.{bin,txt,log}`
5. **Always exits 0** so diagnostics ship even on tofu failure

### Tooling pin (`mise.toml`)

- `opentofu = "1.11.6"` so `tofu` is baked into the dev container
  image.

### Tests (8 new)

- `test_tofu_encryption_passphrase_secret_resource_present` (reader
  = workspace SA, not Coder VM SA; no `_version` resource)
- `test_workspace_state_bucket_iam_present`
- `test_coder_cron_spawn_job_helper_emitted`
- `test_coder_cron_tofu_plan_units_emitted`
- `test_cron_tofu_plan_script_present_and_executable`
- `test_cron_tofu_plan_script_passes_shellcheck`
- `test_mise_toml_pins_opentofu`

Plus a passing test fix: scoped the global ADR 0007 `|| true` ban
to the Coder install block only — `|| true` is a legitimate idiom
in trap cleanup handlers.

### Docs

- `runbook.md` — "TF_ENCRYPTION passphrase for cron" + "Nightly
  tofu plan cron" sections.
- `architecture.md` — two new rows in the on-VM cron table.
- `scripts/README.md` — new entry for `cron-tofu-plan.sh`.

## Operator-side prerequisites (one-time, post-apply)

1. Bake the dev container image (`mise.toml` was bumped) + push

2. Upload TF_ENCRYPTION passphrase to Secret Manager:

   ```

3. Upload Coder admin token (from #72).

author: stultus
body:
## Summary
Three changes to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

1. **Cross-platform Rust matrix.** Run `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy`, and `cargo test --lib` on `ubuntu-22.04`, `macos-latest`, and `windows-latest` instead of Linux only. Catches platform-specific Rust breakage at PR time instead of at tag time.
2. **End-to-end build verification.** New `build` job runs `cargo tauri build --debug` on Linux after `rust` and `frontend` pass — verifies the full frontend → cargo → tauri-cli pipeline actually produces a bundle. Static checks alone don't guarantee the app builds.
3. **fmt + lint gates.** Added `cargo fmt --check` (Rust side) and `npm run lint` (= `prettier --check . && eslint .`, per `package.json`) to the frontend job.

Also added: workflow-level `permissions: contents: read` (least-privilege) and `timeout-minutes` on every job (avoid runaway runs eating action minutes).

## Heads-up
If `cargo fmt` or `npm run lint` finds existing drift, this PR will fail its own CI on those checks. Fix is to run `cargo fmt --all` (in `src-tauri/`) and `npm run format` locally, commit the fixups onto this branch, and push.

## Why
Repo hygiene: existing CI was Linux-only and didn't gate on formatter / lint / full-build. Cross-platform breakage was being caught at release time instead of PR time.

## Summary
- Add `charts/ygg-gateway` Helm chart for the Yggdrasil redemption gateway (Bun/Hono HTTP service from the Ragnarok Breaker workspace). Resources: Deployment + ClusterIP Service (port 8787) + Gateway API HTTPRoute (Traefik) + ExternalSecret/SecretStore wired to AWS SecretsManager (`us-east-2`).
- Add staging overlay `9c-internal/ygg-gateway-staging/` (`ygg-gateway-staging.9c.gg`, 1 replica, secret key `ygg-gateway/staging`).
- Add production overlay `9c-main/ygg-gateway-production/` (`ygg-gateway.9c.gg`, 2 replicas, secret key `ygg-gateway/production`).
- Wire `scripts/bump-modules/ygg.sh` so `scripts/bump-image.sh ygg <hash>` works going forward.
- Initial image pinned to `git-015c233d8a48c63292e6e565f5ea9639bec8f721`, repo `planetariumhq/ragnarok-breaker-ygg-gateway`.

Pattern mirrors `charts/ragnarok-breaker` with one deviation: an `HTTPRoute` is added because YGG marketplace + YGG Quest call this service from **outside** the cluster (unlike `ragnarok-breaker`'s `gs-gateway` which is ClusterIP-only). TLS is handled by the existing cert-manager `*.9c.gg` wildcard already listed in both clusters' `certManager.dnsNames`.

## Pre-flight (before sync)
1. Populate AWS SecretsManager (`us-east-2`) with keys `ygg-gateway/staging` and `ygg-gateway/production`. Required env vars: `YGG_API_KEY`, `YGG_API_SECRET`, `YGG_QUEST_API_KEY`, `YGG_QUEST_BASE_URL`, `AGENT8_ACCOUNT`, `AGENT8_VERSE`, `V8_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `V8_ENV`. (All eight are required at boot — `server.ts` exits if any are missing.)
2. Ensure the `planetariumhq/ragnarok-breaker-ygg-gateway:git-015c233d8a48c63292e6e565f5ea9639bec8f721` image exists on Docker Hub.
3. After merge, register both ArgoCD apps manually (per `GUIDE.md`):
   ```
   kubectl apply -f 9c-internal/ygg-gateway-staging/application.yaml
   kubectl apply -f 9c-main/ygg-gateway-production/application.yaml
   ```

## Test plan
- [ ] `helm lint charts/ygg-gateway` passes (verified locally).
- [ ] `helm template` renders cleanly for both overlays (verified locally).
- [ ] After ArgoCD sync, pods are 1/1 Running; logs show `[ygg-gateway] listening on :8787`.
- [ ] `kubectl -n ygg-gateway-staging get externalsecret ygg-gateway-env` shows `Ready=True`.
- [ ] In-cluster `wget -qO- http://ygg-gateway:8787/healthz` returns `{"status":"ok","v8":true}`.
- [ ] External `curl https://ygg-gateway-staging.9c.gg/healthz` returns 200 with valid TLS.
- [ ] HMAC-signed smoke test against `/get-points-by-address` from outside returns 200.

author: susumutomita
body:
## Summary

「LLM ループが無いと作品として弱い」「mainnet 暴走は絶対防ぎたい」「ブラウザ単体でローカル Claude Code とやり取りしたい」の 3 点を満たす最小構成。デプロイ側に LLM コストはゼロ、Vercel 静的ホスティングのまま動く。

## Architecture (案 A: file/clipboard handoff, no backend)

```
[Browser]                          [Local Claude Code]
buildAgentLoopInput()              /agent-loop slash command
 → clipboard / download                 ↓
                                   read AGENT.md (constitution)
                                   read input JSON
                                   decide ONE PaperTradeAction
                                   write AgentLoopTrace JSON
 ← clipboard paste                      ↓
parseAgentLoopTrace()
validateActionAgainstBudget()
 → "Approve & Sign on Testnet" (MetaMask 経由 / executeFirstSwap)
```

「LLM が考える / ユーザーが署名する / 最大 0.0001 ETH しか動かない」の 3 安全条件を **構造で担保**。

## Layers

### 1. JSON contract (`packages/shared/src/agent-loop.ts`)

- `AgentLoopInput` (sessionId / archetype / playLog / forgeProof / **budget**)
- `AgentLoopTrace` (thought / plan / action / observation / rationale / generatedAt / generatedBy)
- `PaperTradeAction` (`swap` | `hold` | `rebalance` discriminated union)
- `AgentLoopBudget` (maxSwapEth / allowedActions / allowedChainIds)
- `parseAgentLoopTrace` / `safeParseAgentLoopTrace` / `buildAgentLoopInput`
- `compareEthDecimalStrings` — 浮動小数点誤差を避けた decimal 比較
- `validateActionAgainstBudget` — UI が「Approve & Sign」を enable する前の最後の砦

### 2. Slash command (`.claude/commands/agent-loop.md`)

- `AGENT.md` を憲法として読む
- clipboard から input JSON 取得
- 1 手の paper trade を archetype heuristic (defensive/balanced/aggressive/swarm) で決定
- trace JSON を chat 出力 + clipboard にコピー
- **HARD constraint**: budget を超える action は出さない、超えそうなら `hold` を返す
- **HARD constraint**: signing は要求しない、CLI で送らない（browser MetaMask に戻す）

### 3. UI (`packages/frontend/src/components/AgentLoopPanel.tsx`)

- 「📋 Copy input JSON」/「⬇️ Download」で input を export
- 「Paste trace JSON here」textarea + 「Validate」ボタン
- thought / plan / action timeline を描画
- **budget verdict を緑 / 赤で明示**
- `canSign = trace 有効 && budget ok && sessionId 一致` のときだけ「Approve & Sign on Testnet (≤ 0.0001 ETH)」を enable
- swap kind は既存 `handleFirstSwap` (executeFirstSwap = `0.0001 ETH` Sepolia 固定) に流す。hold kind なら署名不要

### 4. Budget envelope (`AGENT.md` 末尾セクション)

- `0.0001 ETH` per action — `executeFirstSwap` の hardcode に揃える
- `allowedActions = [swap, hold]` — rebalance は demo 範囲外
- `allowedChainIds = [Sepolia 11155111, 0G Galileo 16602]` — `SUPPORTED_TESTNET_CHAIN_IDS` のミラー
- agent は envelope を弱めない、超えそうなら `hold` を返す
- agent は秘密鍵を要求しない、CLI で署名しない

## Test plan

- [x] `bun scripts/architecture-harness.ts --staged --fail-on=error` — 違反 0 件
- [x] `bun run lint` (biome) — クリーン (59 files)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — shared / frontend 共に exit 0
- [x] `bun run test` — shared **51 pass (+20 新規)** / frontend 20 pass・1 skip・0 fail
- [x] `bun run build` — shared / frontend 共に成功
- [ ] ローカル dev で 1 サイクル目視: ゲーム完走 → AGENT_LOOP セクションで input copy → ターミナルで `claude /agent-loop` → trace を貼り戻し → thought/plan/action 表示 → 「Approve & Sign」で MetaMask 起動
- [ ] わざと壊した JSON を貼って赤バナーが出ることを確認 (sessionId mismatch / 未知 action.kind / amount=1.0 で budget 超過)
- [ ] hold を返した trace では「Hold (no signature needed)」表記になり MetaMask が起動しないことを確認

## What this PR does NOT do (意図的に out of scope)

- Claude Code 以外の runtime (Hermes など) サポート — 同じ JSON contract で後から足せる
- 連続サイクル — 今は 1 ハンドオフ = 1 trace の片道。ループしたければユーザーが繰り返すだけ
- 自動 clipboard reading — ブラウザ制約上、paste は人間の操作が必要
- 実 swap path の差し替え — agent action は既存 `executeFirstSwap` に流すだけ。amount は依然 hardcode 0.0001 ETH（agent が言ってきた値はあくまで意図表示で、実 tx の量は変わらない）

author: jlopezlira
body:
## Summary

- `bin/prjct` self-heals `~/.claude/skills/prjct/SKILL.md` and `~/.codex/skills/prjct/SKILL.md` on every CLI invocation (mtime-based).
- The baseline `templates/skills/prjct/SKILL.md` is **build-generated** from `core/services/skill-generator/prjct-skill-body.ts` — single source of truth shared with `prjct sync`.

## Why

**Discovery problem.** The prjct skill only landed on a machine if the user ran `prjct start`. `postinstall` is unreliable (`--ignore-scripts`, corporate policies, npm quirks — `scripts/postinstall.js` itself comments on this). Net result: new users open Claude Code in a fresh repo and **Claude has no idea prjct exists** — no skill, no verb intent map, no routing.

**Update problem.** Even when installed, `npm i -g @prjct/cli@<new>` left the OLD skill in place. New instructions in the bundled SKILL.md never reached Claude until the user re-ran the wizard manually.

**SSOT.** A naive fix (hand-write `templates/skills/prjct/SKILL.md`) would create a second source for the skill content alongside `prjct-skill-body.ts` (used by `prjct sync`). The two would drift the moment one was edited.

## How

**Self-heal:** `bin/prjct` already self-installs the statusline using the same `-nt` mtime pattern. This PR adds the prjct skill to that loop. Cold install: dest missing → write. Up-to-date: two stats, no write. Update (`@latest` published): bundled template has fresher mtime → overwrite.

**SSOT:** `prjct-skill-body.ts` exports `PRJCT_SKILL_DESCRIPTION`, `PRJCT_SKILL_ALLOWED_TOOLS`, `buildPrjctSkill(ctx)`, and `emptySkillContext()`. `scripts/generate-skill-template.ts` (bun-runnable) calls `buildPrjctSkill(emptySkillContext())` and writes `templates/skills/prjct/SKILL.md`. `scripts/build.js` invokes it before bundling. `formatProjectHeader` handles empty `projectName` with baseline messaging (uninitialized cwd). `skill-generator.ts` consumes the same exported constants instead of duplicating inline. The generated template is `.gitignore`d (build artifact); `prepublishOnly` ensures it ships in the npm tarball.

## Test plan

- [x] Cold install in isolated `$HOME`: both `~/.claude/skills/prjct/SKILL.md` and `~/.codex/skills/prjct/SKILL.md` created.
- [x] No-op: re-invoking with up-to-date skill leaves mtime unchanged.
- [x] Update: `touch templates/skills/prjct/SKILL.md` → next CLI call refreshes the dest.
- [x] `npm run build` regenerates the template from the TS SSOT (25 KB, 378 lines).
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes.
- [x] `npm run lint` / biome check passes.
- [x] `bun test core/__tests__/services/skill-generator.test.ts` — 31/31 pass.
- [x] lefthook pre-commit (biome check + typecheck) passes.

## Out of scope

- Publishing as a Claude Code plugin marketplace entry (separate PR — covers users who never run `prjct` at all).

author: humancto
body:
## Summary

Implements ROADMAP item L839: per-key revision tree (`KeyHistory`).

Mirrors etcd `keyIndex` (`server/mvcc/key_index.go` at v3.5.16) — append-only stack of generations, each a contiguous run of revisions from one creation to (optionally) one tombstone. Operations: `put`, `tombstone`, `get`, `since`, `since_into`, `compact`, `keep`, `restore`.

The container (sharded `HashMap<Bytes, KeyHistory>`) is intentionally L840 — this PR is the per-key data type only.

### Design choices

- **Returns `KeyHistoryError` instead of panicking.** Etcd panics on invariant violations (non-monotonic put, tombstone-on-empty); workspace `clippy::panic` lint forbids this. Sole legitimate caller (Raft apply) is positioned to escalate.
- **`compact` returns `bool`** so L840's container can drop empties from its map without a separate `is_empty()` round-trip.
- **`keep` vs `compact` divergence** on the trailing tombstone of a non-final generation matches etcd `key_index.go:240-249` (hash-stability requirement). Tested explicitly in `compact_vs_keep_diverge_on_trailing_tombstone`.
- **`since_into<E: Extend<Revision>>`** amortizes allocation for the L859 watch hub. `since` is the convenience wrapper.
- **`compact<S: BuildHasher>` / `keep<S: BuildHasher>`** are hasher-generic so L850's compactor can pass an `FxHashSet` without forcing it through the API.
- **`restore` invariant exception** (single non-empty generation, no trailing empty) is documented; a subsequent `tombstone` works correctly because `tombstone` itself appends the trailing-empty generation.
- **`#[non_exhaustive]`** on `KeyHistoryError` and `RestoreInvalidReason` so future variants are non-breaking.
- **`TODO(L859)`** markers for keysGauge instrumentation at `put`/`tombstone`/`restore`.

### Tests

- 38 unit tests covering: lifecycle (etcd doc-comment fixture), monotonicity, tombstone semantics, get-at-various-revs (including post-tombstone gap and pre-creation), since cross-generation walk + dedup-by-main, since-treats-arg-as-(main,0), compact at all etcd doc cases (2/4/5/6), keep-does-not-mutate, compact-vs-keep divergence, restore validation paths.
- 5 proptest cases (modified monotonicity, compact idempotence, get-after-put, since invariants, keep purity).
- 1 doctest on the module rustdoc lifecycle.

### Verification

- `cargo build -p mango-mvcc --locked`
- `cargo build -p mango-mvcc --features proptest --locked`
- `cargo test -p mango-mvcc --lib --locked` — 70 passed
- `cargo test -p mango-mvcc --features proptest --locked` — 71 passed (2 suites)
- `cargo test --doc -p mango-mvcc --locked` — 1 passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test --workspace --locked` — 371 passed, 8 ignored

## Test plan

- [x] All unit tests pass
- [x] All proptests pass with feature flag
- [x] Module-level doctest passes
- [x] Workspace clippy clean (including `--features proptest`)
- [x] Full workspace test suite passes

author: beveradb
body:
## Summary
- In the Re-sync Existing Lyrics modal, tap mode (spacebar press <200ms) optimistically sets `currentWord.end_time = start + 500ms`. When the next word is tapped within 500ms, `handleKeyDown`'s "fix prev word" branch was gated on `prevWord.end_time === null` and never fired, leaving the previous word claiming to last 500ms past where the next word started.
- Effect: for any song with words sung in rapid succession (median sustained-singing tempo), the karaoke video lights up 2–3 words simultaneously throughout. Surfaced in production on a real client job where 80% of consecutive word pairs overlapped (median 283ms).
- Fix: in `handleKeyDown` and `handleTapStart`, always trim `prevWord.end_time` when it overshoots `currentTime - 5ms`, regardless of whether it was set by the optimistic placeholder. Hold-mode behavior preserved (null end_time still gets the 500ms-or-snap-to-now treatment for huge gaps).

## Test plan
- [x] New regression test `LyricsSynchronizer.tapOverlap.test.tsx` — drives the synchronizer through three rapid taps (200ms apart) and asserts no consecutive word overlaps. Fails on `main`, passes with the fix.
- [x] `npm run test:unit` — 889/889 pass
- [ ] Manual verification on prod after deploy: re-sync a few words quickly in the modal, click Apply, generate preview, confirm word durations are no longer all 500ms and that highlight transitions cleanly word-to-word.

author: sinameraji
body:
Implements the `/remote` feature for running autonomous coding tasks on Cloudflare infrastructure.

## What it does
Type `/remote <prompt>` in the kimiflare TUI and it handles everything automatically:
1. **Auto-deploys** the Cloudflare Worker + container if not already deployed (live progress in chat)
2. **Auto-authenticates** with GitHub via OAuth device flow if needed (shows URL + code in chat)
3. **Starts a remote session** — the agent runs in a Cloudflare Sandbox while your laptop is off
4. **Streams progress** back to your TUI in real-time
5. **Opens a PR** on GitHub when done

## Architecture
- **Orchestrator Worker** (`remote/worker/`) — Durable Objects, SSE streaming, LLM relay, GitHub PR creation
- **Headless Agent** (`remote/agent/`) — Runs in Sandbox, auto-approves tools, commits to Artifacts
- **Local CLI/TUI integration** — `/remote` slash command, `kimiflare remote list|status|cancel`, `kimiflare auth github`
- **Deploy wizard** — `kimiflare remote deploy` for shell-based deployment
- **TUI deploy/auth** — generator-based flows that yield chat-friendly progress messages

## Quick start

```bash
# One-time prerequisites
wrangler login
docker login ghcr.io -u USERNAME -p GITHUB_TOKEN
export CF_API_TOKEN=your_cloudflare_token

# Then just use it
kimiflare
/remote "Refactor the auth module"
```

That's it. Deploy, auth, session start, and progress streaming all happen automatically.

## Files added
- `remote/worker/` — Cloudflare Worker (Durable Objects, SSE, LLM relay, GitHub API)
- `remote/agent/` — Headless agent bundle (auto-approve, progress reporter, git ops)
- `src/remote/` — Local integration (CLI commands, session store, worker client, TUI deploy/auth)
- `src/auth/github.ts` — GitHub OAuth device flow
- `docs/remote-architecture.md` — Full architecture doc
- `docs/remote-local-testing.md` — Local testing guide

See `docs/remote-architecture.md` for full details.

body: ## Why Direct response to: *"review to make sure the price line is active enough to be engaging to user and if the btc price needs decimal points to match price movement."* The price felt static because the headline used **whole dollars** while Coinbase ticks at **$0.01** — most ticks were invisible. Decimals + a tick-flash + a tone-aware fill close that gap. ## What **Decimals where they matter** - Headline price → `$67,432.41` (was `$67,432`). - Tooltip + reference-line labels → cents. - Y-axis tick labels stay whole-dollar (56px gutter constraint). **Tick-flash on the price tag** - Every appreciable tick (≥ $0.005) key-bumps the tag and runs a 480ms green/red wash before settling to neutral. - Sub-half-cent jitter is treated as flat so it's not a strobe. - `aria-live=polite` on the tag — screen-readers announce material moves without spam. **Tone-aware visuals** - Area gradient + line stroke now follow the 24h change (green up, red down). - Smoothed area type to `monotone`. - New live-dot next to `BTC · USD` with a pulsing halo when the WS feed is healthy. - 24h change subtitle (`▲ $X.XX (Y.YY%)`) under the title. ## Tests / checks - 6 focused (`PriceChart.format.test.ts`): cents formatter, axis whole-dollar formatter, tick-tone for up/down/jitter/first-tick. - `tsc --noEmit` clean. - Full suite: **28/28** pass. ## Scope `PriceChart.tsx` only (+ test). ## Next PR 6/8: live MTM in the sell-back surface (already partially in PR3; this hardens the math).

body:
## Summary

Earlier wording said "both pipelines run the same `IndexYearRebuildService.php` algorithm" / "algorithm-level agreement confirmed" / "not bugs".  That was overstating the case.

**Reality:**
- cbdb-online-main-server's weekly SQLite snapshot:
  - `c_index_year` ← PHP `IndexYearRebuildService.php`
  - `c_index_addr_id` ← PHP `IndexAddressRebuildService.php`
  - (both at <https://github.com/cbdb-project/cbdb-online-main-server>)
- User MDB's same two fields: produced by Access `frmBaseMaintenance` VBA maintenance buttons.
- The PHP services are **intended to mirror** the VBA but they are **independent implementations** (likely ported, not the same code).

Per-row differences can come from at least four sources, and a diff alone doesn't tell us which:
1. source-data snapshot drift
2. algorithm / porting divergence between PHP and VBA
3. priority / tie-break differences
4. null / default handling differences

We have **NOT** classified the steady ~575 / 657 246 derived-field diffs we currently observe.  The drift appendix's example bucket is **13 rows total** (3 buckets, both-bucket empty) — illustrative of the *shapes* of disagreement, not statistically representative.  We can't categorically say "this is data drift" without per-row walking.  The thresholds in `test_index_year_xcheck.py` (0.5 % / 0.1 %) are coarse guards against a sudden wholesale jump.

## Files updated

- **AGENTS.md** "NOT a bug" section retitled to "Index-year cross-check: ... (classification still open)" and rewritten — drops "SAME algorithm" claim, lists the four divergence sources, names both PHP services + the GitHub repo, says explicitly that the steady ~575 are not classified.
- **README.md** roadmap row 12 + 中文 summary line: same rewrite. Names both PHP services, calls out independent implementations, warns against opening or closing CBDB issues based on individual diffs.
- **reports/generate_report.py** drift appendix (both en + zh, both docx + md generators):
  - Title: "(not bugs)" → "(differences need per-row classification before being filed as bugs)"
  - Intro paragraph rewritten on the same independent-implementations + four-sources framing, with explicit limitation note that the 13-row sample is illustrative not statistically representative.
- All four `reports/CBDB_Issues_Report_*.{md,docx}` regenerated.

No code changes; no test changes (`test_index_year_xcheck.py`'s existing docstring already reads honestly: "potentially-different rules").

## What this locks

Two FOREVER-STABLE invariants for the pty delta-segmentation + snapshot cadence:

1. **Single source file** — all cadence constants live in exactly one file: `packages/daemon/src/pty/segmentation.ts`.
   - `SEGMENTATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 16` (ch06 §3)
   - `SEGMENTATION_BYTE_CAP = 16384` (16 KiB — ch06 §3)
   - `K_TIME_MS = 30_000` (ch06 §4)
   - `M_DELTAS = 256` (ch06 §4)
   - `B_BYTES = 1_048_576` (1 MiB — ch06 §4)

   The numeric literals (and the named identifiers) MUST NOT appear elsewhere under `packages/daemon/src/`. Imports of the canonical module are exempt — that is the legal way to reference the constants.

2. **No per-subscriber knobs** — the cadence is per-session, broadcast to N subscribers as identical byte ranges (ch06 §3 "Segmentation cadence is per-session"). The lock-spec asserts:
   - `AttachRequest` proto has no `cadence` / `segmentation` / `snapshot_*` / `timeout_ms` / `byte_cap` / `chunk_*` field

`packages/daemon/src/pty/segmentation.ts` is created later by Task #43 (T4.10 delta segmenter) and Task #50 (T4.9 snapshot cadence). The **per-subscriber-knob ban runs unconditionally** so even pre-#43/#50 PRs cannot smuggle in a subscriber-side override.

When #43 / #50 ship the canonical file, the 3 currently-skipped specs activate automatically.

The 2 passing tests are the unconditional per-subscriber-knob bans (proto + signature scan over current `packages/daemon/src/`); the 3 skipped tests gate on `segmentation.ts` and will auto-activate when #43 / #50 land.

💡 **What:** Extracted array spreading in `isLandmarkCollected` into a memoized `allLandmarks` array using `useMemo` in `src/App.tsx`. Updated `FeedSystem` to use this memoized array.

🎯 **Why:** `isLandmarkCollected` is called frequently during render (especially in `CameraView` responding to 60fps `deviceorientation` events). body:
## Summary

Adds `notes/SLO_CATALOG_2026-05-03.md` as the single source-of-truth SLO catalog for the Juniper observability stack.

- Closes R5 entry plan **Q1** *(user-facing primary + internal-supporting)* and **Q3** *(single juniper-deploy doc location)*.
- Defines **5 user-facing release-blocking SLIs** (canopy dashboard availability/render-latency, cascor train-job success / train-step p95, data-service POST availability) — each with concrete PromQL, SLO target, and Multi-Window Multi-Burn-Rate (MWMBR) thresholds at 14.4× / 6× / 3× / 1× per R5 entry plan Q7 (c).
- Defines **8 internal-supporting SLIs** (worker heartbeat freshness, queue depth, broadcast / command-handler latency, data-client latency / error rate, dataset POST cache-hit ratio, HTTP 5xx per service) — graphed but not paged.
- Each SLO target is marked **"initial — to revisit after 30-day soak"**; reasoning for chosen targets (most are 99.5% / p95 < 500ms-style boundaries) is documented inline so the next iteration can adjust with context.
- Cross-links to: R5 entry plan in juniper-ml; R4.1 per-service histogram-rationale docs in cascor / canopy / data; existing `notes/METRICS_AUTH_RATIONALE.md` (Q5 closure); `prometheus/prometheus.yml` and the 4 Grafana dashboards.

## Forward-references

- **R5.4** (`prometheus/alert_rules.yml`) — burn-rate alert rules derive from §3 of this catalog. Each alert will cite a section number in its annotation block.
- **R5.3** (Grafana dashboards) — surface the 5 user-facing SLIs as the headline tile on `juniper-overview.json` and as top-row panels on each per-service dashboard.

## Honest about gaps

Three pre-condition gaps are explicitly flagged in §6:

1. **§3.3 (train-job success)** needs a `juniper_cascor_training_sessions_completed_total{outcome}` counter that does not yet exist in cascor. R5.4 ships the alert in log-only severity until a small cascor PR lands.
2. **§3.4 (train-step p95)** needs a `juniper_cascor_training_step_duration_seconds` histogram that does not yet exist. Same recommendation pattern.
3. **§4.1 / §4.2 (worker heartbeat freshness, queue depth)** are blocked by the **R4.4 worker → Prometheus bridge gap** — heartbeat fields are exposed only on JSON `/v1/workers`, not as Prometheus collectors. Recommendation is for cascor to ship bridge gauges directly (preferred) rather than juniper-deploy running a polling exporter.

For the 2 remaining "tentative pending R5.1" cascor histograms (`inference_duration_seconds`, `resume_replayed_events`) that R5.1b did not re-bucket, the catalog recommends **Option A — flip HELP-string markers without re-bucketing** rather than scheduling R5.1c. Both histograms are internal-supporting and not referenced by any catalog SLI; a re-bucket without a driving SLI would be premature.

## Out of scope

- `prometheus/alert_rules.yml` — R5.4 PR derives burn-rate alerts from this catalog.
- `grafana/provisioning/dashboards/*.json` — R5.3 PR refreshes panels.
- New histogram buckets / new metrics — handled in juniper-cascor (Q1 / Q2 / Q3 follow-up PRs).

## Test plan

- [x] `pre-commit run --files notes/SLO_CATALOG_2026-05-03.md` passes (markdownlint excludes `notes/`; trailing-whitespace + EOF hooks pass).
- [x] All cross-repo references annotated *(in the `<repo>` repo, not this one)* per the project convention used in `notes/METRICS_AUTH_RATIONALE.md`.
- [x] Every PromQL expression uses metric names verified against the upstream `observability.py` files in juniper-canopy, juniper-cascor, juniper-data (post `git fetch`).
- [ ] Reviewer sanity-check: are the §3 SLO targets defensible as initial values, given §2.6 caveat?
- [ ] Reviewer sanity-check: are the §6 pre-condition-gap recommendations the right next sub-tracks (R5.5a / R5.5b)?

## Closes

- METRICS-MON R5 entry plan **Q1** (user-facing primary + internal-supporting)
- METRICS-MON R5 entry plan **Q3** (catalog location: single juniper-deploy doc)

### Motivation

- Reduce latency for payload-anchored requests by adapting the debounce window based on whether a payload is expected and whether payload items are present.
- Avoid unnecessary generation pauses caused by ephemeral typing events and simplify the pause logic to use sent messages as the source of truth.
- Improve observability of batch timing and generation by adding targeted logging around wait selection and generation start.

### Description

- Introduce new configuration constants `ADAPTIVE_PAYLOAD_WAIT_NO_ITEMS_SECONDS`, `ADAPTIVE_PAYLOAD_WAIT_WITH_ITEMS_SECONDS`, `ADAPTIVE_PAYLOAD_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS`, and `ADAPTIVE_PAYLOAD_SEALED_BONUS_SECONDS` to control adaptive wait behavior.
- Add `_adaptive_batch_wait_seconds(...)` to compute an adaptive `selected_wait_seconds` and metadata based on collapsed batch fragments, detected request payload expectation, pending intent, and elapsed time, and adjust `_batch_max_wait_seconds(...)` to accept an optional selected wait.
- Replace typing-based pause logic in `_should_pause_for_recent_typing` to always return `False` (treating typing as diagnostic only) and simplify handling by emitting a `typing_signal_ignored` event instead of pausing generation.
- Update `_schedule_flush` to call `_adaptive_batch_wait_seconds`, compute `selected_wait_seconds` and a dynamic deadline, and to sleep only for the needed interval; update `_flush_channel_buffer` to log generation timing and respect the adaptive wait selection when deciding to flush.

author: matthewmckee4
body:
## Summary

Closes #707. Adds support for the canonical `# pragma: no cover` directive when computing executable lines for coverage. Pragmas are extracted from the comment tokens of a parsed module and the AST visitor consults them when entering a node: a pragma on a simple statement excludes that one line; a pragma on the head of a compound statement (`def`, `class`, `if`, `for`, `with`, `try`, `match`, an `elif`/`else` clause, an `except` handler, or a `match` case) skips the head and stops the walk, dropping the entire body. Matching is case-insensitive and only applies to real comment tokens, so `# pragma: no cover` inside a string literal is left alone.

```python
def expensive_unreachable():  # pragma: no cover
    return _slow_path()

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover
    from typing import Self
```

Both blocks above are now excluded from `Stmts`, matching coverage.py's behaviour.

body:
## Summary
Completely redesigned the launcher control section with a new two-column layout featuring a dedicated hardware status panel for the ESP32-S3 and an enhanced control interface. Added mode switching simulation between Smart (ESP32 PWM control) and Manual (hardware potentiometer) modes with proper state management and visual feedback.

## Key Changes

### UI/Layout Redesign
- Replaced single-column control layout with a two-column `hardware-grid` (0.95fr / 1.05fr split)
- Left column: New "Status Hardware (ESP32-S3)" card displaying GPIO pins, relay states, and PSU readouts
- Right column: Refactored "Kontrol Launcher" card with improved motor controls and toggles
- Added comprehensive CSS styling for hardware status components (mode badges, relay blocks, PSU items, etc.)

### Hardware Status Panel
- Mode badge (clickable) showing Smart/Manual state with visual indicators
- GPIO pin tags for Mode Switch (GPIO 17) and Master Enable (GPIO 42)
- Three relay blocks (A, B, C) with pin assignments and state indicators
- PSU readout section showing 24V, 5V logic, and total current
- Dynamic relay state updates reflecting mode changes

### Control Interface Enhancements
- Renamed motor controls: "Motor Pelontar A/B" and "Motor Feeder C" with PWM GPIO assignments
- Added "Master EN" and "Sync A=B" toggle buttons in card header
- Motor A/B synchronization: when Sync A=B is enabled, moving one slider updates the other
- Servo Pan control marked as "FUTURE" (disabled) with visual tag
- Manual mode overlay that appears when hardware is in manual bypass mode

### Mode Switching Logic
- Implemented `transitionMode()` function with proper sequencing:
  1. Kill PWM outputs (anti-spike protection)
  2. Wait 120ms
  3. Flip relay states
  4. Wait 120ms
  5. Restore PWM display if returning to Smart mode
- Mode badge click toggles between Smart and Manual modes
- Status indicator updates to reflect current mode ("Smart Mode" vs "Manual Bypass")

### State Management
- New `hwState` object tracking: mode, masterEnable, syncAB, motor values, and transition state
- Motor slider listeners with sync logic for A/B pair
- Master Enable checkbox controls relay state display
- PSU current simulation that fluctuates based on combined motor duty cycle

### Responsive Design
- Added media query breakpoints for hardware-grid (1fr on tablets, 1fr on mobile)
- Relay grid remains 3-column on tablets, collapses to 1-column on mobile
- PSU row collapses to 1-column on mobile

### Visual Enhancements
- Color-coded mode badges (green for Smart, orange for Manual)
- Relay blocks with conditional styling (green border/shadow when on, orange when off)
- Monospace font for technical values (pins, voltages, states)
- Manual overlay with backdrop blur and centered messaging
- Smooth transitions and hover effects throughout

## Implementation Details
- Mode switching includes 120ms delays between PWM kill and relay flip to prevent electrical spikes
- Sync A=B feature re-synchronizes B to A's value when re-enabled
- PSU current updates every 1 second with realistic noise simulation
- Manual overlay prevents interaction with sliders when in manual mode via CSS filter and pointer-events
- All hardware state changes are reflected in both the status panel and control interface

This PR integrates [CodSpeed](https://codspeed.io) for continuous performance testing of the dependi-lsp benchmarks.

## Changes

**Benchmark dependency** (`dependi-lsp/Cargo.toml`):
- Replaced `criterion` (v0.8.2) with `codspeed-criterion-compat` (v4.6.0), aliased as `criterion`. This is a drop-in compatibility layer that enables CodSpeed's CPU simulation instrument while keeping the existing benchmark code and `cargo bench` workflow fully functional.

**CI workflow** (`.github/workflows/codspeed.yml`):
- New GitHub Actions workflow that builds and runs the existing 49 benchmarks through CodSpeed on every push to `main`, on pull requests, and on manual dispatch (used by CodSpeed for backtesting).
- Uses OIDC authentication (`id-token: write`) for tokenless uploads.
- Uses `simulation` mode for deterministic, hardware-agnostic measurements.

**README badge**:
- Added a CodSpeed performance badge alongside the existing project badges.

## Benchmarks covered

All existing benchmark suites are measured:
- **Parsers** -- Cargo.toml, package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod, composer.json, .csproj, pubspec.yaml, Gemfile (at 10/50/100 dependency scales)
- **Cache** -- Memory and SQLite get-hit, get-miss, insert operations
- **Version utils** -- Prerelease detection across 7 ecosystems
- **VersionInfo** -- Yanked version lookups

## Note on runners

This repository is owned by a personal GitHub account, so CodSpeed's dedicated `codspeed-macro` runners are not available. The workflow uses standard `ubuntu-latest` runners instead. This means performance variance will be higher than with bare-metal macro runners. If consistent, low-noise measurements become important, consider moving the repository to a GitHub organization. See the [CodSpeed walltime docs](https://codspeed.io/docs/instruments/walltime#usage-on-personal-github-accounts) for details.

## Next steps

1. Merge this PR -- CodSpeed will automatically start tracking performance on the `main` branch.
2. Open a follow-up PR to see performance comparison reports inline.
3. Optionally enable [performance checks](https://codspeed.io/docs/features/performance-checks) to gate PRs on regression thresholds.

PR này ship FOUNDATION (on-disk format + writer + summary script). Wiring vào ``ChatOrchestrator.process(record=True)`` + replay HTML report + CI nightly cron land ở follow-up PR — lock JSONL shape trước.

## Foundation (mới)

### ``app/engine/runtime/eval_recorder.py``

- ``EvalRecord`` Pydantic: ``record_id`` (uuid), ``session_id``, ``org_id``, ``timestamp`` (ISO-8601 UTC), ``request``, ``retrieved_docs``, ``tool_calls``, ``response``, ``sources``, ``metadata``, ``replay_seed``
- ``EvalRecorder.write/read_session/list_sessions``: asyncio.Lock-guarded JSONL append. Layout: ``{base_dir}/{org_id}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{session_id}.jsonl``
- **Path-traversal hardening**: ``org_id`` / ``session_id`` / ``day`` đi qua ``_safe_segment()`` — non-``[A-Za-z0-9._-]`` chars collapse thành underscore, hostile inputs không escape ``base_dir``
- Cross-platform JSONL: ``newline=""`` + literal ``\n`` để Windows không double-translate CRLF làm corrupt JSONL parser
- Skip-malformed-line trên ``read_session`` để 1 bad write không poison cả partition
- ``diff_records()`` helper: token Jaccard similarity + tool-call equality + source overlap + signed latency delta (no LLM judging — Phase 7+)

### ``scripts/eval_summary.py``

- CLI operational tool — spot-check eval JSONL partitions không cần spin up chat stack
- Report: session count, record count, tool calls, sources, response length stats (mean/median/p95), latency stats
- ``--as-json`` mode để CI consume

### Feature flags (default OFF, EXPERIMENTAL tier)

- ``enable_eval_recording: bool = False`` — opt-in per environment
- ``eval_recording_dir: str = "eval_recordings"`` — base directory

## Verification gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| 16 contract test (record shape, JSONL round-trip, partition layout, path-traversal safety, malformed-line tolerance, 4 diff metrics) | ✅ 16/16 pass |
| ``test_feature_tiers`` sau khi register flag mới | ✅ 5/5 pass |
| Wider scope (656 tests, "runtime or eval or feature_tier or messages") | ✅ 655 pass + 1 skipped, 0 fail |
| ``scripts/eval_summary.py`` smoke (handles missing base_dir gracefully) | ✅ exit code 2 với error message |

## Deferred sang follow-up PR

- ``ChatOrchestrator.process(record=True)`` wiring — touch production code path, defer cho fresh PR có deeper testing
- ``scripts/replay_eval.py`` — full replay với HTML diff report (cần ChatOrchestrator integration trước)
- ``.github/workflows/nightly-eval-replay.yml`` cron — cần real traffic data đầu tiên
- Proof-of-concept regression catch — cần chat traffic ghi xuống JSONL
- Storage rotation policy (7d local, monthly archive)

## Out of scope

- Không thay thế ``tests/eval_*`` files hiện tại (complement, không replace)
- Không multi-judge LLM grading (use simple metrics first; Phase 7+)
- Không default ON ở production (opt-in per-org canary)

## Liên quan

- Epic: #207 (KHÔNG ``Closes`` — còn 1 phase + integration follow-up)
- Phase brief: ``.Codex/reports/runtime-migration-briefs/phase-6-eval-harness.md``
- Phase 5a đã merged

author: morganmcg1
body:
## Hypothesis

Your in-flight PR #449 tested log-x coordinate compression applied to **both** surface and volume streams. The advisor follow-up flagged a likely surface↔volume asymmetry: surface points are concentrated near the car body (narrow x range, dense), while volume points span the full domain (wide x range, sparse far-field).

**This experiment isolates the volume stream**: apply log-x **only on volume coordinates**, leaving surface coordinates in raw Cartesian. The motivation:

1. Volume `x` spans a much wider range (free-stream + downstream wake, ~±2 in normalized units) than surface `x` (~±1, vehicle bounds). A single global PE bandwidth can't simultaneously resolve fine near-car wake structure and coarse far-field flow.
2. `log(1 + |x|)·sign(x)` (or `arcsinh(x/scale)`) compresses the wide volume range, giving the volume PE more of its frequency budget to fine near-car structure where the gradient (and pressure variation) is concentrated.
3. Surface points don't need this transform — they're already in a tight range where sincos at our chosen wavelength performs well.

If volume-only log-x improves `volume_pressure` (currently 12.438% test, 2.05× AB-UPT — our second-largest gap after wall_shear_y/z) **without regressing** surface metrics, this is a clean targeted win.

## Instructions

**Code change required.** Add a new flag `--volume-coord-transform <none|signed-log|asinh>` (default `none`) to `target/train.py`. When set to `signed-log` or `asinh`:

1. Locate the volume coordinate processing path. Search `train.py` for where volume points (`vol_pts`, `volume_pos`, or the equivalent) are passed into the encoder/PE — there should be a clear `surface` vs `volume` split in the forward pass.
2. **Apply the transform only to volume coordinates** (NOT surface):
   ```python
   if self.config.volume_coord_transform == "signed-log":
       vol_pts_transformed = torch.sign(vol_pts) * torch.log1p(torch.abs(vol_pts))
   elif self.config.volume_coord_transform == "asinh":
       vol_pts_transformed = torch.asinh(vol_pts)
   else:
       vol_pts_transformed = vol_pts
   # Surface points pass through unchanged
   ```
3. The transform replaces volume coordinates **only as PE encoder input**. If the model also uses raw `vol_pts` for output decoding (e.g. cross-attention queries), keep the original `vol_pts` for those paths. Be explicit in your code about which path gets which.

**Run a 3-arm DDP-4 sweep on a single 4-GPU pod, sequential arms:**

| Arm | `--volume-coord-transform` | rationale |
|---|---|---|
| A | `none` (control) | in-group reference |
| B | `signed-log` | log compression, sign-preserving |
| C | `asinh` | smooth alternative, no sign() discontinuity at zero |

**Common config (Lion SOTA recipe):**

```bash
cd target/
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=4 train.py \
  --agent norman \
  --optimizer lion \
  --lr 1e-4 \
  --weight-decay 1e-4 \
  --clip-grad-norm 0.5 \
  --no-compile-model \
  --batch-size 4 \
  --validation-every 1 \
  --train-surface-points 65536 \
  --eval-surface-points 65536 \
  --train-volume-points 65536 \
  --eval-volume-points 65536 \
  --model-layers 4 \
  --model-hidden-dim 512 \
  --model-heads 8 \
  --model-slices 128 \
  --ema-decay 0.999 \
  --lr-warmup-epochs 1 \
  --seed 42 \
  --wandb-group yi-r31-norman-volume-only-log-x
```

Per-arm: `--volume-coord-transform none` / `signed-log` / `asinh`.

No kill thresholds. Each arm gets the full 6h.

## What to report

Per-arm:
1. Best `val_primary/abupt_axis_mean_rel_l2_pct`, with corresponding test row.
2. **Specifically `volume_pressure_rel_l2_pct`** — that's the targeted channel.
3. **Surface metrics** (`surface_pressure`, `wall_shear`, `wall_shear_y`, `wall_shear_z`) — must NOT regress; if they do, the transform is leaking into surface paths.
4. W&B run IDs.

## Decision rule (advisor side)

- Any arm beats yi merge bar **9.039%** → merge candidate.
- Volume_pressure improves ≥ 0.5pp without surface regression → orthogonal win, merge.
- Surface regresses → bug in path isolation, send back.
- No movement → close; volume_pressure gap is upstream of coordinate representation.

## Baseline

- **Active merge bar:** `val_primary/abupt_axis_mean_rel_l2_pct < 9.039%` (PR #309 thorfinn).
- **Aspirational once PR #490 STRING-sep PE lands:** `< 7.546%`.
- **Volume_pressure target gap:** test 12.438% (PR #311 reference) vs AB-UPT 6.08% — 2.05×, the second-largest channel gap.

## Notes

- Complement to your PR #449 (which tests log-x globally). If #449 wins on surface but loses on volume — or vice-versa — this experiment isolates the cause cleanly. We are deliberately running these in parallel because they are testing different cuts of the same hypothesis space.
- Code change is small (~10 lines). Critical: keep the transform out of the surface path and out of any decoder query paths. Only the volume **PE encoder input** is transformed.
- DDP-4, bs=4, 6h per arm → ~10 epochs. 3 arms × 6h = 18h. Sequential.

# Vercel Speed Insights Installation Report

## Summary
Successfully installed and configured Vercel Speed Insights for the G.W. Hawkins website project.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Package Installation
- Installed `@vercel/speed-insights@2.0.0` via npm
- Added dependency to `package.json`
- Updated `package-lock.json` to lock the version

### 2. Configuration Approach
Since this is a vanilla HTML/JavaScript project without a build system (except for Tailwind CSS watching), I used the CDN-based approach with ES modules:

- Used the unpkg CDN to load the `@vercel/speed-insights` package
- Implemented using ES6 module imports in inline `<script type="module">` tags
- Called `injectSpeedInsights()` function to initialize tracking

### 3. Files Modified
**All HTML files across all language directories (48 total):**
- `index.html` (root)
- German (de/): about, bookshelf, index, legal, news, publishing
- Spanish (es/): about, bookshelf, index, legal, news, publishing

- Italian (it/): about, bookshelf, index, legal, news, publishing

- Traditional Chinese (tc/): about, bookshelf, index, legal, news, publishing

**Configuration files:**

- `package-lock.json` - Updated with new dependency lock
- `.gitignore` - Created to exclude node_modules and other generated files

### 4. Implementation Code
Added the following code snippet after the Tailwind CDN script tag in all HTML files:

```html
<!-- Vercel Speed Insights -->
<script type="module">
  import { injectSpeedInsights } from 'https://unpkg.com/@vercel/speed-insights@2.0.0/dist/index.mjs';
  injectSpeedInsights();
</script>
```

### 5. Technical Decisions

**Why CDN approach?**
- This is a static HTML website without a JavaScript bundler (webpack, rollup, etc.)
- The project uses CDN for other dependencies (Tailwind CSS, Lenis, reCAPTCHA)
- Maintains consistency with existing architecture
- Zero build configuration required
- Faster implementation without adding build complexity

**Why unpkg.com?**
- Reliable CDN that automatically resolves npm packages
- Supports ES modules natively
- Version pinned to 2.0.0 for stability
- Widely used in production environments

### 6. How It Works

1. When a page loads, the browser executes the module script
2. The `injectSpeedInsights()` function is imported from the unpkg CDN
3. The function dynamically injects Vercel's tracking script into the page
4. The tracking script loads from `/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js` (Vercel's CDN)
5. Speed Insights automatically tracks Core Web Vitals and performance metrics
6. Data is sent to Vercel's analytics dashboard (no tracking in development mode)

- ✅ No duplicate installations detected

2. The tracking script will automatically start collecting data
3. View performance metrics in the Vercel Speed Insights dashboard
4. Data will appear after a few days of visitor traffic

body:
## Summary

- **Audit session revival**: When an auditor session dies (crash, rate limit, power loss), the audited task was previously stuck in `pending_audit` forever with no recovery mechanism. The sync reaper now detects dead audit-lane sessions whose tasks are still `pending_audit`, preserves the audit gate state, and flags them for re-spawn. `drainQueue()` Step 1b.5 dedup-checks for existing auditors and enqueues a fresh `universal-auditor` with an 8-minute TTL and full audit prompt. Handles both todo-db and persistent task audits.
- **Session queue DB corruption auto-recovery**: Power loss can corrupt the SQLite WAL, making the entire session queue unusable (`"database disk image is malformed"`). `getDb()` now runs `PRAGMA integrity_check(1)` on open. If corruption is detected, the DB plus `-wal` and `-shm` files are renamed aside as `.corrupt.{timestamp}`, a fresh DB is created, and a `session_queue_db_recovered` audit event is emitted. The session queue is ephemeral — the revival daemon re-discovers running sessions independently.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `reapSyncPass` returns `auditRevivals` array (non-empty when dead audit-lane session exists with task in `pending_audit`)
- [ ] Verify `drainQueue` Step 1b.5 deduplicates against already-queued auditors and only spawns one fresh auditor per task
- [ ] Verify `getDb()` detects a malformed DB, renames it aside, and creates a fresh one without crashing the queue
- [ ] Verify `session_queue_db_recovered` audit event is emitted on DB recovery
- [ ] Confirm existing session-queue tests pass (no regressions)

author: apexbusiness-systems
body:
💡 What: Implemented a granular Zustand selector in `ScreenTimeIndicator.tsx` to return only the active child instead of subscribing to the entire `children` array.
🎯 Why: Because `useParentalStore` uses Immer, updates to ANY child object in the array cause a new array reference to be created. Subscribing to the entire array caused `ScreenTimeIndicator` to re-render unnecessarily on unrelated child updates.
📊 Impact: Prevents full component re-renders when other children properties are modified, reducing unnecessary compute on updates.
🔬 Measurement: Can be verified using React Profiler or by referring to the benchmark in `zustand_children_array_opt.test.tsx` comparing array subscriptions versus granular `.find()` selectors.

author: lpakula
body:
## Summary

Two interrelated timeout bugs were fixed. First, `StepRun.duration_seconds` was counting the entire HITL wait period (e.g. leaving a step unanswered overnight) as agent execution time, causing the very next agent step to immediately trigger a timeout. The fix makes `duration_seconds` use `awaiting_user_at` as the end timestamp when set, so only real agent execution time is counted. Second, when a run timed out the daemon set `run.outcome` but never set `run.completed_at`, then launched a `__post_run__` step. On the next tick the run was still in the active list, the timeout check fired again, and another `__post_run__` step was created — an infinite loop that never completed. The fix calls `mark_completed()` on all error paths before launching the post-run step, and adds an explicit guard to skip `__post_run__` steps in timeout/max_spend checks.

## Changes

```
llmflows/db/models.py          StepRun.duration_seconds uses awaiting_user_at as end time for HITL steps
llmflows/services/daemon.py    Timeout/max_spend checks skip __post_run__ steps; all error paths call
                               mark_completed() before launching post-run step
tests/test_models.py           4 new tests: agent step duration, HITL duration exclusion,
                               HITL still-awaiting, FlowRun duration aggregation
tests/test_services.py         3 new tests: timeout marks run completed, timeout skips post-run steps,
                               max_spend skips post-run steps
```

## Testing

209 tests pass (including 7 new tests covering both bugs):

body:
## Summary

Closes the today-leak hole at the type boundary for derived memory writes. Phase 1A of a multi-phase fix targeting 15 derived-write surfaces; this PR migrates the two episodic-summary builders (handler + scheduler).

## Why

LoCoMo eval cat-2 surfaces predictions like "2026-05-01 (when she discussed it)" when gold is "week before 25 August 2023". Forensic SQL on `cefix14_*conv-26*`:
- `EpisodicMemory` 0/16 carry `observation_date`
- `SemanticMemory` 0/15 carry `observation_date`
- Globally: `tree_reorganizer` 2219 rows + `episodic_summarizer` 195 rows — none carry it

`evaluation/locomo/query.py::_extract_ts` reads `observation_date → chat_time → created_at`. Missing key → falls through to `created_at` = ingest wall-clock. Today-leak.

Root pattern: 15 derived-write paths hand-roll their own `map[string]any` and silently omit the field. Building each fix in-place would recur next time someone adds a derived path.

## What's in this PR (Phase 1A)

**New `internal/memprops` package** — single source of truth for derived-memory props:
- `BuildDerivedMemoryProps` returns `(map[string]any, error)`; rejects empty `ObservationDate` with `ErrObservationDateRequired`
- `LatestObservationDate` helper for parents derived from a row set (Phase 1B will consume it)
- 5 unit tests cover invariant, defaults, trimming, mandatory fields

**Plumb `ObservationDate` through the trigger fan-out:**
- `extractorTriggerInput` grows `ObservationDate`
- `add_fine.go` + `add_fine_atomic_persist.go` pass `fc.ObservationDate`
- `add_buffer.go` passes `""` (no chat_time source today; receiver metric-and-skips rather than today-leaking — Phase 2)

**Migrate the two episodic builders:**
- `handlers/add_episodic.go::generateEpisodicSummary` — signature gains `observationDate`; uses `memprops`
- `scheduler/reorganizer_episodic.go::generateEpisodicSummary` — same
- `scheduler/reorganizer_mem_read.go` + `_parse.go` — `wmInfo.observationDate` computed as `max(observation_date|chat_time)` over source WM rows; threaded into the scheduler twin

## Out of scope (follow-ups, by phase)

- **1B**: `scheduler/tree_summariser.go::persistTierParent` (2219 rows globally — biggest volume)
- **1C**: derive `now` in `reorganizer_mem_read.go:74` from chat_time instead of `time.Now()`
- **Phase 2**: 7 remaining derived sites (`prefs`, `wm refresh/compact`, `skill`, `tool`, `mem_read_legacy/actions`)
- **Phase 2**: buffer-flush chat_time retention
- **Phase 3 (optional)**: rule #10 cross-character bleed env-conditional in `chat_prompt_softening.go`

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` green
- [x] `go test ./internal/memprops/... ./internal/handlers/... ./internal/scheduler/...` green
- [ ] After deploy: re-ingest `conv-26` under fresh `cefix15_*` namespace in `mode=fine`
- [ ] SQL: `SELECT memory_type, count(*), count((properties::jsonb)->>'observation_date') FROM Memory WHERE user_name LIKE 'cefix15%conv-26%' GROUP BY memory_type` — assert all derived rows now carry observation_date
- [ ] LoCoMo eval delta on cat-2 (today-leak) and cat-3 (multi-hop)

Shared install primitives used by ensureGit, ensureTmux, the agent-runtime installer, and the optional gh install path:

- `InstallAttempt`, `canPromptForInstall`, `askYesNo`
- `runInteractiveCommand`, `tryInstallWithAttempts`, `genericInstallHints`

### 2. `lib/startup-preflight.ts` (new — 244 lines)

Runtime preflight checks (distinct from `lib/preflight.ts`, which validates dashboard build artifacts):

- `ensureGit(context)` — interactive install on missing
- `ensureTmux()` — interactive install on missing
- `warnAboutLegacyStorage()`, `warnAboutOpenClawStatus(config)`
- `runtimePreflight(config)` — top-level orchestrator: tools + state warnings + idle-sleep + OpenClaw credentials, called once from `runStartup`

This collapses ~32 lines of inline orchestration in `runStartup` into a single `await runtimePreflight(config)` call.

### 3. `lib/shutdown.ts` (new — 121 lines)

`installShutdownHandlers({ configPath, projectId })` extracts the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler block (85 lines) from `runStartup`'s closure into its own module. The handler logic is identical: stop lifecycle workers → kill active sessions → record last-stop → unregister → await janitor sweep → exit with code 130/0.

## What's NOT in this PR (intentional)

- The duplicated kill-and-record loop in `ao stop` is left as-is. It has different verbosity (spinner, warnings, per-project output) and different options (`--purge-session`) than the signal handler. - No `Prompter` abstraction yet. Of the 7 `isHumanCaller()` callsites, only 2 are the "prompt-or-skip" pattern that benefits from a wrapper; the other 5 are behavioral branches that gain leverage only when PR B restructures the §3.x menu. Deferred to PR B.
