Adds invisible Turnstile to the create form to keep automated abuse off the free-tier R2/D1 quotas. Visible to legit users only on suspicious traffic; the worker rejects POSTs without a valid token.

Ships with Cloudflare's invisible always-pass test key (`2x00000000000000000000AB`) so it works out of the box. To activate real verification:

1. Register a site at https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/turnstile (Managed mode).
2. Replace `data-sitekey` in `public/index.html` with the real key.
3. `npx wrangler secret put TURNSTILE_SECRET` and paste the secret.

Until the secret is set, the worker logs a warning and skips verification (so dev/preview keeps working). Production should always have it set.

author: widgetii
body:
## Summary

- Add `--output=PATH` to `ipctool trace`: parent freopens stdout after fork so streamer logs (Majestic, Sofia) no longer interleave with trace pseudocode and corrupt register-write lines on shared fd 1
- Add a post-processing pipeline under `tools/` (pure Python stdlib) that turns a captured trace into a buildable HiSilicon-shaped sensor driver scaffold and diffs it against a known reference
- Add `tools/capture_sensor.sh` wrapping the camera-side flow for both OpenIPC/Majestic (ssh) and XiongMai/Sofia (telnet + bind-mount over `/usr/bin/Sofia`)
- Add `docs/sensor-driver-extraction.md` — first researcher-oriented doc in the project, covering the full workflow plus the non-obvious gotchas

## Why

The trace command has been around for a while but the README has it as a single line: `ipctool trace /usr/bin/Sofia`. In practice, getting a usable sensor init out of a running streamer requires:

- a UPX-packed binary (XiongMai HiLinux 4.9 kernels reject raw musl-static ELFs with ENOEXEC, busybox sh then tries to interpret the ELF as a script and dies with `syntax error: unexpected word (expecting ")")`)
- redirecting trace output away from the child's stdout (otherwise streamer logs interleave and truncate trace lines mid-write)
- understanding that on XiongMai firmwares, `XmServices_Mgr` is not a supervisor — it forks `SofiaRun.sh` once at boot and doesn't restart it; the watchdog is fed by `XmServices_Mgr`, not by Sofia
- redirecting stdin to `/dev/null` for a backgrounded ptraced chain to avoid SIGTTIN

This PR captures all of that as code and prose so the next researcher doesn't have to rediscover it.

## Validation

End-to-end on SmartSens **SC2315E** + Hisilicon **HI3516EV200**, using `widgetii/smart_sc2315e` as ground truth:

| capture source | address | value | LCS sequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenIPC Majestic (`libsns_sc2315e.so`) | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| XiongMai Sofia (statically linked) | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| Majestic vs Sofia (cross-check) | 100% | 100% | 100% |

172 register writes match exactly across all three. Both streamers ultimately load the same vendor `sc2315e_cmos.c` driver, and `ipctool trace` recovers it byte-for-byte.

## File map

```
src/main.c                                + usage string for --output=
src/ptrace.c                              + --output=PATH flag
docs/sensor-driver-extraction.md          + full researcher manual
tools/capture_sensor.sh                   + build / majestic / sofia subcommands
tools/trace_segment.py                    + pseudocode -> phase JSON
tools/trace_to_driver.py                  + JSON -> C scaffold
tools/trace_diff.py                       + scoped diff vs reference
README.md                                 ~ link to new docs
.gitignore                                ~ exclude tools/dumps and build-arm*
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `tools/capture_sensor.sh build` produces a UPX-packed binary
- [ ] `tools/capture_sensor.sh majestic --host <openipc-cam>` round-trips capture + restart
- [ ] `tools/capture_sensor.sh sofia --host <xm-cam>` produces a clean trace and reboots cleanly
- [ ] `python3 tools/trace_segment.py <log>` produces non-empty `init` phase
- [ ] `python3 tools/trace_diff.py <gen.c> <ref.c> --gen-scope ... --ref-scope ...` reports ≥90% address match for a sensor with a known reference
- [ ] Existing `ipctool trace` invocations (without `--output=`) behave unchanged

author: phpstan-bot
body:
## Summary

PHPStan incorrectly reported placeholder count mismatches for `sscanf`/`fscanf` calls using the `%*` assignment suppression modifier (e.g. `%*[a-z]`, `%*d`). In scanf, `*` means "match the input but don't store it", so these placeholders should not be counted as requiring a variable argument. The fix teaches the placeholder parser to distinguish scanf semantics from printf semantics.

## Changes

- Modified `src/Rules/Functions/PrintfHelper.php`:
  - Added `bool $isScanf` parameter to `parsePlaceholders()` and `getPlaceholdersCount()`
  - When `$isScanf` is true and `*` is captured (in the `width` regex group), the placeholder is skipped entirely via `continue`
  - `getPrintfPlaceholdersCount()` and `getPrintfPlaceholders()` pass `false`
  - `getScanfPlaceholdersCount()` passes `true`

## Root cause

The `parsePlaceholders()` method was shared between printf and scanf without accounting for their different semantics for `*`:
- **printf**: `%*d` means "take width from the next argument" → counts as an extra parameter
- **scanf**: `%*d` means "match but don't assign" → should NOT count as a parameter at all

The fix adds a `$isScanf` flag so that when processing scanf format strings, any placeholder with `*` is recognized as assignment-suppressed and skipped.

## Analogous cases investigated

- **`PrintfArrayParametersRule` (vprintf/vsprintf)**: Only uses printf semantics — not affected.
- **`PrintfParameterTypeRule` (printf/sprintf/fprintf)**: Only uses printf semantics — not affected.
- **`SscanfFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension`**: Uses its own regex (`/%(\d*)(\[[^\]]+\]|[cdeEfosux]{1})/`) which accidentally already handles `%*` correctly — the `\d*` group doesn't match `*`, so suppressed placeholders are never included in the inferred return array type. Added NSRT assertions to lock this in.

## Test

- `tests/PHPStan/Rules/Functions/data/bug-10260.php` — Rule test covering `%*[a-z]`, `%*d`, `%*s`, multiple suppressions, mixed suppressed/non-suppressed, and `fscanf` with suppression.
- `tests/PHPStan/Analyser/nsrt/sscanf.php` — Added type inference assertions for `sscanf` with `%*` to confirm the return type extension correctly excludes suppressed placeholders.

Fixes phpstan/phpstan#10260

author: soulware
body:
## Summary

Two ublk worker threads independently demand-fetching from the same segment after a release/claim cycle each fired their own range-GET, wrote their own `.body` bytes, and raced on the `.present` rewrite. #209 makes the rewrite race benign; this PR removes the duplicate work entirely so that the cold-cache fan-out across 4 workers turns into one range-GET, not four.

## Algorithm

Per-fetcher `FetchCoalescer` keyed by `(segment_ulid, [start, end])`:

- **Claim path**: under one lock, scan in-flight leases for an overlap on the same segment. If none, register a new lease and return it. If found, clone the lease's done-condvar, drop the lock, wait on the condvar, return `None` to the caller.
- **Caller loop in `fetch_one_extent`**: re-read `.present` → recompute batch → `claim_or_wait`. On `None`, loop again — `.present` may now contain the leader's bits, so the target may be present (fast-exit) or only partially covered (smaller batch on the next attempt).
- **Lease drop**: RAII guard removes the entry from the in-flight list and notify-alls the condvar. Panics, errors, and success all release uniformly.

**Disjoint batches on the same segment do not block each other** — the overlap test is `start_a <= end_b && start_b <= end_a`, per-batch, not per-segment. This was the explicit design choice in the discussion: per-segment locking would have serialized two readers fetching far apart within one segment, which is a real workload pattern (random reads on a hot volume).

## Properties

- Same-segment overlapping batches → 1 range-GET shared by N callers
- Same-segment disjoint batches → N parallel range-GETs
- Cross-segment → fully independent
- Leader fetch failure → waiters re-loop and one becomes the new leader (no error poisoning across calls)
- Map churn is segment-event-rate, not LBA-rate

## Layered with #209

#209 makes `write_file_atomic` safe for concurrent callers (per-call unique tmp suffix). This PR avoids those concurrent callers in the first place. Both belong: #209 is the correctness layer; this PR is the perf layer that also makes the concurrent-write case structurally rare.

## Test plan

- [x] 4 unit tests of the coalescer's overlap logic
- [x] Integration test: 8 threads race on entry 0 of the same segment with a 50 ms-delayed counting fetcher; asserts exactly **1** range-GET fired, all calls returned `Ok`, all entries populated
- [x] All 17 elide-fetch tests pass
- [x] All 221 elide-coordinator tests pass (unchanged behaviour for the consumer)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p elide-fetch --tests -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all`

💡 What
Enhances the `StarRating` component by treating read-only and interactive modes differently for screen readers and keyboard navigation.
- For read-only mode, the component now uses a container with `role="img"` and a summary `aria-label` (e.g., "Rating: 4 out of 5 stars"), while hiding individual stars with `aria-hidden="true"`.
- For interactive mode, the component uses `role="radiogroup"` with individual `role="radio"` buttons, proper `aria-checked` and `aria-label` attributes, and adds keyboard focus styles (`focus-visible:ring-2`).

🎯 Why
Previously, the read-only mode forced screen readers to announce multiple disabled buttons sequentially, which is confusing and verbose. The interactive mode lacked clear keyboard focus indicators, making it difficult for keyboard-only users to navigate and select a rating. This update solves both issues, ensuring a smooth and accessible experience for all users.

📸 Before/After
- **Before**: Read-only stars were individual disabled buttons; interactive stars lacked focus rings.
- **After**: Read-only stars are summarized cleanly for screen readers; interactive stars have clear `focus-visible` styling (verified via Playwright screenshot).

♿ Accessibility
- Dramatically improved screen reader flow for read-only ratings.
- Added full keyboard accessibility with explicit focus states.
- Implemented proper ARIA roles (`radiogroup`, `radio`, `aria-checked`) for the interactive rating experience.

### Motivation
- Provide a reusable, auditable conversion/surgery/SVD inspection pipeline for Nemotron LoRA adapters to make the baseline 0.86 conversion fully visible and reproducible. 
- Instrument each conversion stage (prefix rename, expert unfuse, Mamba gate/x merge, SVD compression, etc.) so differences can be logged and analyzed without performing any training or post-finetune changes. 
- Produce the set of deliverables required for conversion-only analysis and candidate proposals (inventory, stage logs, SVD error scaffolding, candidate list, and a generator summary).

### Description
- Add `conversion_audit.py` which inspects `adapter_model.safetensors` and `adapter_config.json`, computes tensor/module counts, rank distribution, zero-shape tensors, unexpected/fused key patterns, prefix/backbone checks, and ZIP inventory, and writes structured JSON/MD reports under `reports/conversion_audit/`.
- Implement a stage-log scaffold covering the nine conversion stages and an SVD-error-report scaffold for later per-module/layer reconstruction metrics, plus a `better_conversion_candidates.md` describing candidate methods and evaluation criteria.
- The script intentionally marks stages as `not_executed_in_this_environment` when runtime Kaggle assets are not mounted, and avoids any training, tensor swapping, residual injection, or rank>32 modifications.
- Output artifacts created: `conversion_audit.py` and the report files `baseline_adapter_inventory.{md,json}`, `conversion_stage_log.{md,json}`, `svd_error_report.{md,json}`, `better_conversion_candidates.md`, and `generator_summary.md` under `reports/conversion_audit/`.

author: tomascarminatti-ux
body:
This PR implements a performance optimization for the `prompt_builder.py` module. 

### 💡 What
- **Caching:** Added `lru_cache` to template loading.
- **Efficient Substitution:** Replaced multiple string `.replace()` calls with a single `re.sub()` pass using a callback.
- **Regex Pre-compilation:** Pre-compiled the variable pattern.
- **Module-level Imports:** Moved `json` import out of the function.

### 🎯 Why
The previous implementation performed $O(N \cdot M)$ operations (where $N$ is template length and $M$ is number of variables) and read from disk on every call. This optimization reduces it to $O(N)$ and minimizes I/O.

### 📊 Impact
- Average time per `build_prompt` call reduced from **0.1113 ms** to **0.0233 ms** (~4.8x faster).
- Reduced memory pressure by minimizing string copies.

### 🔬 Measurement
Run `python3 scripts/benchmark_prompt.py` to see the performance gains.
Run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_prompt_builder.py` to verify correctness.

body:
## Bug

Iron Coach IA (chat do VIP Hub) respondia que "não há dados de desempenho registrados (cargas, séries, repetições) para NENHUM dos seus últimos treinos" — mesmo o relatório tendo todos os dados.

## Causa raiz

A rota `/api/ai/coach-chat` só usa o `context` que o cliente manda. O `CoachChatModal` envia `{ session, previousSession }` — mas isso é o relatório atual + anterior. Quando o usuário abre o chat do VIP Hub (sem estar num relatório), `session` é `undefined` → IA recebe contexto vazio → cega.

A rota nunca consultava o Supabase pra puxar histórico.

## Fix

Novo helper `fetchRecentWorkoutHistory(supabase, userId, 5)` em `src/utils/ai/recentWorkoutHistory.ts` que lê `workouts.notes` (mesma fonte que o `post-workout-insights` usa) e emite um resumo bem compacto por treino:
- `date`, `name`, `durationMin`
- por exercício: `setsDone`, `topSet { weight, reps }`, `volumeKg`

Tight em tokens, suficiente pra IA falar sobre progressão.

A rota `coach-chat` chama esse helper depois do auth e injeta no prompt como seção rotulada. Também adiciono instrução no prompt: "se o histórico estiver populado, USE — não diga 'não tenho dados'".

## Test plan

- [ ] Abrir chat do VIP sem estar em relatório → perguntar "Qual foi meu volume da última semana?" → IA responde com base nos últimos treinos
- [ ] Perguntar "Como estou no supino?" → IA cita o último top set + sets feitos
- [ ] Usuário sem treinos → seção `histórico` chega como `[]` → IA responde apropriadamente
- [ ] Não introduz `console.log` / regressão no `npm run scan:secrets`

## Out of scope (próximo PR)

- Cache do histórico per-user (cada turn refetch — OK por enquanto)
- Endpoint `vip-coach` (estrutura diferente, outro PR)

author: mortalus
body:
## Why

Per **MCP Infrastructure Standard §3.4.4**, premium ingestion must be *\"separated from rebuild (deterministic, schema-driven, fleet-wide)\"* to preserve the canonical pattern's reliability. PR #63 violated this by running \`npm run ingest:paid\` inside the main Dockerfile — every release hammered \`cysec.gov.cy\` + \`EUR-Lex SPARQL\` + \`gdprhub.eu\`.

**Real-world consequence (2026-05-03):** EUR-Lex SPARQL returned sustained HTTP 502 for ~30 min. Two consecutive publish workflow runs failed at the ingestion step. The Feb-25 fix bundle (PR #64 WAL flip + PR #65 soft-fail) couldn't deploy. \`law-cypriot\` crash-looped past 290 restarts. Coupling image production to EU infrastructure uptime is the structural defect; this PR fixes it.

## What

Two-image pattern:

| Image | Built by | Cadence | External HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|
| \`cypriot-law-mcp-data:latest\` | \`Dockerfile.data\` via \`refresh-data.yml\` | weekly Sunday 03:00 UTC + \`workflow_dispatch\` | **Yes** — the only place |
| \`cypriot-law-mcp:latest\` | \`Dockerfile\` via \`publish-ghcr.yml\` | per code commit | **No, ever** |

The main Dockerfile pulls the DB via \`COPY --from=ghcr.io/ansvar-systems/cypriot-law-mcp-data:latest /database.db\`. App image build is now offline and ~30 sec instead of ~25 min.

## What's removed from the main Dockerfile

- \`RUN apk add python3 make g++ curl\` (no native build deps needed at runtime)
- \`RUN npm rebuild better-sqlite3\` (better-sqlite3 only used by ingestion)
- \`COPY data ./data\` and \`COPY scripts ./scripts\` (not needed in app image)
- \`RUN npm run build:db && npm run build:db:paid\` (DB comes from data image)
- \`RUN npm run ingest:paid\` (the headline violation)
- \`RUN node scripts/finalise-db.cjs\` (no longer needed in app build)

## Sequencing for first deploy

The data image does not exist on GHCR yet. After merging:

1. **Merge this PR.** \`publish-ghcr.yml\` will run and fail because \`cypriot-law-mcp-data:latest\` does not exist. **Prod is unaffected** — Watchtower only updates on a digest change, and a failed build produces none. The container keeps running the existing healthy \`:latest\`.
2. **Manually trigger \`Refresh Data Image\`** in the Actions tab (\`workflow_dispatch\`). Build runs ~60 min and pushes the data image to GHCR.
3. \`refresh-data.yml\` then triggers \`publish-ghcr.yml\`, which now succeeds. Watchtower swaps prod within 1h (or via kick).

After step 3, steady state:
- Code change → \`publish-ghcr\` only → 30-sec build → Watchtower deploys
- Weekly Sunday 03:00 → \`refresh-data\` → data refresh → \`publish-ghcr\` triggered → app rebuilt with new DB → Watchtower deploys

## Privacy / legal

The \`cypriot-law-mcp-data\` GHCR package **must be set to private** — same policy as the app image, since it contains ingested third-party regulatory content (CySEC circulars, EUR-Lex NIMs, GDPRhub decisions). Public distribution would be a license violation.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Add \`step_no_runtime_external_fetch_check\` to \`apply-mcp-standard.py\` in arch-docs so future MCPs cannot reintroduce this anti-pattern.
- Audit the rest of the fleet (one prior \`gh search\` showed cypriot as the only \`RUN.*npm run ingest\` violator across 107 law MCPs, but a runtime audit is worth doing).
- Document the two-image pattern in \`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-25-mcp-infrastructure-standard-design.md\` as the canonical spec for any premium MCP whose ingestion is too heavy or too slow to commit binaries to git.

author: clubanderson
body:
Fixes #11678
Fixes #11675

## Problem

The Playwright nightly UX journey test was failing because clicking the CI/CD link in the sidebar navigated to `/acmm` instead of `/ci-cd`. This affected both the nightly UX test (#11678) and the cross-browser Playwright test (#11675).

## Root Cause

The sidebar sort function (`useSidebarConfig.ts:146-153`) reorders navigation items based on their index in the `enabled_dashboards` array returned from the backend `/health` endpoint, **not** the `order` field in the frontend config.

The backend array (`pkg/api/projects.go:11`) has:
```go
"insights", "ai-ml", "ai-agents", "acmm", "ci-cd",
```

But the frontend `DEFAULT_PRIMARY_NAV` had them in the opposite order:
```ts
{ id: "acmm", ..., order: 5.5 },
{ id: "ci-cd", ..., order: 6 },
```

This mismatch caused the visual order to not match the href order, creating a routing bug.

## Solution

Swapped the order of `ci-cd` and `acmm` in `DEFAULT_PRIMARY_NAV` to match the backend `enabled_dashboards` array order. Now both have `acmm` before `ci-cd`, ensuring consistent visual and routing behavior.

## Testing

CI will run the full Playwright test suite including the failing nightly UX journey test.

body: ## Summary Implements Level 1 dump integrity verification: pre/post row-count comparison + dump-line parsing to verify the dump is a 1:1 copy of the database. Results are displayed in the UI with per-table breakdown. ### What's new **Backend:** - `RowCounter` (`dumper/rowcounter.go`): `io.Writer` wrapper that sits in the dump pipeline before gzip and counts rows per table by parsing the raw dump output: - PostgreSQL: parses `COPY ... FROM stdin` blocks and counts data lines - MySQL: parses `INSERT INTO` statements and counts `VALUES` tuples - MongoDB: uses pre/post stats comparison (binary archive format not parseable) - Pre+Post dump stats: pipeline now collects `CollectStats()` both **before** and **after** the dump to detect changes during the dump window - `DumpVerification` struct in `meta.json`: stores pre-counts, post-counts, dump-counts, per-table verdict (`match`/`mismatch`/`partial`/`skipped`), and overall summary - `BuildVerification` logic handles: - Concurrent inserts (more rows in dump than pre-stats → OK) - Estimation tolerance (1% for dump-vs-pre, 5% for pre-vs-post) - Missing data (no post-stats, no dump counting → `skipped`) - Anonymization support when `anonymize-tables=true` is set **UI:** - "Verification" column in Run History table with badge (Verified/Mismatch/Partial/Skipped) - Verification badge in Latest Run card - Detailed "Dump Integrity Verification" table on target detail page showing: - Table name | Pre-Dump Rows | Post-Dump Rows | Dump Rows | Verdict | Detail **Tests:** - 8 `RowCounter` tests (PostgreSQL COPY, MySQL INSERT, escaped strings, MongoDB no-op, passthrough) - 5 `BuildVerification` tests (all-match, mismatch, nil-pre, mongo pre/post, concurrent inserts, tolerance) - 1 `metaJSON` test with verification data ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Deploy the operator with `analyzer-enabled=true` on a source, trigger a backup, and verify the `meta.json` contains a `verification` field with per-table breakdown - [ ] Check the UI target detail page shows the "Dump Integrity Verification" table after a backup run - [ ] Verify the verification badge appears in the Run History table for each run - [ ] Test with a PostgreSQL source to confirm dump row counts are parsed correctly from COPY blocks ### Notes - For MongoDB, dump-stream row counting is not feasible (binary archive format), so verification relies solely on pre/post stats comparison - The 1% tolerance for dump-vs-pre counts accounts for `pg_stat_user_tables` being an estimate, not an exact count - The 5% tolerance for pre-vs-post comparison (when no dump counting available) accounts for live database activity during the backup window Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/be9239cf104a49de8a73490c4c6d8352 Requested by: @behrangalavi ---

## Summary
- v0.5 PR C of the runtime-selection-bench sequence: `BenchScheduler` orchestrator that owns a daemon worker thread and runs PR B's `BenchHarness` off the dispatch hot path.
- Env-var gate `OCTOMIL_RUNTIME_BENCH=experimental` enables background scheduling; `OCTOMIL_RUNTIME_BENCH_ALLOW_PLACEHOLDER=1` bypasses calibration check for tests/CI.
- Calibration refusal closes the v0.5→v1 graduation hole flagged in PR B's consensus: real-device runs cannot accidentally cache a `Result` based on placeholder thresholds.

## What changed
- `octomil/runtime/bench/scheduler.py` — `BenchScheduler` with `lookup_or_schedule` (cache-first, fail-soft on placeholder thresholds), `run_foreground` (CLI/explicit; raises on placeholder), `shutdown`, `queue_depth` / `in_flight` accessors. Per-cache_key dedup via leaf-filename digest. Daemon worker, lazy spawn. Queue cap with drop policy.
- `octomil/runtime/bench/__init__.py` — re-export new symbols.
- `tests/test_runtime_bench_scheduler.py` — 16 pytest cases covering env-var gate, calibration refusal/bypass/dedup-of-refusal-log, cache hit, async drain, dedup, queue capacity, env-var typo warning.

## Why
- Closes PR C of `strategy/runtime-selection-bench.md`. Background bench can't fire without an orchestrator; PR D's CLI calls into the same scheduler.

## How it works
- `lookup_or_schedule(cache_key, ...)`: cache hit → return; cache miss + env on → enqueue background bench, return None (caller falls through to declared defaults). Fail-soft if thresholds are placeholders.
- Per-cache_key dedup uses `CacheKey.leaf_filename()` (canonical-JSON SHA256 from PR A) — `CacheKey` itself isn't hashable.
- Daemon worker pumps a deque guarded by a Condition; `shutdown(timeout_s)` is idempotent.
- Refusal log dedup: per-cache_key `_refused_keys: set[str]` so a high-RPS dispatch path doesn't flood WARNING.

author: ifireball
body:
## Summary

This branch delivers the **Fullsend admin SPA** experience on top of the site Worker: in-browser GitHub sign-in, an organisation list grounded in **your GitHub App installations**, and per-org readiness signals aligned with the CLI install story. It also includes Worker and CI wiring so admin APIs, OAuth, and static assets work together in dev and production.

Below is what **users and operators** will notice relative to `main`.

---

### Sign-in and session

- **GitHub OAuth** is mediated by the site Worker (`/api/oauth/authorize`, `/api/oauth/token`): the SPA bundle does not embed the GitHub OAuth **client id**.
- **Cloudflare Turnstile** is required for the token exchange path where configured.
- **Boot screen** while the app confirms the session (Turnstile + token exchange + GitHub user), with a way to **cancel** and pick another account.
- **Token expiry** is respected in storage; **401** from GitHub user APIs clears the session and surfaces a **Re-authenticate** path instead of leaving the UI in a broken state.
- After OAuth, the app can **restore a simple in-app hash route** you had open before sign-in when it is safe to do so.

---

### Organisation list

- Orgs come from **`GET /user/installations`** (organisations where the GitHub App is installed), not only classic org membership APIs—better match for **GitHub App user tokens**.
- **Progressive loading** while installation pages stream in, with a **visible row cap** (15) and search-as-you-type filtering so the list stays responsive.
- **Empty list** states explain what might be wrong (permissions, app not installed, etc.) with **actionable** copy where we can infer it from GitHub responses.
- **Install the app** flows use a validated **GitHub App slug** (from the Worker env, OAuth state, or installation payloads) so install links stay correct across deployments.
- **Refresh** after installing the app on GitHub is supported (session-backed hint so the list can pick up new installs).
- When the installation list is **paginated past a safety cap**, the UI warns that the list may be incomplete.

---

### Per-organisation rows (Deploy / Configure / blocked)

- Each org row runs a **read-only “layer” analysis** in the browser (mirroring the Go installer’s layers): config repo, workflows, secrets, enrollment, dispatch token, etc.
- **Deploy** vs **Configure** vs **cannot deploy** reflects both analysis results and **deploy preflight** (classic OAuth scopes when GitHub exposes them).
- For **GitHub App user tokens** without useful scope headers, the UI uses **read-only API probes** (repos, Actions, org secrets) to explain missing access instead of guessing from scopes alone.
- **403** responses distinguish **rate limits** from **permission** problems and show hints that work under **browser CORS** (no reliance on headers GitHub may omit in the browser).
- Analysis is **throttled** and **cached** so scrolling and filtering do not hammer the API; **GraphQL** batching hints which orgs have a `.fullsend` config repo before opening every org.

---

### Site Worker and hosting

- Worker serves **admin static assets** and implements **admin BFF** routes (OAuth, GitHub user proxy) with **CORS**, **rate limits**, and tests.
- **Site deploy** and **Wrangler** fixes so admin API routes and secrets work in CI and production.

---

### Tooling and docs

- **Root Vite workspace**, Vitest and **svelte-check** in CI, **mise**-pinned Node for the web toolchain.
- **UX design spec**, **implementation plan** updates, admin **README** / **sample.env.local** guidance, and a small **OAuth localhost experiment** under docs for contributors.

---

### Follow-up hardening (latest commits)

- Avoid **duplicate global 401** events when listing installations.
- **Validate** post-OAuth **hash** fragments before applying them (pattern-based safety without a fixed route whitelist).
- **Cap** org `config.yaml` **size and nesting depth** with clear errors when limits are exceeded.
- Key **install-readiness probe cache** entries by **GitHub login**, not the access token.

---

Fixes #510  
Fixes #511

author: tjwald
body:
## Description

Adds first-class child-resource support to the RabbitMQ hosting integration: virtual hosts, queues, exchanges, bindings, shovels, and policies. App authors can declare their full RabbitMQ topology in the AppHost, and Aspire will provision it against the running broker and surface per-resource health on the dashboard.

```csharp
var rabbit = builder.AddRabbitMQ("rabbit").WithManagementPlugin();

var vhost = rabbit.AddVirtualHost("events");
var queue = vhost.AddQueue("orders");
var exchange = vhost.AddExchange("orders-ex", RabbitMQExchangeType.Topic)
                    .WithBinding(queue, routingKey: "order.*");

vhost.AddShovel("archive", queue, vhost.AddQueue("orders-archive"));
vhost.AddPolicy("ttl", pattern: "^orders.*", applyTo: RabbitMQPolicyApplyTo.Queues)
     .WithQueueArguments(a => a.MessageTtl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10));
```

### How it works

- **Provisioning** — each child resource self-provisions via the `InitializeResourceEvent` lifecycle hook. Resources wait for their dependencies to be healthy before provisioning begins (vhosts wait for the broker; queues/exchanges/policies wait for their vhost; shovels wait for their vhost, source, and destination). Failures are isolated per resource — one bad queue doesn't take down its siblings. Communicates with the broker over AMQP for queue and exchange declares, and the management HTTP API for vhosts, shovels, and policies.
- **Health checks** — every child resource gets its own health check. The check returns `Unhealthy` while the resource is not yet `Running`, and otherwise runs a live broker probe (passive declare for queues/exchanges, shovel status poll, HTTP GET for policies).
- **Plugins** — `WithPlugin(RabbitMQPlugin)` enables a known plugin by name; `WithManagementPlugin()` and `AddShovel` auto-enable the plugins they need.

Fixes #16579

## Checklist

- Is this feature complete?
  - [x] Yes. Ready to ship.
  - [ ] No. Follow-up changes expected.
- Are you including unit tests for the changes and scenario tests if relevant?
  - [x] Yes (tests across builder shapes, provisioner phases, health checks, policies, plugins, public-API validation, and functional topology tests)
  - [ ] No
- Did you add public API?
  - [x] Yes
    - If yes, did you have an API Review for it?
      - [ ] Yes
      - [x] No
    - Did you add `<remarks />` and `<code />` elements on your triple slash comments?
      - [x] Yes
      - [ ] No
  - [ ] No
- Does the change make any security assumptions or guarantees?
  - [ ] Yes
  - [x] No
- Does the change require an update in our Aspire docs?
  - [x] Yes
    - Link to `aspire.dev` issue: will file once the API surface is signed off.
  - [ ] No

### Open follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Cross-broker shovels** — `AddShovel` only accepts a source and destination on the *same* RabbitMQ server. Multiple local servers, or a local-to-remote shovel, are not yet supported. Can be added later by accepting a connection-string parameter for the remote endpoint.
- **Publish & deployment support** — child resources are run-mode only. Manifest emission and deployer integration (so the topology survives `aspire publish`/deploy) is intentionally deferred.
- **Adding a playground** - If you want I can add a playground for the RabbitMQ integration.

**Phase B item.** Five hub goroutines spawned with bare \`go func()\` had no panic recovery. A panic in any of them silently killed that subsystem until the next hub restart:

- \`alertEvalLoop\` (alerts stop firing)
- \`cleanupLoop\` (DB cleanup stops, audit/orphan rows pile up)
- \`versionRefreshLoop\` (agent SHAs go stale, auto-update breaks)
- \`reconnectMonitorLoop\` (rollout circuit breaker stops working)
- \`terminalRelay\` (per-session: WS connection hangs, browser sees dead terminal)

Net effect: invisible degradation that an operator only notices when something downstream breaks.

## Fix

New file \`hub/safety.go\` with three primitives:

- \`runWithRecover(name, fn) bool\` — synchronous recover + log of panic value + stack trace. Returns whether a panic was caught. **Testable seam.**
- \`goSafelyForever(name, fn)\` — for indefinite background loops. Spawns fn; on panic OR unexpected return, logs and restarts after 5s backoff.
- \`goSafelyOnce(name, fn)\` — for one-shot goroutines (e.g. per-session terminal relay). Recover + log, no restart.

Replaces the five spawn sites. Each loop function is unchanged — wrappers are external.

## Test plan

\`TestRunWithRecoverCatchesPanic\` covers five panic shapes table-driven:

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| no panic | returns false |
| \`panic(\"boom\")\` | returns true |
| \`panic(errors.New(...))\` | returns true |
| \`panic(nil)\` (Go 1.21+ \`runtime.PanicNilError\`) | returns true |
| nil-deref runtime panic | returns true |

Each sub-test also asserts the panic does NOT propagate to the test goroutine — that's the actual contract: the wrapper must contain the panic regardless of shape.

The outer \`goSafelyForever\` / \`goSafelyOnce\` are thin wrappers (for-loop + sleep on panic). Testing them deterministically would require injecting a fake sleep — the cost outweighs the benefit since the only logic is the loop. Reviewed by inspection.

- [x] \`cd hub && go test ./... && go vet ./...\` (5/5 sub-tests, full suite green)
- [x] \`cd agent && go vet ./...\` (no agent changes)
- [ ] Smoke-check post-deploy: \`journalctl -u bloxos-hub\` should be silent on \"goroutine ... PANIC recovered\" under normal operation. If a panic does fire later (real bug), the log line + stack trace make root cause obvious.

## Notes

- First Phase B PR. C1–C5 (Phase A) all merged + tagged \`v1.0.0-rc1\`.
- Next: B2 \`/ws/agent\` rate limit (pattern from \`/api/auth/login\`).

author: corrin
body:
## Summary

Two related changes that together stop wasting wall-clock time on every deploy and move OS security patching off the deploy hot path entirely.

### 1. `deploy.sh` skips `server-setup.sh` when its inputs are unchanged (`f40cd708`)

`server-setup.sh` is idempotent, but its no-op path still scans every dpkg-guarded apt install and `command -v`-guarded binary install block. ~80% of PRs touch nothing it actually reads, but they still pay the convergence cost on every deploy.

Hash the files `server-setup.sh` consumes — itself, the two `certbot-dreamhost-{auth,cleanup}.sh` hooks it copies into `/opt/docketworks/certbot-hooks/`, and `templates/logrotate-docketworks.conf` — and skip the re-run when the hash matches the last successful run (`/opt/docketworks/.server-setup-hash`).

- Stamp loss → re-runs (safe).
- Adding a new input to `server-setup.sh` requires adding it to `SERVER_SETUP_INPUTS` in `deploy.sh` — that maintenance burden lives next to the bash invocation it gates, so it's review-visible whenever a PR touches `server-setup.sh`.

### 2. `server-setup.sh` enables unattended security upgrades (`5d12618d`)

`apt update`/`dist-upgrade` has no place in `deploy.sh` or `server-setup.sh`'s runtime path — security patches need to land daily, regardless of whether anyone is deploying. Canonical Debian/Ubuntu solution: the `unattended-upgrades` package + `apt-daily.timer` / `apt-daily-upgrade.timer`.

`server-setup.sh` now installs the package and writes:

- `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades` — turns the timers on (Ubuntu Server ships this by default; written explicitly so a stripped image still gets it).
- `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/51docketworks-unattended-upgrades` — overrides the distro 50-file for the three knobs we care about:
  - `Automatic-Reboot "true"`
  - `Automatic-Reboot-Time "03:00"` (server-local)
  - `Automatic-Reboot-WithUsers "true"` — don't let a forgotten SSH session indefinitely defer a kernel update.
- `Allowed-Origins` is left at the distro default (security pockets only). Postgres / nginx feature-level bumps from the regular `-updates` pocket don't auto-land — those still need a deliberate operator action.

The 51 file is written from a heredoc inside `server-setup.sh`, so any future tweak to the config naturally trips the hash-skip from change 1 and re-converges on every host.

## Test plan

- [ ] **Hash-skip kicks in on a no-op deploy.** On a server where `server-setup.sh` ran successfully on the previous deploy: next deploy logs `server-setup.sh inputs unchanged since last successful run; skipping convergence.` and skips the bash invocation.
- [ ] **Touch any input → re-runs.** Edit `templates/logrotate-docketworks.conf` (one whitespace change), commit, deploy: deploy logs `Converging system-level dependencies via server-setup.sh...` and re-runs.
- [ ] **Stamp loss → re-runs.** `sudo rm /opt/docketworks/.server-setup-hash` then deploy: re-runs, re-stamps.
- [ ] **server-setup failure does NOT stamp.** Force a failure mid-server-setup (e.g. break the cert-domains file), run deploy: deploy aborts (set -e), `.server-setup-hash` is unchanged from before.
- [ ] **unattended-upgrades active.** After server-setup runs: `systemctl status apt-daily.timer apt-daily-upgrade.timer` both `active (waiting)`. `cat /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades` and `.../51docketworks-unattended-upgrades` show the expected content.
- [ ] **Unattended dry-run.** `sudo unattended-upgrade --dry-run -d` reports the security pocket as the only allowed origin and shows what (if anything) would be installed.

This applies the same progress formatting behavior as bitcoin-core/gui#935 to the node headers sync logs.                                                                                                                                       During headers synchronization, the estimated progress was formatted with `%.2f%%`, which rounds to two decimal         places. This could display `100.00%` even when the estimate still had headers left to process.                                                                                                                                                  This patch formats the progress using fixed-point integer arithmetic, truncating to two decimal places instead of       rounding. As a result, the log only displays `100.00%` when the estimated number of blocks left is zero.                                                                                                                                        The same truncation is applied to both headers sync and headers presync progress logs for consistency. 

During a correct sync this is pointless, as the time were this error would happen is minimal, however in some special cases this can create confussion, please read  https://github.com/bitcoin-core/gui/issues/65#issuecomment-4143720788 to get more context.

author: alexgabel
body:
## Summary

This PR completes `v0.17.0` as a narrow formula-backed generator interoperability release.

The main addition is a safe, runtime-only formula-backed generator path that extends symmetry-candidate validation without changing the existing canonical polynomial `GeneratorFamily` semantics.

New public submodule APIs:

- `pdelie.symmetry.FormulaGeneratorFamily`
- `pdelie.reporting.summarize_formula_generator_family(...)`

Updated public validation surface:

- `pdelie.symmetry.validate_symmetry_candidate(...)` now accepts `FormulaGeneratorFamily` objects and strict current formula payload mappings
- formula candidates are reported with `candidate_kind == "formula_generator_family"`

## Scope

`v0.17` supports JSON-compatible formula metadata for scalar 1D Lie-point generator components over `t`, `x`, and `u`.

Supported formula expression nodes include safe AST records such as:

- `const`
- `var`
- `add`
- `mul`
- integer `pow`
- `sin`
- `cos`
- `reciprocal`
- metadata-only symbolic references

Formula-backed candidates can be summarized, checked for safe evaluation diagnostics, and optionally validated through an attached supported finite-transform spec.

## Non-goals

This release does not add:

- arbitrary Python expression strings
- callables or executable external generators
- learned-generator training
- formula-derived finite-flow integration
- new PDEs
- KS runtime promotion
- weak KS
- broad dataset adapters
- operator APIs
- root `pdelie` exports

`FormulaGeneratorFamily` is runtime-only and does not become a new canonical object layer.

## Example

Adds a compact JSON-only example:

- `python -m pdelie.examples.formula_generator_validation`
- `pdelie.examples.run_formula_generator_validation_example(...)`

The example demonstrates formula-backed candidate reporting and empirical configured validation, including passing, partial, and failed formula cases.

## Release/Docs

- bumps package metadata to `0.17.0`
- updates README and changelog for the `v0.17` formula-backed slice
- adds `docs/releases/V0_17_RELEASE_READINESS.md`
- updates `docs/specs/API_STABILITY.md`
- updates CI to the current `v0_17-release-gate`
- keeps PyPI/TestPyPI publication deferred until `v1.0` or later

## Validation

- `python -m pytest`
- `python -m build --sdist --wheel`
- `python -m pdelie.examples.formula_generator_validation`
- existing examples still pass
- `git diff --check`

body:
## Summary

This PR adds a detailed technical design document (`planning/MARKET_DATA_DESIGN.md`) that specifies the complete implementation of the market data subsystem for FinAlly. The document serves as the blueprint for backend engineers to implement the market data module with two interchangeable provider implementations (simulator and Polygon.io REST client).

## Key Changes

- **New Design Document**: `planning/MARKET_DATA_DESIGN.md` (985 lines)
  - Complete architecture specification for `backend/app/market_data/` module
  - Unified `MarketDataProvider` abstract interface with two implementations:
    - `SimulatorProvider`: GBM-based price simulation with sector correlation model
    - `MassiveProvider`: Polygon.io REST API client with tier-aware polling and fallback handling
  - Supporting infrastructure: `PriceCache` (thread-safe in-memory ticker→Tick mapping), `PriceBroadcaster` (SSE fan-out with backpressure), and FastAPI wiring
  - Complete code examples for all major classes with full type hints and docstrings
  - Comprehensive test strategy with unit, conformance, and integration test specifications
  - Edge case handling and future multi-user extensibility design

- **New Review Document**: `planning/REVIEW.md` (312 lines)
  - Automated code review of the design document
  - Quality assessment, alignment with PLAN.md, and implementation readiness analysis
  - Risk assessment and compatibility notes

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Provider Abstraction**: Uses Protocol-based `WatchlistSource` interface for dependency injection, enabling testability without mocking frameworks
- **GBM Simulation**: Mathematically rigorous geometric Brownian motion with one-factor sector correlation model (ρ ≈ 0.7) to avoid linear algebra dependencies
- **Backpressure Handling**: SSE broadcaster uses bounded queues (256 items) with drop-oldest policy to prevent slow clients from blocking the producer
- **Graceful Degradation**: Massive provider swallows HTTP errors and maintains last-known prices; simulator runs deterministically when seeded for testing
- **Environment-Driven Selection**: Single `build_provider()` factory function selects between simulator (default) and Massive based on `MASSIVE_API_KEY` presence
- **Clean Shutdown**: All resources managed via `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` and FastAPI lifespan context manager for proper cancellation and cleanup
- **Future Multi-User Ready**: Cache and broadcaster are global (not per-connection); architecture documented for straightforward extension to multiple users

The design is production-ready and implementation-ready, with no ambiguity on class names, method signatures, module structure, or test patterns.

**What type of PR is this?**
kind/bug

**What this PR does / why we need it:**

`IsReady()` previously only gated on task count against `MinAvailable`, completely ignoring `MinResources`. This meant a gang job could be scheduled before its allocated resources met the PodGroup's minimum resource requirement.

This fix adds a resource check after the task count gate, ensuring `IsReady()` returns true only when both `MinAvailable` and `MinResources` are satisfied.


**Which issue(s) this PR fixes:**

Fixes #5075

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

The `Allocated` field on `JobInfo` is already maintained incrementally (added/subtracted as tasks transition between states), so the added resource check has negligible overhead — no recomputation needed.

body: ## Summary This PR has two layers: 1. **The ML v2 redesign** (original PR scope): replaces silent mid-to-mid label/backtest with honest taker round-trip accounting; pivots to the in-play short-cycle workflow (one coin, 4-6 h collection, per-symbol model, instant train+backtest+deploy); vendors `adaptive_sdk` (VPIN / exhaustion / OBI / MAB) into the repo as zero-dep numpy modules so its analytics become snapshot columns. Spread-aware labels (`cost_mode="taker"`), 100 ms snapshots (was 250 ms), ±50 bp / 5 bp wide-band buckets (40 columns total, tick-size-independent), vendored `backend/adaptive_sdk/` with seven `sdk_*` columns sampled into every snapshot. 2. **Live-trader hardening + safety stack** (subsequent commits): per-symbol live state machine (`paper / probation_live / active_live`) with rolling regime guards (win rate, net bp, drawdown, loss streak, cooldown); pre-trade Guards initialised from `min(soft, hard)` so even a fresh boot respects hard caps; live trader leverage cache invalidation, exit-path predict failure no longer flags the symbol, MARKET order Decimal formatting fix, 12h PnL rebuilt from `pnl_events`. Memory-stable training (column-by-column C-order build) for Polars → numpy → LightGBM on a 16 GB Windows box. Backtest summary persistence to `{models_dir}/backtest/`. 3. **Pause snapshot (final commit, this is where the project stops):** - The v2 ML experiment was run end-to-end across 7 symbols × 3 horizons. Two symbols (LABUSDT +7.04 bp, UBUSDT +6.74 bp on h15s taker) looked deployable on the held-out test split. **Both collapsed on a fresh out-of-sample 6 h window** (LABUSDT to -15.67 bp / hit 0.407, UBUSDT to -4.15 bp / hit 0.611). The direction-prediction-on-time-bars-in-taker approach does not produce a deployable edge under our cost regime on micro-cap altcoins. Numbers and reasoning are recorded in `docs/RESULTS.md`. - **The infrastructure is correct and reusable**, the experiment is conclusive, and the project is suspended pending a different direction. - Documentation added under `docs/`: - `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — module-by-module map of the backend, data flow, hot-path constraints, "where do I look to change X?" cheatsheet. - `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` — every `.env` variable and every UI-editable runtime setting, with defaults, valid ranges, and effects. Recommended starting configurations for local / VPS / training boxes. - `docs/RESULTS.md` — what we trained, how it backtested, and how it broke on out-of-sample. Per-symbol numbers, selection-bias analysis, reproduction commands. Records explicitly that `maker_*` backtest columns are theoretical upper bounds, not deployment evidence. - `docs/ROADMAP.md` — possible directions if the project is reactivated, sized honestly: dollar bars, mean-reversion-after-toxic-flow (the most realistic of three event-prediction targets), larger / more liquid symbols, maker-mode (with the cardinal rule that backtest cannot validate it on its own), alternative strategies (funding arb, liquidation hunting, stat-arb). author: chuckmilton
body:
## Why

PR #168 fixed Node version, but the deploy still failed with:

```
✘ [ERROR] Project not found. The specified project name does not match
  any of your existing projects. [code: 8000007]
```

Investigation: `sharkpark-marketing` exists in the Cloudflare account as a **Worker**, not a Pages project. The `apps/marketing/wrangler.jsonc` confirms this — it uses the modern **Workers Static Assets** pattern (`assets.directory: ./dist`, `not_found_handling: 404-page`), not Pages config.

Wrangler even warned about this on the failed run:
> Pages now has wrangler.jsonc support. We detected a configuration file at `apps/marketing/wrangler.jsonc` but it is missing the `pages_build_output_dir` field, required by Pages.

That's because the file isn't a Pages config — it's a Workers config.

## What

- Switch `pnpm exec wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name=… --branch=main` → `pnpm exec wrangler deploy`
- Workers `deploy` reads name, compatibility_date, and assets dir from `wrangler.jsonc` directly
- Renamed workflow to "Deploy marketing site to Cloudflare Workers" for clarity

## ⚠️ Required token permission change

The `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` was scoped to `Account · Cloudflare Pages · Edit`. Workers deploys require **`Account · Workers Scripts · Edit`** instead (or in addition). If the token isn't updated, the deploy will fail with a 403.

**Action required before merging:**
1. https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens → edit `sharkpark-pages-deploy` (or create a new one named `sharkpark-workers-deploy`)
2. Permissions: **Account · Workers Scripts · Edit** (you can drop the Pages permission)
3. Update the `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` repo secret

## Test

Merge → workflow runs → should successfully deploy to the existing `sharkpark-marketing` Worker.

author: roberdan
body:
## Problem

Convergio's executor (Layer 4) needs to spawn real LLM agents for
pending tasks, not echo the task id. The two practical paths to an
LLM agent are (a) the vendor's CLI (`claude`, `copilot`) and (b)
the vendor's HTTP API directly. Direct API would mean Convergio
manages API keys, double-bills the operator (who already pays for
Claude Max + a Copilot subscription), and re-implements vendor
permission policy badly.

## Why

The operator has *already solved* auth + budget at the vendor
level. Convergio re-using the CLI consumes the existing
subscription, never the API. No keys in env, no rotation policy,
no exfiltration surface, no double-billing risk. ADR-0032 makes
the rule explicit: **never call the raw Anthropic / OpenAI HTTP
APIs**.

## What changed

- **New crate `convergio-runner`** — pure preparer layer.
- `Runner` trait + two impls:
  - `ClaudeRunner` builds `claude -p --model X --output-format json
    --input-format text [--max-budget-usd Y]`, prompt on stdin so
    the graph context-pack survives argv truncation.
  - `CopilotRunner` builds `copilot -p <prompt> --model X
    --allow-all-tools` (the all-tools flag is required by the CLI
    for any non-interactive run; Convergio's worktree boundary +
    audit chain are the actual safety net).
- `RunnerKind` round-trips through `Display`/`FromStr` in the wire
  format `<vendor>:<model>` (`claude:sonnet`, `copilot:gpt-5.2`,
  `copilot:claude-opus`, ...). Unknown model strings forward as-is
  so new models surface without a Convergio release.
- `prompt::build` is the single source of truth for the agent
  contract: task metadata + optional graph context + heartbeat /
  evidence / transition / PR conventions.
- `assert_cli_on_path` fail-fast helper for routing.
- Crate `AGENTS.md` documents invariants + the
  "what this is NOT" boundary.
- `commitlint.config.js` adds `runner` to the scope-enum list.

ADR-0032 — `docs/adr/0032-vendor-cli-runners.md` — documents the
boundary (cost, auth, replaceability, what was rejected).

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all` — clean.
- `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo test -p convergio-runner` — 15 unit tests pass:
  - `RunnerKind` parse + display round-trip
  - prompt content (task id, plan breadcrumb, evidence kinds,
    graph context include/skip)
  - argv shape per vendor (model flag, `--allow-all-tools`,
    `--max-budget-usd`)
  - dispatch routing via `for_kind`
- File sizes: every new file under 260 lines.
- No subprocess execution in tests — that would tie CI to the
  operator's vendor logins and charge real money. End-to-end is
  operator-side via `cvg agent spawn` (follow-up).

## Impact

- **No public-API behaviour change** in this PR — the executor
  still uses `SpawnTemplate::default()` (echoes the task id).
  Wiring the new runner through the executor + adding `cvg agent
  spawn --task <id> --runner <kind>` is the next PR.
- **Unblocks** plan `7ec8a7f8` task `b5d211ef` (T4.01 long-running
  agent sessions) and `2e965bc7` (T4.04 multi-vendor routing) at
  the boundary level. Both still need their own implementation
  PRs but the API surface is now in place.
- **Closes** the "we have spawn primitive but no real runner"
  gap surfaced in conversation today.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #12. The `description:` frontmatter in `skills/compose-expert/SKILL.md` was **1728 chars**. Codex CLI and Copilot CLI both enforce a hard **1024-char cap** on that field and reject the manifest:

> `invalid description: exceeds maximum length of 1024 characters`

Claude Code does not enforce this cap, which is why it shipped green for us but broke for downstream Codex / Copilot installs (also confirmed by @HumboShot in the issue thread).

## What changed

- **Trimmed `description:`** to a focused 843-char pitch covering what + platforms + modes (Compose, CMP, TV, Paging 3, navigation, Review Mode, session_start auto-detection).
- **Preserved the trigger surface** in a new `## When this skill applies` section in the SKILL.md body. Body content is not subject to the 1024 cap; Claude reads it after the skill loads, so the keyword list (Compose APIs, CMP symbols, TV phrases, Paging 3, design-system phrasing, casual phrasings, Review Mode triggers, session_start) stays available for downstream context.
- **Added `scripts/check-description-length.sh`** — regression guard that asserts the field stays ≤ 1024 chars.
- **Wired the new check into both workflows** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (every PR) and `.github/workflows/release.yml` (every tag push) — so a future regression fails CI loudly instead of shipping green on Claude Code and breaking Codex / Copilot installs.
- Bumped to `2.3.1` with CHANGELOG entry.

## Local validation

```
$ bash scripts/check-versions.sh v2.3.1
OK: versions aligned at 2.3.1
$ bash scripts/validate-plugin-manifest.sh
OK: plugin manifest valid (.claude-plugin/plugin.json)
$ bash scripts/check-description-length.sh
OK: description is 843 chars (limit 1024)
```

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (manifest validator + new description-length check + version-consistency tests + manifest schema BATS)
- [ ] After merge + tag `v2.3.1`, release workflow publishes the GH Release
- [ ] Codex CLI install of `aldefy/compose-skill` no longer errors with `invalid description`
- [ ] Copilot CLI install of `aldefy/compose-skill` no longer errors with the same message

body:
## Summary
Captured a real production prompt under `--verbosity debug` and noticed the MIGRATION RULES section emits identifier guidance that's already covered three other ways in the same prompt:

- **REQUIRED TARGET COLUMN NAMES** — SMT pre-resolves every target column name via `targetIdentifier()` and tells the AI "you MUST use exactly these column names". The AI literally cannot make a column-name case error if it follows this section.
- **OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS** — gives the exact fully-qualified target table name (`Use fully qualified table name: public.tags`).
- **Target dialect's `AIPromptAugmentation`** — for postgres, covers lowercase folding, underscore preservation, CamelCase rules, examples, and double-quote semantics in more detail than the auto-generated guidance ever did.

Despite this, `writeIdentifierGuidance` was emitting a fourth source of identifier rules into the MIGRATION RULES section, derived from `TargetContext.IdentifierCase`:

```
- CRITICAL: Unquoted identifiers are folded to lowercase
- Use lowercase for all table and column names (e.g., UserId -> userid, not user_id)
- Do NOT convert to snake_case - just lowercase the original name directly
- Identifiers are case-sensitive when quoted
```

Delete `writeIdentifierGuidance` and its call site. The prompt loses 4 lines on a typical mssql -> postgres run; nothing else moves.

## Verification
- `go test -short ./...` — green
- End-to-end CRM mssql -> postgres on Sonnet 4.6 with cleared cache: 14 tables, 22 FKs, 135 checks. Identical schema to before this PR.

## Test changes
- Delete `TestWriteIdentifierGuidance_SameEngine` (it tested the now-removed function directly).
- Add `TestBuildTableDDLPrompt_NoAutoIdentifierRules` covering all 5 source/target combos that previously triggered the function. It asserts the auto-generated strings stay out of the prompt — a guard against the function quietly coming back.

## Test plan
- [x] `go test -short ./...`
- [x] `go test -run TestBuildTableDDLPrompt ./internal/driver/`
- [x] CRM mssql -> postgres end-to-end migration produces identical schema

author: xang1234
body:
The dynamic groups page was returning US data for non-US markets because the API endpoint split routing between two services:
  - US -> IBDGroupRankService (reads ibd_group_ranks, market-aware)
  - non-US -> MarketGroupRankingService (computes from feature_runs)

The non-US path was brittle: it relied on parsing
config_json["universe"]["market"] from FeatureRun records and recomputing rankings on the fly, which could silently drop or misroute data when the feature-run universe metadata diverged from what the live API expected.

IBDGroupRankService is already fully market-aware (get_current_rankings, get_rank_movers, and get_group_history all accept a market kwarg) and the calculate_daily_group_rankings task persists per-market rankings into ibd_group_ranks for HK/JP/TW/IN/KR/CN. Route the rankings/current, rankings/movers, and bootstrap endpoints (and the shared payload builder) through that service so every market reads the same persisted source.

get_group_detail still uses MarketGroupRankingService for non-US so the group detail modal keeps its market-scoped constituent stocks from the FeatureRun (IBDGroupRankService.get_group_history loads constituents from the latest scan, which is not market-scoped).

author: copilot
body:
The Workflows page (and any page rendering an `outline`-variant `AppButton`) crashed with Flutter's `!(shape != null && borderRadius != null)` assertion in `material.dart`. Flutter's `Material` widget forbids supplying both `shape` and `borderRadius` simultaneously.

## Root cause

`AppButton` unconditionally set `borderRadius` on `Material`, then conditionally also set `shape` (a `RoundedRectangleBorder`) for bordered variants — violating the mutual-exclusivity constraint.

## Fix

- **`lib/shared/widgets/app_button.dart`** — make `borderRadius` on `Material` conditional: set it only when `shape` is `null` (i.e. `side == BorderSide.none`). The radius is already encoded inside `RoundedRectangleBorder` for the bordered path, so there is no visual change.

```dart
// Before
Material(
  borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(10),   // always set
  shape: side == BorderSide.none ? null : RoundedRectangleBorder(...),

// After
Material(
  borderRadius: side == BorderSide.none ? BorderRadius.circular(10) : null,
  shape: side == BorderSide.none ? null : RoundedRectangleBorder(...),
```

body:
## Root Cause
`Kill()` called `p.shutdown(true)` directly, which races with `Run()`'s setup—specifically, `stopRenderer` blocks forever trying to send on the unbuffered `p.rendererDone` channel when the renderer goroutine hasn't started its receive loop yet. The fix makes `Kill()` only cancel the context, letting `Run()` perform cleanup itself after the event loop exits.

## Verification
- ✓ **Fix verified** — patched code passed on a clean VM
- ✓ **Replay verified** — patched code, run against the recorded crash conditions, no longer produces the original failure signature

**Verdict: Both checks passed.** The fix addresses the specific failure we captured, not just a clean-environment pass.

author: shauryam2807
body:
## Summary

The `hclust()` function in `shap/utils/_clustering.py` validates the `linkage` parameter against `("single", "complete", "average")` early in the function (line 272), but the final return block uses an `if/elif/elif` chain without a terminal `else` clause. This means the function has an implicit `None` return path at the end.

## Problem

While the early validation guard prevents unknown linkage strings at runtime, the implicit `None` return causes two issues:

1. **Type narrowing failure:** Static analysis tools (Mypy) infer the return type as `NDArray | None` instead of `NDArray`, which forces all downstream callers to handle `None` unnecessarily.
2. **Refactoring fragility:** If a new linkage type is ever added to `known_linkages` without updating the return block, the function will silently return `None` instead of raising an error.

## Fix

Added an explicit `raise AssertionError(...)` after the `if/elif/elif` chain as a defensive unreachable backstop. This:

- Allows Mypy to prove the return type is always `NDArray` (never `None`)
- Ensures any future linkage additions that miss the return block will fail loudly
- Follows existing SHAP conventions (e.g., `AssertionError` is used elsewhere in maskers and explainers)

## Testing

All 6 existing tests in `tests/utils/test_clustering.py` pass. No new test is needed since the added line is unreachable by design (guarded by the `ValueError` on line 272).

author: robbyczgw-cla
body:
## What

Adds **tool-visibility** — live tool-call previews surfaced into the chat as the agent runs (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure hooks).

## Update 2026-07-25 — resynced with three months of production use

This branch has been running as a patch on a fork since May. The skill's copy of the hook had drifted behind the version actually in use, so it has been brought back in line: `resources/tool-visibility.ts` goes from 478 to 603 lines, with tests and docs updated alongside.

The largest visible change is that **previews are now description-first**. When a tool call carries a `description`, that is what the user sees; the command summary is the fallback rather than the headline. In practice this is the difference between a chat line that reads `🖥️ bash \`cd /srv/app && node --check src/index.js\`` and one that reads `Check the parser for syntax errors`. On a phone, where most of these previews are actually read, it is the whole difference between signal and scroll.

Everything ported, with why:

- **Description-first previews** — prefer `tool_input.description`; the redundant `bash` label is gone.
- **Compact post markers** — failures render as `❌ … · reason`, slow Bash as `✓ Xs · shape`, dropping the repeated `done in` / `bash` noise.
- **Bash peek without inline code** — `N lines → peek` instead of backticks, which survives long multi-line commands intact.
- **`MAX_INPUT_PREVIEW` 80** — tuned down for narrow screens.
- **Heredoc summarizing and `bash script.sh` → basename** — a heredoc no longer floods the preview with its body.
- **Assignment-prefix handling** — a command of the shape `VAR="…" && $VAR host …` previewed only the assignment, hiding the actual command. It now skips the prefix and summarizes what runs.
- **Empty `TodoWrite` suppressed** — `todos: []` emits nothing instead of an empty bullet.
- **UTF-16-safe truncation** — previews never cut inside a surrogate pair, so an emoji cannot end up as half a character in the chat.
- **Task-session detection reads the processing batch** — `isTaskSession()` consults `processing_ack` plus `messages_in.kind` and suppresses only genuine task-only wakes. The earlier heuristic could silence a real chat turn that happened to overlap a scheduled task.

Deliberately **not** ported, because it is specific to the fork's environment rather than to the feature:

- An agent-name allowlist read from a container-local config file.
- An SSH-wrapper unwrapper tied to a local launcher and workspace paths. The generic assignment-prefix handling above covers the same class of case without hardcoding anything.
- Host-side edit coalescing, which lives in `chat-sdk-bridge.ts`. The skill ships the container hook and the `_toolVis` flag; coalescing stays out of scope.

## Conformance to the skills model

Rebuilt as a self-contained skill per `docs/skill-guidelines.md` (was previously branch-merge based):
- Self-contained `.claude/skills/add-tool-visibility/`; apply **copies files in** + makes one minimal reach-in — no branch, no `git merge`.
- **Integration point** = the `claude.ts` provider reach-in: 1 import + appending the visibility hooks to the existing PreToolUse / PostToolUse / PostToolUseFailure arrays. All logic lives in the skill's own `tool-visibility.ts`; the core edit is just the wiring.
- **Two test legs** (`bun:test`, container side, shipped with the skill):
  - *AST wiring test* — asserts the import + all three hook-array memberships + ordering (visibility hook after the core hook). Goes red if the reach-in is deleted or drifts.
  - *Behavior test* — drives the real hooks against real in-memory session DBs (the hooks do raw SQL against inbound/outbound), catching core-consumption drift a typecheck can't.
- **REMOVE.md** reverses everything (hook file, test, import line, the three array appends). Apply is idempotent (re-run guarded). No VERIFY.md.

## Test evidence

Current run, after the resync: **18/18 tests pass across the two skill test files** (`45 expect() calls`, 694 ms), and `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exits 0. New coverage added for the description-first path, the empty-`TodoWrite` suppression, and the task-only batch — including the case that previously misfired, where a mid-turn task row that is not in `processing_ack` must **not** silence a chat turn.

Earlier evidence from the original submission still holds: apply on clean `main` → `bun test` 108/108, container `tsc` clean; negative-probe verified (removing the hooks → 3 tests red; removing the import → wiring test + `tsc` red; restore → green); REMOVE → `git status` clean; apply twice → exactly one import and one set of hook entries.

author: centralkindom1
body:
This PR provides a complete translation solution for Microsoft Excel 2007 users, leveraging the Qwen Plus (DashScope) large language model.

Key features:
1. **Bidirectional Translation**: Automatically detects source language (Chinese/English) and translates to the other.
2. **Bulk Processing**: Efficiently translates large selections with progress tracking in the status bar and UI responsiveness (DoEvents).
3. **UDF Support**: Users can use `=QWEN_TRANSLATE(cell)` directly in Excel formulas.
4. **Caching Layer**: Stores translation results in a session-level dictionary to avoid redundant API calls and reduce costs.
5. **Excel 2007 Optimized**: Uses Late Binding and ADODB.Stream to ensure compatibility without requiring manual reference setting in many cases (though recommended for best results).
6. **Robust JSON/UTF-8 Handling**: Custom escaping and BOM-stripping logic ensures reliable communication with the DashScope API even with complex Unicode characters.

Files included:
- `QwenTranslator.bas`: Main logic, API interaction, and UI integration.
- `JsonConverter.bas`: Optimized JSON parser for VBA.
- `README.md`: Overview and quick start.
- `INSTALL_GUIDE_ZH.md`: Detailed step-by-step setup for Office 2007 users.

author: mizuidekazuhiro
body:
### Motivation
- The pipeline treated any non-zero `article_count` as grounds to fail when `fetch_success_count==0`, which is incorrect after `NIKKEI_SKIP_EXISTING_NOTION_URLS=true` because many articles may be skipped and not actually targeted for fetch. 
- Make fetch outcome decision based on the actual attempted targets (`target_count`) and provide clear, machine-readable diagnostics to investigate failures (especially `empty_body` cases).
- Improve observability so a single skipped-or-empty article does not make the whole run appear as a systemic failure.

### Description
- Produce a fetch summary file `logs/nikkei_fetch_summary.json` in `scripts/nikkei_fetch_articles_full.py` containing `raw_article_count`, `pre_excluded_count`, `article_count_after_pre_filter`, `article_count`, `existing_url_skip_count`, `target_count`, `fetch_success_count`, `fetch_failed_count`, `empty_body_count`, `login_wall_count`, `paid_wall_count`, `access_denied_count`, `timeout_count`, `failure_reason_counts`, `failed_json_path`, and `failed_artifacts_dir`.
- Enrich failure records written to `logs/nikkei_articles_failed.json` with investigation fields: `title`, `final_url`, `reason`, `body_length`, selector candidate info, `resource_block_enabled`, `retried_without_resource_block`, and artifact paths (`html_path`, `screenshot_path`, `text_path`), and leave `status_code` (if unavailable) as `None`.
- Change pipeline gating in `scripts/run_nikkei_paper_pipeline.py` to read the summary and decide based on `target_count` (via new `should_fail_fetch`), with special handling: `target_count==0` logs an info and skips save without error; partial failures log a warning and continue with successful articles; complete failure for `target_count>0` and `fetch_success_count==0` honors `NIKKEI_ALLOW_EMPTY_FETCH`.
- Add unit tests `tests/test_run_nikkei_paper_pipeline.py` covering `target_count==0` success, `target_count>0 && success==0` with `NIKKEI_ALLOW_EMPTY_FETCH` on/off, partial success continuation, and regression that avoids failing based only on `article_count`.
- Maintained existing behaviors (direct issue URL usage, pre-title filter, skip-existing logic, scoring/notion update flags); the change only re-keys failure gating and reporting. The requested deeper retry strategies (explicit `domcontentloaded`/`networkidle` toggles and JSON-LD/meta fallback extraction) were not added beyond the existing retry-without-resource-block and multi-selector extraction improvements.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall scripts src` to validate syntax and byte-compile the modified scripts, which succeeded.
- Ran `pytest -q tests/test_run_nikkei_paper_pipeline.py`, and all tests passed (`5 passed`).

author: ishou
body:
## Why

Two follow-ups to PR #176 on the multiplayer grid:

1. **Lag during zoom/pan.** PR #176 added a `visualViewport.resize`/`scroll` listener in `Grid.tsx` that recomputes the wrapper's `maxHeight` on every event. iOS dispatches those at ~60Hz during a pinch, so we measured `getBoundingClientRect()` + updated inline style + triggered React state sync per frame.
2. **iOS focus-snap during pinch.** iOS Safari has a native behavior: when an `<input>` is focused, it auto-scrolls / zooms to keep it in the viewport during ANY layout change, including the JS-driven CSS transform the library applies during a gesture. Android Chrome doesn't fight the gesture as aggressively. (Distinct from `scheduleVisibleScroll`, which PR #176 already fixed.)

## What

**Fix #1 — rAF-throttle the keyboard-aware resize listener.** Existing `resize`/`scroll` handler now coalesces bursts to one measurement per animation frame: the first event schedules a `requestAnimationFrame`, subsequent events in the same frame are no-ops. Cleanup cancels any in-flight frame so a torn-down component never receives a stale `setState`. Initial sync measurement preserved on mount.

**Fix #2 — blur on pinch/pan, restore on end.** `<TransformWrapper>`'s `onZoomStart` / `onZoomStop` / `onPanningStart` / `onPanningStop` are wired so:
- On gesture start, if `document.activeElement` is a grid cell input, record its `(row, col)` and blur it.
- On gesture stop (when both flags clear — handles iOS chaining pinch → pan), restore focus iff the user didn't tap a different cell during the gesture window.
- A capture-phase `focusin` listener on the grid frame sets the "user tapped during gesture" flag, dropping the restore intent so we don't yank focus from their new target.

Refs only — no React state, no re-renders during the gesture. The hook (`useGridNavigation`) doesn't change.

User-facing iOS behavior: during a pinch the keyboard collapses, the cell loses focus; on gesture end the cell regains focus and the keyboard reopens — user is done gesturing and can resume typing.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` clean
- [x] `pnpm test` — 275/276 pass; sole failure is the documented pre-existing `tests/http-puzzle-repository.test.ts` (`puzzle.width === 5` vs the 10×10 fixture from #106).
- [x] `pnpm build` clean
- [x] New regression: rAF throttle — dispatch 5 synthetic `resize` events in one tick, assert exactly one `getBoundingClientRect` call after the rAF flushes.
- [x] New regression: rAF cancel-on-unmount — schedule rAF, unmount, assert no deferred measurement runs.
- [x] New regression: blur-on-zoom-start, restore-on-zoom-stop.
- [x] New regression: blur-on-pan-start, restore-on-pan-stop.
- [x] New regression: don't restore if user taps a different cell mid-gesture.
- [x] New regression: no-op when no cell was focused at gesture start.
- [x] New regression: chained pinch+pan keeps cell blurred until BOTH flags clear.
- [ ] Manual on iOS Safari: pinch a 10×10 grid — keyboard collapses, no focus-snap fight, smooth gesture; on lift, cell regains focus and keyboard reopens.
- [ ] Manual on Android Chrome: same gesture, no behavior regression (blur is a no-op there).

Solo mode unchanged when no zoom and no keyboard are active.

author: rudolfschmidt
body:
## Summary

Real-world IMAP servers (Dovecot, Cyrus) regularly emit 8-bit bytes in BODYSTRUCTURE responses — typically MIME filenames in non-UTF-8 encodings like Latin-1 or ISO-8859-9 (e.g. Turkish `Görüntü1.png` from Outlook). The current strict 7-bit ASCII parser rejects these, breaking the parse of a single bad mail and desyncing the entire bulk fetch stream — taking down all subsequent FETCH responses in the same buffer.

Two changes:

1. **`is_char` relaxed to accept any non-NUL byte** instead of `0x01..=0x7F`. Matches real-world server behavior; RFC 6855 / IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051) formally allow UTF-8 in these positions.

2. **`*_utf8` functions return `Cow<'_, str>` with lossy decoding** instead of `&str` with strict `from_utf8`. Affected: `string_utf8`, `nstring_utf8`, `astring_utf8`, `quoted_utf8`, `text`, plus `mailbox`, `resp_text`, `trailing_resp_text`, `mailbox_list`, `id_param`, `id_param_list_not_nil`, `id_param_list`. Callers that previously wrapped `&str` results in `Cow::Borrowed` have been simplified.

**Note**: this is a public-API change (`&str` → `Cow<'_, str>` in the `*_utf8` functions). I think it's the right tradeoff — strict UTF-8 enforcement at the parser level is too strict for real-world IMAP — but happy to discuss alternatives (e.g. parallel `*_lossy` variants, or `unsafe { from_utf8_unchecked }` to keep `&str` API).

## Reproduction

A BODYSTRUCTURE with an 8-bit filename literal:

```
* 15 FETCH (BODYSTRUCTURE ("image" "png" ("name" {8}\r\n<G><F6><r><FC><n><t><FC>1) ...
```

Where the 8 bytes after `{8}\r\n` are `0x47 0xF6 0x72 0xFC 0x6E 0x74 0xFC 0x31` (Turkish `Görüntü1` in Latin-1, valid IMAP literal but not valid UTF-8).

On master this fails with `code: TakeWhile1` because:
- `quoted` parser uses `take_while1(is_text_char)` which rejects bytes `>= 0x80`
- Even when `quoted` succeeds, `from_utf8` in `string_utf8` fails on Latin-1 sequences

With the fix the parser proceeds and the filename is decoded lossily (replacement chars for invalid UTF-8 sequences).

## Test plan

- [x] All 82 existing `imap-proto` tests pass
- [x] New regression test `test_body_structure_with_8bit_literal_filename` passes with the fix
- [x] Same test reverted-to-master state fails with the exact `TakeWhile1` error from the field bug report

Run:

```
cargo test -p imap-proto
```

body:
### Motivation
- Fleet disposals were hardcoded to a 24-month lag causing incorrect values in `Fleet_Schedule` and downstream sheets, so disposals must follow the `Vehicle disposal trigger` assumption from the `Assumptions` sheet. 
- Downstream sheets (`Cash_Flow`, `Income_Statement`, `Balance_Sheet`, `Loan_Amortisation`) must therefore reflect disposal timing consistently via the regenerated fleet schedule.

### Description
- Added a new assumption mapping `"vehicle_disposal_trigger": "Vehicle disposal trigger"` and made it required in `REQUIRED_ASSUMPTION_LABELS` in `scripts/python_financial_projection_model.py`.
- Extended the `Assumptions` dataclass and `build_assumptions` to expose `vehicle_disposal_trigger_years` (integer) from the assumptions sheet.
- Replaced hardcoded 24-month disposal lag with `disposal_lag_months = int(a.vehicle_disposal_trigger_years * 12)` in `recalculate_fleet_rows`, and schedule disposals using that computed lag so fleet counts are generated according to the assumption.
- Updated `write_fleet_schedule` to use the same `disposal_lag_months` when populating the `Cars Disposed (end of month)` and `Total Cars Disposed (Cummulative)` columns so sheet output ties to the assumption and downstream pipeline recalculations.

### Testing
- Executed the projection script as an automated run (`python scripts/python_financial_projection_model.py --input data/financial_projections.xlsx --output data/financial_projections_final.xlsx`), which failed in this environment due to a missing dependency: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openpyxl'`.
- No unit tests were present or run in this change set; changes were committed after local edits to `scripts/python_financial_projection_model.py`.
