author: flpanbin
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind e2e-test


---

### Motivation

Currently, cloudtty lacks end-to-end tests.  This makes it difficult to catch regressions in critical lifecycle logic such as CloudShell reconciliation, WorkerPool binding, TTL cleanup, and kubeconfig generation.

This PR introduces a comprehensive e2e test suite based on **Ginkgo v2 + Gomega**, running against a real **Kind** cluster via **Helm** deployment.

### What this PR does

1. **Introduces e2e test framework** (`test/e2e/`)
   - Ginkgo v2 + Gomega as the BDD framework
   - `BeforeSuite` builds & loads images into Kind, installs operator via Helm, and waits for Deployment readiness
   - `AfterSuite` uninstalls the operator
   - `JustAfterEach` automatically collects operator logs on failure for debugging

2. **Adds e2e test utilities** (`test/e2e/utils.go`)
   - `buildDockerImage` / `loadImageToKind` — image lifecycle management
   - `installOperator` / `uninstallOperator` — Helm wrapper
   - `portForwardPod` / `portForwardService` — kubectl port-forward with TCP health checks
   - `getPodLogs` — fetch operator logs via client-go

3. **Adds 11 e2e test specs** covering:

   | Test File | Spec | Scenario |
   |-----------|------|----------|
   | `operator_test.go` | Deployment Ready | Verify operator Deployment and Pods are running after Helm install |
   | `cloudshell_basic_test.go` | Create & Reconcile | Create CloudShell → Worker Pod Running → NodePort Service → Status Ready → HTTP 200 via port-forward |
   | `cloudshell_basic_test.go` | Delete & Cleanup | Delete CR → associated Service & Worker Pod are cleaned up |
   | `cloudshell_ttl_test.go` | TTL Auto-Delete (cleanup=true) | TTL=30s + Cleanup=true → CR is automatically deleted after expiry |
   | `cloudshell_ttl_test.go` | TTL Complete (cleanup=false) | TTL=30s + Cleanup=false → Status.Phase becomes Complete |
   | `cloudshell_kubeconfig_test.go` | Auto-generate Secret | Create CloudShell without SecretRef → controller auto-generates kubeconfig Secret |
   | `cloudshell_kubeconfig_test.go` | Missing Secret | Reference a non-existent Secret → CloudShell stays not-ready |
   | `cloudshell_exposure_test.go` | Default NodePort | Create CloudShell without ExposeMode → defaults to NodePort Service |
   | `workerpool_test.go` | Worker Creation | Create CloudShell → WorkerPool creates and binds a Worker Pod |
   | `workerpool_test.go` | Worker Label Reset | Delete CloudShell → Worker label `worker.cloudtty.io/owner-name` resets to empty |

4. **CI integration** (`.github/workflows/e2e.yaml`)
   - Runs on PR to `main` branch
   - Creates Kind cluster via `helm/kind-action`
   - Builds & loads images, runs e2e tests
   - Exports Kind logs as artifacts on failure

5. **Makefile targets**
   - `make test-e2e` — run e2e tests against an existing Kind cluster
   - `make kind-create` / `make kind-delete` — cluster lifecycle
   - `make local-e2e-test` — one-shot local e2e (create cluster → build → test)

### Notes

- Each test uses a **unique namespace** (`GenerateName`) to avoid conflicts from parallel or repeated runs
- Docker image build is skipped if the image already exists locally (handles environments without Docker Hub access)
- The ClusterIP exposure mode is not tested because the current controller implementation does not create a Service for `ClusterIP` mode (only `NodePort` and `Ingress` are supported)

---

author: keren-tevet
body:
## Summary

The `HOST` constant (used in the `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` endpoint) was hardcoded to `https://mcp.aiven.live`. This causes Cursor to reject connections when the server is accessed through a different domain, since it validates that the advertised resource URL matches the URL it connected to.

This PR makes it configurable via `MCP_HOST` env var — default remains `https://mcp.aiven.live` so there is no change for existing deployments.

Two use cases:
1. Testing (immediate need) — deploy the same mcp-aiven image behind a different domain (e.g. mcp.tunemysql.com) and have the OAuth resource URL match, so clients like Cursor don't reject it.
2. Self-hosted MCP server (future) — if a customer wants to run their own instance of mcp-aiven behind their own domain (e.g. mcp.acme.com), they just set MCP_HOST env var to https://mcp.acme.com and everything works — the OAuth metadata advertises the right URL, clients connect without security errors.

## Changes

- `src/config.ts` — `HOST` now reads from `process.env['MCP_HOST'] ?? 'https://mcp.aiven.live'`
- `README.md` — documents the new env var


Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

author: dpearson2699
body:
## Linked Issue

Fixes #567

## What

Adds explicit QA pending reason plumbing so `/vbw:vibe` explains why it is rerunning QA when a visible verification artifact looks clean. The change updates `scripts/phase-detect.sh` to emit `qa_reason` and `qa_attention_reason`, aligns `scripts/qa-result-gate.sh` with the same legacy `status:` fallback / `result:` precedence rules, and updates `/vbw:vibe` plus phase-detection docs/contracts to surface resolved reason labels instead of a generic “QA is pending” message.

## Why

The root cause was that phase detection collapsed distinct states into `qa_status=pending`: missing artifacts, malformed or legacy frontmatter, deterministic gate rerun requests, and stale PASS artifacts all looked identical. Older verification artifacts also used `status: PASS`, while phase detection only read `result:`. The durable fix is to make phase-detect return both state and reason from one assessment path, and to keep result parsing semantics consistent between phase-detect and the deterministic gate.

## How

- `scripts/phase-detect.sh` — adds frontmatter helpers, legacy `status:` fallback only when `result:` is absent, `phase_verification_assessment()` state+reason output, and final `qa_reason` / `qa_attention_reason` fields.
- `scripts/qa-result-gate.sh` — mirrors `result:` precedence and legacy `status:` fallback, then normalizes semantic result values before routing so mixed/lowercase PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL values do not cause false QA reruns.
- `commands/vibe.md` — maps reason tokens to concise user-facing labels before spawning QA, and the routing table now references the resolved reason label rather than raw `qa_reason`.
- `references/phase-detection.md` — documents result/status precedence and all QA reason tokens.
- `testing/verify-commands-contract.sh` — locks in `/vbw:vibe` reason-field guidance, resolved-label wording, and literal phase-detection docs using fixed-string checks.
- `tests/phase-detect.bats` — covers missing artifacts, legacy PASS/PARTIAL, result precedence, stale reasons, dirty tree reasons, QA attention retarget reason propagation, and modern PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL behavior.
- `tests/qa-result-gate.bats` — covers gate-level legacy fallback, result precedence, blank result non-fallback behavior, and mixed/lowercase semantic result normalization.

## Acceptance criteria verification

1. Legacy `status: PASS` counts as PASS — satisfied by `scripts/phase-detect.sh`, `scripts/qa-result-gate.sh`, `tests/phase-detect.bats`, and `tests/qa-result-gate.bats`.
2. `result:` is authoritative over `status:` — satisfied by shared precedence behavior and conflicting/blank result tests.
3. Modern `result: PASS|FAIL|PARTIAL` behavior remains unchanged — satisfied by phase-detect and gate PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL tests.
4. `qa_reason` and `qa_attention_reason` are emitted — satisfied by `scripts/phase-detect.sh` final output and tests asserting missing/stale/dirty/gate reasons.
5. Parse/missing cases are distinct from stale cases — satisfied by `missing_verification_artifact`, `verification_result_missing`, `verification_result_unrecognized`, and freshness-token tests.
6. `/vbw:vibe` explains pending QA — satisfied by `commands/vibe.md` reason-label mapping and command contract coverage.
7. Wording does not blame `qa-result-gate.sh` for stale artifacts — satisfied by separate labels for gate rerun vs freshness reasons.
8. BATS coverage verifies required behavior — satisfied by `tests/phase-detect.bats` and `tests/qa-result-gate.bats`, including QA round and Copilot-review coverage additions.
9. Debug-target scenario reports clean remediated or stale with explicit reason — satisfied by the state+reason assessment path and terminal-UAT attention retarget tests.
10. `bash testing/run-all.sh` passes — validated locally and in CI.

## Testing

- [x] `bats tests/qa-result-gate.bats` — 167 tests, 0 failures.
- [x] `bats tests/phase-detect.bats` — 133 tests, 0 failures.
- [x] `bash testing/verify-commands-contract.sh` — 470 pass, 0 fail.
- [x] `bash testing/run-lint.sh` — passed.
- [x] `bash testing/run-all.sh` — lint 1/1, contracts 49/49, BATS 3260 passed / 0 failed.
- [x] GitHub Actions on `d0c880763d0574be1bdd04ccf1a190dab9e8ea38` — CI_GREEN, all 18 checks passed.

## QA summary

- Primary QA round 1 (`qa-investigator`): one low contract finding — missing phase-detect PARTIAL coverage. Fixed in `8a98990c`.
- Primary QA round 2 (`qa-investigator`): clean, no legitimate findings. Evidence commit `edd6452a`.
- Cross-model QA: skipped because this session is not Opus-class; no eligible different-family cross-model target under the workflow gate.
- Copilot PR review round 1: `COMMENTED`, four legitimate findings. Fixed in `f529278e`.
- Copilot PR review round 2: `COMMENTED`, one legitimate contract-test hardening finding. Fixed in `d0c88076`.
- Copilot PR review round 3: `COMMENTED`, no new comments; zero unresolved Copilot-authored review threads.
- False positives: none.

The `recharts ^2.15.4 → ^3.8.1` bump in #4 broke `src/components/ui/chart.tsx` (5 TS errors) and 4 chart tests in `src/components/ui/shadcn-primitives.test.tsx`, since v3 retypes the `Tooltip` / `Legend` `payload` and `label` props. Re-pinning is the minimal fix and matches what upstream `smackypants/TrueAI` ships.

### Changes

- **`package.json`** — `"recharts": "^3.8.1"` → `"^2.15.4"`.
- **`package-lock.json`** — regenerated via `npm install` (recharts v2 dependency tree restored).

### Out of scope / follow-ups

- Migrating `chart.tsx` to the recharts v3 API (Option B in the analysis). Recommend copying the v3-compatible primitive from upstream shadcn/ui rather than hand-porting types.
- 126 pre-existing lint warnings inherited from upstream — unchanged by this PR.

### Reviewer note

The Code Review tool flags `@wllama/wllama` as missing a caret in `package-lock.json`. That is intentional: `package.json` pins it to exact `2.4.0` per upstream PR #158's "pin wllama" review fix. No change.

## Lessons learned

- Dependabot major bumps of UI libs need `build:dev` + `test` to gate merge; `npm ci` alone passed here because the type breakage only surfaces in `tsc -b`.
- `@wllama/wllama` is intentionally exact-pinned — don't "fix" the missing caret.
- When `chart.tsx` migration is taken on, prefer wholesale-copying the current shadcn/ui v3 primitive over a hand port.

author: jasnez
body:
## Summary

Pure-TypeScript algorithm that takes the user's last 6 months of transactions and emits candidate recurring charges (subscriptions, rent, insurance, etc.). The DB persistence layer arrives in T2 — this module is intentionally side-effect-free aside from the read.

Most ambitious task in Faza 3 by design. Heavy commit-message documentation + 53 tests because the formula will be tuned with real data once T3 ships.

### Algorithm summary

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Direction** | Outflows only (T1) | Payroll/refunds = T2 expansion if needed |
| **Grouping key** | `merchant_id ?? normalize_description` + `currency` | Account-id agnostic so a sub survives bank switch; currency in key so BAM-NETFLIX ≠ EUR-NETFLIX |
| **Period detection** | Median pairwise interval into 5 buckets (weekly/bi-weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly) | Bi-monthly (~60d) deliberately skipped — extremely rare |
| **Period strictness** | 1.0 if ≥60% of intervals fit bucket, else 0.5 | Resists 4-monthly + 3-weekly mix slipping through |
| **Confidence formula** | `0.30·occ + 0.30·intervalCV + 0.25·amountCV + 0.15·periodMatch` | Weighted blend, all components clamped 0..1 |
| **Min thresholds** | 3 occurrences, 30-day span, 5 KM amount | Prevents single-cluster + coffee-money false positives |
| **Return threshold** | confidence ≥ 0.5 | UI tier-marks ≥ 0.7 as "high" |
| **SQL vs TS** | TS in-memory | 5k tx ~ 180ms; trivial to iterate formula in dev |

### Functional decomposition (all exported, all isolation-tested)

- `passesGlobalFilters(row)`
- `groupTransactions(rows)` → `Map<key, rows>`
- `filterIntraGroupNoise(group)` — drops groups with > 50% same-day duplicates; otherwise dedupes by created_at
- `analyzeIntervals(dates)` → `{ intervals, median, mean, cv }`
- `analyzeAmounts(amounts)` → `{ median, meanAbs, cv }`
- `classifyPeriod(intervals)` → `{ period, matchStrictness } | null`
- `computeConfidence({ occurrences, intervalCV, amountCV, periodMatch })`
- `predictNext(lastSeen, period)` → `Date`
- `buildCandidate(args)` → `RecurringCandidate`
- `runDetectionPipeline(rows)` → `RecurringCandidate[]`
- `detectRecurring(supabase, userId)` → `Promise<RecurringCandidate[]>` (public entry)

### `RecurringCandidate` shape
```ts
{ groupKey, merchantId, description, period, averageAmountCents (bigint),
  currency, lastSeen, nextExpected, confidence, occurrences,
  transactionIds, suggestedCategoryId }
```

## Test plan
- [x] **53 tests, all passing** — 8 backlog acceptance scenarios + 9 robustness extensions + ~36 isolation cases
- [x] Performance verified across 3 runs: 5000 mixed transactions → ~150–200ms (budget: 500ms)

author: ibbybuilds
body:
## Summary Multi-pod deployments (Kubernetes etc.) suffer when every replica boots and tries to run `alembic upgrade head` in parallel. Each pod queues on Alembic's advisory lock and probes time out before startup completes, producing a restart-loop cascade on every release. Reported by Shariq in Discord. This PR ships two complementary fixes plus the CLI escape hatch needed to use them. ### 1. `RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_STARTUP` flag New `AppSettings.RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_STARTUP: bool = True`. Default keeps current behavior so dev / single-pod / docker-compose users notice nothing. Set to `false` in multi-pod deployments and run migrations out-of-band. ### 2. Lock-free fast path `run_migrations_if_needed()` first reads the current revision via a short-lived sync engine and compares against the script directory head. If they match — the steady-state case once a release has rolled — it returns without ever acquiring the alembic advisory lock. Falls back to the full upgrade path on first install (no `alembic_version` row yet) or any precheck error. Net effect on a 10-replica rolling deploy where the schema is already at head: lock-free skip on every pod, ~50ms each instead of 1-2s queueing per pod. ### 3. `aegra db` CLI re-registered The `aegra db upgrade | downgrade | current | history` group was already in the codebase but unhooked since v0.5.x. Re-registered so operators have a first-class command for out-of-band migrations (init containers, Helm pre-upgrade Jobs, deploy scripts). ## Files - `libs/aegra-api/src/aegra_api/core/migrations.py` — new `_is_database_up_to_date` helper + `run_migrations_if_needed` fast path. `run_migrations` retained for unconditional/explicit use. - `libs/aegra-api/src/aegra_api/main.py` — lifespan respects the flag. - `libs/aegra-api/src/aegra_api/settings.py` — new field with prose explaining when to flip it. - `libs/aegra-cli/src/aegra_cli/cli.py` + `commands/db.py` — re-register `aegra db` group, drop stale "removed in v0.5.x" comment. - `.env.example` + CLI scaffold env template — both updated together per CLAUDE.md sync rule. - `docs/guides/deployment.mdx` — new "Multi-pod (Kubernetes, etc.)" section under Migrations + new troubleshooting accordion for restart-loop on rolling deploy. ## Tests - `tests/unit/test_migrations.py` — new `TestRunMigrationsIfNeeded` (skip when at head, run on drift, fallback when precheck raises) and `TestIsDatabaseUpToDate` (head match, head mismatch, no current revision, engine.dispose called on failure). Updated existing async-thread test to assert dispatch to the lock-free helper. - `tests/unit/test_main.py` — two new lifespan tests asserting flag-on still calls migrations and flag-off skips them while keeping the rest of startup intact. - Full regression: 1208 unit+integration aegra-api tests + 181 aegra-cli tests, all pass. ## Migration path for operators For Kubernetes deployments hitting the issue today: \`\`\`bash # pod env RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_STARTUP=false \`\`\` Then run once per release via Helm pre-upgrade Job, init container, or CI step: \`\`\`bash aegra db upgrade \`\`\` Single-pod and docker-compose users don't need to change anything. ## Test plan - [x] `make lint` clean - [x] Full unit + integration regression green (1208 + 181) - [ ] Smoke: run a real `docker compose up` against a clean DB with the flag default-on, verify migrations apply - [ ] Smoke: re-run with the flag off, verify no migration log lines and that `aegra db upgrade` works against the live DB ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_STARTUP to toggle automatic DB migrations on startup. * Added an aegra db CLI command to run migrations out-of-band. * Startup now skips migration work when the database is already at the latest revision to speed startup. * **Documentation** * Expanded deployment guide with Kubernetes multi-pod guidance, troubleshooting for migration lock races, and examples for out-of-band migration workflows. * Added commented "Migrations" section to env example and repository DB/migrations guidance. * **Tests** * Added unit tests covering startup migration gating and conditional migration precheck behavior.

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces a `RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_STARTUP` flag, a lock-free fast-path (`_is_database_up_to_date`) that queries `alembic_version` directly via psycopg to avoid Alembic's advisory lock in steady-state, and re-registers the `aegra db` CLI group for out-of-band migration control. The implementation correctly follows the two-URL CLAUDE.md invariant, previous review issues (MigrationContext bypass, `None` head, stale docstrings) have been addressed, and the test coverage is thorough. The one outstanding concern from a prior review — `aegra db upgrade --env-file .env` silently ignores the provided env file because `settings` is instantiated at `cli.py` import time before `load_env_file` runs — remains unaddressed in this PR.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge for the startup migration path; the outstanding `--env-file` P1 from the previous review remains open and should be tracked before `aegra db upgrade --env-file` is relied upon in production. All previously flagged P1s (MigrationContext AttributeError, None head short-circuit, stale docstrings) were addressed in follow-up commits. The lock-free fast-path implementation correctly follows the two-URL CLAUDE.md invariant and is well-tested. Score is capped at 4 because the known `--env-file` P1 — where `settings` is instantiated before `load_env_file` runs, causing `aegra db upgrade --env-file .env` to silently migrate the wrong database — is still unresolved in this PR. libs/aegra-cli/src/aegra_cli/commands/db.py — the `--env-file` option has no effect on the database URL due to early `settings` instantiation at import time.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | libs/aegra-api/src/aegra_api/core/migrations.py | Adds `_is_database_up_to_date` (queries `alembic_version` directly via psycopg, bypassing MigrationContext and SQLAlchemy URL parsing) and `run_migrations_if_needed` fast path; previous issues all addressed. | | libs/aegra-cli/src/aegra_cli/commands/db.py | Re-registers `aegra db` CLI group; `--env-file` option still cannot affect `settings.db.database_url` because `settings` is instantiated at module import time before `load_env_file` runs (known P1 flagged in previous review, not yet fixed). | | libs/aegra-api/src/aegra_api/main.py | Lifespan correctly gates `run_migrations_async()` behind `settings.app.RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_STARTUP`; stale doc comment was addressed in prior commits. | | libs/aegra-api/src/aegra_api/settings.py | Adds `RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_STARTUP: bool = True` with clear inline documentation; default-on preserves backward compatibility. | | libs/aegra-api/tests/unit/test_migrations.py | Comprehensive new test classes for `_is_database_up_to_date` and `run_migrations_if_needed`, including multi-host URL assertion per CLAUDE.md guidance. | | libs/aegra-api/tests/unit/test_main.py | Two new lifespan tests verify flag-off skips migrations while keeping rest of startup intact; flag-on asserts `run_migrations_async` is called. | | libs/aegra-cli/src/aegra_cli/cli.py | Adds `cli.add_command(db)` to re-register the `aegra db` group; import of `db` triggers early `settings` instantiation which undermines `--env-file` in subcommands. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant FastAPI as FastAPI lifespan participant Settings as settings.app participant MIF as run_migrations_if_needed() participant IDUD as _is_database_up_to_date() participant PG as Postgres (psycopg) participant Alembic as alembic command.upgrade FastAPI->>Settings: RUN_MIGRAT

author: lipkau
body:
## Summary

Closes #519.

`New-JiraIssue`, `Set-JiraIssue`, and `Invoke-JiraIssueTransition` previously resolved every `-Fields` entry against the full global field catalogue (`Get-JiraField`). This caused incorrect ambiguity errors when a Jira instance had two custom fields with the same display name in different projects, because the global catalogue contained both.

This PR resolves `-Fields` entries against the narrowest available metadata first — create metadata, edit metadata, or transition-screen metadata — and only falls back to `Get-JiraField` for keys absent from the scoped set. This eliminates the spurious ambiguity in the common case because each scoped metadata response is constrained to the fields actually on the relevant screen.

## Changes

### New private function
- **`JiraPS/Private/Resolve-JiraField.ps1`** — implements the 9-step field resolution order (scoped-by-ID → scoped-by-numeric-ID → scoped-by-name → fallback-by-ID → fallback-by-numeric-ID → fallback-by-name → error). Callers are responsible for lazily fetching the fallback catalogue; the function itself is pure.

### Updated cmdlets
- **`New-JiraIssue`** — reuses `$createmeta` (already in scope from required-field validation) for scoped resolution; fallback is lazy-fetched only if needed.
- **`Set-JiraIssue`** — fetches `Get-JiraIssueEditMetadata` for scoped resolution; fallback is lazy-fetched only if needed.
- **`Invoke-JiraIssueTransition`** — fetches transition-screen fields via `GET …/transitions?expand=transitions.fields&transitionId=…` for scoped resolution; fallback is lazy-fetched only if needed.

### `Get-JiraIssueCreateMetadata` Cloud fix
- Uses the REST API v3 endpoint on Jira Cloud (v2 `createmeta` is deprecated there). Data Center continues to use v2.

### Tests
- `Tests/Functions/Private/Resolve-JiraField.Unit.Tests.ps1` — 8 tests covering all resolution paths and error cases.
- `Tests/Functions/Public/Get-JiraIssueCreateMetadata.Unit.Tests.ps1` — added Data Center (v2) and Cloud (v3) URI assertions.
- `Tests/Functions/Public/Invoke-JiraIssueTransition.Unit.Tests.ps1` — added "Field Resolution" describe block; added query-param assertion for `expand` and `transitionId`.
- `Tests/Functions/Public/New-JiraIssue.Unit.Tests.ps1` — added "Field Resolution" describe block.
- `Tests/Functions/Public/Set-JiraIssue.Unit.Tests.ps1` — added "Field Resolution" describe block.

### Docs
- Updated `-Fields` parameter help for `New-JiraIssue`, `Set-JiraIssue`, and `Invoke-JiraIssueTransition` to describe the scoped-first resolution behaviour.

## Summary

P0 user-blocking fix. Dev server on main throws `PrismaClientKnownRequestError: The table 'main.User' does not exist` even though `prisma/dev.db` is intact with all 8 tables and rows.

**Root cause**: `lsof` showed the dev server held an fd into `node_modules/.prisma/client/dev.db` (0 bytes) instead of `prisma/dev.db` (2.3 MB). Next 16 + Turbopack drift the Prisma engine subprocess CWD, so `file:./dev.db` (relative) resolves into the generated-client directory and Prisma auto-creates an empty SQLite file there.

**Fix**: `src/lib/db/prisma.ts` now normalizes `DATABASE_URL` at module load — relative `file:` URLs are resolved against `process.cwd()` (project root) and rewritten to absolute before `new PrismaClient()`. Self-healing, idempotent, no-op for absolute paths and non-sqlite providers. Warns if a rogue empty DB is found at the wrong CWD.

Same workspace-root inference class as TM-76 (worktree DB drift) and TM-87 (worktree prisma-client cross-poll). Main was the last place still on relative `file:./dev.db`.

author: copilot
body:
The question was whether `statuses: write` could be replaced with `checks: write` as the minimum job permission for Super-Linter.

Inspecting the v8.6.0 source directly: `lib/linter.sh` constructs `GITHUB_STATUS_URL` as `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{sha}` and `lib/functions/output.sh` posts to it via `CreateGitHubCommitStatus`. This is the **Commit Statuses API** — Super-Linter never touches the Checks API.

- `statuses: write` — required; keeps the existing permission unchanged
- `checks: write` — would be insufficient; Super-Linter doesn't use the Checks API

Updated the comment on `statuses: write` to document this so future readers don't repeat the investigation:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: read
  # Required: super-linter uses the GitHub Commit Statuses API
  # (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{sha}), not the Checks API,
  # so statuses:write is the correct minimum permission (not checks:write)
  statuses: write
```

author: steve-iata
body:
## Summary

Implements the first half of [#14](https://github.com/aerotoysio/documentforge/issues/14) — cross-shard transactions via two-phase commit. Brings `cluster.BeginTransaction()` from "single-node only" to "works across shards with crash recovery."

The acceptance criteria from the issue are substantially met by this PR. Phase D (timeouts) and Phase E (HTTP wire ops + operator endpoints + metrics) follow in separate PRs.

## What ships

| Phase | Commit | What |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | `afa54ed` | `cluster.BeginTransaction()` API + single-shard fast path. Multi-shard threw `NotImplementedException`. |
| **B.1** | `2418554` | Participant `PREPARE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK` on `IShardTransport`. `{db}.prepared.log` for durability. Worker-thread actor holds the existing `ReaderWriterLockSlim` write lock continuously across PREPARE→resolve (works around RWS thread-affinity; hot path bytewise unchanged). |
| **B.2** | `d056e09` | Cluster-side coordinator. `ClusterTransaction.Commit` for >1 participants drives sequential PREPARE → COMMIT/ROLLBACK; aborts surface a `TransactionException`. |
| **C.1** | `1d4a8fe` | Coordinator decision log (`{db}.coord.log`) on the lowest-index participant. `COMMIT_DECISION` before broadcast (point of no return), `DONE` after. ABORT is implicit. |
| **C.2** | `b5f2423` | `cluster.Recover()` sweep — walks each shard's prepared.log, queries the named coordinator's coord.log, finalizes COMMIT or ABORT. Idempotent. Lifts the "data loss possible if coordinator/participant dies" caveat from Phase B. |

## Performance contract

The four hot paths called out in the design are bytewise unchanged: single-node `Insert`, single-node `BeginTransaction.Commit`, `cluster.Insert/Execute` (non-tx), and `cluster.BeginTransaction` touching exactly one shard. Phase A verified against the 2026-05-03 quick benchmark — every metric matched or beat baseline. B.1+ added new code paths only inside `cluster.BeginTransaction` with >1 participants; the worker thread doesn't even spin up unless something has called `PREPARE`.

## Acceptance criteria met

- ✅ Two participants both PREPARE → COMMIT applies to both (`ClusterTx_MultiShard_Commit_AppliesToAllShards`)
- ✅ One participant ABORTs in PREPARE → neither retains writes, abort reason in the exception (`ClusterTx_MultiShard_AbortOnPrepare_RollsBackAllShards`)
- ✅ Coordinator crash with COMMIT_DECISION recorded → participants resolve to COMMIT on `Recover()` (`ClusterRecover_PreparedWithCommitDecision_Commits`)
- ✅ Coordinator crash without decision → participants resolve to ABORT (`ClusterRecover_PreparedWithoutDecision_Aborts`)
- ✅ All Phase 1 (single-node) tests still pass

## Out of scope (follow-up PRs)

- **Phase D**: PREPARE timeout-and-abort. Without it, a coordinator that dies before deciding leaves participants `PREPARED` with their write lock held until manual `Recover()`. Phase D adds a per-tx deadline so participants self-abort.
- **Phase E**: operator endpoints (manual abort), metrics, SLA doc, **HTTP wire ops**. `HttpShardTransport` currently throws on every 2PC method — only in-process clusters work end-to-end so far.
- **Replace + Delete on `ClusterTransaction`**. Phase A only ships `Insert + Find` because doc-location lookup wasn't trivial without the cross-shard plumbing in place.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR (188/188 tests passing locally)
- [ ] Quick benchmark on the dev server matches 2026-05-03 baseline
- [ ] Manual sanity check: spin up an in-process 2-shard cluster, run a multi-shard tx, verify both shards committed
- [ ] Manual sanity check: simulate a crash with the participant test harness, restart, verify `Recover()` resolves correctly

## Summary

Milestone **1.4.0-beta.1** for pi-vision-proxy: `analyze_image` tool with multi-form crop support, enhanced fence metadata, and comprehensive security hardening.

## What's new

### Feature 1 — `analyze_image` tool
- Agent-facing tool for targeted re-querying of images (disabled by default during beta; `/vision-proxy tool on`)
- **Three crop forms**: `region` (named areas), `normalized` (0.0–1.0 fractional), `pixels` (absolute) — all resolve to pixel rectangles with clamping and zero-area validation
- LRU result cache keyed by (hashes, crop signature, question hash, model)
- Model override parameter — agent can switch vision model per call
- Grounding format registry with curated Tier 1 defaults (Qwen, Molmo, DeepSeek, InternVL, Gemini)
- TypeBox schema with `maxItems: 20` hard ceiling

### Infrastructure
- `image-size` integration for dimension extraction (header-only, no full decode)
- In-memory `_imageMeta` map (hash → width/height/filename)
- `readImageFileWithReason` returns file basename
- `fenceUntrusted` handles all three fence tag types

### Cross-cutting
- `<vision_proxy_description>` now carries `image`, `width`, `height`, `filename`, `crop_origin` attributes
- New `<vision_proxy_analysis>` fence for tool results with optional `grounding_format`
- Config: `tool`, `maxImagesPerCall`, `maxBatch`, `cacheSize`, `pHashSimilarityThreshold`
- Slash commands: `/vision-proxy tool|max-images-per-call|max-batch|cache-size`
- Env vars: `PI_VISION_PROXY_TOOL`, `MAX_IMAGES_PER_CALL`, `MAX_BATCH`, `CACHE_SIZE`, `PHASH_THRESHOLD`
- Telemetry: `vision_proxy.tool_call` session entries

### Security hardening
| ID | Fix |
|---|---|
| S1 | `escapeAttr()` on all fence attributes — prevents XML attribute injection via crafted filenames |
| S2 | `sanitizeXml()` on `question`/`prompt` before embedding in `<question>`/`<user_message>` tags — prevents XML breakout |
| S3 | Runtime check in tool `execute` — returns error if tool disabled mid-session |
| S4 | Truncate `reason` (200 chars) and `question` (200 chars) in telemetry entries |
| S5 | Clear `_imageMeta` and `_toolCache` on `session_start` — prevents session state leaks |
| S6 | `fenceUntrusted` neutralizes both `<` and `>` in fence tags |
| S7 | `resolveCropEntry` validates dimensions > 0, removes `!` non-null assertion on region branch |
| S8 | Reject `..` segments in tool image paths |
| Code | Remove dead `dimEntries` code, remove unused `isValidNamedRegion` import |

### Tests
112 tests passing — 15 new test suites covering:
- Crop resolution (region, normalized, pixels, clamping, zero-area)
- LRU cache (eviction, renewal, resize)
- Dimension extraction
- Fence building (description, analysis, attributes, crop_origin)
- Grounding format lookups
- Config backwards compatibility
- New env var parsing

See `PRD.md` and `PRD-Implementation-Status.md` in this PR for full specification and status tracking.

- **beta.3**: Multi-image batched comparison (Feature 2)
- **beta.4**: Grounding-models slash commands (Feature 4)

author: heap-hop
body:
## Summary

This PR is a breaking UX and config refactor for the next Fungi version. It pushes the product model toward:

```text
User -> Service@Device
```

instead of exposing users to ports, peers, catalogs, access rules, and allowlists as separate first-class concepts.

The main changes are:

- Make `fungi service` the primary service management surface.
- Add fast service invocation with `thing@device` and `--device`.
- Replace user-facing peer/allowlist language with device/trusted-device language.
- Move trusted-device persistence out of `config.toml`.
- Move dynamic device addresses out of user-managed device config.
- Reorganize service data directories around `.fungi` control state and visible user workspace roots.
- Add config migration scaffolding for future old-layout migration work.

## Motivation

The old service flow exposed too much implementation detail:

- `service`, `catalog`, `access`, `tunnel`, and `port` created too many concepts.
- Users had to think about peer IDs and port numbers too early.
- Remote service access required too much manual setup.
- `allowed-peer` was accurate internally, but bad product language.
- `--name` on `device add` made a required device name look optional.
- Service/runtime data was starting to mix control-plane config, app data, artifacts, and user files.

This PR makes device and service naming the main user mental model:

```bash
fungi service
fungi service add home-ssh@nas
fungi home-ssh@nas
fungi filebrowser
fungi device add nas <device-id> --addr <multiaddr>
fungi device trust nas
```

## User-Facing CLI Changes

### Service UX

`fungi service` now acts as the primary service overview and management entrypoint.

Supported direction:

```bash
fungi service
fungi service --device nas add
fungi service add home-ssh@nas
fungi service start home-ssh@nas
fungi service stop home-ssh@nas
fungi service remove home-ssh@nas
fungi service set home-ssh@nas local.port=2222
fungi home-ssh@nas
fungi filebrowser
```

Notes:

- `service@device` is the preferred user-facing object reference.
- `--device/-d` is still supported for script/agent-friendly calls.
- If a service name is unique in local cache, `fungi <service>` can open/connect it without requiring `@device`.
- `fungi service` lists available services from local/cache state by default.
- Legacy `tunnel` remains present but deprecated.

### Device UX

Device names are now first-class.

Before:

```bash
fungi device add <device-id> --name nas
```

Now:

```bash
fungi device add nas <device-id>
fungi device add nas <device-id> --addr <multiaddr>
fungi device address add nas <multiaddr>
fungi device address remove nas <multiaddr>
```

### Trusted Devices

The old public `security allowed-peers` flow is removed.

Now:

```bash
fungi device trust nas
fungi device untrust nas
fungi device trusted
```

This is intentionally a device relationship action. `fungi security` remains focused on local trust-boundary settings such as allowed host paths.

Trusting a device still shows an explicit security confirmation. Tests now pass `y\n` explicitly instead of relying on EOF/empty stdin to accept the default.

## gRPC/API Changes

The gRPC surface now uses trusted-device language.

Before:

```text
GetIncomingAllowedPeers
AddIncomingAllowedPeer
RemoveIncomingAllowedPeer

IncomingAllowedPeersListResponse
AddIncomingAllowedPeerRequest
RemoveIncomingAllowedPeerRequest
```

After:

```text
ListTrustedDevices
TrustDevice
UntrustDevice

TrustedDevicesListResponse
TrustDeviceRequest
UntrustDeviceRequest
```

The lower-level swarm state still uses an incoming allow set internally. That is treated as implementation detail.

## Config and Directory Changes

### Config versioning and migration

- Adds config versioning and a dedicated `config-migrate` crate.
- Adds `fungi migrate`.
- Migration scaffolding is split into focused modules for detection, file handling, model conversion, service migration, and application.

Old-layout migration coverage is started, but compatibility for all future breaking changes is intentionally handled in the migration layer rather than by keeping runtime code backwards-compatible.

### Devices

`address_book` is replaced with `devices` semantics.

Persistent device config now represents user-managed devices:

```text
.fungi/devices.toml
```

Dynamic direct address learning is persisted separately:

```text
.fungi/cache/direct_addresses.json
```

This prevents mDNS or learned addresses from creating unexpected user-visible devices.

### Trusted devices

Trusted device state is no longer stored in `config.toml [network]`.

New file:

```text
.fungi/trusted_devices.toml
```

### Service storage

Service state and data are reorganized:

```text
~/.fungi/
  services/svc_xxx/               # service.yaml + state.json
  appdata/services/svc_xxx/       # service private writable state
  artifacts/services/svc_xxx/     # service program assets/static resources

~/Fungi/                          # stable user root
~/FungiDev/                       # dev/nightly user root
  workspace/                      # user home/default workspace
```

Manifest path variables are narrowed to:

```text
$SERVICE_APPDATA
$SERVICE_ARTIFACTS
$USER_ROOT
$USER_HOME
```

Old variables such as `$APP_HOME` / `$SERVICE_DATA` are intentionally removed.

## Service Manifest / Runtime Changes

- Services now use internal `svc_` IDs rather than external `serviceId` / `displayName`.
- Wasmtime artifacts are staged under `.fungi/artifacts/services/<svc_id>`.
- Service app data uses `.fungi/appdata/services/<svc_id>`.
- Runtime default host path policy allows service appdata and user root, not the old `.fungi/data`.
- Docker policy follows the same boundary.
- Simple service creation can now be driven through an interactive creator.
- TCP tunnel-like access can be represented as a service type.

## Tests / Verification

Commands run during this branch work:

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo check -p fungi
cargo check -p fungi-tests
cargo test -p fungi-config
cargo test -p fungi-daemon -- --test-threads=1
cargo test -p fungi --test commands -- --nocapture
cargo test -p fungi --test cli_smoke -- --nocapture
```

Additional migration/config tests were added around:

- Direct address persistence outside `devices.toml`.
- Device names being required and unique.
- Service appdata/artifact directory behavior.
- Manifest path variable expansion.
- Runtime policy boundaries.
- CLI command parsing for `service@device`, `--device`, and `device trust`.

## Breaking Changes

This PR intentionally breaks old internal/user flows:

- `security allowed-peers` is removed.
- gRPC `IncomingAllowedPeer*` methods/messages are renamed.
- `network.incoming_allowed_peers` is removed from `config.toml`.
- `device add <id> --name <name>` is replaced by `device add <name> <id>`.
- Old service path variables such as `$APP_HOME` / `$SERVICE_DATA` are removed.
- Old `.fungi/data/<service_id>` service data layout is replaced.
- `address_book` naming is replaced by `devices` semantics.

Migration support should be completed in the dedicated migration layer before release.

## Review Notes

Areas worth reviewing carefully:

- Whether `device trust` as the primary trust command is clearer than putting it under `security`.
- Whether `security` should grow into a local trust-boundary overview in a follow-up PR.
- Whether all user-facing peer/allowlist wording has been removed from primary flows.
- Whether keeping `incoming_allowed_peers()` inside swarm internals is acceptable as implementation detail.
- Whether the service directory split is enough for near-term service/tool planning without over-abstracting.

## Suggested Follow-Ups

- Implement a richer `fungi security`

author: exafyltd
body:
This PR addresses a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability in `path-to-regexp` (< 0.1.13) transitively used by Express. Because direct dependency updates are handled in a separate workflow, this change implements an application-level mitigation in the gateway service to restrict the number of path parameters and their maximum lengths. 

By enforcing limits (max 5 parameters, each up to 200 characters long), we prevent the catastrophic backtracking conditions required to exploit the vulnerability.

**Changes:**
- `services/gateway/src/routes/middleware/paramLimit.ts`: New middleware that validates `req.params` against count and length thresholds.
- `services/gateway/src/routes/v1/userRoutes.ts` & `projectRoutes.ts`: Applied the `limitPathParams` middleware as representative implementations.
- `services/gateway/test/cve-mitigation.test.ts`: Added unit and integration tests to verify requests are properly accepted or rejected based on parameter characteristics and that rejection happens in <200ms.

**Note for operators / subsequent developers:**
This PR applies the mitigation to two representative route files as outlined in the plan. You must manually verify all other route files under `services/gateway/src/routes/` and apply the same `router.use(limitPathParams())` middleware wherever path parameters are used, until the underlying `path-to-regexp` dependency is globally patched.

## Summary
- Replace the AuthContext placeholder with a full provider that owns the storefront customer session: `{ user, token, isLoading, isHydrating, error }`, plus `login` / `register` / `logout` / `forgot` / `reset` / `updateUser` and a computed `isAuthenticated`.
- On mount, if `localStorage.ti_token` exists, validate it via `authService.me()`. On success, hydrate `user`; on 401, clear the token. The provider also listens for the axios `ti:auth-expired` event, clears the session, queues a polite "Your session has ended — please sign in again." toast, and emits `ti:auth-logout` so cart/wishlist contexts react.
- Login/register dispatch `ti:auth-login` (with the user as detail) so `CartContext.MERGE_GUEST` and `WishlistContext.fetchAndReplace` run. Logout dispatches `ti:auth-logout`. Register auto-logs in if the backend doesn't return a token; reset auto-logs in if it does.

- Dev-only: exposes `window.__auth` under `import.meta.env.DEV` for quick debugging.
- `http.js` already routes `ti_token` for non-admin URLs and `ti_admin_token` for `/admin/*`, and dispatches `ti:auth-expired` (storefront) vs `ti:admin-auth-expired` (admin) — verified, no change needed. Cart/Wishlist already listen for the storefront login/logout events — verified.

author: copilot
body:
Bootstraps the project from an empty repo into a working C++ application with three core dependencies and a REST HTTP API.

## Dependencies
- **FFmpeg** (`libavcodec`, `libavformat`, `libavutil`, `libswscale`) — media probing and PNG thumbnail generation
- **SQLite3** — persistent overlay configuration storage
- **cpp-httplib** — embedded HTTP/1.1 server

Found via `pkg_check_modules` (FFmpeg, cpp-httplib) and CMake's `FindSQLite3` module. A `vcpkg.json` manifest is included for cross-platform builds.

## Structure
| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `CMakeLists.txt` | CMake 3.20 build definition |
| `vcpkg.json` | vcpkg dependency manifest |
| `src/database.hpp/.cpp` | SQLite CRUD for overlay records; RAII statement guards, prepared statements |
| `src/media_controller.hpp/.cpp` | FFmpeg `probe()` + `generate_thumbnail()`; all handles RAII-managed (`AvBufGuard`, `CodecCtxGuard`, etc.) |
| `src/api_server.hpp/.cpp` | cpp-httplib server via Pimpl; inline JSON serialization, no extra deps |
| `src/main.cpp` | Wires components; config via env vars (`OMC_DB_PATH`, `OMC_PORT`) or CLI args |

## REST API
```
GET    /health
GET    /api/overlays
POST   /api/overlays          { name, source_path, x, y, width, height }
GET    /api/overlays/:id
DELETE /api/overlays/:id
PUT    /api/overlays/:id/active  { active: bool }
GET    /api/overlays/:id/probe   → MediaInfo from FFmpeg
```

## Notable details
- `av_malloc` buffer wrapped in `AvBufGuard` — freed on all paths including early returns
- Route handlers use a `parse_id()` helper that catches `std::stoi` exceptions and returns 400 instead of crashing

author: emrahbaysal
body:
## Summary

Sovereign cilium-gateway listeners are moved from privileged ports (80/443) to high ports (30080/30443). The Hetzner LB does the public-facing port translation so the operator-facing URL stays canonical.

## Why

cilium-envoy refuses to bind privileged ports on Sovereigns regardless of every capability/security configuration we tried:

- gatewayAPI.hostNetwork.enabled=true ✓
- securityContext.privileged=true ✓
- NET_BIND_SERVICE capability added ✓
- envoy-keep-cap-netbindservice=true in cilium-config ✓
- Gateway API CRDs at v1.3.0 ✓
- cilium 1.19.3 (PR #684) ✓

Error reproducible on otech45, otech46, otech47:
\`\`\`
listener 'kube-system/cilium-gateway-cilium-gateway/listener' failed
to bind or apply socket options: cannot bind '0.0.0.0:80':
Permission denied
\`\`\`

PID 1 with CapEff=0x000001ffffffffff (ALL caps) and uid=0 still gets EACCES — the bind() is intercepted by cilium-agent's BPF socket-LB program in a way that does not honour container capabilities. This is a known Cilium L7LB / hostNetwork interaction.

## Fix

Listener ports → 30080 (HTTP) / 30443 (HTTPS). HCLB:
- listen 80 → dest 30080
- listen 443 → dest 30443

High-port bind succeeds without NET_BIND_SERVICE (kernel only gates ports < \`net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start\` = 1024).

External users hit \`https://console.<sov>.omani.works/auth/handover\` on standard 443; the high port is never visible.

## Test plan

- [ ] Wipe + provision otech48
- [ ] All 38 HRs Ready=True zero-touch (regression of all prior wins)
- [ ] cilium-envoy listener: \`workers running\`, no \`Permission denied\` in logs
- [ ] HCLB targets healthy on 30080/30443
- [ ] \`curl https://console.otech48.omani.works/\` → 200 with catalyst-ui
- [ ] \`curl https://console.otech48.omani.works/auth/handover?token=...\` → catalyst-api Go handler (not React shell)
- [ ] Browser end-to-end: wizard mints handover JWT, lands operator on Sovereign Console authenticated

author: wyfive
body:
## Summary

  - Every CLI command read `cfg.settings.server.port` to build the HTTP base URL, so any `ConfigValidationError` from settings.json (missing `${VAR}`, legacy `auth_env_key`, etc.) made `server status` lie as
  `not_running` and crashed every other command (`sync`, `view`, …) — even though the daemon was fine, since env vars are rendered at startup, not on every CLI request.
  - `server start` now writes `server.port` next to `server.pid`. New shared `_http.resolve_port()` reads the port file first and only falls back to settings, so the whole CLI fleet stops depending on settings
  being renderable.
  - `server status` now does a real daemon-alive check (pid file + process probe) and surfaces `ConfigValidationError` explicitly rather than masking it as `not_running` — the masking was what made the original bug
   hard to diagnose.

  ## Why this matters

  Concrete failure mode I hit while configuring a fresh install:

  1. settings.json had `"auth_key": "${QWEN_KEY}"` for an OpenAI-compatible embedder
  2. Started the server with `QWEN_KEY` exported — fine
  3. Later opened a new shell without `QWEN_KEY` exported
  4. `memory-talk server status` → `not_running` (lying — daemon was healthy)
  5. `memory-talk sync` → Python traceback ending in `ConfigValidationError`

  Every CLI command was broken whenever the shell didn't have the embedder env var, even though that env only matters at server-startup time.

  ## Test plan

  - [x] new regression test `test_cli_works_when_settings_env_var_unset` — starts daemon with env set, unsets it, confirms both `server status` and a generic CLI command (`view`) still work
  - [x] full `tests/cli/` + `tests/config/` suite — 136/136 pass
  - [x] manual end-to-end: stop+restart real install, `unset QWEN_KEY` then run `status`, `sync`, `view` — all work; previously all failed

author: andrlut
body:
## Diagnosis

PR #72 swapped the Android-safe pure-RN path for `react-native-svg` primitives (`<Polygon>`/`<Line>`/`<Circle>`) on every platform. We had pinned the Android crash on `<Defs>`+`<RadialGradient>`+`<SvgText fontFamily>` only — wrong. **Even basic Polygon/Line/Circle hard-crash this user's Android APK natively.**

## Before vs after

| | Working state (PR #71) | Broken state (PR #72) | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Android | Pure RN Views (no SVG) — fallback | SVG Polygon/Line/Circle | Pure RN Views (no SVG) |
| iOS / web | SVG with gradient | SVG Polygon/Line/Circle | Pure RN Views (no SVG) |
| Components used | `HexChart` + `HexChartFallback` (split) | `HexChart` only (SVG) | `HexChart` only (pure RN) |

User wanted one component everywhere — so we go pure-RN on every platform. iOS/web lose the SVG niceties (gradient fill), but visual parity > fidelity since the user is iterating on the design and needs Android to match local.

## What's in the unified HexChart

- Hexagon outline = rotated `<View>` line segments (`transformOrigin '0% 50%'` + `rotate(angle)`).
- Concentric rings = bordered circles (`borderRadius` + `borderStyle: 'dashed'`).
- Vertex score discs = absolutely-positioned circular Views.
- All text (vertex scores, perimeter labels, center overall) uses regular RN `<Text>` with Manrope.
- Legend: 2 rows × 3 cards (flex:1 inside each row) — no more flexWrap %-width overflow.

## Trade-off accepted

No filled polygon — only outline. The score shape comes through via the violet outline + 6 colored vertex discs at varying radii. Polygon fill without SVG would need either:
1. `react-native-skia` (new native dep, requires APK rebuild), or
2. 6 stretched-skewed triangle Views (complex, fiddly)

Both are out of scope for restoring the Android tab.

## When SVG can come back

Add `react-native-skia` for cross-platform fill (next APK rebuild), or wait for upstream `react-native-svg` fix on the user's Android.

## Test plan
- [ ] Android: Hero opens — hexagon renders, no crash
- [ ] Web: same hex visible (no SVG, but identical to Android now)
- [ ] Tap card → modal opens, scoring works, hex updates immediately on close

author: dghiles
body:
## Summary

Closes **L4** in \`docs/audits/2026-04-24-seo-audit/ACTION-PLAN.md\` — dedupe bearer-token resolution between \`PrincipalMiddleware\` and the \`/admin/*\` handlers.

## Background

\`PrincipalMiddleware\` already gates the \`/admin/*\` prefix (it's been in \`protected_prefixes=(\"/mcp\", \"/admin/\")\` since the Plan-1 follow-up). When a request reaches an \`/admin/*\` handler, the middleware has already:
1. Parsed the \`Authorization: Bearer …\` header
2. Called \`resolve_token()\`
3. Returned 401 on any failure
4. Attached the \`Principal\` to \`request.state.principal\`

But \`/admin/waitlist\` and \`/admin/metrics\` were still doing all four steps **again** inside the handler — duplicate work, duplicate code, two places to keep in sync if auth ever changes.

\`/admin/audit\` already uses the correct \`request.state.principal\` pattern; this PR just brings the other two handlers to match.

## Changes

\`src/markland/web/app.py\`:
- \`admin_waitlist()\` — drop redundant header parse + \`resolve_token()\` call; read principal from \`request.state\`. Still returns 403 for valid non-admin principals.
- \`admin_metrics()\` — same dedupe.
- \`admin_audit()\` — unchanged (already correct).

\`-13 / +6\` net.

## Behavior

Identical at the HTTP layer:
- Missing or malformed \`Bearer\` header → \`401 unauthenticated\` (now from middleware instead of handler — same response body).
- Invalid/revoked token → \`401 unauthenticated\` (middleware).
- Valid token, non-admin user → \`403 forbidden\` (handler).
- Valid token, admin user → \`200\`.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pytest -k \"admin or principal or rate_limit or auth\"\` → **181/181 pass**, including:
  - \`test_admin_waitlist_401_for_anon\`
  - \`test_admin_waitlist_403_for_non_admin\`
  - \`test_admin_waitlist_returns_total_and_breakdowns\`
  - \`test_admin_metrics_*\` (all variants)
  - \`test_principal_middleware_admin\` (gating contract)
- [ ] After merge, sanity-curl: \`curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>\" https://markland.dev/admin/waitlist\` should still return JSON.

### Motivation
- Improve reliability of pixel sampling and avoid `getImageData` out-of-bounds errors when canvas/video sizes vary. 
- Make the UI more user friendly with an auto-fit keyboard region, sliders for fine tuning, and clearer controls. 
- Reduce spurious short notes and merge near-duplicate note events before MIDI export. 

### Description
- Added canvas bounds checks and clamping in `getLumaScore` and `scanLine` to prevent out-of-range `getImageData` calls. 
- Implemented `denoiseAndMerge(events,minNoteMs,gapMs)` to filter short notes, merge adjacent same-pitch notes, and used it in `exportMidi` before calling `buildExactMidi`. 
- Added playback auto-resume logic using `autoResumeRef` so analysis continues automatically for transient pauses and stops when the video really ends. 
- Added automatic keyboard region placement (`fitKeyboardDefault`) and an `updateKeyboardRect` helper plus new UI sliders to tweak `X/Y/W/H` for the keyboard region.

- Project housekeeping: added `.gitignore`, `package-lock.json`, and reordered/updated dependencies in `package.json`.

author: avrabe
body:
## Summary

- Diagnoses why `release-npm.yml` hasn't fired since v0.6.0 and fixes it.
- The Release workflow creates the GitHub Release page using `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub deliberately suppresses downstream workflow triggers from runs that authenticated with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (loop-prevention guarantee), so the historical `release: published` trigger on this file never fires for v0.7.0 / v0.8.0 — both stuck without npm publication despite binaries being on the Release page.
- Switches the trigger to `workflow_run` on the upstream Release workflow — the documented escape hatch for chaining workflows when the upstream uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## Why this approach

| Option | Cost | Tradeoff |
|---|---|---|
| **A: `workflow_run` (this PR)** | ~10 lines of YAML | Clean, no PAT needed, no rotation |
| B: PAT in `release.yml`'s `gh release create` | Generate / store / rotate a `RELEASE_PAT` secret | Keeps original trigger semantics; ongoing PAT chore |
| C: Inline npm-publish jobs into `release.yml` | Largest refactor | Loses workflow isolation |

Picked A.

## Notable changes

- `head_branch` on a tag-pushed source workflow is the tag name itself (e.g. `v0.8.0`), so version resolution stays one liner.
- Tag-format guard added: only proceeds if `TAG` matches `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`.
- Both jobs gated on `workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'` so failed/cancelled Release runs don't fire downstream publishes; `workflow_dispatch` bypasses the gate for manual backfills.
- Adds the standard "release-variant" `concurrency:` block consistent with #258.

## Backfill plan

Once this lands on `main`, manually dispatch the npm publish for the two stuck releases:

```bash
gh workflow run release-npm.yml -f version=v0.7.0
gh workflow run release-npm.yml -f version=v0.8.0
```

Both have all 5 platform binary archives present on their Release pages, so the platform-package jobs will succeed and the root `@pulseengine/rivet` package will publish.

## Conflict note

`#258` (CI concurrency hardening) also touches `release-npm.yml`'s top section. If #258 lands first, this PR will need a small rebase to keep the new variable names (`workflow_run.head_branch` instead of `release.tag_name`). Either order works.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI yamllint passes on this PR.
- [ ] After merge: `gh workflow run release-npm.yml -f version=v0.7.0` → all 5 platform packages publish, then root publishes.
- [ ] After v0.7.0 backfill: `gh workflow run release-npm.yml -f version=v0.8.0` → same.
- [ ] Verify `npm view @pulseengine/rivet version` returns `0.8.0`.
- [ ] Future v0.9.0 release auto-triggers `release-npm.yml` via `workflow_run` (validates the actual fix).

## Summary
Catches controller-wiring regressions per-controller test files miss: a new controller added to \`__init__\` but not to \`start()\`'s init list, or omitted from \`collect_api_commands\`, would silently lose its api commands without breaking any narrower test.

6 tests in \`tests/test_device_builder_lifecycle.py\` instantiate a real \`DeviceBuilder\` against \`tmp_path\` and run \`start\` + \`stop\`. The three network-touching surfaces (firmware's \`_verify_esphome_importable\` subprocess, devices' state-monitor zeroconf browser, MQTT coordinator's broker connect) are patched out; everything else runs end-to-end including catalog loads and the command-handler registration walk.

- **Pre-start**: every controller attr is \`None\`, executor pool eagerly constructed.
- **\`start\`** populates every controller attr.
- **\`command_handlers\`** carries one sample command per controller + the built-ins (\`ping\`, \`subscribe_events\`, \`auth\` alias of \`auth/login\`).
- **\`_bg_task\`** spawned and live.
- **\`stop\`** cancels the bg task, drains tracked tasks (real background task with cancellation observation), tears down devices + editor controllers, drains the executor pool.
- **\`stop\` survives without \`start\`** (aiohttp \`on_shutdown\` fires even on early exception).

author: jeremymcs
body:
## TL;DR

**What:** Registers milestones listed in deep setup `PROJECT.md` as queued DB rows.
**Why:** Fixes `/gsd new-project --deep` producing M001/M002 in the project plan while later `/gsd` or `/gsd auto` reports no active milestone.
**How:** Parses the existing `## Milestone Sequence` when `gsd_summary_save(PROJECT)` persists the root artifact, then inserts non-clobbering queued milestone rows for the parsed IDs.

## What

This updates `src/resources/extensions/gsd/tools/workflow-tool-executors.ts` so root `PROJECT` saves materialize the parsed milestone sequence into the canonical milestone table. It also adds regression coverage in `src/resources/extensions/gsd/tests/workflow-tool-executors.test.ts` proving that saving a PROJECT artifact with `M001` and `M002` makes `deriveState()` select `M001` as the active milestone for the next run.

Closes #5253

## Why

Deep project setup writes `.gsd/PROJECT.md` with a milestone sequence, but runtime state is DB-authoritative. Without DB rows, those planned milestones are visible in markdown but invisible to `/gsd` and `/gsd auto`, causing the next run to stop with no active milestone.

## How

The fix reuses the existing `parseProject()` contract and `insertMilestone()` behavior. Existing rows are preserved by `INSERT OR IGNORE`; newly discovered project milestones are inserted as `queued` unless the project sequence marks them done, in which case they are inserted as `complete`.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Addresses all four priorities from the problem statement:

1. **Reduce peak memory through streaming/two-pass** — `compress_corpus_template_with_metrics` now uses a true two-pass algorithm. Pass 1 reads each file, tokenises + counts, then discards raw bytes immediately (O(1 file) peak instead of O(entire corpus)). Pass 2 re-reads each file and streams encoded entries directly through `msgpack.Packer` → `zstd.ZstdCompressor.stream_writer`, removing the in-memory `encoded_files` list entirely.

2. **Clear fallback when TAR+ZSTD wins** — After building the template output, a TAR+ZSTD comparison is computed. If template output > TAR+ZSTD × 1.10 (configurable via `_CORPUS_FALLBACK_THRESHOLD`), the codec transparently re-encodes as `raw_tar_zstd` mode. The decompressor handles both modes. Nginx logs and other high-cardinality-variable corpora now automatically benefit. New metrics: `tarzstd_size` (always present), `chose_raw_fallback` (bool).

3. **Larger tests: 250 MB and 500 MB** — Added `TestXLargeCorpora` in `test_hardening.py`. Tests are automatically skipped unless ≥ 2 GB / ≥ 4 GB RAM is available (with documented rationale for the multiplier).

4. **Win/loss map documented internally** — Module docstring now includes a "Win/loss map" section explaining when MC beats vs. loses to TAR+ZSTD, and a "Streaming design" section describing the two-pass algorithm.

## Changes

### `metacompressor/corpus_template.py`
- Module docstring: streaming design description, win/loss map, raw_tar_zstd payload format
- Add `import tarfile`
- Add `_CORPUS_FALLBACK_THRESHOLD = 1.10` constant
- `compress_corpus_template_with_metrics`: rewritten as two-pass streaming; adds `tarzstd_size`/`chose_raw_fallback` to metrics; all 7 timing keys maintained
- `decompress_corpus_template`: uses `stream_reader` (required for streaming-compressed frames); handles `raw_tar_zstd` mode via tarfile extraction

### `metacompressor/tests/test_corpus_template.py`
- Updated `test_metrics_keys_present` to include `tarzstd_size` and `chose_raw_fallback`
- New `TestRawFallback` class (3 tests): verifies structured logs don't trigger fallback, `tarzstd_size` is always populated, and raw-mode archives round-trip correctly

### `metacompressor/tests/test_hardening.py`
- New `TestXLargeCorpora` class (2 tests): 250 MB and 500 MB structured-log corpora with memory-skip guards

## Test results

218/218 tests pass. CodeQL: 0 alerts.

author: chrisbra
body:
Problem:  When an error line in a file passed to :cfile / :cgetfile
          is longer than IOSIZE, qf_parse_file_pfx()
          copies the tail (up to LINE_MAXLEN bytes) into the fixed-
          size IObuff with STRMOVE(), overflowing the heap buffer.
          The same code path can also loop indefinitely because
          qf_parse_file_pfx() always returns QF_MULTISCAN when a
          tail is present, and qf_init_ext() unconditionally goes
          to "restofline" without bounding the tail length.
Solution: Remove the STRMOVE() into IObuff.  In the QF_MULTISCAN
          branch, alias linebuf into the tail directly and update
          linelen, requiring strict progress (new length less than
          the previous length) before retrying; otherwise ignore
          the line.

Supported by AI

body:
## Summary

Automated test-analysis run against `6bfb65d91d02eb571131c0ca8b6f00fd7977c78d`.

- **Features analyzed:** 6 (4 phase-0 unchanged, 2 phase-1: 1 unchanged, 1 new)
- **Acceptance criteria:** 29 total · 28 covered · 1 partial · 0 missing · 0 deferred
- **New tests:** 0 added · 0 modified
- **Test run:** pass — `go test ./...` and `pnpm -r --if-present test` both green at this SHA

## What

PR #28 shipped `feature-startup-config-checks`. All 5 ACs cleanly covered with strong package-level tests + meaningful overshoot beyond the spec:

- `phase-1/startup-config-checks` (status: implemented, 5/5 covered) —
  - **AC-1 / AC-2** (short / dev-default JWT secret): covered. Impl extends the spec's `dev / secret / change-me` denylist to 16 entries, case-insensitive, plus an `allSameAfter` trap that catches `change-meXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` padded variants.
  - **AC-3** (non-loopback bind requires `CHAT_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND=1`): covered by 4 SEC-2 tests handling `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`, empty-host bind-all, and malformed addresses.
  - **AC-4** (missing `CHAT_INVITE_CODE` rejected): covered.
  - **AC-5** (stderr + exit non-zero): `main.go:42-44` is the wiring; package-level errors name the offending env var ("got 8 bytes, need at least 32"). `TestErrorsNeverContainSecret` is a non-AC hardening guard that error messages never echo the secret value back.

  See [findings](specs/test-analysis/phase-1/startup-config-checks.md).

## Why

- `phase-1/startup-config-checks` — security hardening that must land in Phase 1. Without it, a misconfigured deploy could ship with `CHAT_JWT_SECRET=secret` or accidentally bind `0.0.0.0` from a default. The four extra weak-secret defenses (length / ASCII / repeated-char / low-entropy) catch the realistic operator mistakes (`AAAAAAA...`, `passwordpassword`, etc.) that a literal-only denylist would let through.

## Cross-feature observation

Several non-spec follow-up commits in this batch wire `CHAT_JWT_SECRET` + `CHAT_INVITE_CODE` into runtime test envs:
- `scripts/smoke.sh` (21ac520) generates both at runtime via `openssl rand`, never committed literals (per `CLAUDE.md` "no hardcoded secrets").
- `tests/server-ws-hub/hub_test.go` (9c7e9cd) and `tests/cli-send-watch/cli_test.go` (69410fa) inject them into the test process env.

The fact that these were needed to keep tests green proves the new validation is load-bearing at the integration boundary — exactly as intended.

`feature-auth-internals` AC-5 ("Token signing key is loaded from config, validated by startup checks") remains partial: `cfg.JWTSecret` is now loaded + validated, but no code path passes it to `auth.Issue` / `auth.Parse`. That wiring lives in the not-yet-shipped `feature-auth-endpoints`. Will firm up there.

## Findings docs

- `specs/test-analysis/phase-1/startup-config-checks.md` — new; 5/5 covered.
- `specs/test-analysis/README.md` — index updated to `6bfb65d`; phase-1 row count grows to 2.

## Caveats

- **No new tests added** — coverage at the package layer is appropriate for all 5 ACs, plus integration tests downstream prove the wiring.
- **Optional one-liner:** add an explicit `TestSEC1_RejectsPaddedDefault` exercising `change-mexxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx` so the `allSameAfter` branch has a named test. Not gated by any AC; catches the regression where someone refactors the loop and drops the prefix-then-padding check.
- **README index intentionally omits the four other in-flight test-agent PRs.** PR #37 (file-perms-and-headers — likely superseded by the new wiring spec in PR #47), PR #40 (sqlite-schema-and-ulid 4/5), PR #43 (body-and-ws-caps 4/4), PR #47 (auth-internals + wiring spec stub) own those rows; once they merge, the next tick reconciles.
- The remaining 5 phase-1 features still have specs but no implementation; agent will write per-feature findings as each lands.

author: samkeen
body:
## Summary

This PR adds visibility into token spending by introducing a per-task and per-model breakdown in the end-of-session summary. The breakdown is computed by replaying `events.jsonl` rather than relying on in-memory state, ensuring it survives crashes and `--resume` cycles.

## Key Changes

- **Instrumented all three model call sites** to emit `model_call` events with a `kind` field:
  - `_run_task()` (worker): `kind="worker"`
  - `_judge_task()` (judge): `kind="judge"`
  - `_self_improve()` (self-improvement): `kind="self_improve"`
  - Each event now includes the `model` field for attribution across providers

- **Added `_token_breakdowns()` function** that replays `events.jsonl` to aggregate tokens:
  - Returns `(by_model, by_task)` tuples
  - `by_model`: maps model name to total tokens
  - `by_task`: maps task ID to a dict with `total` and per-`kind` breakdowns
  - Gracefully handles missing files, malformed JSON lines, and legacy events without `kind`/`model` fields (defaults to "unknown"/"worker")
  - Skips zero-token events to avoid polluting the breakdown

- **Enhanced end-of-session summary** to display the breakdowns:
  - Per-task section sorted by token usage (descending), showing total and split by kind
  - Per-model section sorted by token usage (descending)
  - Helps identify which tasks consumed the most budget and which models were used

- **Updated visualization** (`render.py`) to display model call metadata:
  - Shows `kind` in badge labels (e.g., "judge (iter 3)" vs "iter 1")
  - Includes model name in the meta strip when available
  - Handles legacy events without `kind`/`model` gracefully

- **Documentation updates** (USAGE.md, deep-dives.md, session.py):
  - Documented the new per-task and per-model breakdown feature
  - Clarified that all three sites now emit `model_call` events
  - Explained the replay-based approach and its benefits

## Implementation Details

- The breakdown computation is defensive: it tolerates missing fields, malformed JSON, and zero-token events
- Legacy events (pre-breakdown) are bucketed under "unknown" model and "worker" kind, maintaining backward compatibility
- The `iter` field is only emitted for worker and judge calls (not self-improve), as self-improvement doesn't have a meaningful iteration number
- Token counts are computed as `prompt_tokens + eval_tokens`, matching the existing `add_tokens()` pattern

### Motivation
- Provide a strict JSON schema for magic-chant responses so the client can deterministically parse and execute 3D visual effects without relying on freeform text.
- Enable immediate in-game activation (auto-cast) of the generated effect JSON to streamline the chant → effect workflow.
- Hide the debug panel and top summon modal once when a JSON auto-cast occurs to declutter the UI during live effects.

### Description
- Replaced the server-side chant prompt in `src/server/origin-magic-circle/index.js` to request the provided strict JSON schema and `JSON.parse` the model output, returning it as `magicEffectJson`.
- Updated `public/origin-magic-circle/main.js` to accept callback options in `setupMagicCircleUi(container, options)` and to call `onMagicJsonReady(magicEffectJson)` when a JSON response is returned, which immediately calls `playMagicVisualEffects` to spawn the effects.
- Added one-time hiding behavior for the top summon controls (`topControls`) and the debug panel (`debugPanel`) via `hideTopModalOnce` and `hideDebugOnce` callbacks so they are hidden the first time an auto-cast JSON is processed.
- Adjusted `topControls` scoping so it can be hidden from the outer scope and added flags (`hasHiddenTopModal`, `hasHiddenDebugPanel`) to ensure the hide actions run only once.

author: a3ka
body:
## Why

User feedback 2026-05-03: «Сейчас же нам после дева понадобился ты. ЗАЧЕМ???»

Before TD-dev-push: dev's «готово» required architect to pull commit + push so test-runner could see remote → architect bottleneck on every dev cycle.

This PR removes the bottleneck via mechanical pre-push enforcement.

## What this PR adds

**Hook (`.husky/pre-push`):**
- architect/user: push anywhere
- reviewer: push narrow (existing scope-guard rule, hook permissive)
- 4 dev identities (backend/frontend/icp/registry): push `feature/*` OK; `refs/heads/{dev,main}` REJECTED
- test-runner: `refs/heads/{dev,main}` REJECTED (read-only quality gate)
- non-fast-forward to dev/main REJECTED for everyone (force-push protection)

**Updated rules:**
- `.claude/rules/scope-guard.md::Push permissions` table
- `CLAUDE.md::Branch Model` Push policy
- `.claude/rules/dev-startup.md` Step 5 + Five Hard Rules Rule 3
- `.claude/rules/workflow.md` push policy
- `.claude/rules/architect-protocol.md` slim spec template + fix-iter template

**Updated 5 existing tests** to reflect new policy (m-q22, m-q16, m-q8, m-q10, m-q12).

**Acceptance:** `scripts/verify_TD-dev-push.sh` (19 checks).

## Готово когда

- 13 criteria in `docs/sprints/TD-dev-push.md::Готово когда`
- Acceptance: PASS=19 FAIL=0
- Baseline: 1441 passed (was 1437; +4 from new test) | 18 skipped | 5 todo

## Trade-off

Compromised dev session can push malicious feature/*, but architect's gate-1 merge (autonomous after reviewer APPROVED + CI green) catches before reaching `dev`. Same guarantee as old credential-isolation, with no per-cycle bottleneck.

author: vernonthedev
body:
> Migrated to Typescript, Bun, NextJS, ReactJS, ReactJS & Electron as well as Bun as the package manager and Shadcn for the base ui setup.

## Overview

 This PR marks a major milestone: transitioning the project from a legacy vanilla HTML/JS implementation to a modern React 19 + Next.js 16 stack. The application has been fully redesigned and integrated with Electron to provide a high-performance, native desktop experience.

 ## Key Features & Improvements

   * Modern Frontend Architecture
       * Full Migration: Legacy panel.html and display.html are replaced with Next.js App Router components (src/app/panel and src/app/display).
       * shadcn/ui Integration: Professional UI built using Radix-based components and Lucide React icons.
       * State Persistence: Centralized state management with localStorage persistence to maintain workspace settings across sessions.
   * Electron Desktop Integration
       * Native Wrapper: The app now functions as a native desktop application.
       * Streamlined Dev-Ops: Added PowerShell scripts (scripts/start-electron-dev.ps1) and specialized build configs for portable Windows distribution.
       * Lifecycle Management: Next.js server management is now integrated into the Electron lifecycle for clean process handling.
   * Advanced Bible Integration
       * Live APIs: Real-time content fetching via bible-api.com and bible.helloao.org.
       * Reliability: Robust fallback mechanisms ensure content availability even during API outages.
       * Translation Support: Support for multiple versions (KJV, BSB, etc.) with integrated loading states.
   * UI/UX Overhaul
       * Control Panel: Redesigned panel with advanced toolbar actions, scene management, and live previews.
       * Modern Styling: Full implementation of Tailwind CSS v4 with native dark mode support.
       * Settings System: Comprehensive modal-based settings for typography, backgrounds, and vMix/NDI integrations.

  ## Technical Changes
   * Dependencies: Added lucide-react, shadcn/ui, electron, electron-builder, and @base-ui/react.
   * TypeScript: Full type safety adoption with dedicated configurations for Next.js and Electron.
   * Build System: Standardized on Bun for fast package management and cross-platform script execution.

  ## Legacy Cleanup
   * Removed src/panel.html, src/display.html, and src/index.html.
   * Deleted legacy configuration files (tsconfig.panel.json, tsconfig.build.json).

author: jiahui-gu
body:
## Summary

Wave 2 §5.6 (Task #222) — mechanical guard. Lists files slated for deletion / shrinkage during v0.3 cutover; CI enforces line counts may DECREASE but never INCREASE vs merge-base. More reliable than reviewer self-check.

## Files added/modified

### `.v0.2-only-files` (new, repo root)
16 entries (Tier 2 REWIRE/MOVE pending), all verified to exist in `working`:

| path | base lines | head lines |
|---|---|---|
| electron/main.ts | 320 | 288 |
| electron/updater.ts | 206 | 200 |
| electron/window/createWindow.ts | 356 | 323 |
| electron/notify/sinks/toastSink.ts | 169 | 169 |
| electron/notify/sinks/flashSink.ts | 127 | 123 |
| electron/agent/read-default-model.ts | 50 | 4 |
| electron/prefs/userCwds.ts | 105 | 105 |
| electron/prefs/notifyEnabled.ts | 44 | 44 |
| electron/prefs/crashReporting.ts | 52 | 52 |
| src/components/settings/UpdatesPane.tsx | 188 | 188 |
| src/terminal/xtermSingleton.ts | 242 | 242 |
| src/stores/persist.ts | 120 | 120 |
| src/terminal/usePtyAttach.ts | 477 | 477 |
| src/stores/drafts.ts | 112 | 112 |
| src/stores/slices/sessionCrudSlice.ts | 420 | 420 |
| src/agent/lifecycle.ts | 111 | 111 |

Skipped (per spec): `electron/import-scanner.ts` does not exist post-Wave 0d.2 (`f8ccd8a` moved it to daemon).

Excluded by design (per anti-patterns):
- `electron/db.ts` — staying for v0.3 per #249 deferred-prefs decision
- `electron/tray/*`, `electron/lifecycle/*`, `electron/branding/*`, `electron/sentry/*` — KEEP-shell
- `electron/window/closeAction.ts` — stays in shell

### `tools/check-v02-shrinking.sh` (new)
POSIX bash. Compares HEAD line counts against merge-base.
- Base resolution: `origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}` → `origin/main` → `origin/working` fallback chain.
- Handles: literal paths, globs (via `git ls-tree` enumeration), missing-in-base (treated as 0 = any growth fails), missing-in-head (skip — file moved is OK), comments (`#`) and blank lines.
- Exit 1 if any GROW; exit 0 otherwise.

### `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (modified)
- Added `fetch-depth: 0` to `actions/checkout@v4` (required for `git merge-base`).
- Added step `Check v0.2-only files don't grow` to existing `lint-typecheck-test` job, gated `if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'` (deterministic check; no need to run cross-OS).

### `.github/pull_request_template.md` (modified)
Added checkbox under Wire-up evidence: `If this PR modifies any file in .v0.2-only-files, explain why it grew or confirm net shrink.`

## Local validation

### Clean baseline (PASS, exit 0)
```
check-v02-shrinking: base = 69a83b1b770032098c974bb8d46a7c7222795c99

OK:   electron/main.ts (base=320, head=288, -32)
OK:   electron/updater.ts (base=206, head=200, -6)
OK:   electron/window/createWindow.ts (base=356, head=323, -33)
... (all 16 OK)

check-v02-shrinking: 16 checked, 0 skipped
PASS: no v0.2-only file grew.
```

### Inject 50 grow lines into `electron/main.ts` (FAIL, exit 1)
Note on acceptance criteria #2/#3: spec says "inject 10 grow lines". Since `electron/main.ts` head (288) is already 32 lines below base (320) on `working`, +10 still leaves head < base and would correctly PASS. Used +50 to push head (338) above base (320) and trigger GROW:
```
GROW: electron/main.ts (base=320, head=338, +18)
... (others OK)

FAIL: one or more .v0.2-only-files entries grew vs base.
```
Exit code: `1`. After restore: PASS again.

### Bash + YAML syntax
- `bash -n tools/check-v02-shrinking.sh` → OK
- `python -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(...))'` → OK

## CI step name
`Check v0.2-only files don't grow` (in `lint + typecheck + test (ubuntu-latest)` job).

## Out of scope
- Did NOT add to `lint:no-ipc` script (separate concern, per anti-patterns).
- Did NOT touch typecheck/lint/tests (no app code changed).

## Test plan
- [x] Script runs locally on clean checkout, exit 0
- [x] Inject growth → exit 1 with GROW message
- [x] Restore → exit 0 again
- [x] Bash + YAML syntax valid
- [ ] CI lint job picks up the new step (verify on this PR)
- [ ] Existing CI still green
