author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Major UX simplification of the Live Slots page streaming flow, plus Add Slot modal enhancements, inline scheduling, and improved backend quality auto-downgrade.

**1. Removed the Start Stream modal popup entirely** — Clicking "Start Stream" no longer opens a second popup. Instead, `handleDirectStart` reads the slot's saved `sourceType`/`sourceUrl` directly and starts streaming immediately. The source is configured inline on the slot card itself (which already has Video/YT Link/Drive/Playlist tabs with save functionality). This eliminates the confusing two-popup flow.

**2. Inline thumbnail upload on slot cards** — Each slot card now has an optional "Thumbnail" button that lets you select a thumbnail file. The thumbnail is uploaded automatically when "Start Stream" is clicked, replacing the old modal's thumbnail section.

**3. Enhanced Add Slot modal** — The YouTube URL input in "Add New Slot" now includes:
- A **"Check" button** that calls `streamingAPI.extractYoutubeInfo()` to validate the URL and show a thumbnail + title preview
- A **loop checkbox** for both YouTube and Google Drive sources (previously hardcoded to `loop: true`)
- A **Stream Timing** section with Immediately/Scheduled toggle and End Date picker (consistent with slot card UI)

**4. Inline Start Date / End Date on slot card** — Replaced the separate "Schedule" button with an integrated **Stream Timing** section directly on each slot card:
- **Start mode toggle**: "Immediately" (green, default) starts the stream right away; "Scheduled" (indigo) reveals a datetime picker
- **End Date** picker (optional): sets auto-stop time. If left empty, stream loops infinitely
- **Button adapts**: In scheduled mode, the button changes to indigo "Save Schedule" and saves the schedule without starting. In immediate mode, it stays green "Start Stream" and starts right away
- End date is also saved when starting immediately (for auto-stop support)

**5. Dead code cleanup** — Removed ~180 lines of Start Stream modal JSX, unused state variables (`VideoSourceType`, `videoSource`, `showStreamModal`, `streamThumb`, `streamEndDate`, `gdriveUrl`, `playlistVideoIds`, `streamLoop`, etc.), and unused helper functions (`openStreamModal`, `handleStartStream`, `canStartStream`, `togglePlaylistVideo`). Removed the standalone "Schedule" button from the action row.

**6. Quality auto-downgrade improvements (backend)** — Streams no longer stutter for 30+ seconds before downgrading. Two areas improved:

- **YouTube URL streams** (`streaming_advanced.py`): The `_monitor_and_fallback()` monitor now triggers downgrade after **3 checks (~15s)** instead of 6 (~30s). Added **speed metric monitoring** (`speed < 0.8x` for 3 checks = downgrade). FFmpeg crash with non-zero exit code now triggers **immediate downgrade on 2nd crash** instead of restarting at same resolution forever. Extracted `_downgrade_resolution()` helper for cleaner code.

- **Uploaded video streams** (`streaming.py`): Added `UPLOADED_QUALITY_CHAIN` (1080p → 720p → 480p) with bitrate presets. The watchdog now monitors FFmpeg **speed metric** and auto-downgrades when encoding can't keep up. Also downgrades after **3 consecutive crashes** at the same quality level. Quality level is preserved across restarts via `quality_idx` in `active_streams`.

### Source resolution priority in `handleDirectStart`

When "Start Stream" is clicked, the source is determined in this order:
1. **Scheduled check** — If start mode is "Scheduled" with a date, saves the schedule and returns (no immediate start)
2. **Active inline card input** — If the user has the YT Link tab open and typed a URL (even unsaved), it saves & streams that
3. **Saved slot data** — Falls back to the slot's stored `sourceType`/`sourceUrl` from the database
4. **Default** — Calls `slotsAPI.startStream()` for uploaded video / playlist fallback

### Updates since last revision

- **Timezone double-conversion fix** — Added `toLocalDatetimeValue()` helper that correctly adjusts ISO dates for the user's timezone when displaying in `datetime-local` inputs. Previously, `toISOString().slice(0, 16)` produced UTC strings that were re-parsed as local time, shifting dates by the user's UTC offset. Fixed in both the handler (lines 195-196) and all 4 datetime input display locations.
- **Stale endDate fix** — Separated `userEndDate` (explicit user input only) from `endDate` (with DB fallback for scheduled mode). In "Immediately" mode, only user-explicit end dates are saved — prevents stale `scheduledEnd` from previous sessions auto-stopping new streams.
- **Stream Timing in Add New Slot modal** — Added the same Immediately/Scheduled toggle and End Date picker to the Add New Slot modal for consistent UX.
- **Quality auto-downgrade backend** — Faster FPS-based downgrade trigger, new speed-based monitoring, crash-based auto-downgrade for both YouTube URL and uploaded video streams.
- **Fixed Google Drive sourceType mismatch** — The slot card's Drive "Save" button writes `sourceType: 'gdrive'`, but `handleDirectStart` was only checking `'cloud_gdrive'`. Now checks both: `(srcType === 'cloud_gdrive' || srcType === 'gdrive')`.
- **Fixed stale playlist help text** — The playlist tab in slot cards referenced the now-removed "Start Stream modal". Updated to generic guidance.
- **Fixed quality_idx not passed on watchdog normal restart** — `start_ffmpeg_stream()` previously hardcoded `quality_idx = 0` (1080p). When the watchdog restarted a stream that had been auto-downgraded (e.g. to 720p), FFmpeg would restart at 1080p while `active_streams` still tracked it as 720p — causing a mismatch and incorrect subsequent downgrade decisions. Fixed by adding a `quality_idx` parameter to `start_ffmpeg_stream()` and passing the preserved level from the watchdog's normal restart path.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Quality downgrade restart consistency**: Start a stream, wait for it to auto-downgrade to 720p (or force it by CPU-loading the server). Then cause a normal FFmpeg crash (e.g. briefly disconnect RTMP). Verify in `pm2 logs` that the watchdog restarts at 720p (not 1080p). Look for log lines showing the correct bitrate in the FFmpeg command.
- [ ] **Quality auto-downgrade end-to-end**: Start a YouTube URL stream at 4K/1080p on a resource-constrained server. Monitor logs for `AUTO-DOWNGRADE` log lines. Verify the stream downgrades within ~15-20 seconds of sustained low fps/speed, and continues playing smoothly at the lower resolution.
- [ ] **Stale endDate regression**: Create a slot, set an End Date in the past, start and stop a stream. Then start a new stream with "Immediately" mode and **no** End Date set. Verify the stream does NOT auto-stop (the old past `scheduledEnd` should NOT carry over).
- [ ] **Timezone correctness**: In a non-UTC timezone browser, set a scheduled start time. Refresh the page. Verify the displayed time matches what you entered (not shifted by timezone offset).
- [ ] **Crash-based downgrade for uploaded videos**: Stream a high-bitrate uploaded video that causes FFmpeg to struggle. After 3 crashes at the same quality, verify the watchdog auto-downgrades to 720p then 480p (check `pm2 logs`).

### Notes
- The Schedule modal code (lines ~1062–1092) is still present but no longer reachable from the slot card UI since the Schedule button was removed. Consider removing it in a follow-up if no other code path triggers it.
- The End Date input uses `mt-[29px]` to align vertically with the Start toggle — this is a magic number that could break on different screen sizes or if the toggle height changes.
- The inline `className` on the Start Stream button contains an empty conditional `${slotStartMode[slot.id] === 'scheduled' ? '' : ''}` — harmless but dead code.
- `slotStartMode`, `slotStartDate`, `slotEndDate` are local React state and reset on page refresh. Pre-existing schedule data from the DB is used as fallback defaults in the datetime inputs.

`earthTexture.ts` was a 1084-line monolith blocking all Feature #40 globe stories. Decomposed into focused modules under `src/renderer/components/Globe/`.

## Module breakdown

- **`coastlineData.ts`** — `[lon, lat][][]` coordinate arrays (data file)
- **`projection.ts`** — pure equirectangular math (`toX`, `toY`, `latLonToVector3`)
- **`normalMap.ts`** — height canvas + Sobel normal map generation
- **`textureRenderer.ts`** (65 lines) — thin orchestrator; exports `CoastlineSource` interface enabling future GeoJSON swap without touching render logic
- **`drawLayers.ts`** (196 lines, new) — all canvas draw helpers extracted from the old monolith

## Key design points

`CoastlineSource` decouples data from rendering:
```ts
export type CoastlineSource = () => [number, number][][];

export function createEarthTextures(source: CoastlineSource = () => COASTLINES) { ... }
```

`drawLayers.ts` introduces a private `strokeWrappedPath` helper that eliminates three near-identical antimeridian-break loops. `drawInteriorBorders` centroid uses a single-pass reduce instead of two.

All logic files are ≤200 lines; `coastlineData.ts` (728 lines) is a pure data file and exempt.

## Tests added

11 new tests in `earthTexture.test.ts` covering `toX`/`toY` projection math, `COASTLINES` data structure shape, and `CoastlineSource` re-export contract.

author: milesaheadtoo
body:
## Summary
Closes PR-6 of [TWIN_REWRITE_PLAN.md](docs/TWIN_REWRITE_PLAN.md) — the **last PR in the TMS twin rewrite**. Walks tenant `TransferOrder` + `TransferOrderLineItem` history and returns a `Phase1ShipmentGenerator` configured with fitted parameters instead of bootstrap defaults. Mirrors SCP's Phase-2 pattern (`seasonal_envelope_service.fit_seasonal_envelopes_for_config`) shipped 2026-05-01.

Off `main`. Independent of all open §3.x / 4 / 5.x PRs.

### Diffstat

```
backend/app/services/digital_twin/__init__.py            |  12 ++++
backend/app/services/digital_twin/phase2_fitter.py       | 408 ++++++++++++++++ (new)
backend/app/services/digital_twin/shipment_generator.py  |  23 ++-
backend/tests/services/digital_twin/test_phase2_fitter.py| 488 +++++++++++++++++ (new)
docs/TWIN_REWRITE_PLAN.md                                |   2 +-
5 files changed, 933 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

### What lands

`phase2_fitter.py`:

| Symbol | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `HistoricalShipment` | Input dataclass — independent of the SQLAlchemy ORM so the fitter is exercisable from synthetic test data or ERP-extracted rows alike. |
| `FitParameters` | Tunable knobs: `tier`, `seasonal_period`, `min_full_periods_for_seasonal`, `min_buckets_for_volume_fit`, `fallback_envelope_spread`, `default_base_volume`, `seed`. |
| `fit_phase2_shipment_generator(history, *, params)` | Pure in-memory fitter. |
| `load_history_for_config(config_id, db, ...)` | Async DB wrapper — joins TransferOrder × TransferOrderLineItem within `history_window_days`, maps Integer site IDs to canonical `"site:<id>"` form. |
| `PHASE2_TENANT_CALIBRATED_PRODUCER_SIGNATURE = "tms:to_arrival_phase2:v0.1.0"` | Stamped on `TransferOrderEnvelope.produced_by`. |

`shipment_generator.py`:

- `Phase1ShipmentGenerator.__init__` gains a `producer_signature` kwarg (default `PARAMETRIC_STUB_PRODUCER_SIGNATURE` — **backward-compatible**).
- `generate_envelope`'s `phase_indicator` now derives from the signature: `tms:to_arrival_phase2*` prefix → `PhaseIndicator.TENANT_CALIBRATED`, else `PARAMETRIC_STUB`.

### What the fitter produces

For each `(origin, dest, product)` channel and each `(origin, dest)` lane in the history:

1. **Channel discovery** — distinct `candidate_lanes` / `candidate_products` / `candidate_units`, sorted.
2. **Per-channel base_volume** — mean qty per occupied ISO-week bucket. Sparse channels (< `min_buckets`) drop from the map and inherit `default_base_volume` at generator-time.
3. **Per-lane SeasonalEnvelope** via Core's `fit_seasonal_envelope`, when the lane has ≥ `min_full_periods` (default 1.5) annual cycles. Lanes with thinner history skip the seasonal fit (fall through to the parametric `envelope_spread`).
4. **Per-product unit override** when a product ships in a single UOM; mixed-UOM products fall through to the rotation.

### Tests (26 new, all passing)

- HistoricalShipment validation (4)
- Empty / minimal history paths (2)
- Channel discovery — lanes, products, units (3)
- Unit overrides — single-UOM vs mixed (2)
- Base volume fitting — mean-per-occupied-bucket, multi-shipment bucket aggregation, sparse-channel fallback, threshold tunability (4)
- Seasonal envelope fitting — full-history success, thin-history skip, threshold tunability, winter > summer pattern (4)
- Producer signature + phase indicator — including backward-compat that PR-6 doesn't change Phase-1's default signature (3)
- End-to-end integration — fitted seasonality propagates to emitted envelopes, only observed channels appear, deterministic output, fitted + unfitted lanes coexist (4)

Full digital-twin suite: **129 passed, 1 failed** (pre-existing main-branch flake `test_attached_model_equipment_only_consumed_by_accepted_loads` — unrelated to PR-6).

### Provisioning integration (follow-up)

The fitter ships here as a substrate. The natural call site is a tenant-bootstrap step:

```python
history = await load_history_for_config(config_id, db, history_window_days=730)
generator = fit_phase2_shipment_generator(history)
# persist `generator` for downstream simulator instantiation
```

Wiring that into `provisioning_service.py` is intentionally out of scope here — the substrate is the contract; the call-site is a thin glue PR.

### Closes the rewrite plan

This is the last PR in `TWIN_REWRITE_PLAN.md`. After PR-1 through PR-6 land, the TMS twin rewrite is complete:

| | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| PR-1 | Scaffolding | merged |
| PR-2 | Phase-1 parametric shipment generator | merged |
| PR-3.A/B | Carrier acceptance + lane transit physics | merged |
| PR-3.C/D/E | Dock queue + equipment flow + spot-rate | open ([#27](https://github.com/azirella-ltd/Autonomy-TMS/pull/27) / [#28](https://github.com/azirella-ltd/Autonomy-TMS/pull/28) / [#29](https://github.com/azirella-ltd/Autonomy-TMS/pull/29)) |
| PR-3.F | Exception generator | open ([#32](https://github.com/azirella-ltd/Autonomy-TMS/pull/32)) |
| PR-3.G | Intermodal + tracking | open ([#34](https://github.com/azirella-ltd/Autonomy-TMS/pull/34)) |
| PR-4 | Seasonal observation features | open ([#35](https://github.com/azirella-ltd/Autonomy-TMS/pull/35)) |
| PR-5.A/B/C | SCP-shape pipeline extraction | open ([#36](https://github.com/azirella-ltd/Autonomy-TMS/pull/36) → [#37](https://github.com/azirella-ltd/Autonomy-TMS/pull/37) → [#38](https://github.com/azirella-ltd/Autonomy-TMS/pull/38)) |

This represents roughly a 3x speedup for this specific line execution on very large git outputs without storing the result in memory as a transient list.

author: lijunzh
body:
## Summary

Closes #1211.

The inference Enter (`QueueNext` lane) and Ctrl+J ("later" lane) handlers in `koda-cli/src/tui_handlers_inference.rs` sent textarea contents straight to the engine with no `text.starts_with('/')` check. So typing `/cancel agent:1` during a `WaitTask` would:

- inject `/cancel agent:1` to the model as a raw user message,
- render `📥 Next: /cancel agent:1` in scrollback as if it were a real steer,
- and never actually cancel the bg agent.

Same footgun for `/clear`, `/model`, `/compact`, etc. The `tui_context/menus.rs:362` comment already documented the limitation (`/cancel <id>` (idle) or Esc cancel-all (during inference)) but nothing in code enforced it.

### Why this is a koda-specific bug

Field study from #1210 confirms reference TUIs (claude-code / codex / gemini-cli) don't have this trap because their slash surfaces aren't routed through the same input path during inference. We do, so silent steer is unambiguously a bug — Option B from the issue (reject with visible warning) is the right shape.

## Changes

- **`koda-cli/src/tui_handlers_inference.rs`**:
  - New small testable classifier `is_slash_command_attempt(&str) -> bool` that trims leading whitespace and matches a leading `/`.
  - Both Enter and Ctrl+J inference handlers consult it before queueing. On hit: clear the textarea and push a visible warn line via `tui_output::warn_msg` telling the user to Esc-interrupt and retry at idle.
  - The guard fires *before* history append, db push, scroll-buffer preview, and command send — so a rejected slash never pollutes any persistent state.
- **`koda-cli/src/tui_handlers_inference.rs` (tests)**: new `slash_guard_tests` module with 5 tests pinning the classifier:
  - bare slash commands (`/cancel`, `/clear`, `/model`)
  - slash commands with args (`/cancel agent:1`)
  - leading whitespace doesn't bypass (` /cancel`, `\t/model`)
  - plain text passes through (empty / whitespace / regular sentences)
  - mid-text slashes are NOT commands (paths, URLs, fractions)
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — Unreleased → Fixed entry crediting the post-#1213 design alignment.

## UX after this PR

Type `/cancel agent:1` during a `WaitTask`:

```
  ⚠ Slash commands are disabled during inference. Press Esc to interrupt, then run the command at idle.
```

…and the textarea clears so the user can immediately Esc → retype.

## Tests

```
cargo test -p koda-cli --lib                 # 605 passed (was 600 → +5)
cargo clippy -p koda-cli --all-targets       # clean
```

## Out of scope

- **End-to-end test of the rejection path.** The Enter/Ctrl+J handlers are tightly coupled to `TuiContext` field-borrows + `EngineCommand` channel + DB; no scripted-TUI harness exists yet. Classifier-level coverage is the cleanest available surface.
- **Per-command "safe mid-turn?" classification (Option A from the issue).** Deferred until concrete demand surfaces — today's slash set has no command that's both safe AND useful mid-inference.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the 3.0.x storyboard CI baseline. The workflow's overlay step was silently no-op'ing on every 3.0.x run because it looked for the SDK compliance cache at \`node_modules/@adcp/sdk/compliance/cache\` (main's post-rename path) but 3.0.x still ships \`@adcp/client@5.21.1\`. With the overlay skipped, the storyboard runner read the SDK's frozen 3.0.0 snapshot — which has no \`fixtures:\` block or \`controller_seeding: true\` flag — so pre-flight \`comply_test_controller.seed_product\` was never invoked.

Result: 11 storyboards have been failing with \`PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND\` (or similarly-shaped seed-prerequisite errors) on 3.0.x's CI baseline since the workflow forward-merge from main:

- \`sales_guaranteed\`, \`sales_broadcast_tv\`
- \`media_buy_seller\`, \`media_buy_seller/delivery_reporting\`, \`media_buy_seller/governance_approved\`
- \`creative_generative/seller\`
- \`governance_delivery_monitor\`, \`governance_spend_authority\`
- \`idempotency\`, \`brand_baseline\`, \`brand_rights\`

## Investigation

Reproduced locally and traced through the SDK runner:

1. Storyboard runner calls \`runControllerSeeding(client, storyboard, options, context)\` for each storyboard. Without the overlay, the loaded storyboard object has \`hasFixtures: false\` and \`prerequisitesControllerSeeding: undefined\` because the YAML loader reads from the SDK's frozen \`compliance/cache/3.0.0/\` snapshot, which was synced before fixtures were added.
2. The seed loop short-circuits on \`storyboard.prerequisites?.controller_seeding !== true\`, returning \`null\`.
3. Every storyboard's \`create_media_buy\` (or equivalent) then can't find products like \`sports_preroll_q2_guaranteed\` or \`outdoor_display_q2\`, since those products only exist in the local repo's \`fixtures.products\` block — not in the SDK's static catalog (\`product-factory.ts\` aliases only define \`test-product\`, \`sports_ctv_q2\`, \`outdoor_ctv_q2\`, \`local_display_dynamic\`).

The CI's overlay step was supposed to copy \`static/compliance/source/\` onto the SDK cache before each run to bring fixtures into the runner's view. The step was operating correctly on \`main\` (where the cache is at \`@adcp/sdk/compliance/cache\`); the path predicate just hadn't been generalized for 3.0.x's \`@adcp/client\` location.

## Fix

Try the new path first (\`@adcp/sdk\`), fall back to the old one (\`@adcp/client\`). Both branches now converge on a single workflow file that works regardless of which package the SDK is installed as.

## Verification

Applied the workflow's new overlay logic locally (against the actual \`@adcp/client@5.21.1\` install) and ran each previously-failing storyboard:

\`\`\`
sales_guaranteed                     ✓ 11P / 0S / 0N/A
sales_broadcast_tv                   ✓ 13P / 0S / 0N/A

author: brentbarkman
body:
Closes #131

## Root cause

PR `d4a8f81` ("hide declined events to match Google Calendar default") added `myResponseStatus !== "declined"` filters to every timeline surface (desktop sidebar, today, main calendar; iOS Today, Calendar, Next Up). That correctly hides invitations the user declined — but it also hides events the user *organized* and then declined themselves.

The reporter's exact wording: *"Missing events I created with no attendees. Those should show."*

Two real-world paths produce a declined organizer-owned event:

1. The user creates an event with a single self-attendee row (Google sometimes auto-adds the organizer when you save the event), later RSVPs No to it as a placeholder, but keeps the event on their calendar. Pre-`d4a8f81` it stayed visible; after the fix it silently disappears.
2. The user organized a meeting, declined themselves because they can't make it personally, but is still hosting it for others / wants the time slot blocked. Same disappearance.

Google Calendar itself doesn't hide organizer-owned events from the "Hide declined events" toggle — declining your own event is rare enough that the user almost always still wants to see it.

## Approach

Three options considered:

1. **Filter "declined" only when the user did NOT organize the event** (chosen). Matches Google Calendar's actual behavior; the simplest semantic that keeps the original fix's intent intact for the common case (declined invitations from others).
2. Add a "show declined" toggle in Settings. Higher effort; the existing `myResponseStatus !== "declined"` filter site is already in 5 different files, so building a setting + plumbing it through every surface is overkill for a bug whose correct default is unambiguous.
3. Stop hiding declined events entirely (revert `d4a8f81`). Loses the user-affirming behavior of `d4a8f81`. The reporter explicitly likes the `d4a8f81` behavior — they just want the organizer carve-out.

Option 1 also matches the existing data we have: the server already computes `event.organizer.self === true` for events the user organized (see `apps/api/src/services/calendar-sync.ts` line 519). No new server work, no schema change, no migration.

## Implementation

Single-source-of-truth helper in `@brett/business`:

```ts
export function isHiddenDeclined(
  event: Pick<CalendarEventRecord, "myResponseStatus" | "organizer">
): boolean {
  if (event.myResponseStatus !== "declined") return false;
  return event.organizer?.self !== true;
}
```

iOS gets its own typed `CalendarEvent.isOrganizer` computed property since Swift can't import the JS helper:

```swift
var isOrganizer: Bool {
    (organizer?["self"] as? Bool) == true
}
```

Then every filter site updated:

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx` sidebar | `e.myResponseStatus !== "declined"` | `!isHiddenDeclined(e)` |
| `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx` today | `e.myResponseStatus !== "declined"` | `!isHiddenDeclined(e)` |
| `apps/desktop/src/pages/CalendarPage.tsx` | `e.myResponseStatus !== "declined"` | `!isHiddenDeclined(e)` |
| `apps/ios/.../CalendarPage.visibleEvents` | `myResponseStatus != .declined` | `myResponseStatus != .declined \|\| isOrganizer` |
| `apps/ios/.../TodayPage.todaysEvents` | `myResponseStatus != .declined` | `myResponseStatus != .declined \|\| isOrganizer` |
| `apps/ios/.../TodayPage.nextUpcomingEvent` | `myResponseStatus != .declined` | `myResponseStatus != .declined \|\| isOrganizer` |

## Tests

Added 5 tests for `isHiddenDeclined` in `packages/business/src/__tests__/calendar-validation.test.ts`:

- `hides events the user declined and someone else organized` — preserves `d4a8f81`'s intent
- `keeps declined events the user organized visible` — direct guard for the bug
- `treats declined-with-no-organizer-info as hidden (defensive)` — null organizer falls back to hide
- `keeps non-declined events visible regardless of organizer` — covers the (status × organizer) matrix
- `treats organizer.self omitted as not-organizer` — Google API absent-default semantics

Added 6 tests for `CalendarEvent.isOrganizer` in `apps/ios/BrettTests/Models/CalendarEventOrganizerTests.swift`:

- `selfTrueOrganizerIsTrue` / `selfFalseOrganizerIsFalse` — happy paths
- `missingSelfFieldIsFalse` / `nilOrganizerIsFalse` / `malformedOrganizerJSONIsFalse` — defensive defaults
- `filteringDeclinedKeepsOrganizerOwnedEvents` — end-to-end behaviour: a mixed list of `[my-declined, their-declined, their-accepted]` filtered with the new predicate keeps the right two and hides the right one

**Test-prevention reflection:** could a test have caught this bug? Yes — `keeps declined events the user organized visible` fails against the pre-PR filter for every variant of the data. Adding tests for the *category* (declined + organizer matrix) also guards against future regressions where someone tightens the filter again without thinking through organizer events.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @brett/business test` — 212 passed (212), including the 5 new ones
- `pnpm --filter @brett/business typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm --filter @brett/desktop typecheck` — clean (after building `@brett/ui` first to populate `.d.ts` cache)
- Pre-existing `@brett/api-core` `prisma.ts` typecheck errors are present on `main` and unrelated to this change.
- Swift toolchain not available on this Linux agent runner. CI does not build iOS. Please run `Brett` scheme tests in Xcode (or on a Mac runner) before merging. The new test suite auto-registers via XcodeGen.

## Self-review findings

1. First pass put `isHiddenDeclined` as a private helper in `apps/desktop/src/api/calendar.ts`. On review — it's the same predicate iOS needs (semantically) and is pure domain logic. Moved to `@brett/business/calendar-validation.ts` so there's one source of truth for the rule. iOS still has its own implementation because Swift can't import JS, but the test contract pins the same behaviour on both.
2. The `Pick<CalendarEventRecord, "myResponseStatus" | "organizer">` parameter type lets the helper accept any compatible shape — both `CalendarEventRecord` and `CalendarEventDetail` (which extends `CalendarEventRecord`) work without coercion.
3. iOS `isOrganizer` defensively returns `false` for nil organizer JSON and missing `self` field, matching the test expectations. A cast failure (e.g. `self: 1` instead of `true`) also returns false rather than crashing.
4. Considered making `myResponseStatus !== "declined" || isOrganizer` an inline expression at every site rather than extracting a helper. Five call sites with the same predicate is the kind of duplication that drifts — better to centralize, especially given the reasoning for the carve-out is non-obvious.
5. Multi-user safety: no `userId` scoping concerns — purely per-event display.
6. Backwards-compatible: API unchanged. The wire format still ships `myResponseStatus = "declined"` for declined events; only the client-side filter changes.
7. iOS ↔ desktop parity: both clients now apply the same rule. No drift.
8. Searched for every other `myResponseStatus` reference in the codebase; only AI / intelligence filters use `myResponseStatus !== "observer"` (different rule) and the RSVP UI reads it for badge display. No other timeline filters need updating.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **Risk:** for events created on a *secondary* calendar (where the user is the calendar owner but not necessarily the organizer email), Google's `organizer.self` may be `true` if the organizer email matches the calendar's email, but `false` if it doesn't. Edge case — out of scope for this bug.
- **Risk:** if Google ever changes the meaning of `organizer.self`, the carve-out drifts. Documented in the helper's docstring; the `treats organizer.self omitted as not-organizer` test pins the expected behaviour.
- **Follow-up (out of scope):** if Brent later wants a "show declined" toggle in Settings, the helper is the natural extension point — add a `showDeclined?: boolean` parameter and short-circuit when tr

Targets `claude/elastic-lamarr-1af992` (not main).

## Why

Phase 3 (#209) rewrote `.dockerignore` and dropped several defensive globs from the original — most importantly `**/TANK`, the personal scratchpad pattern that must never reach the production image. That was a mistake on my part: pruning "unused" patterns saves nothing in build context size and removes a cheap safety net.

## What

Two commits:

1. **Restore TANK + the obviously-relevant defensive blocks** — `**/TANK`, build/cache globs (`**/dist`, `**/.output`, `**/.tanstack`, `**/.cache`, etc.), editor/OS junk (`**/*~`, `**/.idea`, `**/*.sw[op]`, etc.), JS log files, stray artifacts (`**/count.txt`, `**/todos.json`).

It also refactors the startup logic to support these modes, improves error handling for output file paths, and adds a new regression test for preflight checks. These changes enhance usability and robustness, especially for deployment and automation scenarios.

**New CLI features:**

* Added `--validate` mode to perform config file validation without starting tracking, and `--preflight` mode to check config and output paths before running. These modes are mutually exclusive and can be invoked from the CLI. (`exec/fictrac.cpp`, `CHANGELOG.md`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f4f9e3bfee45574d99531800a2bdc6d7e8b74538f18f5d9945220c051092893fL28-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f4f9e3bfee45574d99531800a2bdc6d7e8b74538f18f5d9945220c051092893fR41-R42) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f4f9e3bfee45574d99531800a2bdc6d7e8b74538f18f5d9945220c051092893fR56-R61) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-f4f9e3bfee45574d99531800a2bdc6d7e8b74538f18f5d9945220c051092893fR76-R92) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-f4f9e3bfee45574d99531800a2bdc6d7e8b74538f18f5d9945220c051092893fL84-R115) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR11)

author: jiahui-gu
body:
## Root cause (Task #306 research)

PR #976 (Wave 0e persist.ts cutover, commit `1ed581c`) accidentally collapsed the renderer boot paint-gate.

- **Pre-#976**: `loadPersisted()` in `src/stores/persist.ts` awaited `window.ccsm.loadState(STATE_KEY)` — real async IPC, multiple event-loop turns. This gave React a paint frame after `root.render()` to commit the skeleton before hydration replaced it.
- **Post-#976**: `localStorage.getItem(STATE_KEY)` is sync inside the async wrapper, so the await resolves on the next microtask.
- Sibling `hydrateDrafts()` ALSO sync-bails at `src/stores/persist.ts:26` (`if (!window.ccsm) return;` — `window.ccsm` was nuked in Wave 0b PR #948).
- Net: `void hydrateStore()` at `src/index.tsx:68` completes within the same microtask as `root.render()`. Skeleton never paints. All 8 harness-ui cases waiting on skeleton/hydrated transitions / theme-init order / opacity transitions time out.

PR #985 probe trace evidence: `loadStateWrapped:true, hydrated:true, hasSidebarSkeleton:false`.

## Fix (Option B from research, architectural)

One-line change at `src/index.tsx`: wrap `void hydrateStore()` in `requestAnimationFrame(() => ...)`. This defers hydration past the next paint, restoring the pre-#976 paint-gate behavior.

- No `persist.ts` touch. Keeps `persist.ts` semantically truthful (sync IO described as sync).
- Locates the paint-gate at the boot wiring layer where the explanatory comment already lives.
- Comment block at `src/index.tsx:42-50` extended with 5 lines explaining why rAF is required after #976.
- Includes a `typeof requestAnimationFrame === 'function'` guard for non-DOM unit-test environments (jsdom has rAF, but defensive).

## Expected recovery (8 harness-ui e2e cases)

- settings-updates-pane
- titlebar
- theme-toggle
- import-empty-groups
- rename
- move-to-group-excludes-own-group
- sidebar-long-name-truncates
- startup-paints-before-hydrate

## Local checks

- lint: passing (0 errors, warnings unrelated)
- typecheck: passing (exit 0, both `tsc --noEmit` configs)
- build: passing (`npm run build:app` exit 0, webpack 5.106.2 + tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json)
- unit tests: 821 passing / 10 failing — **all 10 failures are `better-sqlite3` `NODE_MODULE_VERSION 145 vs 137` env mismatch**, unrelated to this change. vitest exit 0.
- e2e: **not run locally — harness-ui requires Linux+xvfb, this hotfix was developed on Windows**. Trusting CI Linux runner for the e2e signal per task instructions.

body:
### Motivation

- Implement a self-contained, generic open-addressing hashtable that aligns with common `std::unordered_map` usage and supports engineering features like pre-reservation and adjustable load factor.
- Improve delete semantics to avoid unnecessary object resets and enable tombstone reuse for performance with complex types.
- Provide fair multi-round benchmarking against `std::unordered_map` and basic functional tests to validate behavior and performance.

### Description

- Introduce a templated `hashtable<Key, T, Hash, KeyEqual>` implementing quadratic probing with buckets kept as a power-of-two and an initial bucket count of 16. 
- Add `reserve(size_t)`, `rehash(size_t)`, and `max_load_factor(float)` APIs, where `max_load_factor` is validated to be within `[0.1, 0.95]`, and resizing keeps bucket counts as powers of two. 
- Change `erase` to mark buckets as `Tombstone` without resetting `key`/`value`, track `size` and `tombstones`, and reuse tombstones on subsequent inserts via `place_new_bucket`. 
- Implement internal utilities including `next_power_of_two`, `mix64` hash mixing, `ensure_capacity_for_insert`, and `rehash_to_bucket_count`; provide `insert`, `find`, `contains`, `operator[]`, and `clear` operations. 
- Add multi-round benchmark harness (`run_multi_round_bench`) and a functional test suite (`run_functional_tests`) that exercise insertion, lookup, erase, `reserve`, and `max_load_factor` behavior; benchmark compares average insert/find times against `std::unordered_map` over `kRounds = 5` with `kCount = 300000` keys.

### Testing

- Ran the built-in functional assertions via `run_functional_tests`, and all assertions passed (reported "[TEST] 工程化功能测试全部通过。").
- Executed the multi-round benchmark (`run_benchmark`) comparing the custom `hashtable` and `std::unordered_map` over `kRounds = 5`, which completed and printed average insert/find times for both containers.
- No additional automated test frameworks were run as part of this change.

## Summary

Iter-2 left pacta-wis2's conformance classes invisible in combined mode because pygeoapi owns ``/conformance`` (ADR 0012 § 6). Iter-3 task 11 closes the gap with a proxy intercept.

- New ``ConformanceUnionMiddleware``: buffers ``GET /conformance`` from the downstream pygeoapi mount, parses the JSON, appends each pacta-wis2 ``CONFORMANCE_CLASSES`` entry not already present (preserving downstream order, deduplicating), recomputes ``Content-Length`` and re-emits the merged document.
- Pass-through on non-200, missing ``conformsTo``, invalid JSON, non-``/conformance`` paths, and non-GET methods.
- Wired by ``build_combined_app`` ahead of the auth + gating stack. The wrapper helper was renamed ``_wrap_pygeoapi_with_pacta_gating`` → ``_wrap_pygeoapi_with_pacta_extensions`` because it now always carries at least the conformance middleware (even without a verifier).

## Test plan

- [x] Combined-app conformance test upgraded with a realistic pygeoapi-shaped stub asserting the merged shape
- [x] ruff / pyright / vulture / lint-imports / deptry clean

## Notes for task 14

The middleware adds two new ADR-vs-code invariants:
- ADR-0012-§6-augmented — combined-mode ``/conformance`` includes both pygeoapi's and pacta's conformance classes (proven by ``test_conformance_unions_pygeoapi_and_pacta_classes``)
- order + dedupe — downstream classes appear first, in original order; pacta classes follow only if not already declared (proven by ``test_classes_appended_in_extra_order`` + ``test_duplicates_are_deduplicated``)

body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The FastAPI application lacked limits on uploaded file sizes, enabling memory-exhaustion Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. Exception handlers were also leaking internal file paths and stack traces via raw `str(e)` output in 500 errors. Furthermore, the `colors` parameter in the KMeans endpoint lacked boundaries.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could crash the application by uploading excessively large files or specifying massive color clusters. Additionally, error messages could be leveraged to gain insights into the server's internal filesystem structure.
🔧 Fix: Implemented a 10MB limit on `UploadFile.size` before reading payloads into memory. Replaced raw exception strings with generic 'Internal Server Error' messages. Added bounded integer validation via FastAPI `Query` to the `/predict/colors` endpoint.
✅ Verification: Code syntax was verified with `py_compile`, formatted with `flake8`, and the legacy test suite was executed to ensure stability.

author: godsboy
body:
## What does this PR do?

The Kanban board is documented as shared across all Hermes profiles, but the implementation resolved `kanban.db`, the workspaces root, and the per-task log directory through `get_hermes_home()`, which returns the **active profile's** HERMES_HOME. So when the dispatcher spawned a worker with `hermes -p <profile> --skills kanban-worker chat -q "work kanban task <id>"`, the worker's `_apply_profile_override()` rewrote HERMES_HOME to `~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>` before `kanban_db.py` imported, opening a profile-local `kanban.db` that did not contain the dispatcher's task. `kanban_show` and `kanban_complete` failed; the dispatcher's row stayed `running` and got retried/crashed. The same defect applied to the worker log directory, so `hermes kanban tail` did not see worker output either.

This PR adds a `kanban_home()` helper that anchors at the shared Hermes root (the parent of any active profile) and reroutes every kanban path consumer through it. Profile-specific config, `.env`, memory, and sessions stay isolated; only the kanban surface is shared, matching the user-guide page and the long-standing module docstring ("profile-agnostic on purpose").

The helper resolves through:

1. `HERMES_KANBAN_HOME` env var (explicit override for tests and unusual deployments).
2. `get_default_hermes_root()`, which already understands the `<root>/profiles/<name>` shape and Docker / custom HERMES_HOME paths.

## Related Issue

Fixes #19348

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`:
  - Add `kanban_home()` (resolves `HERMES_KANBAN_HOME` first, then `get_default_hermes_root()`).
  - Reroute `kanban_db_path()`, `workspaces_root()`, `_default_spawn`'s log dir, `gc_worker_logs`, and `worker_log_path()` through it.
  - Refresh module docstring and the `kanban_db_path` / `workspaces_root` / `resolve_workspace` docstrings to describe shared-root behavior.
- `hermes_cli/kanban.py`: tiny help-string update for the `log` subcommand (was `$HERMES_HOME/kanban/logs/`, now `<kanban-root>/kanban/logs/`).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py`: new `TestSharedBoardPaths` regression class (8 tests).

The user-guide page already says "shared across all your Hermes profiles", so the docs are not changed in this PR. The `HERMES_KANBAN_HOME` override is documented in the helper's docstring.

No schema changes, no new config keys, no changes to the dispatcher loop, claim/heartbeat logic, or CLI command surface.

## How to Test

Reproduction (without the fix):

1. On a host with at least one non-default profile (e.g. `nehemiahkanban`), start the gateway (no profile) so the dispatcher uses `~/.hermes/kanban.db`.
2. `hermes kanban create "smoke" --assignee nehemiahkanban`. The task lands in `~/.hermes/kanban.db`.
3. The dispatcher claims and spawns `hermes -p nehemiahkanban --skills kanban-worker chat -q "work kanban task <id>"`.
4. Worker resolves `kanban_db_path()` to `~/.hermes/profiles/nehemiahkanban/kanban.db` (a different file). `kanban_show` / `kanban_complete` fail; the row stays `running`.

After the fix, both sides resolve to `~/.hermes/kanban.db` and the worker can complete the task.

Automated coverage:

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_core_functionality.py
```

The bug-reproducing tests in `TestSharedBoardPaths` (notably `test_profile_worker_resolves_to_shared_root`, `test_dispatcher_and_profile_worker_converge`, and `test_dispatcher_and_worker_share_a_real_database`) fail on `origin/main` and pass with this PR. The full kanban surface (186 tests) stays green.

Manual cross-platform note: the fix only changes path computation through `pathlib.Path` (no shell, no process management changes). Windows-safe.

### Migrating an in-flight installation

If the bug has already produced profile-local `kanban.db` files, kanban tooling will stop reaching them after this fix. Either:

- Move the rows you care about into `~/.hermes/kanban.db`, or
- Delete the stale profile-local boards (e.g. `rm ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/kanban.db*`).

The original symlink workaround documented in #19348 (`ln -s ~/.hermes/kanban.db ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/kanban.db`) keeps working as a stop-gap if needed.

### Note on the `Tests` workflow

The `Tests` job currently fails on `main` with 15 unrelated test failures (gateway teams, systemd unit generation, update flow, concurrent interrupt, credential pool env fallback, dockerfile pid1 reaping, etc.). The exact same set of failures appears on this PR. None of them touch the kanban path layer or are caused by this change. Once the upstream regressions land green on `main`, this PR should follow.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(kanban): ...`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_core_functionality.py` and 186 tests pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (regression tests fail on `origin/main`, pass with this PR)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu Linux

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (`kanban_db.py` docstrings describe the shared-root behavior; the user-guide page already says "shared across all your Hermes profiles")
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A (no new config keys; `HERMES_KANBAN_HOME` is an env-var-only escape hatch)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A (the fix follows AGENTS.md's existing "Profile operations are HOME-anchored, not HERMES_HOME-anchored" guidance for the same architectural reason)
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — only `pathlib.Path` arithmetic, Windows-safe
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

author: tfatykhov
body:
## Summary
PR #410's F027 prompt rewrite worked (LLM merges 4 of 5 clusters, up from 0 of 5 baseline). But the action audit then revealed admission was rejecting 3 of those merges as "redundant" — composite scores 0.52-0.59 vs prod threshold 0.60.

Audit judge said 2 of 3 rejections were **wrong** — the merges were substantively useful consolidations that admission incorrectly tagged as redundant.

## Root cause

Cluster_consolidation by design **restates existing fact content** as a single compressed fact. Admission's novelty score is therefore naturally low for these — admission would always penalize correct consolidations as "you already have this content elsewhere", which is exactly the redundancy the merge is trying to eliminate.

Same logic applies to F031 contradiction_resolution MERGE actions (currently surviving admission only because their confidence is hardcoded to 0.8; if that ever drifts they hit the same trap).

## Fix

Add both `cluster_consolidation` and `contradiction_resolution` to the default `bypass_sources` list. These are post-LLM consolidation operations, not new content — admission's quality filter doesn't apply.

Safety preserved by the **supersede chain**: if a merge turns out wrong, the source facts remain reachable via `superseded_by` links and can be re-activated.

## Verification path (eval framework)

After deploy:
1. Trigger sleep cycle (POST /sleep/trigger)
2. Re-run `nous_eval.probes.sleep_action_audit`
3. Expect F027 quality_score to rise from 50% (today, 2 merged + 3 false-rejected) toward ~80-100% (admission stops rejecting valid merges)

## Test plan
- [x] 2 new tests in `tests/test_admission.py::TestBypass`:
  - `test_cluster_consolidation_bypasses` — verify bypass triggers even with `max_existing_similarity=0.95` (the case admission penalizes hardest)
  - `test_contradiction_resolution_bypasses` — same, for F031 MERGE
- [x] 7 bypass tests pass total
- [x] Existing admission behavior unchanged for all other sources

## Related
The eval-find-then-fix loop continuing into a third iteration:
- PR #404 found F027 produced 0 output
- PR #405 fixed the cap
- PR #410 fixed the LLM-refusal pattern (20% → 50%)
- THIS PR fixes the admission false-rejections (50% → expected 80%+)

author: os8ai
body:
## Goal

Phase 4 Track B desktop side. Pairs with **PR 4.5** (already merged in `os8dotai#15`). Emits structured events at install state transitions; flushes in batches with strict allowlist sanitization and double-hashed client IDs. Default OFF; first-install consent moment surfaces it.

## What changed

**`src/services/app-telemetry.js`** (new):
- `getClientId` / `rotateClientId` — random UUID at `~/os8/.telemetry/client-id` (mode 0600); rotation severs the link between past and future events.
- `isEnabled(db)` — reads `app_store.telemetry.opt_in` (defaults `false`; flipped at first-install consent).
- `enqueue(db, event)` — no-op when opted out; sanitizer drops every key not in `ALLOWED_FIELDS` so a future contributor adding `userEmail` can't leak. `os` / `arch` always pinned to runtime values.
- `fingerprintFailure(line)` — SHA-256 of `strip(/[\d\/\\]/, slice 256)` → 16-char hex. Deterministic clusters; never the raw line.
- `flush(db)` — drains `TELEMETRY_BATCH_SIZE` (25) pending events to `https://os8.ai/api/apps/telemetry` via `fetch` with 15s timeout. Marks `sent_at` on success; leaves rows unsent on HTTP/network failure for next cycle. Drops pending on opt-out flip mid-batch. GCs `sent_at` rows older than 7d. Re-schedules if more pending exist.

**`src/services/app-installer.js`** — wires `AppTelemetry.enqueue` at `install_started` (in `approve()`) and `install_succeeded` / `install_failed` (around `_runApprove`). Failure fingerprint reads the last `[stderr]` line from `app_install_jobs.log_path` (never the raw line). Helpers resolve adapter/framework from `manifest.runtime.kind` / `manifest.framework`. Telemetry failures never disrupt the install.

**`src/services/app-auto-updater.js`** — emits `update_succeeded` / `update_failed` alongside the existing `onUpdated`/`onFailed` callbacks. `listEligible` now SELECTs `manifest_yaml` so the telemetry payload can carry adapter/framework.

**`src/renderer/install-plan-modal.js`** — first-install consent moment: `maybeShowFirstInstallConsent` reads `app_store.telemetry.consent_shown`; if `false`, sets `state.firstInstallConsent` so the consent block renders above the footer with a default-checked toggle. On Install click, writes `opt_in` + flips `consent_shown` so the block hides forever. Wired in all 3 modal-open paths (BySlug / FromYaml / FromManifest).

**`src/renderer/settings.js`** — `loadAppStoreSettings` + `saveAppStoreSettings` round-trip `app_store.telemetry.opt_in`. `appStoreTelemetryReset` button click calls `window.os8.appStore.resetTelemetryClientId`.

**`src/ipc/app-store.js` + `preload.js`** — `app-store:reset-telemetry-client-id` handler dispatches to `AppTelemetry.rotateClientId`. `resetTelemetryClientId()` preload export.

**`index.html`** — "Send anonymous install telemetry" toggle + "Reset anonymous client ID" button in App Store settings, with privacy-explainer hints.

**`styles/install-plan-modal.css`** — `.install-plan-modal__consent` styling.

## Tests

```
✓ tests/app-telemetry.test.js (23 tests)
  - isEnabled (default off / opt-in flipped / missing settings table)
  - enqueue (no-op when opted out, write when opted in, sanitizer
    drops unknown keys, sanitizer pins os/arch from runtime, refuses
    no-kind events)
  - fingerprintFailure (hex shape, determinism, line-number
    differences collide via path/numeric strip, empty input)
  - getClientId / rotateClientId (UUID shape, persistence, rotation
    yields different ID)
  - flush (POSTs pending when opted in; drops when opted out at
    flush time; leaves rows on network failure / HTTP 500; respects
    TELEMETRY_BATCH_SIZE; no-op when nothing pending)
  - sanitize (allowlist-only output; drops null + undefined)
```

Full suite: **1334 / 1337 pass** across 97 files (+23 vs prior; 1 pre-existing flake; 2 skipped).

## Privacy contract recap

- Default OFF; first-install consent moment surfaces it (default checked).
- Sends only: `adapter` / `framework` / `channel` / `slug` / `commit` / `failurePhase` / `failureFingerprint` / `durationMs` / `os` / `arch` / `overrideReason`. Allowlist enforced.
- Never sends raw logs, paths, secrets, hostnames, usernames, or anything from per-app secrets / dev-import toggles.
- Anonymous client ID is a random UUID; user can rotate via Settings. PR 4.5 server re-hashes with HMAC + secret salt before storage.

## Smoke gate

None gating, per `phase-4-plan.md` §6 ("No gate for 4.4/4.5 — no way to smoke telemetry beyond unit tests + 24h soak time"). Once the fleet starts emitting, the dashboard at `/internal/telemetry/install` (PR 4.5) will surface real events; if data doesn't flow as expected, fix-forward.

## Vercel env reminder

For Leo / Vercel: PR 4.5 needs `TELEMETRY_HASH_SALT` and `OS8_CURATORS` env vars set on the production deployment for ingest + dashboard to work. Without them the route returns 503 (which the desktop emitter handles by leaving rows unsent and retrying).

## Summary

- Adds `ShowControl/OSCFabric/` — a new shared package with `FabricClient` and `load_network_config()`, implementing the on-change + heartbeat fire semantics required by ADR-0007 that neither FlowerBeds nor FundingCAPTCHA had actually built
- Wires both elements to use it, deleting their duplicated ad-hoc OSC send code and hardcoded `network.json` path traversal
- Adds `change_epsilon` to `network.json` as a tunable show-level parameter
- Creates stub hook scripts (`scripts/hooks/smoke_test.py`, `scripts/hooks/firmware_config_gen.py`) that the existing PostToolUse hooks referenced but didn't exist

## What changed per file

**`ShowControl/OSCFabric/client.py`** — `FabricClient(element, config, transport=None)` with three methods: `report(signal, value)` (on-change send), `send_event(event)` (one-shot, no args), `tick(dt)` (heartbeat accumulator). Real OSC transport swallows network errors. Inject a `Transport` for tests.

**`ShowControl/OSCFabric/config.py`** — `load_network_config(path=None)` finds `ShowControl/network.json` from a single known location. Raises `FileNotFoundError` rather than returning `{}` silently.

**`ShowControl/OSCFabric/test_client.py`** — 19 tests covering on-change suppression, epsilon threshold, independent signal tracking, one-shot events, heartbeat timing/accumulation/reset, and config loading.

**`ShowControl/FlowerBeds/main.py`** — removes `load_network()` and `_build_treehouse_client()`; frame loop now calls `fabric.report("activity", v)` + `fabric.tick(1/fps)`.

**`ShowControl/FundingCAPTCHA/server.py`** — removes `_OSC_AVAILABLE`, `_osc_clients`, `_send_osc`, `NETWORK` path constant; adds `_fabric` global and a 1-second async heartbeat task in the lifespan (no frame loop available in this element).

- [ ] `python ShowControl/FlowerBeds/main.py --config ShowControl/FlowerBeds/settings.json --mock-camera --no-osc` — runs without error

All per-phase loops `ok=1 skip=0 err=0`; cohort emit returned `session_overlays=8 binned_overlays=8 mean_trace=2 mean_video=2` (mean_video gated to short window per C7.7 default).

author: ziyadedher
body:
Disclaimer: written by AI, but reviewed by me and currently running in my home lab setup.

## What

Adds a new optional `grpc_metadata` map to the provider config that gets appended as static gRPC metadata (HTTP/2 headers on the wire) on every outgoing call.

```hcl
provider "temporal" {
  host = "temporal-grpc.example.com"
  port = "443"
  grpc_metadata = {
    "cf-access-client-id"     = "abc.access"
    "cf-access-client-secret" = "shh"
  }
}
```

Also reads `TEMPORAL_GRPC_METADATA` (comma-separated `k=v` pairs) for parity with the existing env-var pattern.

## Why

Useful for reverse-proxy authentication that lives at the HTTP/2 header layer rather than the OAuth Bearer layer:

- **Cloudflare Access service tokens** (`cf-access-client-id` / `cf-access-client-secret`) — the original motivation. CF Access can't gate gRPC on most plans, so users front Temporal with their own reverse proxy that validates a header
- **caddy-security with API keys** (`x-api-key` / `x-auth-realm`)
- **AWS WAF custom-rule headers**
- **Tailscale Funnel headers**
- **Internal mTLS proxies** that translate certs to a header for the backend

The provider already supports OAuth Bearer (via `client_id`/`client_secret`/`token_url`) but that's only one shape of header auth. For everything else, users currently have to set up SSH tunnels or `cloudflared access tcp` wrappers — fine for ad-hoc, painful as a documented pattern.

## Implementation

- New `temporalProviderModel.GrpcMetadata` (`types.Map`) with `tfsdk:"grpc_metadata"`. Schema marks `Sensitive=true` (typical use is credentials).
- `Configure()` reads the map AND the `TEMPORAL_GRPC_METADATA` env var; provider config takes precedence (mirrors the existing pattern for other attrs).
- `CreateGRPCClient` takes the metadata as a new trailing arg; threads through to all three constructors (`Authenticated`, `Secure`, `Insecure`).
- Each constructor adds matching `grpc.WithChainUnaryInterceptor` and `grpc.WithChainStreamInterceptor` that call `metadata.AppendToOutgoingContext` per RPC. Returns nil interceptor for empty/nil metadata so we don't add a no-op to the dial chain.
- For `CreateAuthenticatedClient`, the existing OAuth Bearer interceptor chains with the new metadata interceptor via `WithChainUnaryInterceptor`, so both the Authorization header AND the extra metadata land on every call.

## Tests

- Existing `provider_oauth_test.go` call sites updated to pass `nil` for the new arg.
- New `provider_metadata_test.go` covers:
  - Insecure client appends configured headers
  - Authenticated client appends BOTH OAuth Bearer AND extras
  - Empty/nil metadata produces no dial options (no no-op interceptor)
  - `parseGrpcMetadataEnv` handles whitespace, missing eq, empty keys/values

## Compatibility

Backwards compatible — every existing call site passes `nil` for the new arg and behaves identically. No schema deprecations.

## Verification

Built locally with these changes via `dev_overrides`, deployed against a real CF-Tunnel-fronted Temporal cluster gated by a Caddy reverse-proxy that validates `X-Api-Key` headers (the caddy-security setup). `tofu plan`/`apply` against three `temporal_schedule` resources succeeds end-to-end with the metadata reaching the origin.

## Summary

This PR is part of the Shielded Voting merge sequence, split for ease of review. Please view [this document](https://hackmd.io/@TJGUVkqNQYieiMqJQQBDeA/B1nzBrBA-g/edit) for details.

Brings the SDK up to released versions of `librustzcash`, `orchard`, and the wider zcash crate ecosystem; drops the `[patch.crates-io]` block; applies the four mechanical FFI changes the new APIs require.

## Version changes

| Crate | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `zcash_address` | 0.10 | 0.11 |
| `zcash_client_backend` | 0.21 | 0.22 |
| `zcash_client_sqlite` | 0.19 | 0.20 |
| `zcash_primitives` | 0.26 | 0.27 |
| `zcash_proofs` | 0.26 | 0.27 |
| `zcash_protocol` | 0.7 | 0.8 |
| `zcash_transparent` | 0.6 | 0.7 |
| `sapling-crypto` | 0.6 | 0.7 |
| `orchard` | 0.12 | 0.13 |
| `pczt` | 0.5 | 0.6 |

The entire `[patch.crates-io]` block is removed — every previously git-rev-pinned crate now has a matching released version.

## Why

- The current `librustzcash@438657c5` + `orchard@6b12c77` pins are stale enough that downstream wallets (zashi-ios, zodl-ios) can't link the SDK against the wallet stacks they ship with — typically failing with "multiple different versions of crate `orchard` / `zcash_primitives` in the dependency graph".
- `pczt 0.6` and `zcash_client_sqlite 0.20` are required transitively by `voting-circuits 0.4.x` and `zcash_voting 0.3.x`, so this is also the prerequisite for layering the voting feature on `main`.

## FFI adapter changes

Mechanical, no behaviour change:

- `get_spendable_transparent_outputs` and `propose_shielding` gained a `TransparentOutputFilter` parameter — pass `::All`.
- `ReceiverFlags::to_address_request` now returns `ReceiverRequirementError`; propagate via `anyhow!`.
- `ConfirmationsPolicy::try_from` error widened from `()` to `Display`; format via `{e}`.

author: ejosterberg
body:
## Summary

Promotes **Oklahoma** from tier-2 (rate-only via SST data) to tier-1 (fully maintained taxability matrix + tests). OK is an SST member; statewide rate **4.5%** per **68 O.S. section 1354**.

## Headline findings

- **HB 1955 of 2024 (signed 2024-02-27, effective 2024-08-29)** eliminated the **state portion** of the food/food-ingredients sales tax (4.5% → **0.000%** state rate). **Local sales taxes still apply** at the full local rate. Encoded with ``rate_modifier=Decimal(\"0.000\")`` per the AR/KS pattern. OK's grocery definition is **broader than SST** -- expressly includes bottled water, candy, and soft drinks.
- **August Sales Tax Holiday** under **68 O.S. section 1357.10** (state-side) and **68 O.S. section 1377** (parallel county/municipal-side): clothing and footwear under $100 per item, first Friday-Saturday-Sunday in August. **2026 dates: August 7-9**. Notably narrow scope -- ONLY clothing and footwear, not school supplies / electronics (contrast with AR's 26-52-444 multi-scope holiday).
- **Notable peer-state difference -- digital goods NOT taxable.** Per **OAC 710:65-19-156** + OK Tax Commission letter rulings, electronically-delivered digital products (music, video, e-books, prewritten software downloads, online cards, etc.) are NOT subject to OK sales/use tax. Underlying rationale: 68 O.S. section 1354 only reaches tangible personal property; OK has not adopted SST's \"specified digital products\" definitions. Joins NV in the small minority of SST states with this property.
- **Marketplace-nexus quirk** (informational only): marketplace facilitator threshold is **\$10,000** vs **\$100,000** for remote sellers (68 O.S. § 1391 et seq.). Documented in module docstring; does not affect rate calculation.

## What changed

- new `src/opensalestax/states/oklahoma.py` -- full StateModule subclassing `SstStateModule`
- new `tests/unit/test_state_oklahoma.py` -- **27 tests** (metadata, Protocol, registration, taxability matrix, holiday count + dates + cap, jurisdiction-type mapping, statutory-citation enforcement, defensive regression that the holiday scope stays narrow)
- removed `Oklahoma` class from `src/opensalestax/states/_tier2.py` (tier-2 count 13 → 12; `TIER_2_CLASSES` updated)
- `src/opensalestax/states/__init__.py` -- alphabetical `oklahoma` import added
- `tests/unit/test_state_tier2.py` -- count 13 → 12; OK removed from `EXPECTED_TIER_2_ABBREVS`; OK added to `phase_1_states_all_registered` set
- `tests/integration/test_api.py` -- OK added to SST tier-1 lists in two assertions
- `specs/research/references.md` -- full `### OK -- Oklahoma` section with statutes, Administrative Code citations, sources, and notes
- `MAINTAINERS.md` -- OK row added alphabetically (Nevada → Oklahoma → South Carolina); tier-2 list updated 13 → 12

## Quality

- 0 ruff issues; 0 ruff format diffs; 0 mypy issues (72 source files)
- All **703** unit tests pass (was 682 baseline; +27 OK tests, −6 tier-2 parametrized tests for OK's removed tier-2 entry)
- Statutory citation in **every** TaxabilityRule.notes AND HolidayWindow.notes
- All money values are `Decimal`
- DCO sign-off on the commit

## Test plan

- [x] `poetry run ruff check .` clean
- [x] `poetry run ruff format --check .` clean
- [x] `poetry run mypy src/` clean
- [x] `poetry run pytest tests/unit/ -q` -- 703 passed
- [ ] CI matrix (PostgreSQL + MariaDB) green
- [ ] Integration tests (`/v1/states` shows OK tier-1 SST) green in CI

## Flags for the orchestrator

- **SST jurisdiction-type code mapping is an ASSUMPTION.** OK's actual rate-file codes were not empirically validated at promotion time; the module defaults to the canonical MN/WI mapping (45=state, 00=county, 01=city, 63=district). Validating against an actual `OKR<...>.csv` file is the natural next maintenance task -- documented in module docstring, references.md, and MAINTAINERS.md.
- **HB 1955 grocery elimination is encoded with `rate_modifier=Decimal(\"0.000\")`.** The engine does not yet apply `rate_modifier` (deferred to v0.6+). Until that lands, the engine over-collects the 4.5% state portion on grocery line items in Oklahoma. Same caveat as AR (Grocery Tax Relief Act) and KS (HB 2106 phase-down) -- all three states share the pattern.
- **Holiday scope deliberately narrow.** A defensive regression test (`test_oklahoma_holiday_excludes_school_supplies`) catches a future maintainer who might copy AR's six-scope pattern. OK's statute covers ONLY clothing/footwear.

Replaces the static grep-chain TS check with a python step that:

- Applies the universal builtin allowlist (bindings/, tests/, scripts/, mcp-adapter/, *vscode*/, cli/, mod.ts, lsp-server.ts, deno-*/, etc.)
- **Reads the per-repo `.claude/CLAUDE.md` 'TypeScript Exemptions' table at CI time** and treats each `Path` row as allowed.

Why: the previous static allowlist required editing the workflow whenever a legitimate per-repo exemption was needed. This made the per-repo `.claude/CLAUDE.md` exemption table (the documented source of truth) and the workflow drift apart. Now they're the same single source.

To exempt a path going forward: add one row to `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s 'TypeScript Exemptions' table — no workflow edit required.

To migrate off TS: see Human_Programming_Guide.adoc migration chapter (in affinescript repo).

## Summary
- The three function-style capture helpers (`capture_firmware_events`, `capture_enqueue_order`, `capture_devices_events`) all swapped `controller._db.bus` (and `capture_enqueue_order` also `_queue`) and never restored the originals. Fine in practice because the factory builds a fresh controller per test, but a latent footgun if a future test held a controller reference past the assertion.
- Convert each to a `@pytest.fixture` that yields a factory callable. Call sites stay identical (`captured = capture_X(controller, EventType.Y, ...)`); each test signature picks up the fixture by name. Auto-restore via fixture teardown reinstates the originals so sibling tests can't see a leaked stub.
- Add `CaptureEventsFactory` / `CaptureEnqueueOrderFactory` / `CaptureDevicesEventsFactory` type aliases so test signatures get a clean type for the fixture parameter.
- Drops the `from .conftest import capture_*` imports across 8 firmware test files and 5 devices test files.

## Summary

Telegram bot (`@Humaeera_bot`) "Freepik Tryon Bot" dengan dua fitur:

- **👗 Mannequin Tryon** — user kirim 1 foto outfit, bot kembalikan 2 hasil (close-up + full-body) dengan dress baru terpasang di mannequin. Pantulan cermin ikut diganti dengan outfit baru.
- **🧥 Hanger** — user pilih 1–5 outfit, kirim satu per satu, bot kembalikan 2 hasil (wide rack + close-up) dengan baju hanger diganti, urut kiri-ke-kanan.

### Pendekatan: masked inpainting (Ideogram)

Sebelumnya pakai text-to-image dengan reference (Nano Banana Pro). Hasilnya framing sering bergeser (close-up jadi full-body, hanger background/angle berubah). Pindah ke **masked inpainting** via `POST /v1/ai/ideogram-image-edit`:

1. 4 mask PNG di-bundle bareng master image (`mannequin_1_mask.png`, dst). Black region = boleh di-edit (dress + pantulan cermin / area hanger), white region = harus persis sama dengan master.
2. Saat user upload outfit, bot kirim master + mask + prompt + outfit sebagai `style_reference_images` ke Ideogram.
3. Mask menjamin framing, background, mannequin, cermin, rack, lighting tidak boleh berubah — hanya region yang ada di mask yang di-render ulang.

### Sistem token & rotasi key

- 1 token = 1 gambar yang berhasil di-deliver (atomic deduct, audit log).
- Notif sisa token ≤ 10: "Token sisa X segera hubungi admin untuk Top-up Token" + footer "By : Aksara Strategy".
- Admin command: `/grant <user_id> <amount>`, `/users`, `/keystatus`.
- API key rotation: 401/403 → permanent blacklist, 402/429 → cooldown 120 s, 5xx/network → retry sampai 4× lintas pool.

### UI

- Tidak ada mention Freepik / Gemini / Ideogram / Nano Banana di copy user-facing.
- Pilihan rasio per fitur: 1:1, 3:4, 4:3, 16:9, 9:16. Master + mask di-center-crop ke ratio sebelum dikirim, tetap aligned.
- Progress bar 0–100% live di pesan Telegram yang sama.

### File yang berubah di commit inpainting

- `freepik.py`: `create_inpaint_task()` + `wait_for_task(path=...)` untuk endpoint Ideogram.
- `generator.py`: `run_inpaint_batch()` + `InpaintTaskInput`.
- `images.py`: `mask_filename()`, `crop_pair_to_aspect_ratio()` (master + mask di-crop bareng).
- `bot.py`: ganti flow ke inpainting, prompt per-asset.
- `prompts.py`: prompt jauh lebih pendek, fokus garment fidelity.
- `assets/*_mask.png`: mask untuk 4 master.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Test ulang **Mannequin Tryon** dengan beberapa outfit (background polos vs flat-lay) di rasio 1:1 dan 3:4 — pastikan framing close-up tidak drift dan pantulan cermin ikut menampakkan baju baru.
- [ ] Test **Hanger** dengan qty 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — pastikan baju selalu **center**, jumlah persis, rack/dinding/cahaya tidak berubah.
- [ ] Test rasio extreme (16:9 dan 9:16) — center-crop bisa agresif untuk master 3:4; pastikan hasil masih bisa diterima atau pilih ratio dekat-master (3:4 / 1:1) untuk hasil paling utuh.
- [ ] Verifikasi token system: kirim `/grant <user_id> 5` lalu generate beberapa kali, cek saldo tepat ter-deduct sesuai jumlah gambar yang sukses ter-deliver.
- [ ] Verifikasi notifikasi "Token sisa ≤ 10" muncul + footer "By : Aksara Strategy".

### Notes

- 50 unit tests pass (`pytest tests/ -q`), `ruff check` clean.
- Preview untuk 5 ratio × 2 fitur dengan daster contoh sudah dishare di chat.
- Bot di VM Devin sudah saya restart pakai code branch ini supaya bisa langsung dicoba. VM tidak persistent — untuk produksi perlu deploy permanen (Fly.io / Railway / VPS).

author: bennich
body:
## Summary

Three features adapted from Li Zuqiang's `SHG_SharpCap-Script-20250922`:

1. **Solar tracking rate** — switches the mount to ASCOM `Solar` tracking at session start (and restores the previous rate on exit / abort), removing the ~30″/min drift that sidereal tracking introduces during solar observing. Falls back gracefully on drivers that don't expose `SetTrackingRate`.

2. **`SlewTo`-based return-to-start** — between cycles, instead of dead-reckoning back at `-RETURN_MULTIPLIER` for a computed time, save `(RA, Dec)` of the leading limb after `find_solar_limb()` and `SlewTo` it at the end of the cycle. Encoder-precise, no accumulating navigation error. Same pattern in the post-loop disk-centre park.

3. **Bidirectional capture** (`ENABLE_BIDIRECTIONAL = True`) — after the forward scan ends in dark sky past the trailing limb, immediately scan back at `-scan_multiplier` for the same `scan_duration` to capture the disk in reverse. Doubles scans per cycle and amortises alignment overhead. Each scan is tagged via `SharpCap.TargetName` as `<base>_fwd` / `<base>_rev` so the two sets are easy to identify in JSol'Ex.

## Why bidirectional matters most at high FPS

Empirical analysis on the SVBONY SV503 + TOUPTEK G3M867M + SHG-700 + SAL-33 rig at ~370 fps:

| Metric | Forward-only | Bidirectional |
|---|---|---|
| Scan time | ~15 s | 2 × ~15 s = 30 s |
| Fast return | ~5 s | 0 (just reverses direction) |
| Alignment overhead per cycle (avg) | ~13 s | ~13 s |
| **Per-cycle wall time** | ~33 s for 1 scan | ~44 s for 2 scans |
| **Time per scan** | ~33 s | ~22 s |
| **Scans per 3-min coherence window** | ~5 | ~8 |

At low FPS the gain is more like 5–10%; the value comes from amortising the fixed alignment cost across two scans.

## JSol'Ex workflow note

Reverse-direction SERs reconstruct as a horizontally mirrored disk because the time axis is reversed. The post-processing flow is:

1. Reconstruct `*_fwd.ser` files normally.
2. Reconstruct `*_rev.ser` files **with horizontal inversion turned on** (per-file option in JSol'Ex).
3. Hand both sets to JSol'Ex's stacking tool to align and average — gets you ~√2× SNR improvement over a forward-only stack of the same length.

## Relationship to other PRs

- **Built on top of [#2](https://github.com/bennich/sharpcap-solar-scanning/pull/2)** (back-up-rate fix). Bidirectional depends on the symmetric scan endpoints that fix establishes — without it, the reverse leg would inherit the same trailing-limb shortfall. The back-up fix commit appears in this PR too (cherry-picked); whichever PR merges first makes the other partially redundant.
- **Independent of [#1](https://github.com/bennich/sharpcap-solar-scanning/pull/1)** (SideOfPier). No conflicts expected at merge time.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run a single bidirectional cycle and confirm SharpCap writes two SER files with `_fwd` / `_rev` suffixes in the configured target folder.
- [ ] Confirm the printed `Tracking: switched to Solar (was ...)` line appears at the start of the session and `restored to ...` at the end.
- [ ] Confirm cycle-to-cycle returns now print `Returning to saved limb position via SlewTo...` instead of doing the dead-reckoning slew, and that the next cycle's `find_solar_limb()` succeeds quickly.
- [ ] Verify reverse SER reconstructs cleanly in JSol'Ex with horizontal flip enabled, and stacks against the forward reconstruction.
- [ ] On a driver that doesn't expose `SetTrackingRate`, confirm the script prints the fallback warning and proceeds.
- [ ] On a driver where `SlewTo` fails, confirm the script prints the fallback message and continues (does NOT silently leave the mount mispositioned).
- [ ] Hit `Ctrl+C` mid-session and confirm the tracking rate and `SharpCap.TargetName` are both restored.

## Summary

Follow-ups surfaced by the 2026-05-03 plugin-test acceptance run (full report bundled in this PR under `planning/test-reports/2026-05-03-12-18/`). Both items were noted as non-blockers in the report; this PR closes them out.

## Changes

- **Guard `ObsidianGeminiSettingTab.display()` against concurrent invocations** (`src/ui/settings.ts`). Each call claims a fresh `renderToken`; after every await, sections compare the captured token against `this.renderToken` and bail out if a newer call has taken over. Without the guard, calling `display()` twice in quick succession (e.g. `app.setting.open(); openTabById(...)` chained, or any path that triggers `redisplay()` while a render is mid-await) appended a second copy of every settings section into the same container.
- **Regression test** at `test/ui/settings-display-race.test.ts` — uses a deferred-promise gate to interleave a second `display()` call mid-render, asserts that downstream sections run exactly once. Confirmed to fail when the token guard is reverted.
- **Doc fix** in `docs/guide/ai-writing.md` — command-palette label is "Rewrite text with AI" (was "Rewrite selected text"); right-click menu is "Gemini Scribe: Rewrite Text..." (was "Rewrite with Gemini"). Verified against the actual `addCommand`/`setTitle` calls in `src/main.ts:514` and `src/main.ts:573`.
- **Test report** bundled under `planning/test-reports/2026-05-03-12-18/` (`REPORT.md`, `scope.md`, plus 13 screenshots covering Pass 2 + chat round-trip). Acts as a baseline for the next plugin-test run, since the skill checks prior reports for test-count drift.

author: ymrymr
body:
### Motivation
- The Windows installer previously registered a SYSTEM `ONSTART` scheduled task using the installed executable path without verifying the install directory, which allows local privilege escalation if an admin/all-users install targets a user-writable location.
- The change aims to prevent automatic boot-time service registration from potentially writable custom install paths while preserving the default all-users Program Files behavior.

### Description
- Add an Inno Setup `[Code]` function `IsProtectedAdminInstallPath` that returns true only for admin/all-users installs whose `{app}` is rooted under `{autopf}` (Program Files).
- Require `IsProtectedAdminInstallPath` in the `bootservice` task `Check` so the task is only shown/selected for protected Program Files installs.
- Require `IsProtectedAdminInstallPath` in the `Run` entry that executes the installed binary with `--install-service` so the installer will only auto-register the SYSTEM task for protected Program Files installs.

### Testing
- Verified the new guard appears in `installer/windows/setup.iss` by searching for `IsProtectedAdminInstallPath` and related keys with `rg`, which returned the updated task and run checks.
- Inspected the modified `installer/windows/setup.iss` contents with `nl -ba`/`sed -n` to confirm the `Check:` lines and the new `[Code]` function were inserted as intended.
- Confirmed the produced diff shows the `bootservice` and `--install-service` checks updated and the new `IsProtectedAdminInstallPath` function added by comparing the file before/after the change with a file diff tool.

author: zhbforum
body:
## Summary

This PR extends the habits feature with goal-based progress tracking and habit groups.

It also refactors the existing habit editor/details flow into smaller components and dedicated state hooks. This makes the habits feature easier to maintain before adding more complex flows such as grouped habits, value-based progress, dashboard integration, stats, and achievements.

## What changed

### Habit editor/details refactor

- Split the habit editor sheet into focused sections:
  - identity
  - schedule
  - goal configuration
- Split the habit details sheet into focused sections:
  - header
  - goal summary
  - value/progress actions
- Moved large style blocks into dedicated style modules.
- Added dedicated hooks for editor/details state management.
- Extracted habit mutation actions into reusable hooks.

### Goal-based progress

- Added goal/value-based progress sections for habits.
- Added completion helpers for resolving progress state.
- Added form value helpers for habit editor flows.
- Updated habit summary cards to support the new goal/progress presentation.

### Habit groups

- Added habit group domain helpers:
  - analytics
  - card presenters
  - detail presenters
  - validators
- Added habit group persistence service.
- Added habit group editor flow.
- Added habit group details sheet.
- Added habit selector list for group members.
- Added habit group summary cards and group list section.

### Habits screen integration

- Integrated habit groups into the main habits screen.
- Updated habits screen controller/view model to support both individual habits and groups.
- Added route param handling for opening habit or group details directly.
- Updated habit heatmap/screen presentation where needed.

## Why

The previous habits implementation was focused mostly on individual habits. Adding goals and groups significantly increases the amount of state, UI logic, and persistence logic involved in the feature.

This PR separates responsibilities more clearly:

- components handle focused UI sections
- hooks manage editor/details/mutation state
- model helpers prepare derived habit/group data
- services handle persistence
- the screen composes the final user flow

This structure should make follow-up work easier to review and safer to extend.

## Scope

Included:

- habit editor/details decomposition
- goal-based habit progress support
- habit mutation hooks
- habit group model helpers
- habit group storage
- habit group editor flow
- habit group details/list UI
- integration into the habits screen

Not included:

- home dashboard redesign
- stats calendar redesign
- achievement system
- profile screen refactor
- shared activity heatmap extraction

Those changes are intentionally left for separate follow-up PRs.

## Testing

Automated tests are not added yet.

Manual checks:

- created a new habit
- edited an existing habit
- opened habit details
- updated today's habit progress
- verified goal/value progress rendering
- created a habit group
- edited a habit group
- selected/removing group members
- opened habit group details
- verified habit group summary cards
- verified habits screen renders both individual habits and groups
