author: avifenesh
body:
## Why

Closes the dev/test footgun from memory note `project_ff_script_stale_lua_in_dev.md`. `ensure_library` only re-loads Lua when `flowfabric_lua_version` disagrees between client and server. If a dev edits Lua sources locally without bumping the version sentinel, a long-lived dev Valkey keeps serving the stale cached `FUNCTION LIBRARY`. Symptoms: silent stale FCALLs. Cost the PR-F cap-exceeded investigation a session of red herrings before we root-caused it.

The PR-level CI guard (`ff-script lua drift` in `.github/workflows/matrix.yml`) already catches un-bumped Lua edits before merge. This env covers the inner dev loop — the iteration where the change isn't pushed yet.

## What

- Adds `FF_FORCE_LUA_RELOAD` env. Truthy values (`1`/`true`/`yes`, case-insensitive) make `ensure_library` skip the version fast-path and always `FUNCTION LOAD REPLACE`.
- README env-var table + CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry.
- Production deploys leave it unset; the version-guard stays intact under concurrent deploys.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p ff-script` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p ff-script --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo test -p ff-script --lib` — 25 passed, no regressions on existing classification tests
- [ ] CI green on this PR

## Tradeoff

Considered a dev/test `cfg` flag instead of an env var. Rejected: consumers run the loader in their own tests + dev harnesses, so flipping via env is more portable than recompiling a workspace feature. Env also matches the pattern of `FF_DEV_MODE` already in use.

No behaviour change on unset; the existing version-guard path is untouched.

author: migueldotl
body:
## Summary

Implements the bulk of #107 — structured ContactForm validation with inline errors, aria plumbing, and a real fix for the error-state animation that wasn't firing.

### Validation
- React-owned validation via `validate(formValues)` — required fields, email shape, message `>=20` chars. Custom copy per failure mode.
- `noValidate` on the form so the browser doesn't show native popups; React renders inline messages instead.
- On submit: if errors, focus the first invalid field in document order and abort. After a failed submit, errors are derived from `formValues` each render so they clear themselves as the user fixes fields (no `useEffect` cascade).

### A11y plumbing
- Each required input gets `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` pointing at its inline `<span role="alert" aria-live="polite">`.
- Inline message styled small + red (`#fca5a5`) with tightened spacing under textarea so it matches input spacing.

### Bug fixes folded in
- **Error animation never fired** — `.catch` was spreading prior `formStatus` (success: null), so `.danger` class never landed and `error-icon` never rendered. Now sets `success: false` explicitly.
- **Status message wrapped to 2 lines** — `.form-status-message` padding tightened from `13px 26px` to `13px 13px`.
- **Storybook ContactForm stories all forced into Error path** — `viteFinal` block defines `import.meta.env.VITE_MOCK_FORM` as `''` for Storybook builds so per-story axios mocks aren't bypassed. (Cherry-picked from #114; collapses on rebase if #114 lands first.)

### Story coverage (Components/Composites/ContactForm)
- `Empty`, `Filled`, `Submitting`, `Success`, `Failed` (renamed from `Error`)
- `Error` — Last Name empty (required field)
- `MalformedEmail` — bad email format
- `MessageTooShort` — under 20 chars
- `SubmittedInvalid` — asserts focus moves to first invalid field

Example user across all stories changed from `Miguel Lozano` to `Alex Smith` so the public-facing Storybook doesn't show the author's own data.

### Cleanup
- Dropped `:user-invalid` CSS selectors (dead with `noValidate` — `aria-invalid="true"` drives the red treatment).
- Dropped `is-resolved` class (was a workaround for `:user-invalid` firing on cleared post-submit fields; obsolete now).

## Out of scope (follow-ups for #107 if wanted)
- Honeypot validation feedback (botcheck currently trips silently)
- WCAG contrast verification on the invalid-border red
- Phone format validation (intentionally left permissive per discussion)

## Test plan

- [ ] `Components/Composites/ContactForm`:
  - [ ] `Empty` / `Filled` render normally
  - [ ] `Submitting` pins button to "Sending..."
  - [ ] `Success` shows envelope icon + "Thanks for reaching out, I'll be in touch!" message animation
  - [ ] `Failed` shows error icon + "Oops! Request Failed..." message animation
  - [ ] `Error` shows inline "Last name is required."
  - [ ] `MalformedEmail` shows inline "Enter a valid email address."
  - [ ] `MessageTooShort` shows inline "Please write at least 20 characters."
  - [ ] `SubmittedInvalid` — focus moves to First Name field (story asserts via `toHaveFocus()`)
- [ ] `npm run dev` — submit a fully filled valid form and verify success path against a real Web3Forms key (or mock)
- [ ] Note: closes #107 won't auto-fire on dev merge — close manually after review

author: rowandark
body:
## Summary
This PR improves the reliability and compatibility of requests to the crt.sh certificate transparency API and Wayback Machine service by implementing request jitter, adjusting retry timing, filtering expired certificates, and updating HTTP headers to use a standard Firefox user agent.

## Key Changes
- **crt.sh improvements:**
  - Added random jitter (0-500ms) before the first request to reduce thundering herd issues
  - Increased retry delay from 3 seconds to 5 seconds
  - Added `excluded=expired` parameter to filter out expired certificates from results
  - Updated HTTP headers to use a standard Firefox user agent and include additional headers (Accept-Language, Connection) for better compatibility
  
- **Wayback Machine improvements:**
  - Updated User-Agent header to use standard Firefox user agent instead of custom scion identifier

## Implementation Details
- The jitter is implemented using `math/rand` with a select statement that respects context cancellation
- HTTP headers now more closely resemble a standard browser request, which may improve compatibility with services that filter non-browser requests
- The `excluded=expired` parameter helps reduce noise in certificate results by filtering out certificates that have already expired

## 리뷰 예상 시간

약 10분

## 작업 요약

로그인/회원가입 모바일 뷰를 변경된 디자인 시스템에 맞춰 정리하고, 기본 다크 모드와 라우팅 보호 정책을 적용했습니다. 회원가입 성공 후에는 새 온보딩 페이지로 이동해 선호 장르와 플레이 파트를 선택하도록 연결했습니다.

## 작업내용(Changes in this branch)

- 앱 기본 테마를 다크 모드로 설정
- 컬러 시스템과 dark token 기준으로 인증 화면 배경/텍스트/상태 색상 정리
- 공용 `Input`에 `roundedFull`, `underline` variant 추가 및 focus 스타일 조정
- 로그인 모바일 UI를 rounded full 입력과 SNS/약관 액션 구조로 수정
- 회원가입 모바일 UI를 underline 입력, 약관 체크, SNS 영역 포함 구조로 수정
- SNS 빠른 로그인 영역을 `SocialLoginSection` 공유 컴포넌트로 추출
- `Button` typography override가 외부 `className`을 우선하도록 수정
- 모바일 헤더를 페이지 이름 중심으로 단순화하고, 뒤로가기는 `arrow-right` asset 회전으로 통일
- `/login`, `/signup` 외 페이지에 루트 라우트 보호 정책 적용
- `/onboarding` 라우트와 장르/파트 선택 플로우 추가
- 장르 목록, 포지션 목록, 이메일 중복확인 임시 API와 MSW 핸들러 추가
- 회원가입 성공 후 프로필 업데이트 API로 nickname/email 저장
- 온보딩 완료 후 프로필 업데이트 API로 favoriteGenres/skills 저장
- 회원가입 성공 후 `/onboarding?name=...`으로 이동
- Light/Dark 모드별 key color 정책을 `key` semantic token으로 분리
- 인증/온보딩/공용 UI의 CTA, focus, checked 상태를 `bg-key`, `text-key-foreground`, `border-key`, `outline-key` 기준으로 정리

## 주요 고민 및 해결 과정(Implementation Highlights)

- 로그인과 회원가입 입력 형태가 달라 공용 `Input`에 variant를 두고, 각 폼은 시각 변형만 선택하게 했습니다.
- 헤더는 탭/우측 액션을 직접 들고 있는 구조를 줄이고, 기본 페이지 제목 + 선택적 뒤로가기 + 선택적 우측 유틸리티 구조로 단순화했습니다.
- 라우팅 보호는 개별 페이지마다 `requireLogin`을 반복하지 않고 루트 `beforeLoad`에서 공통으로 강제했습니다.
- 백엔드 계약 확정 전까지 장르/포지션 목록과 이메일 중복확인은 임시 endpoint와 MSW 응답으로 연결했습니다.
- 프로필 통합 수정 API 계약에 맞춰 회원가입 직후 기본 프로필 저장과 온보딩 결과 저장을 같은 `updateMyProfile` 어댑터로 처리했습니다.
- Dark 모드에서 secondary 계열이 key color로 쓰이는 정책을 컴포넌트별 `dark:*` 분기 대신 semantic token으로 흡수했습니다. Light에서는 `key=primary-main`, Dark에서는 `key=secondary`로 매핑해 컴포넌트는 팔레트 이름을 직접 알지 않도록 했습니다.

## User-facing changes

- 앱은 기본적으로 다크 모드로 렌더링됩니다.
- 로그인/회원가입 화면이 모바일 시안에 맞는 다크 인증 플로우로 표시됩니다.
- 회원가입 성공 후 홈이 아니라 온보딩 페이지로 이동합니다.
- 사용자는 선호 장르와 가능한 플레이 파트를 선택하거나 나중에 진행할 수 있습니다.
- 비로그인 사용자는 `/login`, `/signup` 외 페이지 접근 시 로그인 화면으로 이동합니다.

author: alvarobeltransantiago
body:
This PR introduces two key performance optimizations to the cookie clicker application:

1. **DOM Caching**: Achievement elements are now cached during initialization. This removes the need for `document.getElementById` calls within the click handler, making each click operation more efficient.
2. **Persistence Debouncing**: Saving the game state to `document.cookie` is now debounced with a 1000ms delay. This prevents frequent, expensive I/O operations and integrity hash calculations during rapid clicking. A `visibilitychange` listener ensures that any pending state is committed immediately when the user leaves the page.

Benchmarks showed that for 100 rapid clicks, DOM lookups were reduced to zero in the handler and cookie writes were reduced to just the necessary final updates.

author: derekmwright
body:
## Summary

The `scan → exchange-repartition → consumer` pattern was running as two separate distributed tasks: the scan wrote an unpartitioned WSHF, then a shuffle task read it and re-emitted partitioned WSHF. This PR fuses them into a single scan task that hash-partitions its filtered output directly via the worker's existing `writePartitionedShuffle`.

**Per fused pair this saves**:
- 1 S3 PUT (intermediate unpartitioned WSHF)
- 1 S3 GET (the shuffle reading it back)
- 1 NATS round-trip (separate dispatch + completion)
- 1 batch of intermediate-task heap pressure

## Audit

`TestAuditFusedJoinChains` — fusion firing across the join-heavy queries:

| Query | scan stages absorbed | exchange-repartitions remaining |
|---|---|---|
| Q02 | 2 | 5 |
| Q07 | 2 | 2 |
| Q08 | 3 | 3 |
| Q21 | 3 | 3 |

~half of the exchange-repartition stages eliminated per query. The remaining ones are between joins (not directly downstream of a scan), which would need producer-direction fusion or multi-stage Task messages — those are deferred follow-ups.

## Implementation

- `planner/physical/fuse_scan_shuffle.go` — new pass after `EnsureDistribution` + final `assignStageDistributions`. Walks stages, finds `(scan, exchange-repartition)` pairs satisfying safety conditions, moves the exchange's keys+count onto the scan, rewires consumers, drops the exchange.
- `coordinator/execute_stage_dag.go` — `dispatchScanFilterStage` propagates `stage.Exchange.{Keys,Count}` into `task.ShuffleKeys + task.NumPartitions`, and buckets result files by partition number when fused (matching `runShuffleSide`'s contract).
- `planner/physical/plan_tpch_test.go` — `sqlToStages` now mirrors prod by setting `UseEnsureDistribution=true` (otherwise tests miss the fusion path; harness was always correct).

## Safety conditions in `fuseScanShuffle`

1. exchange has exactly one dependency (the scan)
2. scan is plain `StageScan` (not scan-aggregate — that path owns its own RoundRobin fan-out)
3. scan has no other dependents (would break their unpartitioned expectation)
4. scan has no prior `Exchange` (would conflict with this one)

## Test plan

- [x] new `TestFuseScanShuffle_BasicAbsorbs` / `SkipsScanWithMultipleConsumers` / `SkipsFusedAggScans` (planner unit tests)
- [x] `TestTPCH_EnsureDistribution_Snapshot` golden files updated to reflect absorbed exchanges across Q02-Q22 (-45 lines net)
- [x] `cmd/tpch-harness --mode=local`: 25/25 PASS — distributed correctness gate (HARD RULE per `feedback_tpch_harness_local_gate`)
- [x] `internal/coordinator`: ok (196.8s)
- [x] `internal/planner/physical`: ok
- [ ] SF10 EC2: not yet — local runs already show 5-15% per-query speedup; the EC2 win will be larger where each S3 PUT/GET round-trip is 50-200ms instead of <1ms.

## Context

This is the first incremental step on Path B from `project_per_task_setup_audit_2026-05-03.md`. The broader multi-stage Task message work (chain N stages into one worker task) remains a multi-week project; this is the contained piece that's clearly safe because the worker already supports it via `writePartitionedShuffle`.

author: kamronbatman
body:
## Summary

Phase 3.3 of the message-interpolation cleanup. Eliminates the `rank.ToString().ToLower()` two-allocation pattern in ConPVP trophy-award messages.

- Adds `TrophyRank.LowerName()` extension returning a static lowercase string per enum value via switch expression.
- Updates 10 call sites across Tournament, KingOfTheHill, DoubleDom, CTF, BombingRun (2 each - cash and no-cash branches).

The handler now appends a static interned string directly into the packet buffer; no `ToString()` formatter and no `ToLower()` allocation per call. Source comment in BombingRun.cs ("There is no formatting flag for Lowercase, we may need a custom interface to get rid of it") is now resolved at the call-site level.

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet build ModernUO.slnx` clean
- [x] `dotnet test ModernUO.slnx` all pass
- [ ] Manual smoke test: trigger end of a ConPVP match, verify trophy message reads "gold"/"silver"/"bronze" (lowercase) as before

## Note on the broader pattern

A future PR will introduce a `:L` format specifier on `RawInterpolatedStringHandler` so the pattern `$"...{rank:L}..."` works for any enum without per-enum extension methods. This PR ships the immediate fix for the TrophyRank cluster - once `:L` lands, the LowerName extension can be removed and the call sites simplified further.

body:
## Summary

Replace the `original / reference / estimate` taxonomy with `primary / reference / commercial`. Better-fitted names for what the registry actually contains, plus a colour palette refresh that retires red from tier rendering.

## Renames + reclassifications

| From | Count | To | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `original` | 11 | **`primary`** (rename) | IRS, BLS, SSA, HUD FMR, eCFR, etc. — same set, new label. |
| `reference` (state portals) | ~205 | **`primary`** (reclassify) | State DOR / SNAP / Medicaid / CHIP. A state agency IS the publisher of authority on its own program, not a third-party interpreter. |
| `reference` (commercial) | 5 | **`commercial`** (reclassify) | Zillow ×2, RentCafe, Care.com, Numbeo. Proprietary or crowd-sourced methodology. |
| `reference` (research) | 9 | **`reference`** (unchanged) | KFF, EPI, CBPP, Tax Foundation, NCSL, AAA, HUD Handbook, Child Care Aware. |
| `estimate` | 0 | — | None existed; tier removed. |

End distribution: **215 primary / 9 reference / 5 commercial = 229**.

## No `reviewed.tsv` rows

The rename is taxonomy-only — no source's URL, data, or verification claim changes. `reviewed.tsv` is the verification log; this PR doesn't add one.

## Visual + threshold updates

- **Tier colours**: green (primary) / slate-blue (reference, shares colour with AI provenance) / gold (commercial). Red retired from tier rendering — was reading as "warning" when reference is a neutral relationship.
- New `T.commercialAccent` (#7A6628 deep gold) theme token.
- `/sources` Composition row labels + tooltips rewritten.
- `/sources` Status row tones now unconditional — Overdue / Broken stay in tone colour even at zero count.
- Tooltip labels use the cell's tone colour again (except Total cited which keeps cream since `T.ink` on `T.ink` is unreadable).
- Tier review windows: **primary 90d, reference 180d, commercial 90d**. Commercial inherits the primary cadence — index-style data updates frequently, deserves the same review pace as primary, not estimate's old 365d.
- `ThresholdsNote` rewritten with new vocabulary + colour-keyed strong text per tier.
- Citation popover `TierPill` mirrors the new colours.
- DesignLab synthetic data + helpers updated.
- Staleness issue generator + source-inventory script renamed `byTier` keys and queue label ("primary tier sources awaiting human pass").

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn verify` clean (lint + format)

## Summary

Closes the last three unchecked items in #84. After this, every test case the issue scoped runs against a real Postgres in CI.

| Test | File | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `bag_min_slot_is_non_negative_for_every_container` | `base/resources.rs` | Future change to slot-min logic that opens `slot_id = -1` to legitimate grant reservation, breaking the move-swap sentinel's safety. |
| `sentinel_slot_does_not_leak_when_swap_tx_rolls_back` | `inventory/move_/concurrency_tests.rs` | Schema-level rollback regression — a future refactor to the swap path that fails to restore `slot_id` after rollback would leave a permanent ghost row at the sentinel. |
| `vendor_purchase_and_concurrent_move_serialize_on_container_lock` | `inventory/move_/concurrency_tests.rs` | Cross-handler version of the move-vs-grant test — vendor purchase and move on the same container must serialize on the same `pg_advisory_xact_lock(player_id, container_id)` primitive. Without it, the unique-slot index rejects mid-race or the purchase silently lands on a slot the move was about to vacate. |

## Implementation notes

- **Forced-rollback test design:** Can't easily inject a failure between steps 1 and 3 of the real move handler without modifying production code. Instead, the test stages the same SQL sequence (park source at -1, move occupant into source's old slot) directly inside a Rust-managed transaction, then rolls back. This validates the schema's transactional rollback semantics for the sentinel slot, which is what actually matters for the no-leak guarantee.
- **Vendor-vs-move test:** Resolves the vendor template + store_index + price from `resources.item_list_items` at runtime rather than hardcoding ids. Follows seed renumbers automatically.
- **Bonus assertion in every concurrency test:** all of them now end with `WHERE slot_id = -1` count check. Even tests that don't exercise the swap path get the no-leak invariant pin "for free."

author: egonschiele
body:
## Summary

Make the typechecker reflect the runtime semantics of the `!` validation suffix on type annotations. Previously, the parser, AST, backend, and runtime all handled `!` (wrapping values in `Result<T, string>` via `__validateType`), but the typechecker silently ignored the `validated` flag — so `const x: Person! = obj; x.name` typechecked at compile time but crashed at runtime.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-03-bang-validation-typechecker-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-03-bang-validation-typechecker.md`

Five typechecker sites updated, each backed by a single helper (`applyValidationFlag`):

- **Variable declarations** — `const x: Person!` declares `x: Result<Person, string>`. RHS still checked against the un-bang'd type.
- **Function return types (declared)** — `def foo(): Person!` exposes `Result<Person, string>` to callers; body return statements still checked against `Person`.
- **Function return types (inferred)** — when a function has any validated parameter and no explicit return annotation, the inferred type is auto-wrapped in `Result<inferred, string>` to reflect the failure short-circuit.
- **Function return types (explicit + validated params)** — error if the user annotates a non-Result return type with validated params present (e.g. `def greet(name: string!): number` is rejected; user must write `Result<number>`).
- **Call-site validated params** — accept either the un-bang'd type `T` or any `Result<…>` (failures pass through unvalidated per the schemas docs).
- **Handler params** — `!` is rejected outright with a clear error; handlers don't have caller-observable return types, so the validation-failure semantics don't apply.

The "no rewrap" rule from `docs-new/guide/schemas.md` is honored — `Result<Person>!` stays `Result<Person, …>`.

## Test Plan

- [x] All 2298 tests pass (`pnpm test:run`)
- [x] Clean `make` build
- [x] 13 new tests in `lib/typeChecker.test.ts` (`v2: bang (!) validation` describe block)

author: davidfic
body:
## Summary
Quick Win 1 from [plans/lifecycle-trust.md](plans/lifecycle-trust.md). Closes the "11 duplicate \`completed\` grab_history rows for one release" failure mode that surfaced via the Maul S01E07 investigation today.

## Root cause
The dedup guardrail in \`rss_sync.go\` was series-wide:
\`\`\`go
activeSeries := map[string]bool{}
for _, g := range activeGrabs { activeSeries[g.SeriesID] = true }
// ... later:
if activeSeries[matched.ID] { continue }
\`\`\`

Once a grab terminated as \`completed\` but the importer didn't flip \`has_file=true\` (anime numbering pre-fix, content_path race, file format issues), the next 15-min RSS tick saw "no active grab for this series" and re-grabbed the same release. Production result: 11 dup rows for Maul S01E07 1080p ETHEL on Apr 22, each \`completed\` with 1.07 GB downloaded but no actual file on disk.

## Fix
1. **Per-episode dedup** — \`activeEpisodes\` keyed by \`episode_id\` instead of series_id. Allows legitimate parallel grabs of different episodes in the same series while preventing re-grabs of the SAME episode.
2. **Recently-completed skip** — second-line guard. Skip episodes with a \`completed\` grab in the last 6h regardless of \`has_file\`. Importer drift / file-in-flight races don't trigger fresh RSS grabs.

Implementation:
- New helper \`buildRecentlyCompletedEpisodes\` reuses the existing \`ListGrabHistoryByStatusSince\` query.
- DB error on the recently-completed lookup is non-fatal: log + fall back to active-only dedup. QW4's DB unique index will be the belt-and-braces backstop.
- The \`completedSkipWindow\` constant pinned at 6h (test enforces 1h–24h range).

## Test plan
- [x] \`go test ./internal/scheduler/jobs/...\` — 5 new tests pass
- [x] \`make check\` — lint + tsc clean
- [x] Manual verification on the live stack: the 11 dup rows for Maul S01E07 already cleaned up; with this PR live, future RSS ticks won't re-create the pattern

## Out of scope
- Full integration test of \`runRSSSync\` — function takes concrete \`*indexer.Service\` / \`*downloader.Service\` pointers, not interfaces. End-to-end coverage needs a refactor that's QW-scoped separately.
- Prism-side equivalent (movies have the same pattern) — covered by the planned shared SDK extraction post-QW5.

author: mohsen1
body: ## Summary Return-type inference (`infer_return_type_from_body`) walks the function body speculatively to compute its return type. When a parameter is a lib type (e.g., `HTMLDivElement`), the property walk during inference can consume the entire 50,000-op thread-local global resolution fuel budget. The speculation rollback mechanism restores per-context state (diagnostics, node-type cache, flow cache), but does NOT restore the global fuel counter. After rollback, the post-speculative `check_statement` pass re-evaluates the body — this time WITH narrowing context, expecting to emit any diagnostics for real. But every `consume_fuel()` call now short-circuits to `false` (global fuel exhausted), causing `get_type_of_node_with_request` to return `TypeId::ERROR` immediately. Property access on `error` is silenced, so the post-rollback `error_property_not_exist_at` is never reached. The visible symptom is that property-access diagnostics inside arrow expression bodies on lib-typed parameters are silently dropped — e.g. `(x: HTMLDivElement) => x.notAProperty` emits nothing. Worse, fuel persists for the rest of the file, so every subsequent type computation in the same source also returns `error`. A direct top-level `d.notAProperty` placed AFTER such an arrow is also silenced — a fundamental cache-pollution-by-fuel-exhaustion bug. ## Fix Snapshot the global fuel counter alongside the per-context caches in `ReturnTypeSnapshot::cache`, and restore it on `rollback_return_type`. The speculative work is real, but it is billed against a budget that gates the actual non-speculative pass — that work must be allowed to complete. (Pathological recursion in the original code would still exhaust on the post-rollback pass and bail safely; the rollback only restores fuel that was burned by speculation about to be redone.) ## Test plan - [x] Verified standalone reproducer: `const f: (x: HTMLDivElement) => any = (x) => x.propertyNotOnHtmlDivElement;` now emits `TS2339 Property 'propertyNotOnHtmlDivElement' does not exist on type 'HTMLDivElement'.` - [x] `cargo nextest run -p tsz-checker --lib` (3275 passed) - [x] `cargo nextest run -p tsz-solver --lib` (5602 passed) - [x] Pre-commit gate: 14776 tests passed, fmt/clippy clean ---

💡 What: Moved the `normalize` function outside of the main `for` loop in `LogParser.ts`.

🎯 Why: In loops processing millions of log entries, defining a function closure inside the loop causes a severe performance hit due to repeated object/function allocations and the subsequent garbage collection sweeps. Moving it outside the loop prevents this overhead.

📊 Impact: Reduces time spent in log parsing loop. Tested with a 10 million iteration loop which dropped the execution time from ~130ms to ~40ms.

🔬 Measurement: Verified the performance improvement via an external node script measuring `console.time`. The changes preserve functionality completely as verified by visual inspection of code correctly moving the function out of the loop and ensuring variables are passed appropriately. No regressions caught by build and linter.

## Summary
- complete Macro Task 4 advanced metrics: fakeable `EmbeddingClient` / `JudgeClient` provider boundaries, OpenAI-compatible default clients, and `bertscore-like` + `refusal-quality` aliases
- extend `citation-groundedness` with deterministic `metadata.citation_evidence` marker+quote matching and count-only details
- add structured provider usage aggregation to `EvalReport`, JSON reports, and Markdown reports for token/cost/latency summaries
- add runtime guardrails: normalized timeout/retry/strict config, provider retries for Laravel HTTP connection failures/429/5xx, and opt-in `MetricException` propagation
- expand README comparison with explicit `✅ YES` / `⚠️ PARTIAL` / `❌ NO` prefixes across every comparison cell

## Subtask PRs
- #18 embedding/BERTScore-like: merged into macro branch at `b7fa442`
- #19 refusal-quality judge: merged into macro branch at `e4af70b`
- #20 citation evidence spans: merged into macro branch at `0265a6f`
- #21 usage summaries: merged into macro branch at `13ac58b`
- #22 runtime provider guardrails: merged into macro branch at `d3b5b45`

## Guardrails
- package remains headless; no UI assets added
- provider clients remain fakeable and unit tests use `Http::fake()` only, with no live network calls
- malformed judge/provider responses fail closed; report usage parsing ignores malformed/non-finite values
- embedding response indexes normalize integer-like strings, including zero-padded values, before ordering and reject invalid/partial index payloads
- BERTScore-like embeds each normalized token once per sample and reuses vectors per occurrence to avoid duplicate provider cost
- citation evidence spans reject partially malformed quote lists instead of lowering the required evidence count
- runtime retry/sleep integer config falls back to safe defaults for overflowed numeric strings/floats instead of clamping to huge ints
- provider retry wrapping is limited to Laravel HTTP `ConnectionException`; unexpected request/config throwables bubble immediately and are documented on provider contracts
- strict runtime mode rethrows `MetricException` only; default report failure capture is unchanged
- built-in provider usage attaches only safe token/cost/latency fields; raw prompts/provider payloads remain out of report summaries
- built-in provider clients do not synthesize local wall-clock `latency_ms`; only explicit provider/custom-client latency fields are propagated
- provider and judge failure messages do not include raw HTTP bodies or malformed judge responses that could leak prompts/sample data into reports
- partial provider usage keeps per-field `reported` counts and renders missing Markdown usage values as `n/a` instead of synthetic zeroes
- provider usage from captured metric failures is included in usage summaries when HTTP succeeded but strict metric parsing failed, without reusing stale usage on later pre-provider failures
- `ProvidesUsageDetails` now documents current-attempt reset semantics so third-party providers do not leak stale usage into failure summaries

## Review fix rounds
- addressed Codex connector feedback by normalizing `data[].index` digit strings before embedding response ordering
- added regressions for out-of-order digit-string indexes, invalid indexes, and partially indexed embedding responses
- addressed Copilot feedback by making `AGENTS.md` branch-neutral, adding optional `ProvidesUsageDetails`, propagating provider usage into metric details, falling back to JSON-encoded sample input when judge samples omit `question`, preserving the default judge prompt when config is null, and rejecting non-finite embedding components

- addressed Copilot failure-usage/input feedback by failing closed on non-JSON-encodable shape-agnostic judge input and aggregating safe usage details from captured metric failures
- addressed Copilot expected-output/stale-usage feedback by failing closed on non-encodable judge expected output, documenting unexpected provider throwables, and snapshotting provider-backed metric usage per score attempt
- addressed Copilot usage-contract/token-cost feedback by documenting usage reset semantics for third-party implementations and deduplicating BERTScore-like token embeddings before provider calls
- addressed Copilot latency/redaction/docs feedback by removing synthesized local latency from built-in provider clients, redacting provider/judge raw failure payloads from metric exceptions, fixing README renderer class names, and adding leakage regressions
- addressed Copilot citation/index feedback by failing closed on malformed citation evidence quote lists and normalizing zero-padded digit-string embedding indexes
- addressed Copilot runtime normalizer feedback by preventing oversized digit strings/floats from clamping to `PHP_INT_MAX` for retry/sleep config

author: iron-ham
body:
**Stacked on #459.** Fourth and final phase of #281 — delivers acceptance criteria #3 (\"approve/reject proposed memories through CLI and MCP\") and #4 (\"approval records reviewer and timestamp in Notion-visible metadata\"). After this lands, every AC on #281 is covered.

## What changes

- **`MemoryService.recordReview({ memoryId, verdict, reviewer, reason? })`** — paired property-then-audit write that flips a `Status: proposed` memory to `accepted` (`verdict: \"approve\"`) or `rejected` (`verdict: \"reject\"`) and appends a `## Reviewed (YYYY-MM-DD)` audit block to the page body recording the verdict, reviewer, optional reason, and timestamp. Property write fires first (mirrors `rekeyTopicKey`'s partial-state posture), so a property-success-then-audit-failure leaves the load-bearing status flip durable; the cosmetic audit miss surfaces via the new `MemoryReviewAuditError`. A non-proposed row throws `MemoryReviewStateError` before any write — these actions are inbox-only.
- **Default-recall extends to `rejected`.** The Phase-2 default-exclude broadens from `proposed` to **both** `proposed` AND `rejected` so a `lore inbox reject <id>` row stays out of recall instead of leaking back in. The exclusion now composes via the shared `reviewTerminalStatusExclusionFilters` / `isNotReviewTerminalStatus` helpers used by `MemoryService.list`, contains-mode search, semantic search, and `queryStaleConfidence`. Explicit `status: \"rejected\"` short-circuits the exclusion for the audit path.
- **`lore inbox archive` now enforces the inbox-only contract.** A non-proposed row rejects with an actionable error pointing at `lore-memory action='archive'` for general archives. Without this, a fat-fingered `lore inbox archive <accepted-uuid>` would soft-delete a load-bearing memory.
- **MCP**: extends `lore-memory` polymorphic dispatcher with `action='approve'` and `action='reject'`. Reviewer is resolved via the engineer-identity chain (`LORE_USER_NAME` → `users.me`) when the caller doesn't pass an explicit `reviewer`. The polymorphic prompt-budget caps bump from 7000 → 7300 (combined) and 5200 → 5700 (per-tool) to absorb the two new discriminated-union branches plus the new `reviewer` input field. Both bumps are documented inline as #281-Phase-4 single-action additions, not surface-doubling regressions. Six new dispatch tests in `polymorphic.test.ts` exercise the happy paths, the identity fallback, the no-identity error, and the discriminated-union rejection paths.
- **CLI**: new `lore inbox` command with four subcommands —
  - `inbox list [--project <name>] [-n <limit>]` — list memories awaiting review.
  - `inbox approve <memoryId> [--reason <text>] [--reviewer <name>]` — promote to `accepted`. Optional `--reviewer` overrides the resolver.
  - `inbox reject <memoryId> [--reason <text>] [--reviewer <name>]` — flip to `rejected`.
  - `inbox archive <memoryId>` — inbox-only archive via `MemoryService.archive`.

  Approve/reject branch on `MemoryReviewAuditError`: exit code **2** (vs **1** for state errors) lets a wrapper script distinguish \"review didn't happen\" from \"review happened but audit is missing\" without parsing the stderr message.
- **Audit block format** — `## Reviewed (YYYY-MM-DD)` with verdict (`approved` / `rejected`), reviewer, and optional reason lines.
- **`docs/mcp-tools.md`** updated to document the two new actions.
- **Schema invariant test** — `notion/schema.test.ts` pins every `MemoryStatus` literal as a registered Status select option so a future schema rename can't silently break `recordReview`'s `select.name` writes.

## Resulting end-to-end flow

After all four PRs in the stack land:

1. (Phase 3) Operator sets `hooks.proposeAutosaveLearnings: true` in `.lore.yaml`.
2. The autosave sub-agent writes every atomic learning with `Status: proposed`.
3. (Phase 2) `MemoryService.list` / `search` / `queryStaleConfidence` default-exclude the proposed rows from recall.
4. (Phase 2) Wake-up surfaces the proposed memories in their own \"Proposed Memories\" section, oldest-first, with the true total in the heading and a saturation cue when the slice is smaller.
5. (Phase 1) `lore status` shows the inbox count broken down by source / agent.
6. (Phase 4) The reviewer runs `lore inbox list` to triage, then `lore inbox approve <id>` / `lore inbox reject <id> --reason <...>` to act. Rejected rows stay out of default recall.

The same approve / reject path is reachable from MCP via `lore-memory action='approve'` / `'reject'`, so an authorized agent can review on the operator's behalf.

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 3895/3895 pass; new tests cover the rejected-default-exclude shape across list/search/staleConfidence, the explicit-status short-circuit on both proposed and rejected, the inbox-only archive guard, the MCP dispatch paths for approve/reject (happy + identity-fallback + no-identity + Zod rejections), and the schema invariant on Status options
- [x] Read-only sanity: `lore inbox list` and `lore status` against the production Mail vault both render cleanly with no regressions

body:
## Summary

PostHog data audit revealed three structural blockers preventing meaningful marketing analysis:

1. **0 attribution** between landing visitors and signups — anonymous landing distinct_id never bridged to backend user id
2. **No UTMs on any outbound surface** — channel performance was guesswork
3. **100% bounce on every blog article** — single generic CTA, no topic tailoring, nothing at the end of the article

This PR fixes all three across landing, blog, app frontend, email, and tweet pipeline.

## What changed

### Tracking fixes (the main analytics blockers)
- `posthog.identify(user.id, {email, plan})` on signin/signup completion in `src/stores/user.js` — bridges the anonymous landing cookie to the backend user id so `auth:user_signup`, `workspace:workspace_create`, `explorer:subscription_create` events finally roll up to the originating marketing visit
- Expose PostHog client on `window` so the existing `window.posthog.capture(...)` calls in onboarding components actually fire
- Explicit `autocapture: true` and `ip: true` on both PostHog inits (app + landing)

### UTM tagging on every outbound link we control
- Tweet pipeline blog promos (`utm_source=twitter&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=blog_promo`)
- Drip email sequence — per-step campaign + brand header/footer
- Demo-ready transactional email
- Prospect cold emails (regex post-processor adds UTMs to any `*.tryethernal.com` URL in AI-generated body, preserves the unsubscribe URL)
- Landing navbar / mobile nav / footer (Sign In, Get Started)
- Blog footer Sign In, blog article mid/end CTAs
- Free tools inline CTAs (`utm_source=tool&utm_medium=inline_cta&utm_campaign=<tool_name>`)

### Blog conversion (`blog/src/layouts/PostLayout.astro`)
- Topic-aware CTA picker with 6 variants based on frontmatter tags:
  - **Comparison** → "See how Ethernal compares" → /pricing + /etherscan-alternative
  - **Security/Auditing/MEV/DeFi** → "Trace any transaction" → signup + tracing demo article
  - **L2/Infrastructure/Blobs** → "Run a block explorer for your L2" → signup + /pricing
  - **Ethernal/Developer Tools** → "Try Ethernal on your chain" → signup + /features
  - **EVM/Smart Contracts/Ethereum/AA/ZK/etc.** → "Need an explorer that understands modern EVM?" → signup + live explorer demo
  - **Default fallback** → original generic copy
- Always-rendered end-of-article CTA card between body and related posts (previously nothing — readers hit the related rail and bounced)
- Mid-article CTA now uses the same topic-aware copy and triggers on 2+ headings (was 3+) so short EIP posts also get one
- All CTAs tracked with `cta_position: mid_article|end_article` for downstream funnel analysis

### Chain page comparison cross-links
- Every `/chains/*` page now links to the relevant comparison page in its Related section:
  - L1s + Sepolia → `/etherscan-alternative`
  - BNB Chain → `/etherscan-alternative` (titled "BscScan Alternative")
  - All L2s/L3s/testnets → `/blockscout-alternative`

### llms.txt polish
- Tightened lede with concrete value props ("in under 5 minutes", "Used by L2s, appchains, and private networks in production")
- Added "Quick facts" block so LLMs grab pricing, setup time, supported chains, and alternative names in the first chunk
- Sharpened Comparisons section descriptions

### PostHog project setting (applied via API, not in this diff)
- Added `$referring_domain not_regex tryethernal\.com$` to project `test_account_filters` to drop bot-subdomain referrer pollution from dashboards

## Test plan

- [ ] After deploy, in 24h confirm `$identify` events fire (currently 0)
- [ ] Re-run "landing visitors → signup overlap" query — should now be non-zero
- [ ] `SELECT properties.utm_source, count() FROM events WHERE event='$pageview' AND properties.utm_source IS NOT NULL` — should show twitter / landing / blog / drip / tool / prospect rows
- [ ] Spot-check `$el_text` is populated on a normal CTA click event
- [ ] `$geoip_country_code` should populate on new pageviews
- [ ] Visit a blog article from each topic group (e.g. `/blog/best-block-explorers-evm-chains-2026`, `/blog/the-bug-auditors-tools-miss`, `/blog/evm-opcodes-101`, `/blog/transaction-tracing-with-ethernal`, `/blog/what-is-l2-why-rollup-needs-block-explorer`) and verify the right CTA variant renders both mid and end of article
- [ ] Visit `/chains/ethereum` and `/chains/arbitrum-one` — comparison link should appear in Related section above Pricing
- [ ] Visit each `/tools/*` page, perform an action that triggers the inline CTA, click it — confirm the URL contains the right `utm_campaign`
- [ ] After deploy + 24-48h, build the saved Insight: pageview → auth:user_signup → workspace:workspace_create → explorer:subscription_create, broken down by utm_source

body:
## Summary

ChatGPT's Choice 3 — keep the catastrophe germs, change the visible carrier model — implemented and validated. **Spike-3 PASSES at 8-bit AND 16-bit.** Wall time 0.40 s. This is the production substrate path for Phase 1.

## Outcome

| | 8-bit | 16-bit |
|---|---|---|
| SHA-256 roundtrip | **PASS** | **PASS** |
| RS frames failed | 0 / 21 | 0 / 21 |
| RS bytes corrected | 1 | 0 |
| Decode wall time | 0.07 s | 0.09 s |
| Total wall time | 0.40 s | 0.40 s |

## What changed (renderer / carrier separation)

The original proposal conflated CRYPSOID's strict density renderer with the phoxoidal carrier's display function. Bug + ChatGPT's analysis: those don't have to be the same. CRYPSOID's anti-Gaussian thesis is about the catastrophe-germ basis, not the action functional. Spike-3 keeps the basis verbatim and chooses a display-optimized action:

```
spike-2 (CRYPSOID strict):  intensity = exp(-0.5 * (mahal_sq + H²))
spike-3 (display-optimized): intensity = sigmoid(baseline + amp * H)
```

H is the same Pearcey-class catastrophe-germ polynomial:
```
H(s, t) = κ₁s² + κ₂t² + χ(s³ − 3st²) + ω(3s²t − t³) + ζ(s⁴ + t⁴)
```

CRYPSOID's renderer remains the truth model for 3DGS scene rendering. The phoxoidal carrier uses a different display function for 8-bit visibility.

## Why this works at 8-bit when spike-2 didn't

| Property | spike-2 (strict H²) | spike-3 (sigmoid) |
|---|---|---|
| Sign of H | Lost (squared) — 1 bit/germ overhead | **Preserved** — full 40 bits/germ |
| Saturation | Corners saturate to 0 at 8-bit floor | **Bounded in (0.01, 0.99)** |
| Inverse | Nonlinear LM trust-region | **Linear LSQ in logit space** |
| Local minima | Yes (H² ambiguous basins) | **None** (convex) |
| Pre-restart | ±warm_start, multi-restart | **Not needed** |
| 8-bit byte error rate | 14.4% (over RS threshold) | **~0%** (1 byte in 5,359) |
| Wall time per germ | ~6 ms | **~0.06 ms** (100× faster) |
| 8-bit gate | FAIL (Brotli error) | **PASS** |

## The amp parameter

Empirical sweep at sigma=4, half_size=12, unit codebook, 50 random germs at 8-bit pixel depth:

| amp | Byte-exact germs | Byte error rate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.10 | 25/50 | 12.8% | Signal too weak vs pixel noise |
| 0.20 | 50/50 | 0.0% | |
| **0.30** | **50/50** | **0.0%** | spike-3 default |
| 0.50 | 50/50 | 0.0% | |
| 1.00 | 20/50 | 46.4% | Sigmoid saturates at corners; logit blows up |

Sweet spot: `amp ∈ [0.2, 0.5]`.

## Sweep across all three spikes (1,000-germ payloads)

| Spike | Forward model | 16-bit gate | 8-bit gate | Wall time | Bits/germ |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 (linear) | `baseline + amp · envelope · H` | PASS | FAIL | 0.31 s | 40 |
| 2 (CRYPSOID strict) | `exp(−0.5·(mahal+H²))` | PASS | FAIL | 6.18 s | 39 |
| **3 (sigmoid)** | `sigmoid(baseline + amp · H)` | **PASS** | **PASS** | **0.40 s** | **40** |

Spike-3 dominates: CRYPSOID-thesis-aligned (vs spike-1's linear hack), works at 8-bit (vs spike-2's failure), and 15× faster than spike-2.

## Files added

```
phoxcar/spike3/
├── README.md                                   (scope + renderer/carrier framing)
├── basis.py                                    (Cholesky orthonormal basis; reused from spike-2)
├── density.py                                  (NEW — sigmoid forward model)
├── solver.py                                   (NEW — linear LSQ in logit space)
├── germ_codec.py                               (NEW — 40 bits/germ, byte-aligned, no sign convention)
├── header.py                                   (AXP6 inner header; reused from spike-2)
├── ecc.py                                      (RS(255, 223); reused from spike-2)
├── encoder.py / decoder.py                     (composed pipeline)
├── test_roundtrip.py                           (the gate)
└── results/
    ├── SPIKE3_REPORT.md                        (full report)
    ├── spike3_carrier_8bit.png                 (354 KB; passing 8-bit carrier)
    ├── spike3_carrier_16bit.png                (1.2 MB; passing 16-bit carrier)
    └── *.manifest.json + roundtrip_*.json
```

## Spike retention

- **spike-1** stays in tree as the linear-model sanity baseline.
- **spike-2** stays in tree as the CRYPSOID-strict reference / truth model documentation.
- **spike-3** is the production substrate going forward.

## Phase 1 P3 next steps (per `SPIKE3_REPORT.md` §9)

Each is a discrete bridge per `phoxoidal_carrier_proposal/07_INTEGRATION_BRIDGES.md` (revised). Spike-3 unblocks all of them:

1. Manifest cluster bootstrap — encode positions in carrier itself, not JSON sidecar.
2. Tier C aesthetic-field design — make the carrier look like a photograph.
3. Synthetic capture-noise tolerance profile (perspective tilt, focus blur, JPEG, rolling shutter, moiré).
4. Real V2/V3 capture roundtrip — display on MSI G27C4X, capture with S21 FE / Z Flip 4 / S23 Ultra.
5. Density at scale — 6M germs (full AXP6 sample carrier scale).
6. CRYPSOID format compatibility — write `.3dphox` v40 native germ chunks.

## Reproduce

```bash
pip install brotli reedsolo numpy scipy Pillow
cd phoxcar/spike3
python3 test_roundtrip.py --bit-depth 8     # PASS
python3 test_roundtrip.py --bit-depth 16    # PASS
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm `density.py` uses `tools/crypsorender/math/germ.py`'s 5-coef Pearcey basis verbatim
- [ ] Confirm `solver.py` is plain linear LSQ (no LM, no nonlinear)
- [ ] Read `results/SPIKE3_REPORT.md` §3 for the spike-2 vs spike-3 comparison
- [ ] Read §6 for the three-spike summary
- [ ] Read §9 for the Phase 1 P3 next-bridge sequence
- [ ] Decide: authorize spike-3 as Phase 1 P3 baseline?

Draft PR — Phase 1 awaits this and the open `09_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` items (capture envelope, lane home in Aurexis Core).

|---|---|---|
| **CPI components** | CPIHOSSL, CUSR0000SAS, CUSR0000SACL1E, CPIENGSL, CPIUFDSL, CUUR0000SETA02 | CPI Shelter / Services / Core Goods / Energy / Food / Used Vehicles |

Each entry declares its FRED transform via the `units` field (`pc1` for Y/Y, `pch` for Q/Q) so the proxy fetches the precomputed transform rather than scaling client-side. Capacity thresholds are stress-regime values (e.g. 8% for shelter inflation, 85% for capacity utilization).

body:
## Summary

# タスク指示書: Amazon PA-API の本格実装

## 概要
バックエンドの `amazon.py` は現在スタブ実装である。Amazon Product Advertising API (PA-API 5.0) を呼び出す本格実装に置き換える。リクエスト署名（AWS Signature V4）を含む通信処理を実装し、モックによる単体テストでカバーする。

## 背景・正本
- **API仕様の正本**: Amazon Product Advertising API 5.0 公式仕様（PA-API 5.0）
- **インターフェースの基準**: 既存スタブ `amazon.py` の関数シグネチャを基準とする
- 既存スタブのシグネチャと PA-API 5.0 仕様が矛盾する場合は、**API 仕様を優先**して既存側を修正してよい

## 対象ファイル/モジュール

### 必須調査対象（plan 時に Read/Glob/Grep で実態確認）
- `amazon.py`（既存スタブ本体。場所はリポジトリ内を Glob で特定）
- `amazon.py` の呼び出し元すべて（Grep で全箇所列挙）
- 既存の設定/環境変数読込機構（`config.py` / `settings.py` / `.env` ローダ等の有無）
- 既存のテスト構成（テストディレクトリ、テストパターン、モックヘルパー）
- 依存パッケージ管理ファイル（`requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` / `Pipfile` 等）

## 作業内容

### 優先度: 高

#### 1. 既存スタブと呼び出し元の調査（plan）
- `amazon.py` のスタブ実装を読み、公開されている関数のシグネチャ（関数名・引数・戻り値の型）を確定する
- すべての呼び出し元を Grep で洗い出し、戻り値がどのように消費されているかを把握する
- 既存スタブのシグネチャと PA-API 5.0 仕様（オペレーション名、必須パラメータ、レスポンス構造）の対応関係を整理する
- 矛盾がある場合は「API 仕様に合わせるための修正点」を計画レポートに列挙する

#### 2. 設定/認証情報の取得経路の決定（plan）
- 既存の設定システム（設定ローダ・環境変数アクセサ）の有無を調査
- 既存システムがあればそれを使う。なければ `.env` を読む経路を新設（標準的な方法でよい）
- 必要な認証情報: `AccessKey` / `SecretKey` / `PartnerTag`（AssociateTag）
- マーケットプレイスは日本固定（`www.amazon.co.jp`）、ホストは `webservices.amazon.co.jp`、リージョンは `us-west-2`（PA-API 5.0 日本の正規値を仕様で確認）

#### 3. PA-API 5.0 通信処理の実装（implement）
既存スタブが提供しているオペレーションに対応する関数を、PA-API 5.0 への実通信に置き換える。

- **エンドポイント**: `https://webservices.amazon.co.jp/paapi5/<operation>`
- **HTTPメソッド**: POST
- **必須ヘッダ**: `Content-Type`, `X-Amz-Date`, `X-Amz-Target`, `Content-Encoding: amz-1.0`, `Host`, `Authorization`
- **ペイロード**: JSON（`PartnerTag`, `PartnerType=Associates`, `Marketplace=www.amazon.co.jp`, オペレーション固有パラメータ, `Resources`）
- **署名**: AWS Signature Version 4
  - `service = ProductAdvertisingAPI`
  - `region = us-west-2`
  - 正規リクエスト → 文字列 to sign → 署名鍵導出（`AWS4` + SecretKey → date → region → service → `aws4_request`）→ HMAC-SHA256 で署名
- レスポンスは PA-API 5.0 の JSON 構造をパースし、既存呼び出し元が期待する形に整形して返す（呼び出し元が期待する構造も plan で確定する）

#### 4. エラーハンドリング・リトライ（implement）
- HTTP 429（TooManyRequests）および PA-API のレート制限相当エラーで **指数バックオフによるリトライ** を行う
  - リトライ回数の上限を設ける（具体値は plan で決定し、定数化）
  - 待機時間は指数バックオフ（必要なら jitter）
- 上記リトライで回復しない場合、および 429 以外の API エラー（4xx/5xx、PA-API エラーレスポンス内 `Errors` 配列含む）は **例外を送出**
  - 例外型は既存例外があればそれに合わせる。なければ新規定義（plan で決定）

#### 5. 単体テスト作成（write_tests）
モックによる単体テストのみ作成する。実 API は叩かない。

- **HTTP クライアントをモック化**して以下を検証:
  - 正常系: 想定リクエスト（URL / ヘッダ / ボディ）が正しく組み立てられる
  - 正常系: レスポンス JSON を期待する戻り値構造に整形できる
  - 異常系: 4xx/5xx で例外が送出される
  - 異常系: PA-API エラーレスポンス（`Errors` を含む 200 以外）で例外が送出される
  - リトライ: 429 が返った後に成功するケースで指数バックオフが動作してリトライされる
  - リトライ: リトライ上限を超えた場合に最終的に例外が送出される
- **AWS Signature V4 署名生成ロジックの単独テスト**:
  - 固定の入力（AccessKey, SecretKey, タイムスタンプ, リクエストペイロード, ヘッダ）に対し、期待される `Authorization` ヘッダ／署名文字列が生成されることをアサート
  - 期待値は AWS 公式仕様の手順に沿って事前計算した値を使用
  - 正規リクエスト・StringToSign・署名鍵・最終署名の各段階で検証できると望ましい
- 設定ローダ部分のテスト（既存設定機構ありの場合は既存パターンに従う、なしの場合は環境変数読み出しが正しいことを検証）

### 優先度: 中

#### 6. 依存ライブラリの追加（必要なら）
- HTTP クライアント、`.env` ローダなど、リポジトリに既存があればそれを使う
- なければ追加する。追加した場合は依存ファイル（`requirements.txt` 等）も更新する
- AWS SigV4 はサードパーティライブラリに頼らず標準ライブラリ（`hmac`, `hashlib`）で実装してよい（テストしやすさ・依存最小化のため）

### 優先度: 低
- なし（このタスクのスコープ内で残作業を作らない）

## ユーザー明示の制約
- **対象マーケットプレイスは日本のみ**。複数リージョン対応はしない
- **テストはモックによる単体テストのみ**。実 API を叩く統合テストは作成しない
- **API 失敗時は例外を投げる**（隠蔽しない）
- **既存インターフェースは基本維持**だが、PA-API 5.0 公式仕様と矛盾する場合は仕様を正本として既存側を修正してよい

## 確認方法
- 単体テストがすべてパスすること
- 署名生成テストが PA-API 5.0 / SigV4 の期待値と一致すること
- ビルド/型チェック（プロジェクトに設定があれば）でエラーなし
- `amazon.py` 内にスタブ実装の残骸（`pass` だけの関数、`NotImplementedError`、ダミー戻り値など）が残っていないこと
- 呼び出し元すべてが新しい実装で問題なく動作する（呼び出し元の引数・戻り値消費箇所が想定どおりに整合）

## やらないこと（ユーザー明示）
- 複数マーケットプレイス対応
- 実 API を叩く統合テスト
- 後方互換コード（旧スタブの形を残すための分岐等）

## Open Questions
（技術的不明点がある場合のみ。スコープ判断は含めない）
- なし（既存スタブの内容・既存設定機構の有無・呼び出し元・テスト規約はワークフロー側でコード調査により確定すること）

## Execution Report

Workflow `default` completed successfully.

body:
No system-wide type scale existed; font sizes and spacing were scattered magic numbers across components, and the launcher's section header used the same styling as individual tile labels. A cascade ordering bug in `calc` also caused the generic `Textual` rule to silently override the specific `ExpressionLine`/`ResultLine` sizes.

## stile: typography token module

New `stile::typography` module exported from `stile::lib`:

```rust
// Type scale (logical px)
pub const SCALE_DISPLAY: f32 = 48.0;  // calc result
pub const SCALE_H1:      f32 = 32.0;  // clock time
pub const SCALE_H2:      f32 = 20.0;  // section heading
pub const SCALE_H3:      f32 = 15.0;  // tile label, panel header
pub const SCALE_BODY:    f32 = 13.0;  // body, window title, expression line
pub const SCALE_LABEL:   f32 = 12.0;  // AM/PM, status bar
pub const SCALE_CAPTION: f32 = 10.0;  // paths, fine-print detail

// Spacing rhythm (4 px grid)
pub const SPACE_XS: f32 =  4.0;
pub const SPACE_SM: f32 =  8.0;
pub const SPACE_MD: f32 = 12.0;
pub const SPACE_LG: f32 = 16.0;
pub const SPACE_XL: f32 = 24.0;
```

## petals: hierarchy and cascade fixes

**`Description::ApplicationTitle`** — new variant distinguishes the launcher "Applications" section header from per-tile `ApplicationName` labels. `default_stylable_for` grants it font styling. The section header now renders at `SCALE_H2` (20 px, Bold) vs tile labels at `SCALE_H3` (15 px).

**Calc cascade ordering fix** — the generic `Textual` base rule is now placed *before* `ExpressionLine`/`ResultLine` in the rules vec, so specific overrides win the cascade correctly. Previously all three rendered at 22 px:

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Key labels | 22 px | `SCALE_H3` 15 px |
| Expression line | 22 px (bug) | `SCALE_BODY` 13 px |
| Result line | 22 px (bug) | `SCALE_DISPLAY` 48 px |

**Constants applied** across `calc`, `chrome`, `clock`, `launcher`, `showcase`; spacing normalized to the 4 px rhythm.

## Tests

Two new focused tests assert hierarchy at the rule level:
- `expression_line_font_size_is_distinct_from_result_line` — verifies all three calc text roles resolve to distinct, correct sizes
- `section_title_uses_application_title_description_and_is_larger_than_tile_labels` — verifies `ApplicationTitle` is present and `font_size` exceeds `ApplicationName`

---

- **What canonical concept owns this meaning?** `Presence` — visual surface styling tokens have no behavioural semantic; they govern how typed UI surfaces are presented, not what they mean.

- **Is this introducing truth or compatibility?** Compatibility surface — typography tokens and spacing constants are presentation-layer conventions, not typed-world truth.

- **If compatibility, what is the canonical typed-world concept underneath it?** The `Description` enum is the typed classification; these rules govern how descriptions render. The constants encode shared presentation contracts between stile (style engine) and petals (structure).

- **Are new names aligned with ontology and classification docs?** `ApplicationTitle` follows the `Application*` namespace already in use. `SCALE_*`/`SPACE_*` are presentation tokens with no ontological meaning.

- **Does this align with `docs/migration/concept-mapping.md`?** No kernel, ABI, or concept-mapping surfaces touched. Pure UI presentation layer.

Increments when CoinGecko returns `market_cap=null/0` but `current_price>0` — the silent-rejection shape that caused the RIV (riv-coin) 100x miss on 2026-05-03. body:
## Summary

Fixes critical shell injection vulnerability in dashboard/server.js config API endpoints.

**Attack:** PUT `/api/config/agent/:name/*` and DELETE `/api/config/governor/agents/:name` accepted unsanitized `:name` URL params that flowed directly into `execSync()` → RCE as root via sudo.

## Changes

- **Add input validation** (`VALID_AGENT_NAME` regex + `ENABLED_AGENTS` allowlist) to all 6 PUT config routes, GET prompt route, and DELETE route
- **Harden `writeEnvVar`**: replace `execSync(echo ... | sudo tee)` with `fs.writeFileSync` + atomic `sudo mv` — eliminates content injection
- **Harden `removeEnvVar`**: replace `execSync(sudo sed -i)` with in-process regex replace + atomic write
- **Add `VALID_ENV_KEY`** validation to prevent regex injection via key params
- **Add `shellQuote()`** helper for remaining necessary shell commands
- **Rewrite `setEnvFlag`/`removeEnvFlag`** to delegate to hardened functions
- **Harden POST create** with `fs.writeFileSync` + atomic mv

## Testing

- `node --check dashboard/server.js` passes ✅
- No functional changes to valid requests — only rejects malformed agent names

Fixes #11759

## Summary

- **`set_memory`** — completely overwrites persistent memory with new content (total rewrite, not append). Useful for reorganising, cleaning up, or correcting memory without leaving old entries behind.
- **`load_memory`** — reads and returns the current memory contents on demand. Lets Claude (or the user) inspect what's been remembered at any time.
- Minor: clarified `save_memory` description to explicitly say "append" to distinguish it from the new `set_memory`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `save_memory` still appends as before
- [ ] `set_memory` with new content fully replaces `data/memory.md`
- [ ] `load_memory` returns current memory contents

body:
#### Context

Implement a complete autonomous agent orchestration system that polls Linear issues, manages concurrent agent workers, and coordinates multi-turn interactions with a Codex app-server via JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over stdio.

#### TL;DR

*Add Symphony: a Python orchestrator that manages autonomous agents working on Linear issues, with workspace lifecycle management, retry logic, and Codex integration.*

#### Summary

- **Orchestrator** (`orchestrator.py`): Main event loop that polls Linear for candidate issues, dispatches agents with concurrency control, handles retries with exponential backoff, and reconciles running tasks against issue state changes
- **Agent Runner** (`agent_runner.py`): Manages per-issue lifecycle including workspace creation, hook execution, and multi-turn Codex sessions with continuation prompts
- **Codex App-Server Client** (`codex/app_server.py`): Implements JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over subprocess stdio, handles initialization handshake, turn streaming, approval/tool-call dispatch, and Linear GraphQL tool execution
- **Linear Client** (`linear/client.py`): Async GraphQL client for fetching candidate issues, refreshing state, and executing raw queries (exposed to agents via tool)
- **Configuration** (`config.py`): Typed dataclass-based config resolution from WORKFLOW.md YAML front matter with environment variable expansion
- **Workspace Manager** (`workspace.py`): Per-issue directory lifecycle with safety validation, hook execution, and cleanup
- **Workflow Loader** (`workflow.py`): Parses WORKFLOW.md files (YAML front matter + Markdown body)
- **Prompt Builder** (`prompt.py`): Jinja2-based template rendering for per-issue prompts with issue context
- **CLI** (`main.py`): Entry point with graceful shutdown, logging configuration, and workflow path resolution
- **Models** (`models.py`): Core data structures (Issue, LiveSession, RunningEntry, RetryEntry, OrchestratorState)
- **Logging** (`log.py`): Structured key=value logging for operational visibility

#### Alternatives

- Monolithic single-turn agent: Would require manual orchestration and retry logic at call site
- Synchronous implementation: Would block on I/O and prevent concurrent agent execution
- Direct Codex subprocess management: Orchestrator abstracts protocol complexity and enables tool/approval handling

#### Test Plan

- No automated tests included in this diff; integration testing against live Linear instance and Codex app-server required
- Manual verification: workflow loading, issue polling, agent dispatch, turn streaming, and workspace cleanup

author: fatel3ss
body:
Movement was poll-based: _process checked Input.is_action_pressed every 0.2s, which works for real keyboards (OS sends key-up on release) but breaks for AI-injected events that never auto-release. The action stayed "pressed" forever and the poll fired indefinitely.

Add an edge-triggered _input handler that fires one move on the just-pressed edge of any movement action and resets the poll timer. Real keyboards still get continuous walk via the existing _process poll when held. is_action_pressed(action) filters echo events so keyboard auto-repeat doesn't double-fire.

Pairs with an auto-release in the local godot_mcp runtime helper to guarantee MCP key events behave as taps.

author: itc-linux
body:
In d3d12_command_list_resolve_render_pass_attachments(), barrier deduplication for resolve destinations uses an incorrect subresource comparison.

Current code:

    found_dst = found_dst || !memcmp(&regions[j].srcSubresource,
        &regions[k].dstSubresource, sizeof(regions[j].dstSubresource));

This compares srcSubresource (region j) against dstSubresource (region k), which is inconsistent with the deduplication intent for destination barriers. The first argument must be regions[j].dstSubresource:

    found_dst = found_dst || !memcmp(&regions[j].dstSubresource,
        &regions[k].dstSubresource, sizeof(regions[j].dstSubresource));

As a result of the bug:
1. Required dst barriers may be skipped when src/dst subresources happen to cross-match.
2. Duplicate dst barriers may be emitted when dst subresources actually match but the buggy check fails to detect it.

This fixes the destination subresource comparison used by resolve barrier deduplication.

## Summary

PR 2 of the [reader-ui-refresh spec](../blob/main/specs/reader-ui-refresh.md), landing on top of the toolchain bump from #11. Implements the full v1 scope: design tokens, light/dark theme with persistence, theme toggle in Settings, and iPad-Safari touch polish.

## What lands

**Design tokens (`web/src/styles/tokens.css`)** — color, spacing, type scale, radii, plus a `--tap-target: 44px` token. Light is the default; dark applies via `[data-theme="dark"]` OR (no explicit choice AND `prefers-color-scheme: dark`).

**CSS Modules** — `App.module.css` and `SettingsPane.module.css` for component styles. Vite supports CSS Modules natively, no new deps. ESV-rendered HTML stays under a global stylesheet (`styles/passage.css`) since those classes (`verse-num`, `woc`) are emitted by the API, not by us.

**Theme system (`web/src/theme.ts`)** — `readTheme/writeTheme/applyTheme` + `useTheme()` hook. Choice routes through the existing `ToggleStore` platform abstraction; key is top-level `theme` with values `"light" | "dark" | "system"` (default `"system"` = no localStorage entry).

**3-state toggle in Settings** — System / Light / Dark, alongside the existing auto-load-daily-reading toggle.

**FOUC guard** — sync inline script in `index.html` `<head>` reads localStorage and sets `data-theme` before paint, so users who picked dark don't see a flash of light.

**iPad-Safari polish:**
- `viewport-fit=cover` + safe-area insets on the app shell and settings pane (both orientations)
- 44×44 CSS px tap-target floor on every interactive control via `--tap-target`
- `font-size: 16px` globally on input/select/button — kills iOS zoom-on-focus
- `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the reading surface; no `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch` (no-op on current iOS)

## Spec lifecycle

- **Status: In Progress → Shipped** (this PR makes it user-visible on merge).
- Last Open question (load-bearing CSS audit) closed: `grep` found no test/external refs to component class names.
- 5 new Decisions added: load-bearing audit result, FOUC inline script, theme module shape, tap-target enforcement strategy, and the status flip itself.
- `specs/README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` updated.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` (Vite 8) succeeds; embedded SPA loads from the Go binary.
- [x] `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` pass.
- [ ] **Manual desktop smoke** (Chrome / Safari / Firefox): theme toggle works (System / Light / Dark), choice persists across reloads, system-theme change is followed when set to "System". No FOUC on cold load with dark chosen.
- [ ] **Manual iPad Safari** (real device or simulator): cold load lands in correct theme, safe-area honored in portrait + landscape, tap targets feel right, no zoom on input focus, passage scroll has native momentum, overscroll stays contained.
- [ ] **Qualitative perf parity check** on the same iPad: chapter-switch and page-turn don't feel slower than the pre-refresh build.
- [ ] No visual regressions in `passage-reader` (chapter / range selection, verse rendering, formatting toggles).
- [ ] No regressions in `auto-load-daily-reading` (toggle still works from Settings).

⚠️ I could not run the browser smoke checks myself — the boxes above are intentionally unchecked. Please verify on a real iPad / desktop browser before merging.

author: thefourcraft
body:
## Summary

Adds `[[layers.operational.commands]]` support to the Operational DAP layer. Configured commands are run via `SubprocessRunner`, with findings, metrics, and `reproduce_cmd`. No commands configured → runner not added, no latency, no skipped results.

## Configuration

```toml
[[layers.operational.commands]]
name       = "db-migrate-check"
cmd        = "python"
args       = ["manage.py", "migrate", "--check"]
cwd        = "backend"    # relative to project root; omit = project root
timeout_ms = 10000        # default: 30000

[[layers.operational.commands]]
name = "lint"
cmd  = "ruff"
args = ["check", "."]
```

Existing `.barzel.toml` files without `[[layers.operational.commands]]` load cleanly — `#[serde(default)]` on the field.

## Design

**Timeout enforcement** (`run_timed` in `process.rs`):
- Trait method `run_timed(cmd, args, cwd, timeout_ms)` with default that delegates to `run()` (backward compatible for all existing runners).
- `OsProcessRunner::run_timed()` uses `wait-timeout` crate: spawns child with piped stdout/stderr, drains both in background threads to prevent pipe-buffer deadlock, calls `child.wait_timeout()`, kills + waits child on timeout so no processes leak.

**Severity policy**:
- Non-zero exit → `High` / `OPERATIONAL_COMMAND_FAILED` — includes output snippet truncated at 300 Unicode scalar values (char-boundary safe; emoji/multibyte output tested)
- Spawn failure (binary not on PATH) → `Critical` / `OPERATIONAL_COMMAND_SPAWN_FAILED`
- Timeout → `High` / `OPERATIONAL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` — suggestion includes `timeout_ms` config key

**`reproduce_cmd`**: executable and every arg are POSIX single-quoted; `cwd` is prepended as `cd '<dir>' &&` when set. Tested with spaces and embedded single quotes.

**cwd resolution**: relative paths joined with `project_root`; absolute paths used as-is. Tested with a cwd-recording mock.

**`MockProcessRunner` changes** (additive, backward-compatible):
- `failing(stdout)` — original semantics restored: `Ok(success=false, stdout=...)`
- `spawn_error(msg)` — new: `Err(io::Error::NotFound)`, used in spawn-error tests
- `unavailable()` — original semantics preserved
- `sequence(vec)` — new `SequentialMock` for ordered per-call responses

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test --bins` — 550 tests pass (29 new across config/process/runner/run)
- [ ] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` — clean
- [ ] No commands → no operational-cmd layer in report
- [ ] Two commands parse with defaults (timeout_ms=30000, args=[], cwd=None)
- [ ] Existing `.barzel.toml` with only health_checks loads cleanly (no commands key)
- [ ] Pass: success=true → Pass layer, metrics.passed
- [ ] Non-zero exit → High finding with output snippet and reproduce_cmd
- [ ] Spawn error → Critical finding, message includes binary name and command name
- [ ] Timeout → High finding, suggestion mentions timeout_ms
- [ ] reproduce_cmd: cmd/args/cwd all shell-quoted; spaces and embedded single quotes handled
- [ ] cwd relative → joined with project root; absolute → used as-is
- [ ] Long ASCII output truncated at 300 chars; multibyte (emoji) output truncated safely without panic
- [ ] timeout_ms from config forwarded to run_timed

author: matweiss
body:
## Phase 2 status (2026-05-03)

CC shipped Phase 2 dashboard scope on branch `tmw618-phase2`. PR ready
for review at https://github.com/Matweiss/clawd-brain-data/tree/tmw618-phase2.

### What shipped (commit-per-step)

1. **scaffold import** — clawd-dashboard had been on the VPS but never
   committed. Single `chore(dashboard): import existing scaffold`
   commit lands the Next 14 + Tailwind 3 setup so the rest of the PR
   reads as Phase 2 work only. The orphan
   `clawd-dashboard-phase1-pathBprime/` (byte-identical duplicate of
   `app/`) was left untracked — separate cleanup decision.
2. **init** — `lib/supabase-server.ts` (server client, accepts
   `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` or legacy `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY`),
   `@shared/*` tsconfig alias pointing at `../shared/`,
   `clawd-dashboard/.env` populated from `/root/.config/clawd-state/env`.
3. **signed-url helper** — `lib/meetings/signed-url.ts` with
   `createMeetingFrameSignedUrl` + batch + `not_found` fallback.
4. **API routes (7)** — list / detail / reanalyze / push-to-notion-501
   / signed-urls/refresh / devices / rotate-key-501. Granola helper at
   `lib/meetings/granola.ts` shells out to
   `skills/granola-bridge/scripts/granola-query.py`.
5. **list page** — `/meetings` between Contacts and Deals in nav,
   real-data table + `?demo=1`-gated mock-states table for visual QA.
6. **detail page** — UnspokenCallout hero, transcript + visuals split,
   Lightbox with ←/→/Esc keyboard nav and the locked
   archived-image fallback copy ("Image archived after 90 days —
   caption preserved.") with `slide_text` rendered prominently.
   Reanalyze button verified end-to-end against meeting
   `4364062c-411d-4793-b08a-6e5dc6747e31`.
7. **Realtime** — `useMeetingReviewRealtime` hook, filtered by
   `granola_meeting_id` (never broad-subscribes), refetches detail on
   any emit.
8. **devices page** — `/meetings/devices` with stale chip when
   `last_seen > 24h`, 5-min poll, rotate-key visible-but-disabled
   button hitting the 501 stub. Cross-link to/from `/meetings` via
   `PageShell` rightMeta.
9. **responsive** — single-column tab strip below 900px (Unspoken /
   Transcript / Visuals); two-column hero+split at 900px and up.

### Deviations from CC-PHASE2-BRIEFING.md

- **File layout**: brief had `clawd-dashboard/src/app/(authed)/meetings/...`
  but the actual repo is flat — `app/`, `lib/`, `app/components/`. No
  `(authed)` route group either; Cloudflare Access gates at the edge.
  Followed the existing `app/contacts/page.tsx` convention instead.
- **`shared/db.ts` typing**: server Supabase client is intentionally
  untyped (`SupabaseClient` not `SupabaseClient<Database>`) because the
  hand-written `shared/db.ts` is missing the per-table `Relationships`
  field that supabase-js's generic constraint requires — without it,
  `.from()` collapses to `never`. Routes cast at the boundary using
  types from `@shared/db`. Cheapest fix until `shared/db.ts` is
  regenerated via `supabase gen types typescript`.
- **Detail response shape**: adds a `meeting` field with Granola meta
  (title, started_at, ended_at, attendees) alongside `review`. Lets
  the page render the live title and meta even when no review row
  exists yet (status=null empty state) without a second round-trip.
  Slight extension to `docs/granola-bridge-contract.md`.
- **Granola CLI returns `id`**: contract uses `granola_meeting_id`;
  list route maps at the boundary.
- **`SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` accepted**: the dashboard `.env.example`
  documents `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` but `/root/.config/clawd-state/env`
  uses `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` — server client accepts either name to
  match the analyzer's env naming.
- **Signed-URL refresh route** lives under
  `/api/meetings/[granola_meeting_id]/signed-urls/refresh` per the
  storage spec; bundled into step 3 (the brief's six API routes do not
  list it, but the spec calls for it).
- **Open-in-Granola button**: not shipped. Neither `granola-bridge`
  scripts nor the Granola cache JSON expose a deeplink URL pattern.
  Slot is reserved in `ActionBar.tsx`; drop in the `<Link>` once a
  pattern is documented. No dashboard PR needed beyond setting the
  href.
- **Real meeting `4364062c`** in the brief is a prefix; full
  `granola_meeting_id` is `4364062c-411d-4793-b08a-6e5dc6747e31`.
- **`DeviceRow.tsx`**: brief listed it as a separate file; folded
  inline into `DevicesClient.tsx` since it's purely presentational and
  used in one place.

### Branch publish notes

- Workspace `main` was 32 commits ahead of `origin/main` when CC
  started, with secrets in `backup-snapshots/.../config/.env` etc.
  blocking GitHub push protection. `tmw618-phase2` was rebased onto
  `origin/main` so the branch publishes cleanly. The 32-commit-ahead
  state on local `main` remains a separate cleanup.
- Mat's pre-existing tracked-file modifications were stashed
  (`pre-tmw618-rebase`) before the rebase; partial pop afterwards left
  unmerged markers for files created in the rebased-away commits, which
  CC reset to HEAD. Stash@{0} preserves the original state for any
  recovery; safe to `git stash drop stash@{0}` once Mat has resolved.

### Phase 2 known limitations / followups for v1.5

- Server Supabase client untyped — fix by regenerating `shared/db.ts`
  via Supabase CLI when available (`supabase gen types typescript
  --project-id tntoclpqyisfttpchajh > shared/db.ts`).
- Open-in-Granola URL pattern needs documenting; trivially adds a link.
- Realtime channel disconnect / reconnect UX is unmodeled — if the WS
  drops, page still shows last-known status. Consider a "live · stale"
  badge if this becomes an issue.
- Browser-driven smoke (visibilitychange refresh, 5-min device poll,
  Realtime live transition) was not exercised from CC's side — needs
  an SSH-tunnel eyeball or E2E (Playwright) coverage.
- Reanalyze button optimistically flips local status to analyzing;
  Realtime overwrites within ~100ms. If Realtime is broken at the
  Supabase level, the spinner stays stuck — currently no fallback
  poll. Could add a single 30s poll-after-click as a safety net.
- `clawd-dashboard-phase1-pathBprime/` orphan still untracked on disk;
  Mat to decide delete vs. keep.

### Smoke summary (server-side; tsc clean throughout)

- `GET /api/meetings/list?limit=3` — 200, 3 Granola meetings (1
  complete + 2 not_yet_analyzed).
- `GET /api/meetings/sample-meeting-insights-001` — 200, full detail
  payload; first signed URL fetched a 34KB JPEG with valid SOI marker.
- `GET /api/devices` — 200, 3 devices (real `mac-macbookpro` plus 2
  sample devices), none stale.
- `POST /api/meetings/.../push-to-notion` and `/devices/.../rotate-key`
  — 501 with `not_implemented` body.
- `POST /api/meetings/.../signed-urls/refresh` — 200 with two fresh
  signed URLs, scoped by meeting.
- Reanalyze flow: `analyzing` flips synchronously in route, then
  `complete` ~2s later via analyzer subprocess; `generated_at`
  preserved by analyzer's idempotent regeneration.

### Dev loop

```bash
# On VPS, in clawd-dashboard:
cd /root/.openclaw/workspace/clawd-dashboard
npm install   # one-time
npm run dev   # binds 127.0.0.1:3000

# From Mac:
ssh -L 3000:localhost:3000 root@100.91.33.9
# Then http://localhost:3000/meetings in any Mac browser.
```

`npm run dev` warns about Next 14.2.15 having a known security
advisory; bumping is a separate decision Mat owns and was not in scope.

author: chphch
body:
## Summary

Adds an inline sort picker for the archived (inactive) sessions list, surfaced where the data is — directly under the "Hide archived" toggle.

- **Started** (default): sort by `session.createdAt` (current behavior — newest started first)
- **Last seen**: sort by `session.activeAt` (newest activity first)

Date group headers ("Today" / "Yesterday" / "N days ago") are recomputed from the chosen field so the headers match the visible order in both modes.

Gated behind an experimental **`expArchiveSortByLastSeen`** setting, **off by default**. With it off the picker row is not emitted at all and archived sessions sort by `createdAt` exactly as upstream. Users opt in from Settings → Features.

## UX

A small right-aligned row appears under "Hide archived" with the two options inline as text pills: `↑↓ Started · Last seen`. The current selection is shown in bold; the other is dimmed. Tapping either pill switches directly to that ordering — no popup, no hidden state, both alternatives are visible at all times so the user always knows what they're switching between.

The row is rendered as a new `archive-sort` `SessionListViewItem` emitted by `useVisibleSessionListViewData` only when archive is visible (between the "Hide archived" toggle and the first date header). It collapses with the rest of the archive section.

## Why a picker, not a default change

#636 proposed flipping the default sort for the entire connections list and was closed `not_planned`. This is narrower:

- Archive section only — active sessions are unchanged. (Complements #1440's `sortSessionsByActivity`, which orders the *active* list; the two are independent settings.)
- Opt-in twice over — behind an experiment flag, and the default within it stays `Started`.
- Two equally valid mental models (when I started it vs when I last touched it), surfaced inline so each user picks.

## Scope

App-only. No server / sync protocol / encryption changes. `activeAt` is already on `Session` and exposed via `SessionRowData` for inactive sessions, so no new data plumbing is needed.

- Two settings: `archivedSessionsSortBy: 'createdAt' | 'lastSeenAt'` (the value, default `'createdAt'`) and `expArchiveSortByLastSeen: boolean` (the gate, default `false`)
- New `SessionListViewItem` variant: `{ type: 'archive-sort'; current: ... }`
- `useVisibleSessionListViewData` resorts + regroups + emits the inline picker row when the flag is on
- `SessionsList.tsx` renders the row as two `Pressable` text pills with active/inactive styling
- 10 language translations + spec update

Forward/backward compatible: older clients ignore the unknown setting fields via the existing partial-parse path in `settingsParse`.

## Proof

End-to-end run on standalone `happy-server` (PGlite) + Expo web, driven headlessly by Playwright. Cursor sprite injected as a DOM overlay so the click target is visible (Playwright headless does not capture the OS cursor).

The 5-frame GIF cycles a full there-and-back interaction:

1. Default sort. Indicator: **Started** · Last seen. Order reflects `createdAt` (newest started first): `bravo-feature` → `delta-spike` → `charlie-bug` → `alpha-project`.
2. Cursor moves to "Last seen" pill (showing what's about to be tapped).
3. After tap → list reorders inline. Indicator: Started · **Last seen**. Order reflects `activeAt` (newest activity first): `alpha-project` (1h) → `delta-spike` (7h) → `bravo-feature` (1d) → `charlie-bug` (5d). Date group headers (`Today` / `Yesterday` / `5 days ago`) recompute from the chosen field.
4. Cursor moves back to "Started" pill.
5. After tap → reverts to original order. Indicator back to **Started** · Last seen.

![archive sort reorder](https://github.com/chphch/happy/releases/download/pr-proofs/archive-sort-toggle.gif)

The 4 archived sessions in the GIF are synthetic fixtures injected via a tiny capture-only shim on `window.__happyStorage` (production code unchanged) — picked so the two orderings differ in 3 of 4 positions, making the reorder visually unambiguous.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `settings.spec.ts` — defaults include `archivedSessionsSortBy: 'createdAt'` and `expArchiveSortByLastSeen: false`
- [x] Web smoke (Playwright + standalone happy-server): inline picker appears below archive toggle, both pills always visible, list reorders end-to-end on tap, indicator reflects state in real time, fully reversible

## Summary
Foundation for the visual brush-up. Each per-section view used to re-spell the same Tailwind chain for buttons / cards with subtle divergence (\`px-3.5\` vs \`px-4\`, \`primary-500\` vs \`primary-400\`, some hover scale and some not). This commit centralises the patterns so future tweaks land in one place — and removes a few visible inconsistencies as a side effect.

## What's new
- **\`src/components/common/button.tsx\`** — \`variant: primary | secondary | ghost\`, \`size: sm | md | lg\`. Renders as \`<a>\` when \`href\` is supplied, \`<button>\` otherwise.
- **\`src/components/common/card.tsx\`** — \`variant: default | interactive | muted\`. Hero, Stacks, Features, Getting Started all switch to it.
- **Semantic tokens in \`styles.css\`**:
  - \`--color-surface-card / -elevated / -muted\` — three opacities of "card surface"
  - \`--color-code-bg / -code-fg\` — replaces hardcoded \`bg-slate-900\` on \`<pre>\` blocks

## Visible side effects (intended)
- Stacks tile CTA padding aligns with Hero CTA (was \`px-4 py-2\`, hero was \`px-3.5 py-2.5\`)
- Getting Started step circle now uses \`primary-600/400\` (was \`primary-500/600\`) to match Button primary
- Stacks outer wrapper goes from \`bg-white/50 dark:bg-slate-900/50\` to \`bg-surface-muted\` (semantically the same; just named)
